Vulkan-Hpp handle header opening and object-handle wrappers (2026-11-06; source interval only; no new GD or body/path/LOC credit): inspected `workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_handles.hpp:1-600` for initial forward declarations and alias ordering, then `2935-4100` for the handle-type trait and wrapper implementations beginning with SurfaceKHR, debug callbacks, DisplayKHR, SwapchainKHR, Image, Semaphore, Fence, PerformanceConfigurationINTEL, QueryPool, Buffer, PipelineLayout, and DescriptorSet. No distinct discrepancy established; the intervening forward-declaration range and later handle classes remain open. No Vulkan operation or build was run; source-only.

**OD2298 — HID mouse tablet-range arithmetic can send Intuition an invalid zero denominator:** a reversed-by-one absolute range produces zero exactly; the full signed 32-bit interval overflows the signed calculation and cannot fit the tablet’s 32-bit range field. Scoped to selected USB HID mouse packages when the tablet event reaches Intuition. See [OD2298](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2298) and the [descriptor/range trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-full-width-tablet-range-overflow-od2298). Source-only; no descriptor or input event was used.
**EK798 — Per-core PC frequency queries sample APERF/MPERF on the caller CPU:** `GetCPUInfo()` selects the requested CPU's saved record, but standalone frequency sampling reads counters on the executing CPU; unpinned SysExplorer per-core queries can display another CPU's frequency. Scoped to APERF/MPERF-enabled standalone PC systems when execution and selected CPU differ. See [EK798](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek798) and the [selected-core sampling trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L2549). Source-only; no query or MSR access was run.
**OD3523 — PCIPC can leak ACPI IRQ route nodes when PCI driver registration fails:** route nodes are accumulated before PCI/PCIPC objects are created. PCI-base construction failure strands the local bridge list; per-host PCIPC driver construction failure frees the bridge node without freeing its nested route nodes. Scoped to PC builds with ACPICA and nonempty host-bridge route lists during allocation failure. See [OD3523](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3523) and the [registration failure/ownership trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pcipc-acpi-driver-registration-failure-route-ownership-od3523). Source-only; no allocation failure or ACPI enumeration was induced.
**OD3415 — ACPI device HIDDs retain unused discovery nodes:** fan, battery, AC-adapter, power-meter and thermal drivers keep one staging node per discovered device after successful registration, and also strand nodes on namespace or registration failure. Successful paths pin the module, so these allocations persist for its lifetime. See [OD3415](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3415) and the [five-initializer ownership trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#L28209). Source-only; no firmware walk or allocation failure was run.
**GD6223 — Appearance theme preview uses a one-plane scratch bitmap on planar screens:** the offscreen render can encode only pixel indices 0 and 1, then is copied directly into the preview, so multi-pen themes lose their colors. Scoped to Appearance Preferences on classic planar screens with depth greater than one; HIDD friends take a different allocation path. Separate from GD6229's PenMode state mismatch. See [GD6223](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd6223) and the [bitmap allocation and draw trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd6223-planar-preview-depth-recheck). Source-only; no GUI or bitmap operation was run.
**GD6229 — `SetRPAttrsA()` applies direct-RGB pen mode to planar RastPorts:** the setter toggles `RPF_NO_PENS` without checking bitmap type, but only writes the direct color into the GC for HIDD bitmaps. Appearance Preferences uses this combination in its theme preview; on a classic planar screen the one-plane friend bitmap stays planar and preview fills can use the default GC color. External planar callers share the API defect. See [GD6229](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd6229) and the [Appearance Preview caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd6229-appearance-preview-planar-caller-recheck). Source-only; no drawing operation was run.
**GD4817 — Generic JAM2 alpha-template blending misses the foreground value at full alpha:** the `/256` channel interpolation leaves each differing channel one value toward the background when alpha is 255 (or zero with inverted alpha). Applies to generic HIDD bitmaps inheriting `PutAlphaTemplate()` in non-transparent color-expansion mode. See [GD4817](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd4817) and the [arithmetic/caller recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L14611). Source-only; no rendering operation was run.
**GD5855 — IconList label clipping uses the object X coordinate as its top edge:** `DrawEntryLabel()` sets `objrect.MinY = objX` instead of `objY`; this is active in Wanderer’s default direct-display path because buffering is off by default and the only buffer-enable branch is disabled by an undefined macro. Depending on the object’s screen position, labels can be clipped out or stale. See [GD5855](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd5855) and the [default rendering-path recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L14459). Source-only; no GUI redraw was run.
**OD11027 — AHI_CA can leave its public screen locked when GUI construction fails:** after `LockPubScreen()`, VisualInfo/menu/layout failure returns before `UnlockPubScreen()`. The unconditional `CloseGUI()` cleanup cannot unlock it because the screen pointer is local and is not stored. The leaked visitor count prevents the screen owner from closing the public screen. Scoped to explicitly building optional `AHI_CA`, omitted from the default executable list. See [OD11027](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11027) and the [caller and visitor-count trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahi-ca-public-screen-lock-rollback-od11027). Source-only; no GUI or screen was used.
**OD3575 — HDAudio publishes a codec with an empty capability list:** if both the DAC and function group report no sample rates or sample sizes, initialization still publishes the card. The normal AHI requester then queries min/max rates and passes index `-1` into the unchecked frequency-table lookup; allocating the mode also indexes an empty list. See [OD3575](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3575) and the [capability and requester trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#hdaudio-zero-capability-requester-caller-recheck-od3575-2026-11-01). Scoped to native HDAudio builds with a codec reporting an empty capability. Source-only; no codec or query was used.
**EK125 — task.resource can fault and retain its task-list lock after iterator allocation fails:** `LockTaskList()` obtains the shared semaphore before allocating its handle and returns NULL without releasing it; `NextTaskEntry(NULL)` dereferences NULL before its guard. Selected callers either fault in enumeration or skip unlock on NULL, leaving the semaphore held. See [EK125](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek125) and the [task-list caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L9189). Source-only; no allocation failure was induced.
**OD4442 — USB PTP cannot represent independent DOS protection bits:** mixed WRITE/DELETE restrictions are normalized to writable, and a READ-only restriction is cached as successful although `ACTION_READ` still proceeds. Scoped to the optional PTP class on devices advertising `SetObjectProtection`. See [OD4442](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4442) and the [protection/read-path trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#L28101). Source-only; no protection change, read or device operation was run.
<a id="gd9875"></a>**GD9875 — `ChangeVPBitMap()` can dispose a planar HIDD wrapper during a concurrent view refresh:** its bitmap conversion and `MakeVPort()` run before the active-view semaphore, so a mixed planar/HIDD transition can dispose the wrapper while `LoadView()` passes that VPD to display methods. The checked-in Intuition swap/rethink routes share `LockIBase`; no maintained caller performs the mixed-representation sequence, so this remains a medium-confidence public-API concurrency candidate. See [GD9875](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd9875) and the [caller/lock-boundary reconciliation](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L13976). Source-only; no swap or concurrent refresh was run.
**EK9334 — RDB table serialization masks block-write failures:** table writer ignores BADB/PART/FSHD/RDSK write results, and treats the LSEG writer’s error block number as progress; it returns success and HDToolBox clears the changed flag. See [EK9334](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9334) and the [write-result/caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#rdb-partition-table-write-error-propagation-recheck-ek9334-2026-11-01). Source-only; no write or I/O error was induced.
**EK9333 — RDB trusts `DE_TABLESIZE` beyond fixed environment arrays:** loading and writable DosEnvec updates use the unvalidated count for copies into/out of 20-entry arrays; sufficiently large sizes exceed their enclosing allocations, and selected DOSBoot/USB callers pass the size to `MakeDosNode()`. See [EK9333](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9333) and the [copy-bound/caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#rdb-dosenvec-size-downstream-caller-closure-ek9333-strengthened-2026-10-26). Source-only; no malformed RDB was used.
**EK9331 — EBR traversal can loop on a nonzero link cycle:** the parser follows link blocks until a zero link or error, without tracking visited blocks or bounding the chain; nonempty entries can also allocate duplicate handles on each pass. See [EK9331](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9331) and the [EBR traversal trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ebr-backend-and-recursive-caller-pass-ek9329ek9330ek9331-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no EBR media was read.
**EK9330 — EBR AddPartition dereferences a failed handle allocation:** its constructor can return NULL, but the backend immediately forms `&new_ph->ln` for insertion. See [EK9330](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9330) and the [allocation/insertion trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ebr-backend-and-recursive-caller-pass-ek9329ek9330ek9331-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no allocation failure was induced.
**EK9329 — EBR table-open failure orphans earlier logical-partition handles:** the backend enqueues handles while walking the chain, but a later error causes the generic wrapper to discard the table list without calling backend cleanup. See [EK9329](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9329) and the [partial-open cleanup trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ebr-backend-and-recursive-caller-pass-ek9329ek9330ek9331-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no EBR disk or allocation failure was used.
**EK9328 — MBR backend trusts caller-supplied slot indices:** AddPartition and writable `PT_POSITION` paths index the four-entry array without range checks, and AddPartition can replace an occupied slot while its old handle remains live. HDToolBox’s checked path chooses a free slot, so scope is other callers or invalid API input. See [EK9328](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9328) and the [backend/caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#mbr-partition-backend-full-body-and-public-caller-pass-ek9328-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no MBR edit or write was run.
**EK9327 — GPT’s maximum-length partition name lacks a NUL in `ln_Name`:** a name with 36 nonzero low bytes fills the 36-byte node-name array without termination. The generic `PT_NAME` getter is bounded and safe; direct node-name string consumers can read beyond the name. See [EK9327](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9327) and the [name termination/caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#gpt-partition-name-termination-and-consumer-recheck-ek9327-2026-11-01). Source-only; no GPT media was used.
**EK9326 — GPT parser trusts unchecked entry dimensions:** entry count and size arithmetic determine the allocation, while the loop reads fixed fields and UTF-16 names without validating `EntrySize`; undersized entries or wrapped allocation arithmetic can lead to reads past the table buffer. See [EK9326](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9326) and the [entry-table bounds trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#gpt-parser-full-body-caller-and-failure-boundary-pass-ek9325ek9326-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no GPT media was read.
**EK9325 — GPT validation trusts an on-disk header size beyond its one-block buffer:** after minimum checks, the declared size is passed to CRC without checking it against the allocated block. See [EK9325](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9325) and the [header-bound trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#gpt-parser-full-body-caller-and-failure-boundary-pass-ek9325ek9326-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no GPT media was read.
**EK9324 — GPT partition handles narrow 64-bit LBAs to `ULONG`:** GPT attribute getters retain full LBAs, but handle construction narrows start/count before raw read/write offsets are reconstructed from the handle geometry. At 512-byte sectors the start wraps above 2 TiB. See [EK9324](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9324) and the [GPT-to-handle trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#gpt-parser-full-body-caller-and-failure-boundary-pass-ek9325ek9326-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no GPT disk or I/O was used.
**EK9323 — Partition.library can miss 64-bit I/O capability on large disks:** its NSD probe uses a 32-bit capacity product and omits the inclusive high cylinder; if that leaves the estimate at or below 8,388,608 sectors, legacy read/write commands remain selected even when the device supports 64-bit commands. See [EK9323](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9323) and the [geometry/command trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#partition-geometry-to-nsd-command-selection-pass-ek9323-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no disk or I/O was used.
**EK9322 — DOSBoot can overrun the partition-name buffer while suffixing a duplicate:** `PT_NAME` accepts 31 characters into a 32-byte array, then the collision path appends `".1"` without checking capacity. See [EK9322](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9322) and the [name-bound trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-duplicate-partition-name-bound-recheck-ek9322-2026-11-01). Source-only; no scan was run.
**EK9321 — DOSBoot can leak its blank mouse-pointer buffer:** if the no-media window and pointer allocation succeed but animation setup returns NULL, `anim_Stop()` skips freeing the buffer because it only does so when animation data exists. See [EK9321](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9321) and the [pointer allocation/cleanup trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-no-media-animation-constructor-and-teardown-pass-ek9320ek9321-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no allocation failure was induced.
**EK9320 — DOSBoot renders the no-media animation after frame storage allocation fails:** `banm_Init()` returns a non-NULL animation descriptor even when its chunky frame or planar backing allocation is missing; the caller immediately renders from that state. See [EK9320](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9320) and the [allocation-to-first-render trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-no-media-animation-constructor-and-teardown-pass-ek9320ek9321-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no allocation failure or display was induced.
**EK9319 — DOSBoot leaks graphics and intuition references on quiet screen retries:** when a no-media screen cannot be opened, the quiet helper returns without closing libraries it opened; DOSBoot retries and opens them again. See [EK9319](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9319) and the [screen retry ownership trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-quiet-screen-retrylibrary-ownership-pass-ek9319-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no display failure was induced.
**EK9318 — PPC DOSBoot leaks the Radeon HIDD open reference on setup failure:** Sam440 and CHRP standalone configurations open `radeon.hidd`; if subsequent graphics setup fails, the early return skips `CloseLibrary()`. See [EK9318](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9318) and the [PPC setup/cleanup trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-radeon-hidd-open-reference-recheck-ek9318-2026-11-01). Source-only; no driver was initialized.
**EK9317 — DOSBoot retries menu setup without a failure bound:** failed gadget population or `OpenWindow()` leaves the page result at -1, which does not satisfy the loop's exit conditions. Persistent setup failure can hold early boot indefinitely. See [EK9317](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9317) and the [setup/retry trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-menu-setup-retry-recheck-ek9317-2026-11-01). Source-only; no allocation or window failure was induced.
**EK9316 — DOSBoot leaves its Topaz font reference open:** non-m68k builds open a font while populating Boot Options but do not close that reference; GadTools releases only the separate references it opens for the listviews. Reopening the page can retain additional font references. See [EK9316](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9316) and the [font ownership recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-topaz-font-probe-lifetime-pass-ek9316-added-2026-10-22). Source-only; no GUI was run.
**EK9315 — DOSBoot truncates boot-list selection indices to a signed byte:** the listview returns a `WORD` selection, but DOSBoot matches it using signed `BYTE`; high rows cannot be represented, and overflow makes the result compiler-dependent. See [EK9315](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9315) and the [listview/index trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-boot-list-index-width-pass-ek9315-2026-10-22). Source-only; no GUI was run.
**EK9314 — DOSBoot accepts a short `DosEnvec` then reads `de_DosType` past its end:** the menu accepts table index 15, while `de_DosType` is index 16; with media present this can produce an invalid displayed type or a fault. See [EK9314](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9314) and the [bound recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-variable-length-dosenvec-bound-recheck-ek9314-2026-11-01). Source-only; no device or menu was used.
**EK9313 — DOSBoot can wrap the displayed disk capacity on 32-bit builds:** `DosEnvec` geometry fields are multiplied at `IPTR` width before the result is assigned to `UQUAD`; totals above 2^32−1 sectors can therefore be shown too small or as zero. Scope is the optional Boot Options capacity display; disk I/O is not implicated. See [EK9313](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9313) and the [width recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-capacity-arithmetic-width-recheck-ek9313-2026-11-01). Source-only; no disk or menu was used.
**EK9312 — DOSBoot applies device toggles to the wrong MountList slot:** the Devices list omits entries without a startup device, but its compact row code indexes state later consumed in full MountList order. With a skipped node before a displayed row, toggling that row can disable another node during final reorder. Scoped to the optional Boot Options menu and such MountList ordering. See [EK9312](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9312) and the [state-index trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-device-row-selection-index-recheck-ek9312-2026-11-01). Source-only; no menu or boot was run.
**EK9311 — DOSBoot leaks Boot Options label nodes on setup failure:** labels are allocated before window creation, but `freeGadgets_PageBoot()` runs only after a successful OpenWindow/message loop. A failed context or window setup therefore leaves successfully allocated labels behind. Scoped to the optional Boot Options page with row allocations followed by setup failure. See [EK9311](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9311) and the [ownership trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-boot-options-label-ownership-failure-recheck-ek9311-2026-11-01). Source-only; no failure was induced.
**EK9310 — DOSBoot resolves filtered boot-list rows against the full MountList:** with a nonbootable entry before bootable entries, clicking the second displayed boot option can select the first; accepting it then promotes the wrong node for boot. Scoped to the optional Boot Options menu when those list orders occur. See [EK9310](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9310) and the [selection trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-boot-options-filtered-list-index-and-selection-recheck-ek9310-2026-11-01). Source-only; no GUI or boot was run.
**EK9309 — DOSBoot dereferences a failed Boot Options row allocation:** after the per-device `AllocVec()` fails, an open-error/no-media formatter still reads `listNode->ln_Name`. Scoped to the optional boot menu and a MountList row whose label allocation fails. See [EK9309](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9309) and the [source trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-device-row-allocation-failure-trace-ek9309-rechecked-2026-11-01). Source-only; no menu or allocation failure was run.
**EK9308 — DOSBoot can drop or overrun its stale USB boot-node state:** it sizes `devicesEnabled` from the initial MountList, then later processes the live list. A late USB partition can be omitted with no menu; growth beyond twice the snapshot count can make the menu index past the array. See [EK9308](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9308) and the [source recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#dosboot-mountlist-snapshot-race-source-recheck-ek9308-rechecked-2026-11-01). Source-only; no menu or boot was run.
**EK9307 — i386 omits a valid memory-map entry ending at 4 GiB:** the exclusive-end sum wraps to zero, so `mmap_InitMemory()` rejects the range and does not create MemHeaders for that RAM. **EK9306 — `pthread_rwlock_trywrlock()` succeeds when its caller already owns the write lock:** the selected implementation routes through reentrant Exec `AttemptSemaphore()` and increments the nest count, although POSIX requires `EBUSY`. `pthread_rwlock_tryrdlock()` correctly fails in this case and is excluded. Applies to clients linking `linklibs-pthread`; no in-tree caller was found. See [EK9306](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9306) and the [corrected coverage trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#pthread-rwlock-try-call-self-owner-contract-recheck-ek9306-corrected-2026-11-01). **EK9303 — i386 Exec startup dereferences a missing optional boot command line:** both selected Multiboot parsers can omit `KRN_CmdLine`, but priority-0 `exec_boot()` passes the zero default to `strstr()` before `RawIOInit()`. **OD1946 expanded — partial first-read/write allocation failure leaves an AUDIO handle open with incomplete buffer/request state; retry can use an invalid request or make zero progress, and close can abort an uninitialized request.** See [OD1946](AROS-other-drivers.md#od1946) and the [allocation/caller recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahi-handler-od1946-dos-error-return-and-partial-allocation-state-recheck). Source-only; no allocation failure or I/O was induced.
**OD1451 expanded — AHI-Handler accepts unsupported `UNIT=` values, including `AHI_NO_UNIT` and wrapped negative values, then queues ordinary file I/O through a NULL `io_Unit`.** See [OD1451](AROS-other-drivers.md#od1451) and the [parser/device caller trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahi-handler-unsupported-unit-range-and-null-unit-io-od1451-expanded). Source-only; no device or I/O was run.
**OD10991 — AHI-Handler plays compressed AIFC data as raw PCM:** it ignores the COMM compression type and submits encoded bytes as signed PCM. Scoped to compressed AIFC input played through the documented `copy file.AIFC AUDIO:` route; Filesave emits uncompressed `NONE`. See [OD10991](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10991--ahi-handler-plays-compressed-aifc-payloads-as-raw-pcm) and the [reader cross-check](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahi-handler-aiffaifc-input-reader-and-filesave-writer-cross-check-od10991-added-no-bodyloc-credit-2026-10-31). No file or audio device was used; source-only.
**OD9572 expanded — Filesave preserves a zero AHI mixing rate: recording divides by zero, and AIFF/AIFC playback hangs in header finalization when Stop waits for the worker.** See [OD9572](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9572) and the [Filesave finalization recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#filesave-zero-mix-rate-playback-finalization-recheck-od9572-expanded-2026-10-31). Source-only; no AHI call or audio operation was run.
**EK8952 — Reusing a deleted pthread TLS key exposes stale per-thread values:** key deletion leaves per-thread slots intact, and re-creation reuses an index without resetting active threads; `getspecific` and the new destructor can consume the previous value. Scoped to applications linking optional `linklibs-pthread`; no checked-in caller found. See [EK8952](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8952) and the [coverage trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#pthread-tls-key-reuse-ek8952-rechecked). Source-only; no pthread operation or thread was run.
**OD4056 expanded — USB Audio leaves over-capacity sample rates selectable:** the selected Deneb RTIso path reserves controller-buffer slices from endpoint MaxPktSize but copies the rate-derived hook length without a slice bound, so an over-capacity mode can overwrite adjacent controller-buffer RAM. See [OD4056](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4056) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only; no descriptor, stream, or controller was exercised.
**OD3196 expanded — xHCI RTIso Stop can allow a completion to submit fresh periodic transfers after Stop returns:** besides leaving submitted TRBs live, the event task refills the pending-transfer target after each completion without checking a stopped state; an interleaving can rearm the supposedly stopped USB Audio stream. See [OD3196](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3196) and the [xHCI Stop/event-task trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#xhci-stoprtiso-event-task-refill-race-od3196). Source-only; no transfer or concurrent Stop was run.
**OD3192 expanded — optional AHI plus USB Audio builds can dereference a NULL current mode after ordinary unit close:** startup queues default gain and volume updates to the separate worker; the in-tree AHI-Handler opens the device on first use and closes it on last `ACTION_END`, so if that close frees the mode before the signal is consumed, the worker reads the cleared unit pointer. The finding also covers cross-mode routing and teardown clearing while another control remains live. See [OD3192](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3192) and the [AHI lifecycle trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only; no AHI open/close or worker schedule was exercised.

**OD9548 expanded — PCIUSB can hide a failed grouped HCD and skip rollback:** later HCD initialization can overwrite an earlier failure, publishing a partial unit; the UHCI case can route root-hub status or close-time teardown through a register base the failed initializer never assigned. See [OD9548](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9548) and the [grouped-controller source trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pciusb-grouped-hcd-failure-od9548). Source-only; no device or failure was induced.

**GD10101 expanded — `DamageList.c` can traverse region nodes while a refresh frees them:** its delayed `RegionRectangle` walk has no layer lock, while `EndUpdate()` clears that list under the lock. The finding also covers `CRList.c` live ClipRect traversal. See [GD10101](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10101) and the [four-file `test-layers` re-review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#test-layers-damagelist-live-traversal-gd10101-expansion). Source-only; no refresh interleaving was run.

**OD10535 — WirelessManager's optional D-Bus passive scan can send probe requests:** with D-Bus New enabled, the handler converts an explicit-channel passive request into a wildcard-SSID scan, and user-space MLME decides to probe from channel regulatory flags rather than the requested scan type. Scoped to soft-MAC SANA-II interfaces and channels not marked passive-only; D-Bus New is disabled in the checked-in `.config`. See [OD10535](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10535) and the [targeted scan trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#wirelessmanager-dbus-passive-scan-trace-od10535). Optional configuration only; no scan was run.

**OD9757 expanded — deferred SANA-II completion reads `io_Unit` after `ReplyMsg()`:** both Broadcom4400 and nvidianet release the unit semaphore by rereading the request after replying it; a resumed caller may already reuse or free that request. Trigger requires a contended unit semaphore and caller scheduling before the post-reply read. See [OD9757](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9757) and the [source-order recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nvidianet-request-body-and-post-reply-ownership-recheck-od9757-expanded). Source-only; no request or scheduler was run.

**EK10311 — M68040 MOVEC rejects valid MMU control-register transfers:** the selected M68040 bridge uses a C68020 whitelist, so valid MOVEC encodings for TC, ITT0/1, DTT0/1, MMUSR, URP and SRP raise illegal-instruction exceptions. Scoped to explicit optional `m68kemu.library` use; guest impact depends on those registers being used. See [EK10311](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10311) and the [MOVEC coverage pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#moira-movec-m68040-register-coverage-ek10311). Source-only; no guest instruction or build was run.

**OD10533 — PCIUSB can retain stale PCI device objects after releasing ownership:** closing a USB unit releases PCI ownership but leaves cached controller pointers; an expungeable backend can then dispose those unowned objects, and PCIUSB's scan-once path reuses them on a later open. Scoped to optional PCIUSB builds with an expungeable backend such as hosted Linux PCI. See [OD10533](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10533) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). No device close, backend expunge, or reopen was run; source-only.

**EK9432 rechecked — m68k thunks mishandle guest pointers and structures:** `GetRGB32()` passes the guest ColorMap shadow as a native object; five region APIs read guest Rectangle inputs as host words; `GetDisplayInfoData()` copies native-endian and host-layout records into guest buffers; and Intuition `GadgetMouse()`/`SysReqHandler()` write host-endian values to guest output slots. Added these cases to the existing optional m68kemu boundary finding. See [EK9432](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9432) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No guest graphics call or palette/region operation was run; source-only.

**EK10310 — Graphical boot consoles fail on a framebuffer shorter than one glyph:** a 1–13 pixel height becomes zero text rows. On PC, startup then assigns the NULL result of `AllocMem(0)` as the mirror and the next debug character dereferences it; the unsigned scroll row also underflows. Raspberry Pi AArch64 can scan beyond its one-row mirror or use an underflowed fallback copy if firmware echoes a nonzero sub-glyph mode. See [EK10310](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10310) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#zero-row-framebuffer-caller-pass-ek10310-added-2026-10-31). No boot or framebuffer was used; source-only.

**OD10532 — CAMD's 10-microsecond retry wait can take a VBlank interval:** AROS CAMD opens `timer.device` on `UNIT_VBLANK`, so `DoIO()` completion is tied to VBlank processing; on the PC timer's 50 Hz emulation, a retry can wait nearly 20 ms. This can slow MIDI output retries and SysEx completion polling. Applies when the explicitly buildable `workbench-libs-camd` target is used; it is not selected by the checked-in `workbench-libs-complete` edge. See [OD10532](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10532) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#camd-retry-wait-vblank-cadence-pass-od10532-added-2026-10-31). Source-only; no MIDI operation, timer request or build was run.

**OD2297 — Serial mouse PnP probing can classify no or truncated responses using uninitialized stack bytes:** the no-marker path tests uninitialized `buf[0]`, and the short PnP-frame path parses fixed fields beyond the received length, potentially matching a false product ID. Scoped to explicitly selected serialmouse with a usable serial-unit HIDD; default boot inclusion is not established. See [OD2297](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2297) and the [full-body serialmouse review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#serialmouse-full-body-and-pnp-protocol-decoder-recheck-od11045). Source-only; no serial probe was run.

**OD11045 — Serial mouse PnP accepts Mouse Systems devices but parses them as Microsoft packets:** the table maps `PNP0F04` to `P_MSC`, but the receive handler ignores the selected protocol and always groups and decodes Microsoft three-byte packets. See [OD11045](AROS-other-drivers.md#od11045) and the [full-body serialmouse review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#serialmouse-full-body-and-pnp-protocol-decoder-recheck-od11045). Scoped to explicitly enabled serialmouse with a matching PnP device; default inclusion is not established. Source-only; no serial device was exercised.

BoingIconBar final preferences-line newline handling (GD5659 confirmed and qualified; 2026-10-26): traced ReadPrefs' FGets/strlen/unconditional last-byte removal to DOS FGets' EOF semantics and final category/icon consumers (workbench/tools/BoingIconBar/iconbar.c:769-818; rom/dos/fgets.c:24-36,57-75). A newline-terminated record loses its newline; an EOF-terminated final record loses its last data character. Compared BoingIconBar Preferences' separate importer, which conditionally strips newline, and exporter, which writes newline after every record (workbench/prefs/boingiconbar/prefs.c:62-66,121-141). Qualified trigger to externally edited/supplied files without a final newline. No prefs file was loaded; targeted source/caller pass only, no full-body or LOC credit.
SANA-II success WireError candidates withdrawn (OD3105, OD3114, OD3289; 2026-10-31): Revision 7 says `ios2_WireError` may be supplied when `io_Error` is nonzero and requires it when an applicable error exists; it is not a specified success output. The uninitialized-success-field findings were removed as unsupported API claims. No body credit changed. [Specification](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/SANA-II_Revision_7#Errors).
OOP_DisposeObject SysExplorer PCI caller recheck (2026-10-31): the optional PCI module disposes its temporary PCI-controller object only after synchronous enumeration returns and only on successful construction; callback device objects are borrowed. No new disposal defect or LOC credit. Source-only.

BoingIconBar focus-timer device-close trace (GD5657 confirmed; 2026-10-26): followed optional tool startup and cleanup (workbench/tools/BoingIconBar/iconbar.c:424-445,678-690), including periodic completion/rearm (:567-581,625-635), and compared Exec's CloseDevice contract with timer.device Open (rom/exec/closedevice.c:37-55; rom/timer/lowlevel.c:407-426). On successful OpenDevice the cleanup aborts/waits for any pending request then deletes the IORequest and port without CloseDevice, leaving the open reference unmatched. The workbench-tools-iconbar edge is not included in the default tools aggregate at the reviewed manifest (workbench/tools/BoingIconBar/mmakefile.src:13-18); report scopes the finding to runs where this target is selected. timer.device is noexpunge, so no unload blockage is claimed. No device open or tool run was performed; source-only.

MUI input-handler timer-scale contract trace (GD5654 confirmed and caller-scoped; 2026-10-26): compared public MUI header flag definitions with Application registration and periodic re-arm (workbench/classes/zune/nlist/include/libraries/mui.h:597-601; workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1474-1497,1626-1655). SCALE10 and SCALE100 define hundredth-/tenth-second units and both together mean seconds, but both timer conversion sites use ihn_Millis directly as milliseconds and check only MUIIHNF_TIMER; the internal header does not define the scale bits. The checked-in Area timer uses plain milliseconds and no scale flags (classes/area.c:1591,2130-2134), so the active trigger is an MUI client using the documented scaled form. Confirmed that such intervals are scheduled too early by the scale factor; no timer request was run. Targeted API/caller pass only; no full-body or LOC credit.

GD5653 withdrawn as a duplicate of GD9493 (2026-10-31): both candidates describe the same signed-WORD delta narrowing in the generic HIDD line renderer and public Draw() path. GD5653 also overstated the effect as zero loop iterations; the axis swap bounds the loop by the small delta, omitting most of the line. Consolidated the valid trigger and caller evidence in [GD9493](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd9493); no path/LOC credit changed. No line was drawn.

Zune Navigation drag/active-color preference trace (GD5652 confirmed and scoped; 2026-10-26): traced Navigation Preferences load/save for drag buttons/modifiers, autostart/threshold, drag look and active-object pen (workbench/prefs/Zune/navigationp.c:226-280), then Configdata assignments to MUI_Prefs (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/configdata.c:381-393,726-736). Whole-tree muimaster field-consumer search found no runtime reads for drag_left_button, drag_middle_button, drag_autostart, drag_autostart_length, drag_look, drag modifiers, or active_object_color; prefs.h labels several as yet unused (:174-184). Excluded balancing_look because balance.c consumes it. Confirmed the listed settings are stored but not applied by the selected runtime. No config update or drag operation was run; targeted pass only, no LOC credit.

Zune Listviews Leading sizing-versus-render trace (GD5651 confirmed and qualified; 2026-10-26): traced slider range/load/save, Configdata default and prefs assignment, List Setup snapshot, AskMinMax, CalcVertVisible, row rendering and scroll increments (workbench/prefs/Zune/listviewsp.c:53-58,103-109,203-210,271-276; workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/configdata.c:207,715-719; workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/list.c:1761-1773,888-905,1845-1858,2088-2091,2116-2165). Leading is added to minimum/default size estimates, but visible-line division and rendering/scrolling use entry_maxheight alone; commented terms confirm no inter-row gap. Narrowed GD5651 to a sizing effect without visible row spacing. No preference update or GUI operation was run; targeted slice only, no LOC credit.

Zune cycle-menu speed preference trace (GD5650 confirmed; 2026-10-26): traced the Speed slider through Preferences load/save and Configdata's prefs population (workbench/prefs/Zune/cyclesp.c:50-55,98-101,170-176,194-224; workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/configdata.c:203-205,695-704). prefs.h still labels cycle_menu_speed “yet unused” (:152-156). Searched its references and compared cycle.c's consumers of position/minimum-entry prefs; the speed field is not read by the runtime cycle implementation. Updated GD5650 with the persisted-but-unused path. No prefs save, build or cycle interaction was run; targeted source pass only, no LOC credit.

GD5649 nullable Popstring child source recheck (retained; 2026-10-26): re-read Popstring construction and Popasl/Popscreen hooks (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/popstring.c:41-57; popasl.c:108-129; popscreen.c:27-65). The string child is fetched with default NULL and conditionally omitted from the Group; both hooks initialize their output string pointer to NULL, call get() without checking the object, and subsequently pass/dereference that pointer. Existing report scope remains the optional-child construction path; maintained callers may require the child and are not claimed as triggers. No object or requester was run; source-only, no LOC credit.

GD5648 duplicate disposition (2026-10-26): compared the indexed claim with the VMM Preferences Open/Save As implementation and existing GD6027 section. Both refer to MenuOpen/MenuSaveAs in workbench/system/VMM/MUI/menus.c:7-59; GD6027 already covers the 80-byte stack buffers, unbounded fr_Drawer copies, and ignored AddPart result. No independent stale-tail behavior established. Removed GD5648 from the active index and retained the disposition; GD6027 remains authoritative. Source-only; no path selection.

MUI context-menu constructor failure cleanup trace (GD5647 confirmed; 2026-10-26): traced zune_open_menu's ZMenu allocation, GetVisualInfoA, CreateMenusA, LayoutMenusA and cleanup exits (workbench/libs/muimaster/menu.c:1510-1558), then its selected area-class caller (classes/area.c:1862-1888). Once GetVisualInfoA succeeds, CreateMenusA failure frees zmenu but returns without FreeVisualInfo; the VisualInfo is freed only on the success path after layout. The caller stores NULL and continues handler setup, with no access to the local VisualInfo. Confirmed conditional leak; no allocation failure or context menu was run. Targeted function/caller pass only; no full-body or LOC credit.

MUI MutualExclude mouse-index/caller comparison (GD5646 confirmed; 2026-10-26): followed HandleMouseClick's selected MenuItem into HandleCheckItem and compared with Intuition's keyboard shortcut/check path (workbench/libs/muimaster/menu.c:330-360,367-434; rom/intuition/menus.c:156-176,188-200,221-245). MUI initializes local itemnum to zero and never assigns the selected sibling index; HandleCheckItem then exempts index zero while applying the selected item's mask. Intuition computes and passes itemnum/subnum. For a nonzero selected sibling whose MutualExclude mask includes bit zero, another checked first sibling is incorrectly left checked. Source-confirmed conditional mouse-selection defect; no menu event was run. Targeted slice only; no full-body or LOC credit.

MUI stale submenu selection pointer/click trace (GD5645 confirmed; 2026-10-26): re-read FindSubItem/FindItem, HandleMouseMove, HandleMouseClick, AddToSelection and KillSubMenuWin (workbench/libs/muimaster/menu.c:223-269,330-363,558-624,1433-1454,976-985). After a submenu row is active, returning to the same parent row produces the same activeitemnum, so the parent-window branch skips KillSubMenuWin and retains the prior activesubitemnum/pointer. A click on the parent window follows HandleMouseClick's parent-item path but AddToSelection uses the stale submenu state and can queue the enabled submenu item if ItemAddress still matches. Confirmed as a conditional pointer-selection defect; no GUI sequence was run. Targeted slice only; no full-body or LOC credit.

m68k Intuition configured-vector completeness pass (GD10090 expanded; 2026-10-27; no file/LOC credit): compared public `intuition.conf` function declarations with generated wrapper definitions and both Intuition dispatch tables. Confirmed `DrawBorder` (offset 108), `PrintIText` (216), `IntuiTextLength` (330), `BuildSysRequest` (360), `AllocRemember` (396), `FreeRemember` (408), `EasyRequestArgs` (588), `BuildEasyRequestArgs` (594), and `OpenScreenTagList` (612) have no generated or manual entry; neighboring table offsets verify each gap. The generic missing-LVO handler returns zero without calling native code (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_moira.cpp:280-290`). Expanded GD10090 with these omissions and their API-specific no-op/zero-return consequences. `CloseScreen`, `CloseWindow`, and `AutoRequest` were excluded because the manual table has handlers; `FreeMonitorList` remains under EK9432 because its paired raw-pointer ownership failure is already documented. `BuildSysRequest()` is additionally qualified because native `FreeSysRequest()` and `SysReqHandler()` document that family as unsupported. No emulated call or requester/drawing/screen operation was run. Source-only.

Intuition/MUI temporary menu-window open-failure cleanup pass (GD5643/GD5644 confirmed and qualified; 2026-10-26): traced Intuition main/submenu decorator allocation and MDM_INITMENU calls through OpenWindowTagList and the KillMenuWin/KillSubMenuWin guards (rom/intuition/menutask.c:1204-1277,1368-1430). If opening fails after decorator init, the NULL window makes kill cleanup skip MDM_EXITMENU and frees; user-buffer leak requires nonzero requested size and successful allocation. Also compared MUI MakeMenuWin/KillMenuWin and public Menu.Flags declaration: both Intuition and MUI set read-only MIDRAWN unconditionally after window open, then clear only when the window pointer exists (workbench/libs/muimaster/menu.c:870-899; compiler/include/intuition/intuition.h:159-162). No in-tree MIDRAWN readers were found, so GD5644 records an inconsistent public state with limited verified impact. Targeted function/caller pass; no full-body or LOC credit and no window failure was induced.

GD5641/GD5642 m68kemu thunk disposition and later optional-target restoration (rechecked 2026-10-31): the 2026-10-26 check correctly found no default ROM/package edge, but treated that as excluding an explicitly buildable optional `kernel-m68kemu-library` from the candidate reports. Restored the two distinct API mismatches under Exec/Kernel IDs EK10316 and EK10317: the manual `OpenWindowTagList` thunk leaves `TAG_MORE`'s guest address untranslated and ignores its non-NULL A0/NewWindow argument. `TAG_SKIP` entries are copied and then interpreted by native tag traversal, so no `TAG_SKIP` bug is claimed. These findings remain conditional on explicit optional-library use, with no default-image or checked-in guest caller asserted. See [EK10316](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10316), [EK10317](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10317) and the [tag-chain/API recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#openwindowtaglist-tag-more-translation-recheck-ek10316). No emulator or runtime call was exercised.

GD5640 disposition (Nouveau MST fallback GUID race withdrawn; 2026-10-26): verified the package graph at the reviewed commit: Nouveau is commented out of workbench drivers and the PC graphics-driver metatarget (workbench/mmakefile.src:36-41; arch/all-pc/drivers/mmakefile.src:7-13), and the module makefile disables its inclusion metatarget (workbench/hidds/nouveau/mmakefile.src:14-29). Re-read the GUID fallback and resume call (workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/display/drm_dp_mst_topology.c:2191-2208,2709-2717,3825-3835); generation writes a local call's GUID then the branch field, with no shared mutable GUID buffer established. Removed GD5640 from the active master index and retained this disposition for audit traceability. No build, display link, or resume was run; source-only.

picture.datatype DTM_FRAMEBOX input/output contract recheck (GD5639 confirmed; 2026-10-26): compared DT_FrameBox() and its dispatcher (workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:1394-1449,2194-2198) with the public dtFrameBox field annotations (compiler/include/datatypes/datatypesclass.h:335-344) and selected callers. The structure specifies dtf_ContentsInfo as input and dtf_FrameInfo as output, but the handler writes dimensions and FIF_SCROLLABLE only through dtf_ContentsInfo, never populating dtf_FrameInfo, while returning success for a non-NULL contents record. The inspected in-tree callers pass the same record for both arguments, masking the mismatch. Confirmed GD5639 for distinct input/output records; no external client or runtime call exercised. Targeted handler/dispatcher/caller pass only; no full-body or LOC credit.

PanelGroup scan/add allocation-failure trace (GD5638 confirmed and narrowed; 2026-10-26): re-read `PanelGroup__MUIM_PanelGroup_ScanPanels()`, `AddPanel()`, `OM_NEW()`, and panel-list consumers (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/panelgroup.c:175-235,408-483,523-672`). A recognized child remains in the Group child list when `mui_alloc_struct(PanelNode)` fails; `ScanPanels()` ignores the AddPanel result, overwrites `panel_count` with the accepted-child count, and returns TRUE. `OM_NEW()` ignores the scan result and returns the object. The missing list node then makes per-panel collapse/expand/toggle/state operations skip or default that child and list-wide operations omit it. Confirmed the finding is conditional on node-allocation failure; no ownership violation or runtime reproduction claimed. Replaced the placeholder with source evidence and narrowed the index title. Targeted function/caller slice only; no full-body or LOC credit.

Review correction (2026-10-23): GD4853 is retained with narrowed wording. `bitpack_read_msb()` takes bytes through an unsigned pointer but shifts them as promoted `int`; at nonzero `endbit`, a valid byte with high bits set can make `b->ptr[0] << (24 + endbit)` exceed `ULONG` range, which is undefined. The sign-bit case at offset zero alone is implementation-defined.

Review correction (2026-10-23): GD6104 remains an array-bound candidate because each feature table has 31 entries while its loop can test 32 bits. Its `1 << 31` expression is not independently undefined under the applicable C rules; whether the bit test reaches `table[31]` depends on implementation-defined conversion behavior. No selected compiler result or processor response was established.

Raspberry Pi VideoCore GPU MemHeader caller/lifecycle recheck (GD9405-GD9406 added; 2026-10-23): traced the `InitMem()` extension header through `MEMF_MANAGED`, `IsManagedMem()`, `AvailMem()` and Exec's managed-header query path. `vcgfx` sets `mhe_Avail` and `mh_Free` but never sets `mhe_Magic`, so the selected availability query treats the node as an ordinary header with an empty `mh_First`. Separately traced its `SysBase->MemList` publication through graphics-library/display-driver init failures into genmodule's failed-init free; no unlink path exists. Added GD9405 for the ignored availability callback and GD9406 for the reclaimed linked node. The two findings have separate success-path versus failed-init triggers; the latter is distinct from GD6256's IRQ-node lifetime. No memory query, allocation, or failed module load was run; source-only.

ExecSMP MemList publication recheck (GD9803 strengthened, 2026-10-25): re-read VCGfx `InitMem()` and resolved the module-init phase from its selected package/configuration. `arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:143` includes `hidd-vcgfx`; `vcgfx.conf:5` sets resident priority 9, which genmodule maps to `RTF_COLDSTART` (`tools/genmodule/writeinclibdefs.c:31-45`). `InitCode(RTF_COLDSTART)` calls matching resident initializers (`rom/exec/initcode.c:57-96`), after Exec's first COLDSTART resident enables multitasking (`rom/exec/exec_init.c:53-61`). The kernel `platform_PostInit()` calls `ARMI_Init()` before then on ExecSMP, and Exec's SMP init pins the boot task after secondaries are released (`arch/arm-native/kernel/platform_init.c:84-107`; `arch/arm-native/exec/platform_init.c:248-288`). Thus VCGfx `InitMem()` is reached in the multi-CPU coldstart phase on that package/config. The unsynchronized `AddTail()` versus Exec's `MemListSpinLock` readers is confirmed. The contemporaneous claim that no selected allocator walk was found was superseded by the selected input-device task reader traced in the correction below; interleaving remains conditional. No package was built or initialized; source-only.

# Build-selected m68k P96gfx HIDD (local C/header pass complete; external callers and hardware closure open)

`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src` selects P96gfx in the ROM/expansion and ordinary module payloads (`:187,:375`). Its module manifest selects five C translation units with 3,642 `cloc 2.06` C code lines, and five included local headers with 2,229 code lines. All selected bodies and local headers have full-body credit: 5,871 / 5,871 local C/header lines (100%). Findings GD5995-GD5999 were added for constructor cleanup of an unlinked bitmap node and unchecked allocation results in card construction, mode registration, VRAM setup and cursor-color-map setup. P96 card discovery/rollback reconciliation (GD4806 retained; GD6000 detailed, 2026-10-22/25; caller scope refined 2026-11-01): followed `.card` library enumeration under `Forbid()` through `P96GFX__InitCard()`, resolution population, per-card VRAM-header construction, attribute-base failure and module-init rollback (`p96gfx_hiddclass.c:1624-1702,1741-1817`). Confirmed the two `P96GFX__FreeCardCIDList()` failure callers and its empty body, as well as the successful path that skips cards with empty resolution lists without freeing them. Expanded GD6000 to identify the card, board-info, optional VRAM header, and mode/resolution allocations abandoned by those callers. Rechecked GD4806 separately: enumeration retains a raw Library pointer across `Permit()` and invokes `.card` vectors without opening a reference. The selected P96 monitor deliberately keeps its requested `.card` library open (`workbench/devs/monitors/P96/p96.c:8-18,129-141`), so GD4806 requires a different already-listed card whose final reference closes during the scan, or an external caller establishing that overlap; no in-tree overlapping closer was found. No card library, mode probe, allocation failure or initialization rollback was induced; source-only.

P96Gfx HIDD constructor/mode/cursor allocation-failure pass (GD5996-GD5999 detailed, 2026-10-25): re-read `P96GFXCl__Root__New()` and traced its allocation consumers through discovered-card `AddDisplayDriver()` registration and the cursor methods (`p96gfx_hiddclass.c:310-645,1145-1165,1184-1327,1369-1379,1820-1847`). Confirmed unchecked dynamic board-name strings and four mode-tag arrays are written during construction (GD5996), an unchecked `RTGMode` node is filled and linked for each mapped mode (GD5997), each eligible card's unchecked VRAM `MemHeader` is populated before any guard (GD5998), and failed sprite color-map object construction is not a reason to reject the HIDD despite later cursor color-map calls (GD5999). These are separate failure sites and consequences; the tag-array issue occurs even on card modes whose eventual display is not used. No allocation failure, display-driver registration, cursor update, or hardware operation was run; source-only; local file bodies were already credited in the P96 inventory.

P96Gfx bitmap palette-failure cleanup recheck (GD5995 detailed, 2026-10-25): traced depth-8 palette allocation failure through the constructor's `ok == FALSE` disposal branch. The instance data was zeroed, and because allocation failed, the bitmap's node never reaches the later `AddTail()`; its `Root::Dispose()` nevertheless reaches unconditional `Remove(&data->node)`. Checked Exec `Remove()`'s list-membership precondition and direct `ln_Pred`/`ln_Succ` dereferences, confirming invalid cleanup on this failure path. Expanded GD5995 with the allocation size, unlinked-node state, and consequence. No allocation failure or disposal was run; source-only; no body-line credit change.

# Graphics and Desktop coverage ledger

This ledger is being reconstructed. On 2026-10-22 this path was found to contain a byte-for-byte copy of the master index (`../AROS.md`) rather than the prior per-file review ledger. The master index remains preserved separately. No backup of the old ledger was found in the checked workspace, temp, cache, or source locations. Therefore its previous per-file rows, reviewed/unreviewed line totals, and historical review notes are not recoverable from the current files. Do not interpret this reconstructed ledger as a completeness claim.

## Re-established source passes

CGFX `DoCDrawMethodTagList()` scratch-buffer and row-stride follow-up (GD5754 strengthened; GD9407 added, 2026-10-23): reread the full `RenderHook()` fallback and the public `CDrawMsg` layout. Confirmed `tocopy_h` is calculated but neither transfer nor `cdm_ysize` is limited to it before the callback; traced the generic bitmap default `ObtainDirectAccess()` failure and confirmed PlanarBM inherits it. Separately traced `aHidd_BitMap_BytesPerRow` from the generic chunky row-size calculation into the `UWORD` public hook field, and confirmed ChunkyBM's selected direct-access method returns TRUE, establishing the wide-row truncation path for that class. The fallback is conditional on non-direct bitmap selection; the truncation requires a hook that consumes row stride. No HIDD operation or hook was run. Source-only.

Generic CopyBox cross-display cursor-state recheck (GD5738 detailed, 2026-10-25): traced both CursorFB unwraps, display selection, semaphore acquisition, source/destination intersection checks, unwrapping and final render (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1252-1310`). Confirmed that destination wrapper wins display selection, and `GfxDisplay_CursorIntersects()` matches against only that selected display's `cursor_bm` (`gfx_displayclass.c:296-307`); a wrapped source on another display is therefore not hidden before the generic copy reads its real framebuffer. Traced the selected graphics.library HIDD CopyBox call (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:642-650`). Scoped the trigger to cross-display copies with both wrapped operands and the source cursor overlapping the read rectangle. No bitmap or copy was run; source-only.

Generic standard-PixFmt startup partial-failure recheck (GD5735 detailed, 2026-10-25): reread `create_std_pixfmts()`, `delete_pixfmts()`, and `GFX_ClassInit()` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_init.c:172-207,270-328`) and the internal lookup (`gfx_dmenumclass.c:1321-1335`). Traced affected standard-format lookups in generic bitmap, display, and ChunkyBM callers (`gfx_bitmapclass.c:2608,2740,2904,4405`; `gfx_displayclass.c:1003`; `gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:415,684`). Thus earlier table entries can be stale and later ones NULL if initialization continues. No failure or lookup was induced; source-only.

PlanarBM FillRect write-mask caller recheck (GD5734 detailed, 2026-10-25): traced `SetWriteMask()` into `rp->Mask`, `GetDriverData()` into `GC_COLMASK` for depth-at-most-eight bitmaps, and public `RectFill()` through `fillrect_render()` to the planar override (`rom/graphics/setwritemask.c:48-49`; `graphics_inline.h:82-89`; `rectfill.c:68-101`; `gfxfuncsupport.c:330-337`; `gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:443-502`). The fast path checks only bitmap presence and Copy draw mode, then writes every non-null plane; its superclass fallback uses generic scanline drawing, whose pixel-write logic applies the GC mask (`gfx_bitmapclass.c:1484-1510`). Thus a partial RastPort plane mask is ignored only by this selected fast path; non-Copy drawing modes retain the generic behavior. No fill was run; source-only.

ChunkyBM RGB16_LE alpha-image row-step recheck (GD5733 detailed, 2026-10-25): re-read the signed `WORD` `src_step`/`dst_step` locals and both alpha-image row loops (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:439-557`), then traced `WritePixelArrayAlpha()`'s public `UWORD srcmod` through `RenderHook()` to `HIDD_BM_PutAlphaImage()` (`workbench/libs/cgfx/writepixelarrayalpha.c:37-47,116-128`). Confirmed `AllocBitMap()` maps `PIXFMT_RGB16_LE` to the HIDD format and ChunkyBM has a matching branch (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:26-38,285-296`; `gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:498-557`). A 40,000-byte modulo and width 1 produce source step 39,996, which cannot be represented by signed `WORD`; supported 16-bit two's-complement targets wrap it negative and subsequent rows use the wrong source address. The destination step is subject to the same narrowing for wide rows. No operation was run; source stride and target conversion are source/API-derived; source-only.

IconList maximum-line-width input and allocation-bound recheck (no new GD; 2026-10-23): traced `MUIA_IconList_LabelText_MaxLineLen` from the Wanderer view-settings read/write and volume-list setup through `IconList__OM_NEW()`, `IconList__OM_SET()` and `IconList__LabelFunc_CreateLabel()`. Values below the accepted minimum six are reset to the default ten; for an unusually large width, a shorter label takes the exact-label-size branch rather than allocating `maxWidth + 1`. Confirmed `AllocVecPooled()` returns NULL for a zero-sized request (`rom/exec/allocvecpooled.c:55-57`), so the maximum-width wrap-to-zero case cannot reach the subsequent copy. No separate max-width allocation/copy finding established. This does not mitigate GD6243, which arises in the independent multiline splitter's fixed 256-byte output buffer for an unbounded AppIcon label. No preference was imported or changed and no label was rendered. Source-only.

IconList multiline AppIcon label destination-bound pass (GD6243 added; 2026-10-23): traced the 256-byte `AllocVecPooled()` result through per-line output offsets and `strncpy()` lengths in `IconList__LabelFunc_SplitLabel()`, then followed the selected `IconWindowVolumeList` AppIcon refresh to `AppIcon_GetLabel()` and the public `AddAppIconA()` storage of its caller-supplied text pointer. At the accepted six-character minimum line width, 50 six-character runs separated by 49 spaces produce a 349-character label; the splitter skips each inter-run space but advances its destination by six copied bytes plus one line slot, so the last copy writes indices 343–348 of a 256-byte allocation. This input avoids the existing splitter's delimiter-probe overread: each six-character run exactly matches the measured line width and the shorter-than-line search does not execute. Added GD6243 for the independent output-buffer overrun. The AppIcon label is caller-provided and has no length limit in `AddAppIconA()`; the volume-list preference path supplies the minimum line length and multiline setting. No AppIcon, preference, allocation failure, or GUI operation was run; source-only.

IntelGMA startup meta-class failure detail pass (GD5984–GD5985, 2026-10-25): rechecked the display-class allocation result and both cleanup/instantiation callers. When `IntelG45DisplayClass` allocation fails, startup continues; the graphics HIDD constructor passes the null class and null ID to `OOP_NewObject()`, which returns NULL, but still returns its graphics object. The compositor constructor then rejects its null display and returns NULL; the selected `driver_Setup()` path can accept a HIDD with no exposed display, while `G45_Init()` bases success on `PCIDevice`. Replaced GD5984 with this bounded no-display startup consequence. Separately confirmed failed startup cleanup disposes the nested compositor/I2C/bitmap/Gfx meta-class objects but omits the successfully allocated display meta-class; removed the unsupported suggestion that it necessarily blocks reinitialization and scoped GD5985 to retained OOP resources. No allocation failure or HIDD registration was run; source-only; no body-line credit change.

IntelGMA CopyBox and Gallium batch-buffer findings detail pass (GD5986–GD5988, 2026-10-25): traced the duplicated `bm_src->fbgfx` predicate through the distinct-bitmap CopyBox caller into the destination framebuffer address submitted to the 3D engine, and checked bitmap construction paths that assign ordinary `AllocMem()` addresses with `fbgfx == FALSE`; expanded GD5986 to the qualified source-backed/destination-system-memory case. Re-read Gallium batch create/destroy callbacks and Exec semaphore nesting. GD5987's post-free `gmabatch->iws` argument reaches `IntelGMA_ReleaseBuffers()`, whose nested `AttemptSemaphore()` succeeds for the owning task and whose traversal invokes the winsys `buffer_is_busy` callback; the pointer is used, not merely read. GD5988's unchecked CPU map is dereferenced by constructor reset if graphics allocation succeeds, while graphics allocation failure returns without freeing the already allocated batch and CPU map. ## WinGDI keyboard callback prototype reconciliation (GD10578; 2026-11-01)

Reconciled `gdikbd_data.kbd_callback` and the key IRQ callback invocation against the shared `InputIrqCallBack_t` definition (`arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/gdi.h:73-76`; `wingdi_kbdclass.c:50-82`) and the constructor assignment at `:133`. The field is pointer-payload typed and the producer calls it with `&kEvt`, but construction casts the incoming handler to `VOID (*)(APTR, UWORD)` before assigning to the field. This is an incompatible function-pointer assignment and is expected to fail under the default warning-as-error compiler flags. The field's later invocation uses the pointer typedef, so no runtime truncation is asserted. Added GD10578; the local source bodies already have full-body credit. No compiler or build was run; source-only.

## RISC-V OpenSBI Headless graphics HIDD and monitor loader

The OpenSBI boot manifest selects `kernel-hidd-gfx-headlessgfx` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:51`); the HIDD manifest also builds the `Headless` monitor loader as a dependency. Read the three module C bodies (`headlessgfx_init.c`, 79 `cloc 2.06` code lines; `headlessgfx_hiddclass.c`, 315; `headlessgfx_bitmapclass.c`, 64), the loader `disk_startup.c` (138), all three local headers (103), `headlessgfx.conf`, and the module/boot manifests: 596 C lines and 103 header lines, 699 combined. Traced initialization and rollback through `AddDisplayDriver`, object/display construction through the selected `HW_AddDriver` and display-registration callers, mode/pixel-format tags against `stdpixfmts_le.h`, and monitor tooltypes through attribute acquisition and registration. Added GD6086: after acquiring all nine OOP attribute bases, resident initialization returns failure on graphics-library open or display-driver registration errors without releasing them; the configuration has no expunge cleanup either. Added GD6087: failed display-object construction is not propagated by the graphics HIDD constructor, and graphics.library treats a driver with no display as successfully set up, retiring its boot-replay entry. The default depth/geometry bounds and tag-array capacities are internally consistent, and the selected bitmap overrides only visibility state while delegating bitmap methods to the chunky superclass. Cross-file GD5924 reachability: default 8/16/24 formats at one sync plus inherited Direct framebuffer mode makes the generic chooser select 8-bit; see the dated caller trace below and the findings report. This is 100% body-read credit for this local target slice, not Graphics/Desktop completion. The downstream VNC reader/client was not identified in the selected sources; firmware/display handover and boot-time allocation behavior remain source-only. No build, monitor load, allocation failure or display operation was run.

GD6087 caller-path verification (2026-10-23): reread `HW__HW__SetUpDriver()` and confirmed its default implementation unconditionally returns TRUE (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:418-422`). `driver_Setup()` only returns FALSE when `HW_AddDriver()` returns NULL; when a non-NULL graphics HIDD reports a NULL `DisplayDefault`, it logs and continues to its success return (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:369-385,414`). `driver_ReplayBootQueue()` frees the entry on that success result (`:296-323`). This confirms the report's queue-retirement consequence. No display failure was induced; source-only.

HeadlessGfx GD6086-GD6087 candidate-detail recheck (2026-10-25): for GD6086, confirmed `GetAttrBases()` rolls back only when an `OOP_ObtainAttrBase()` itself fails (`headlessgfx_init.c:32-57`), while the later resident-only graphics-library open and `AddDisplayDriver()` failure paths return FALSE without calling the release helper (`:85-125`). The disk monitor loader is excluded because the auto-registration branch runs only when `FindResident(MOD_NAME_STRING)` succeeds. For GD6087, re-read the HIDD root constructor (`headlessgfx_hiddclass.c:288-338`): it returns the parent-created root even if default-display creation returns NULL. Followed that non-NULL object through `HW_AddDriver()` and `driver_Setup()`; base setup succeeds and the NULL default display is logged but not converted to failure (`hwclass.c:418-422`; `graphics_driver.c:369-385,414`), so boot replay frees the queue entry (`:296-323`). Expanded both report entries with the respective exact trigger and consequence. No load, object allocation, or replay failure was induced; source-only; selected-body credit unchanged.

GD5728 fast-method dispatch and constructor consequence recheck (2026-10-25): traced the selected `gfx_histogramclass.c` cache initialization through `BMHUNMAPPIXEL`, `BMHFINDCOLOR`, and `BMHADDCOLOR` (`gfx_histogramclass.c:53-80`; `gfx_intern.h:607-648`) and matched method offsets to the `Hidd_BitMap` and `Hidd_BMHistogram` method lists in `gfx.conf`. The cached UnmapPixel method is PutPixel; the cached AddColorEntry method is FindColorEntry, whose offset happens to equal PutPixel's numeric offset. The constructor starts with an empty histogram and its misdirected Add calls therefore never insert an entry. The incompatible unmap message is consumed as PutPixel coordinates/value; selected generic ChunkyBM and PlanarBM writers compute memory addresses without coordinate checks (`gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:107-139`; `gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:356-385`), so unintended writes are possible, with exact address consequences depending on runtime values and implementation. Confirmed `gfx_histogramclass.c` is in the selected GFX module manifest and found no in-tree histogram constructor caller. No histogram or bitmap operation was run; source-only.

Sync PixelTime Get/Set caller and zero-clock recheck (GD5729 expanded; GD9682 added, 2026-10-25): traced the `aoHidd_Sync_PixelTime` getter and parser through `Sync__Root__Get()`, `parse_sync_tags()`, constructor and variable-mode Set callers (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_syncclass.c:265,347-358,483,525-571`) against the public attribute units in `gfx.conf:731-738`. Confirmed the Get case falls through and overwrites the picosecond result with the pixel clock; a direct nonzero `PixelClock` from 1 through 999 also makes `pixelclock / 1000` zero before the getter's division. Confirmed the PixelTime Set conversion has an unchecked `1e9 / tag->ti_Data`. Reconciled LinuxFB's selected mode producer (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/linuxfbgfx_displayclass.c:177-243`): it passes nonzero `vsi->pixclock` as PixelTime, but truncates the tags before index 9 when the pixclock is zero, matching its comment that the zero case crashes. No in-tree PixelTime getter or zero-valued parser call was found; the generic public API remains exposed to both cases. No mode was queried or constructed; source-only; no body-line credit changed.

Generic DMEnum terminal allocation and selected caller pass (GD5730 expanded, 2026-10-25): traced recursive `querymode()` to its `syncidx >= num_syncs` base case and through unwinding into `DMEnum__Hidd_DMEnum__QueryModeIDs()` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_dmenumclass.c:175-271,749-809`). The terminal frame allocates `numfound + 1` ModeIDs, then unconditionally adds `numfound` and writes the invalid-ID sentinel; if AllocVec fails, this invalid pointer operation occurs before the method can return. Confirmed the selected generic `graphics.library/display_Setup()` caller checks NULL only after the query returns (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:76-80`), so its cleanup cannot catch the internal write. P96 and AmigaVideo provide separate per-architecture QueryModeIDs overrides. No query or allocation failure was run; source-only; no body-line credit changed.

AddAppMenuItem key collision NULL-field recheck (GD5839 confirmed, 2026-10-25): traced the documented NULL default through zero-cleared AppMenuItem allocation and the `keyUsed()` scan. When a new non-NULL key is supplied after a key-less item, `strlen(ami->ami_CommandKey)` is called on that prior NULL field before any NULL guard. Confirmed the scan does hold `wb_BaseSemaphore`, ruling out concurrent insertion as the cause; scoped the fault to valid list contents with an optional key omitted. No AppMenuItem was created; source-only; no body credit change.

AddAppMenuItem command-key check/insert interleaving recheck (GD5840 confirmed, 2026-10-25): traced `keyUsed()` lock acquisition/release and the later independent lock around `AddTail()`. Since the check releases `wb_BaseSemaphore` before insertion, two callers with the same currently unused key can both observe it unused and then both append. The tag documentation says an already-used key is ignored, so concurrent registration can violate uniqueness. No concurrent addition was run; source-only; no body credit change.

UpdateWorkbench notification stub and icon caller recheck (GD5841 confirmed, 2026-10-25): compared the method body with its documented add/change/remove notification contract and traced the selected `PutIconTagList()` and `DeleteDiskObject()` callers. Both invoke UpdateWorkbench after successful disk-object changes, but the function only emits a debug log and returns TRUE without sending a handler/application message. Callers ignore the result, so the refresh failure is silent. No icon update or Workbench UI was run; source-only; no body credit change.

Held Workbench relay registration flush recheck (GD5834 confirmed and caller impact detailed, 2026-10-25): traced `OpenWorkbenchObjectA()` drawer handling into a `WBHM_TYPE_OPEN` relay, no-app queueing in `__HandleRelay_WB()`, and `RegisterWorkbench()` port assignment. Confirmed registration neither signals the handler nor flushes `hc_HeldRelayMsgs`; the only drain is on a later relay. This leaves an accepted open request and its owned name/message pending, so the drawer is not opened unless a subsequent relay occurs. No drawer request or registration was run; source-only; no body credit change.

Workbench handler CreateNewProc failure/search-path ownership recheck (GD5827 confirmed and narrowed, 2026-10-25): traced `WBOpen()` from `Cli()->cli_CommandDir` through `DuplicateSearchPath()` assignment to `CreateNewProc()` failure. Confirmed that branch only closes library dependencies and exits the retry loop; it neither frees nor clears `wb_SearchPath`. A subsequent open duplicates into the same field, orphaning the prior path nodes and `DupLock()` references. Scoped to a nonempty CLI path and actual process-creation failure; handler task startup failure after successful `CreateNewProc()` is a separate behavior. No process or lock operation was run; source-only; no body credit change.

OpenWorkbenchObjectA launch-tag allocation failure recheck (GD5828 confirmed and scoped, 2026-10-25): traced Tool and Project launch callers into `WB_LaunchProgram()`. Both construct `NP_StackSize` and `NP_Priority` entries, reaching the forwarded-tag allocation branch. Confirmed `AllocateTagItems(3)` is assigned to `message->wbcm_Tags` and immediately dereferenced for all three entries without a NULL check; `DestroyWBCM()` cleanup is only reached through later error handling. Checked the one-tag possibility but did not promote it because the in-tree callers always supply both tags. No allocation failure or launch was run; source-only; no body credit change.

OpenWorkbenchObjectA UAE branch icon ownership recheck (GD5829 confirmed, 2026-10-25): traced `GetIconTags()` result through the UAE forwarding branch and the ordinary branch. The UAE branch neither passes nor frees the icon, while the ordinary branch unconditionally calls `FreeDiskObject(icon)` for non-NULL results. Confirmed `FreeDiskObject()` releases the object and its freelist-managed allocations. Scoped the leak to forwarded 68k launches for which icon lookup returned a DiskObject. No UAE launch or icon operation was run; source-only; no body credit change.

UAE pooled launch-message allocation failure recheck (GD5830 confirmed, 2026-10-25): traced the `OpenWorkbenchObjectA()` UAE branch to `forward_to_uae()`. Confirmed the pool-success path assigns `AllocVecPooled()` directly to `msg`, dereferences `msg->mempool`, and only then tests `msg`; a failed message allocation therefore reaches a NULL write, and the pool is not deleted before the fault. Scoped to pooled message allocation failure after successful pool creation. No UAE forwarding or allocation failure was run; source-only; no body credit change.

## Build-selected Radeon HIDD

The PPC Sam440 module dependency list and CHRP/Efika package select hidd-radeon; each architecture wrapper selects a same-named `radeon_bios.c` replacement (`arch/ppc-sam440/boot/mmakefile.src:14–16,50; arch/ppc-sam440/hidd.radeon/mmakefile.src:3–7; arch/ppc-chrp/efika/boot/mmakefile.src:4–13,61–80; arch/ppc-chrp/hidd.radeon/mmakefile.src:3–7`). `config/make.tmpl:1661–1669` removes same-basename architecture objects from the common source list, confirming the selected BIOS body differs by target. The shared-source inventory is 9,297 `cloc 2.06` lines. For the selected Sam440 target, the architecture replacement removes the shared 257-line BIOS parser and adds a 248-line body, giving 9,288 / 9,288 local C/header code lines read. For CHRP/Efika the 263-line replacement gives 9,303 / 9,303. The Sam440 variant also includes `radeon_bios_rom.h`, a 61,441-byte static BIOS image reported by `cloc` as 3,844 data lines; this opaque firmware payload is tracked separately from executable source review. These local source-body figures do not close caller/configuration or external hardware-contract review.

ILBM class DTM_WRITE dispatch and raw-helper reachability correction (GD5295-GD5297/GD5299-GD5301/GD5303 withdrawn, 2026-10-23): traced the active ILBM class construction and dispatcher (`workbench/classes/datatypes/ilbm/libfunc.c:115-155,165-177`) against `ilbm.conf` and the selected Picture superclass method manifest (`workbench/classes/datatypes/ilbm/ilbm.conf`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/picture.conf:42-47`). The live ILBM `DT_Dispatcher()` handles only `OM_NEW`; every other method, including `DTM_WRITE`, is sent to `DoSuperMethodA()`. `IFF__DTM_WRITE()` in `ilbmclass.c` is not referenced by that dispatcher, and `ilbm.conf` does not register it. Therefore `SaveILBM()`, `Save_BitMapPic()` and `WriteBytes()` are unreachable from the selected ILBM DTM_WRITE path; withdrew the associated handle-close, error propagation, allocation, BMHD, padding and 24/32-bit raw-save findings from the detailed report and index. The selected Picture superclass does register `DTM_WRITE` as `DT_Write`; its writer uses the Picture color registers, so the prior EHB claim that pixel colors necessarily lose their half-bright appearance is also unsupported and withdrawn. Retained parser/read-path findings GD5290-GD5294, GD5298 and GD5302, which are reachable through `ILBM__OM_NEW()`. No save or image operation was run; source-only.

Hyperlayers XOR clipping failure caller trace (GD6186 expanded, 2026-10-23): traced `_CreateClipRectsFromRegion()` through all selected `_CreateClipRectsFromRegion()` and `_BackupPartsOfLayer()` callers. The helper ignores `XorRegionRegion()`/`XorRectRegion()` and the subsequent `AndRegionRegion()`/`AndRectRegion()` results, then toggles `invisible` and constructs the next cliprect pass (`rom/hyperlayers/basicfuncs.c:389-476`). `XorRegionRegion()` preserves its destination when its temporary allocations fail (`rom/graphics/xorregionregion.c:58-105`); the rectangle wrapper propagates that failure (`xorrectregion.c:52-74`). Thus the second pass may be formed from a region that was never complemented, and the cliprect partition can misclassify or duplicate area. Expanded existing GD6186 to include this path; this is the same unchecked region-operation failure class, not a separate ID. `basicfuncs.c` already has focused review evidence, so no whole-body line credit is added. No allocation failure or layer operation was run; source-only.

## Raspberry Pi VideoCore `vcgfx` HIDD (selected local body/header pass complete; lifecycle and hardware closure open)

The package manifests select `vcgfx` for 32-bit Raspberry Pi and AArch64 Raspberry Pi (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:187`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:220-226`). The AArch64 init path declines BCM2712 before hardware setup; the package keeps `fbgfx` as the display fallback. All 12 selected module translation units (3,793 code lines), the included shared bitmap helper (276 lines), and six local headers (562 lines) have explicit full-body/header review credit: 4,631 / 4,631 local C/header code lines (100%).
