HTML construction-failure cleanup candidate recheck (GD6278 retained; no new finding, 2026-10-23): followed each `call_parser()` failure return through `Html__OM_NEW()`'s `CoerceMethod(OM_DISPOSE)` into `Html__OM_DISPOSE()`. Confirmed `data->page` remains NULL until parse, parse-finalization, and `layout_init()` all succeed; the parser frees its partial page on parse/parse-end/layout-init failure, while disposal unconditionally calls `layout_free(data->page)`, whose first operation dereferences `page->ldata`. Thus GD6278 covers all three stages, including the case where a page was allocated and already freed. The pool-allocation failure path is also direct: `parse_init()` can return NULL before publishing a page, and disposal still receives NULL. No allocation or object construction was induced; source-only, no new line credit.

VESA boot-console takeover caller recheck (no new GD; 2026-10-23): traced the two `RawPutChar(0x03)` sites in `vesaDoRefreshArea()`/`ClearBuffer()` through the selected bitmap `UpdateRect`/scroll and display `Show` methods (`rom/hidds/vesagfx/vesagfx_bitmapclass.c:159-161,214-216`; `vesagfx_displayclass.c:188-218`). Both normal display paths hold `framebufferlock` while the first takeover and `HWData.owned` update occur; initial `initVesaGfxHW()` clearing is before the HIDD is published. Thus duplicate takeover through these normal callers is serialized. The separate registered `ResetHandler()` calls `ClearBuffer()` without that lock (`vesagfx_hiddclass.c:25-35`). The subsequent reset-path recheck establishes the selected ExecSMP cross-CPU overlap and is recorded as GD6316. No screen, reset, or framebuffer operation was run; source-only.

VESA reset-callback framebuffer race added as GD6316 (2026-10-23): traced registration/disposal in `VESAGfx__Root__New/Dispose()` (`rom/hidds/vesagfx/vesagfx_hiddclass.c:45-74,83-89`) to Exec `ShutdownA()`/`ColdReboot()` and `Exec_DoResetCallbacks()` (`rom/exec/shutdowna.c:58-60`; `coldreboot.c:51-53`; `doresetcallbacks.c:65-184`). In the non-supervisor path, callbacks run serially in a support task; this does not stop tasks on other CPUs. The selected x86-64 PC package includes VESA and supports an ExecSMP target (`arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:63-75`; `configure.in:1650-1670`). Therefore a cross-CPU display update can overlap the reset callback's unlocked `ClearBuffer()` even though ordinary Show/UpdateRect paths share `framebufferlock`. This establishes the unsynchronized clear/draw overlap and the conditional inconsistent framebuffer consequence; GD6316 records it with medium confidence for any lasting visible effect because reset is underway. No reset, screen update or SMP interleaving was run; source-only.

GD6317 WinGDI rollback consequence expansion (2026-10-25): rechecked the exact class interfaces and registration order after detailing the report entry. `CLID_HW_Kbd` and `CLID_HW_Mouse` both derive from `CLID_HW_Input` (`rom/hidds/kbd/keyboard.conf:25-37`; `mouse.conf:29-48`); `InputHW__HW__AddDriver()` injects the normal event callback and consumer list before calling the generic hardware registry (`rom/hidds/input/inputsubsystem.c:204-237`). Therefore WinGDI's first `HW_AddDriver(kbd, ...)` can register its keyboard object; its next legacy `HIDD_Input_AddHardwareDriver(ms, ...)` uses an `IID_Hidd_Input` method on the wrong hierarchy and fails. The subsequent legacy remover is likewise sent to the wrong receiver and does not unlink the prior keyboard driver. Expanded GD6317 to state the stranded registration without assuming how the failed module loader handles class-code lifetime. X11's exact mismatched calls are `arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/startup.c:75-77`. No startup or rollback was run; no code-line credit change; source-only.

Confirmed that failed creation of the mouse singleton occurs before the unchecked legacy method dispatch, after a successful keyboard registration can already have been published; the null receiver faults before the normal rollback branch. Added GD9638 separately from GD6317's wrong-interface dispatch because the construction-failure trigger is independent. No allocation failure or startup was induced; local WinGDI source bodies already have full-body credit; source-only.

SDL event-batch focus-state follow-up (GD6357 added; GD2620 retained, 2026-10-23): reread the complete 108-code-line `arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/event.c` worker and the selected mouse HIDD event callback. The `active` flag is initialized to true inside each VBlank loop iteration, while focus-loss state is only applied to mouse events in the same `SDL_PeepEvents()` batch. A later poll therefore forwards mouse motion/button input even if the SDL window remains unfocused, on host backends that report such events. Added GD6357 with that host-delivery condition; this is independent of GD2620's stale stack-local interrupt node after failed startup. The SDL event body already has full-body credit; this pass adds caller/configuration evidence only. No input event or callback was run; source-only.

Wanderer view-settings aligned-offset width follow-up (GD3069 expanded; arithmetic corrected 2026-10-26): re-read import, export, the standard Workbench/Drawer row construction, the type-0 image-spec change hook, and Zune's `MUIA_Imagedisplay_Spec` duplication path. The four-byte-aligned `strlen(spec)+1` offset reaches 256 at a 252-character spec and wraps to zero when stored in `UBYTE` in both parser and exporter. Recounting the selected non-`DEBUG_MULTLINE` type-0 export path gives 17 tags (136 bytes), not all 20 slots in the fixed-capacity tag array; export allocates those 136 bytes at wrapped offset zero, then `sprintf()` writes the 253-byte NUL-terminated spec, 117 bytes past the allocation. `DEBUG_MULTLINE` adds two tags but does not make the allocation large enough. A <=1,024-byte imported view-settings payload can set the long spec and trigger the selected Save path; import option decoding also uses the wrapped offset. Restored the detailed GD3069 report entry and corrected its arithmetic. This extends existing `wpeditor.c` body credit; no new body-line credit or runtime reproduction. Source-only.

SDL event-task startup/rollback caller reconciliation (GD2620 and GD6357 retained; no new GD, 2026-10-23): re-read the full `event.c` body and traced `sdl_event_init()` through the selected `startup.c` ladder. After the event task signals readiness and registers its stack-local `tick_int`, failures from `sdl_hidd_init()` or `sdl_Startup()` both reach `sdl_event_expunge()` (`startup.c:275-300`); that helper calls `RemTask(eventtask)` but does not call `RemIntServer()`, preserving GD2620's exact post-startup-failure trigger. ## AArch64 Raspberry Pi `fbgfx` fallback HIDD (local source/header pass complete; lifecycle and hardware review open)

The AArch64 Raspberry Pi package includes `fbgfx` in its HIDD package list and describes it as the fallback framebuffer driver when `vcgfx` declines the board (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:220-226`). The selected module manifest builds five C translation units; `cloc 2.06` reports 604 C code lines. The five local headers add 137 code lines. All 741 local C/header code lines were read in full, and the config and module/package manifests were checked. Traced `FBGfx_Init()` and AddDisplayDriver registration into graphics.library's queued boot-driver replay, the graphics HIDD's nested display construction, bitmap visibility and refresh calls, reset callback registration/removal, and selected Exec/OOP implementations. Added GD9392 for cleanup removing the reset callback before it is registered on display-construction failure. Firmware framebuffer validity, display-mode/runtime behavior, pixel-format hardware semantics and allocation-failure execution remain unverified; this is not a Graphics/Desktop completion claim. Source-only.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi `fbgfx` returned-depth contract recheck (GD9421 added; 2026-10-24): traced the firmware's framebuffer allocation response through boot-tag publication, native kernel storage, `KrnGetSystemAttr()` and the selected fallback HIDD. `vcfb_init()` accepts a nonzero returned depth and passes it through `KRN_FrameBufferDepth`; `initFBGfxHW()` ignores that attribute and hardcodes 32-bit/4-byte pixels. The display mode advertises that hardcoded format, while `fbDoRefreshArea()` copies four bytes per pixel using the returned pitch. Added GD9421, conditional on firmware returning a depth other than the requested 32; the generated config requests 32, and no supported-board mismatch or exact allocation overrun was established. No framebuffer operation was run. Source-only.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi `fbgfx` UpdateRect contract and caller pass (no additional finding; 2026-10-24): traced the override's `(x,y,width,height)` endpoint construction through the shared renderer and graphics.library callers. The rectangle convention is half-open: selected `UpdateBitMap()` forwards the requested extent unchanged, full bitmap refresh uses `(0,0,width,height)`, and the generic HIDD path intersects with the bitmap's visible rectangle before translating to display coordinates. `fbgfx` applies the equivalent display offset and clips destination coordinates to the physical framebuffer; for in-bounds bitmap updates, clipping adjusts the source origin consistently. Scroll-triggered full refresh likewise uses the bitmap extent. No independent off-by-one or source-edge defect was established for valid in-bounds requests; arbitrary out-of-bitmap HIDD rectangles and actual framebuffer behavior remain untested. No line credit. Source-only.

RastPort blit-wrapper endpoint narrowing recheck (GD9401 retained, 2026-10-23): re-read the three wrapper bodies and shared `do_render_with_gc()` early-return/clip branches (`rom/graphics/bltbitmaprastport.c:118-136`; `bltmaskbitmaprastport.c:116-138`; `blttemplate.c:96-112`; `gfxfuncsupport.c:113-129,165-205`). The destination origins and sizes are signed `WORD`s, but adding a positive size to a near-maximum origin can produce an endpoint above `WORD_MAX`; assignment to `Rectangle.MaxX/MaxY` narrows it before the shared helper's inverted-rectangle check. Thus a request crossing the representable edge is rejected before clipping, while a wider intersection would retain the visible portion and adjust source offsets. The three paths share the mechanism; the mask wrapper additionally rejects nonpositive sizes. Existing GD9401 wording and confidence remain supported. This recheck adds no body-line credit and does not claim a maintained caller supplies an edge-crossing request. No graphics operation was run; source-only.

MoveRaster region-failure transactional-semantics recheck (GD9398 retained; no new independent finding, 2026-10-23): reread `MoveRaster()` and its `ScrollRegion()`, `OrRegionRegion()` and `AndRectRegion()` calls against the region implementations. `ScrollRegion()` only swaps its in-place region after all temporary operations and the final union succeed; failure leaves the original `DamageList` at pre-scroll coordinates. `OrRegionRegion()` constructs a temporary region and replaces its destination only on success, so ignored union failure leaves the old `DamageList` intact while the new `Damage` is disposed. `AndRectRegion()` is explicitly documented as non-failing and performs in-place clipping without allocation, so its ignored void return does not establish another failure path. Confirmed `MoveRaster()` continues its blit/refresh path after the two BOOL failures as stated in GD9398. No GUI or allocation failure was run.

Region relative-span boundary and point-query pass (GD9412 added; 2026-10-23): traced the empty-destination fast path of `OrRectRegion()` through WORD rectangle storage and `IsPointInRegion()`'s coordinate translation. A non-evil public rectangle may span more than 32,768 pixels while each endpoint remains a valid WORD; its relative maximum is then narrowed to an unrepresentable positive WORD. On low-16-bit signed narrowing, the resulting inverted local rectangle makes even its left/top endpoint fail the point test. Added GD9412 with compiler behavior and lack of maintained large-dimension callers qualified. `orrectregion.c` and `ispointinregion.c` already have full-body credit; this adds no new body-line credit. Wider region-operation semantics, other producers, external callers, and selected compiler conversion behavior remain open; no region or point query was run. Source-only.

Region-span sibling API reconciliation (GD9412 expanded; 2026-10-23): extended the prior empty-region `OrRectRegion()` boundary trace to `XorRectRegion()` and `XorRectRegionND()` (which directly store the relative rectangle span in WORD fields) and `OrRectRegionND()` (whose shared band output is normalized through `_TranslateRect`, also storing WORD deltas/endpoints). Kept the concrete `IsPointInRegion()` false-negative example scoped to `OrRectRegion()` on an empty destination. The methods share the same accepted-endpoint versus signed-relative-span limit, so this remains one candidate rather than duplicate IDs. No additional line credit; the bodies and helper were previously reviewed. No region operation or point query was run. Source-only.

Intuition WaitPort caller-family census and decorator unload follow-up (GD9413-GD9414 added; 2026-10-23): classified all six direct `WaitPort()` call sites in `rom/intuition`: `sysrequest_intern.c` has the previously traced private requester port/GetMsg consumer; `menutask.c` retains GD5818's unchecked startup port; `screennotifytask.c`'s dedicated task drains its private port; `wbtasktalk.c` uses a stack-local single-waiter reply port; `intuition_misc.c` creates, waits on, dequeues and deletes its private screen-notification reply port; and `decoration.c` waits for its one destroy-message reply. No new WaitPort multi-consumer issue was established in these callers. The decoration path exposed two separate unload problems: queued `int_removedecorator()` mutates/frees the ScrDecorSem-protected list without the semaphore or a reference-count recheck (GD9413), and ignored action-record/reply-port allocation failures suppress destruction of a zero-reference decorator (GD9414). Full repo-wide WaitPort caller inventory remains open; this is Intuition-only caller coverage. No port, screen, task, or allocation failure was exercised. Source-only.


ScrollRegion NULL-rectangle contract correction (GD9415 added, 2026-10-23): revisited the earlier no-finding conclusion against `IsPointInRegion()`'s absolute-bounds check plus relative-rectangle lookup (`rom/graphics/ispointinregion.c:51-70`). `TranslateRect(Bounds(region), dx, dy)` shifts the represented pixels by changing the origin; it does not clip the translated pixels to the saved original bounds. The API comment explicitly says NULL uses the region bounds as the rectangle (`scrollregion.c:28-37`), and the explicit-rectangle branch clips translated contents back to its rectangle (`:68-88`). Corrected the prior ledger claim that bounds-only translation was consistent. Direct caller census found only `MoveRaster()` and it passes a non-NULL rectangle (`gfxfuncsupport.c:861`), so the candidate is limited to external/public NULL-rectangle calls. Added GD9415; no region or caller was run. Source-only.


Animation Realtime-hook/tapedeck state-sharing pass (GD9416 added, 2026-10-23): traced `PLAYER_Hook` installation in the selected Animation constructor (`animationclass.c:140-157`), Realtime `Pulse()` callback dispatch while holding `RT_CONDUCTORS` (`workbench/libs/realtime/pulse.c:76,119-135`), the `PM_TICK`/`PM_SHUTTLE` writes (`animationplayback.c:42-78`), and tapedeck frame scrubbing followed by conductor update (`animationclass.c:1400-1415,1434-1443`). The frame-list semaphore is not acquired by either writer; the conductor lock acquired by `SetConductorState()` occurs after the UI write and does not serialize it with Pulse. Added GD9416 for the conditional lost-update/stale-frame result. Animation is an explicit local build target; the parent aggregate is commented out. No player, input, realtime tick or interleaving was run; source-only.


Intuition converted cursor allocation-failure caller recheck (GD5824 expanded, 2026-10-23): traced `MonitorClass__MM_SetPointerShape()` through the selected `AllocBitMap()` failure return and `BltBitMap()` implementation. The method frees any old `tmpPtr`, stores the new allocation result, and unconditionally blits into it (`rom/intuition/monitorclass.c:1942-1954`). For this branch the source bitmap is known non-HIDD, then `BltBitMap()` evaluates `IS_HIDD_BM(destBitMap)` with `destBitMap == NULL`; the macro dereferences `bitmap->pad` (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:123`; `rom/hidds/gfx/include/gfx.h:632`). Expanded GD5824 to distinguish this immediate failed-allocation fault from its existing successful-allocation/failed-install stale-cursor consequence. No allocation failure or pointer change was induced; source-only.

MonitorClass cursor replacement retained-source claim recheck (GD5824 narrowed, 2026-10-25): separately inspected the generic display, VGA, X11, AmigaVideo and P96 `SetCursorShape()` paths. The selected methods consume/copy pixels synchronously; this pass did not establish that a failed install retains the old converted bitmap as its backing store. Removed the unsupported stale-cursor/use-after-free subclaim from GD5824. Retained the independent allocation-failure defect: failed conversion allocation is passed to `BltBitMap()` as a NULL destination and dereferenced by its HIDD bitmap check. No driver method or allocation failure was run; source-only.


Generic software cursor save-under failure recheck (GD9417 added, 2026-10-23): traced `cursor_AllocBackup()` through `Display__Hidd_Display__SetCursorShape()`, the `cursor_Draw()` guard, Intuition's pointer-shape method, and LinuxFB's selected class definition. When the target/PixFmt are valid but backup `AllocVec()` fails, the setter ignores FALSE and returns TRUE after replacing the cursor image; `cursor_Draw()` immediately returns on the missing backup. LinuxFB subclasses `CLID_Hidd_Display` and does not override `SetCursorShape`, so the generic implementation is inherited (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/linuxfbgfx.conf:43-60`). Added GD9417 for accepted-but-invisible cursor state on this allocation failure. Other HIDD descendants and the pointer-dimension size limits remain to be reconciled. No allocation failure or cursor operation was run; source-only.


Generic software cursor dimension/allocation bounds pass (GD9418 added, 2026-10-23): traced HIDD bitmap dimensions through `PointerClass__OM_NEW()` and `AllocSpriteDataA()` to the generic display cursor setter, ARGB extraction and save-under use. The public `AllocSpriteDataA()` path also accepts ULONG `SPRITEA_Width` without a cursor-size maximum, allocates the HIDD output bitmap at that width, and passes it through `ChangeExtSpriteA()` to `HIDD_Display_SetCursorShape()` (`allocspritedataa.c:85-95,141-167,240-253`; `changeextspritea.c:60-88`). i386 `IPTR` is unsigned 32-bit. For 65,536 × 16,385 pixels, the ARGB and 4-byte save-under products each wrap from 4,295,229,440 to 262,144 bytes. The HIDD GetImage call’s signed WORD width prevents asserting that the ARGB extraction writes all source pixels; the independent framebuffer save-under write is the supported overrun. Confirmed the selected i386-PC package includes VESAGfx and its display class inherits the generic `SetCursorShape()` (`arch/i386-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:75-79`; `rom/hidds/vesagfx/vesagfx.conf:27-43`). VESA routes non-displayable friends of its bitmap class to generic ChunkyBM (`vesagfx_displayclass.c:150-167`), whose backing allocation is `height * bytesperrow` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:65-78`); the stated 8-bit pointer bitmap/output each requires about 1.07 GB, representable on i386 if sufficient memory is available. Added GD9418, qualified on a very large source bitmap and available memory. No large bitmap or cursor operation was created; source-only.


GD9418 HIDD `GetImage` dimension-type correction (2026-10-23): the generic image method's width/height are signed `WORD` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:525`; `gfx_bitmapclass.c:2632-2633`), so the earlier note's 65,536-pixel example does not establish a full-dimension write by `HIDD_BM_GetImage()` during ARGB extraction. Corrected GD9418 to rely on the independent save-under path: the cursor retains the original IPTR width/height, `cursor_AllocBackup()` allocates the wrapped `width*height*bpp` size, then `cursor_Draw()` calls GetImage with the clipped framebuffer rectangle (e.g. 640×480, representable as WORD), which writes 1,228,800 bytes into a 262,144-byte backup for the stated 32-bpp/dimension case. No runtime operation was performed; source-only.


GD5743 failed-scaler caller and output-state follow-up (2026-10-23): expanded the previously summary-only report after tracing `AllocSpriteDataA()`'s BMF_CLEAR destination through `BitMapScale()`'s void HIDD dispatch and the generic `BM__Hidd_BitMap__BitMapScale()` three-buffer setup (`rom/graphics/allocspritedataa.c:242-253`; `rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:454-459`; `rom/graphics/bitmapscale.c:125-131,211-220`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:4937-4965`). Scaler setup/scratch allocation failure returns without populating the cleared bitmap, but the sprite is still returned; selected PointerClass accepts that result and creates a shared pointer (`rom/intuition/pointerclass.c:103,119-149`). The default pointer palette leaves index 0 transparent (`:128-139`), supporting a blank pointer consequence. No allocation failure or pointer was induced; source-only.
Workbench Edit public-port sender follow-up (GD5184 expanded, 2026-10-23): traced the second-instance `find_janoed()` path from `FindPort(JANO_PORT)` through private reply-port allocation and `PutMsg()` (`workbench/tools/Edit/Events.c:437–456`), against `close_port()` and normal cleanup (`:495–500`). This is the same borrowed-public-port lifetime defect already identified for Preferences Editor senders: owner cleanup removes/frees the port, while a client may be preempted between lookup and enqueue; queued-message draining cannot cover a sender not yet enqueued. Expanded GD5184 rather than duplicating it. `send_pref()`'s selected CMD_KILL and GUI callers are not covered by this pass and remain open for lifecycle analysis. No IPC or shutdown overlap was induced; source-only.
Workbench Edit `send_pref()` public-port lifetime cross-check (GD5184 expanded, 2026-10-23): followed `send_pref()` from `FindPort(JANOPREFS_PORT)` through request copy, `PutMsg()` and private reply wait (`workbench/tools/Edit/Events.c:479–493`), then classified its selected callers. `setup_winpref()` issues `CMD_SHOW` (`Prefs.c:529`), while `CloseMainWnd()` issues `CMD_KILL` (`Gui.c:579–581`). The target handles `CMD_KILL` by closing its window and replying, not deleting the public port (`workbench/prefs/Editor/PrefsPort.c:121–128`; `JanoPrefs.c:341–360`); therefore that command alone is not a shutdown trigger. Independent target cleanup still removes/deletes the public port (`PrefsPort.c:99–109`), leaving the same conditional stale-pointer window for `CMD_SHOW`. Updated GD5184's detail; no separate finding. No IPC or shutdown overlap was induced; source-only.
GD9401 BltTemplate direct-caller closure recheck (2026-10-23): traced all maintained direct C callers (`rom/graphics/text.c:381-388`, `rom/graphics/bltpattern.c:115-189`, `workbench/system/ftmanager/fontbitmap_class.c:290-306`) and compared coordinate/size derivation. The normal Font Manager glyph-builder target is its private bitmap, with accepted output dimensions strictly below 32,000 (`fontbitmap_class.c:152-156`), so this caller does not establish the endpoint-crossing case. `Text()` does: its template-based renderer forwards the RastPort cursor plus glyph extent and the measured raster width without clipping the request first (`text.c:381-388`); a WORD cursor at 32,000 and a 125-character 8-pixel fixed-font string yield a 1,000-pixel request crossing `WORD_MAX`, while the visible prefix remains in range. Whether the narrowed maximum becomes negative depends on implementation-defined signed-`WORD` conversion; no selected compiler result was checked, so the report now states this dependency explicitly. Expanded GD9401's maintained-caller evidence and affected scope; no new ID. `BltPattern()` callers remain constrained by their own pattern/source-derived geometry in the checked paths. No text draw, bitmap allocation, or graphics operation was run; source-only.

GD9401 bitmap-to-RastPort GELS caller closure (2026-10-24): traced `AddVSprite()` through `_ValidateIntVSprite()` and the `DrawGList()` Bob/VSprite renderer (`rom/graphics/addvsprite.c:54-67`; `rom/graphics/gels_internal.c:101-123`; `rom/graphics/drawglist.c:146-166`). The public fields are signed WORD `X`/`Width`, and GELS documents/uses `Width` as words; a positive width of 63 therefore builds a 1008-pixel backing bitmap and reaches either bitmap-to-RastPort wrapper with `xDest = VSprite.X` and `xSize = 1008`. At `X=32000`, that request crosses the signed-WORD right endpoint while retaining a visible prefix. No AddVSprite-side width or coordinate clamp precedes the draw call. This establishes a maintained caller path for the existing GD9401 condition, subject to the same implementation-defined narrowing behavior already called out; no new finding ID. The generic draw and mask wrappers share the pre-clipping endpoint construction, so the Bob `ImageShadow` branch is also covered by this caller trace. No VSprite, Bob, bitmap or render was created; source-only.

GD9401 Intuition `DrawImageState()` caller-family check (2026-10-24): inspected the planar-image branch and its selected bitmap blit (`rom/intuition/drawimagestate.c:187-211`) against the public `struct Image` layout (`compiler/include/intuition/intuition.h:744-757`) and all maintained direct C call sites. The path forwards `leftOffset + image->LeftEdge` and `image->Width` to `BltBitMapRastPort()`; both are signed WORD fields, so it can reach the same endpoint-narrowing wrapper condition when the destination is near the signed coordinate limit. This is consistent with GD9401 and adds no independent mechanism. The call-site census found ordinary gadget, menu, requester, and frame rendering users, but did not establish a checked-in instance with the required near-limit destination; the demonstrated `Text()` and GELS callers remain the concrete maintained examples. Boopsi-image drawing, external `DrawImageState()` clients, and actual high-coordinate rendering remain open. No image was drawn; source-only.

VMM GD9629 active-paging reachability qualification (2026-10-24): re-read `AllocAddressRange()` and its selected startup callers after the full `fault.c` pass. In AROS builds, the function's `#else` only emits a TODO and returns `SUCCESS` without assigning `VirtAddrStart` or `VirtAddrEnd` (`workbench/system/VMM/mmu_table.c:908-929`); later managed-region publication dereferences the resulting NULL base (`VM_Manager_Init.c:742-780`). A follow-up sequencing check found that `Init_VM_Manager()` launches and waits for `PageHandler` before that publication (`VM_Manager_Init.c:701-711`; `:88-130`); the page handler installs its trap handler before reporting successful initialization (`workbench/system/VMM/pagehandler.c:114-176,535-570`). Therefore the eventual startup failure does not prove that page-fault activity is impossible in the interval. The uninitialized `TableStart` remains definite, while whether AROS reaches a `PT_TABLE` eviction before the later NULL dereference is uncertain. The detailed report now says so. No extra finding or body-line credit; no handler was built or started.

VMM AROS address-range startup caller pass (GD9419 added, 2026-10-24): rechecked the AROS conditional in `AllocAddressRange()` through `Init_VM_Manager()`, `InitPageHandler()`, support-task launch, and managed-memory publication. Confirmed the function's only assignments to `VirtAddrStart`/`VirtAddrEnd` are excluded by `#if !defined(__AROS__)`, but the AROS branch returns `SUCCESS`; `VirtAddrStart` is zero-initialized with no other assignment, and the later `VirtAddrEnd` assignment is derived from that zero base. The page handler consequently indexes `RootTable` from address zero and calls `MarkAddress()`, whose implementation is compiled out on AROS but still returns `SUCCESS`. On the manager's later publication path, the standard-starter branch calls `AddMemList()` with base NULL (whose selected implementation immediately dereferences it), while the library-start branch writes through `VirtMem == NULL`. Since the page handler is launched and reports initialization before managed-region publication, the eventual failure does not prove that it cannot handle faults in the interval (see GD9629). Active Workbench:System edges select the VMM app and handler; the path still requires a successful build and reaching this startup stage. No handler, memory map, or page table was run or modified; source-only.

VMM finding ID collision reconciliation (2026-10-24): GD6358 had already been withdrawn as a duplicate of GD6175 for a Hyperlayers smart-refresh allocation path (see the 2026-10-23 entries above). AArch64 Raspberry Pi fbgfx reset-callback failed-construction cleanup recheck (GD9392 detailed, 2026-10-24): traced `FBGfx__Root__New()` through nested display construction and its failure Dispose call, then compared callback registration with `FBGfx__Root__Dispose()`. The reset interrupt is registered only after the nested display exists; failed nested construction instead disposes the outer object, whose unconditional `RemResetCallback()` reaches `Remove()` on the reset node before it was linked. Exec OOP root allocation clears the instance (`rom/oop/rootclass.c:115-120`), so both list links are NULL; `Remove()` dereferences `ln_Pred`/`ln_Succ` without membership validation (`rom/exec/remove.c:51-62`). Confirmed the AArch64 Raspi package includes `fbgfx` as the fallback after `vcgfx` declines the board. Expanded GD9392 with this direct cleanup consequence and package scope. No allocation failure or object construction was induced. Source-only.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi fbgfx returned-depth/pitch consequence qualification (GD9421 detailed, 2026-10-24): followed the actual firmware-returned `fb_depth` and pitch from `vcfb_init()` into the kernel attributes and `initFBGfxHW()`. The HIDD ignores the returned depth, hardcodes four-byte pixels, and `fbDoRefreshArea()` copies `w * 4` bytes per row while advancing destination rows by firmware pitch. The checked-in boot config requests depth 32; no supported-board mismatched response was established. Narrowed GD9421's memory-overrun consequence to incompatible layouts with `pitch < width * 4`, while retaining the unconditional hardcoded-format assumption and conditional trigger. No framebuffer or firmware operation was run. Source-only.

CyberGraphX no-match result contract recheck (GD5747 retained; 2026-10-24): reconciled the API's `NULL if there are none` result comment with the constructor's allocate-before-enumeration/unconditional-return path (`workbench/libs/cgfx/alloccmodelisttaglist.c:53-57,129-135,172-235`). The only maintained reference outside the implementation is the direct m68k-emulator ABI thunk, which returns the pointer unchanged (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:368-373`); `FreeCModeList()` accepts an empty initialized list and safely frees it (`workbench/libs/cgfx/freecmodelist.c:40-62`). This confirms the API contract mismatch and safe cleanup, while the caller-visible false-success consequence remains conditional on an external client using NULL to detect no matches. No direct in-tree C caller, mode enumeration or list operation was found/run; no new finding or line credit.

`SetRegion()` and rectangle-list allocation-failure recheck (2026-10-24; GD4662/GD6181 retained, no new finding): reread the complete `_LinkRegionRectangleList()` failure path and `SetRegion()` caller. Confirmed that for an initially empty destination, `prev` is NULL and a chunk-allocation failure after at least one successful chunk leaves the partial list unreachable; for a populated destination, rollback severs and frees the appended suffix but leaves `SetRegion()` returning FALSE after assigning source bounds and copying the overlapping prefix. This is already covered by GD4662; ignored results at selected layer callers and their incomplete snapshots remain GD6181. No separate root cause or consequence established. No allocation failure or region copy was induced; source-only.


Raspberry Pi VideoCore shared bitmap palette-fallback caller recheck (GD9420 added; 2026-10-24): corrected the prior note that treated the selected truecolor display mode as closing all palette behavior. The on-screen framebuffer is truecolor, but `VideoCoreGfxOffBM::New()` also accepts displayable/friend bitmap requests and, with GPU placement disabled, zeroes `BitmapData` before returning its ChunkyBM-backed object. Its shared `SetColors()` method delegates to the generic superclass and then range-checks against the still-zero `data->bpp`; valid palette updates above entry zero therefore report FALSE after mutating the generic colormap. Added GD9420 with the `AllocBitMap()` internal caller qualification: it issues one-entry calls and ignores the status, while direct HIDD clients can observe the false failure. No separate palette-memory corruption was established because the selected offscreen path has `VideoData == NULL` and does not use the subclass cmap cache. Full body credit remains 276 `cloc 2.06` C code lines; no palette or bitmap operation was run. Source-only.


VideoCore `SetColors()` direct-caller census for GD9420 (2026-10-24): repository-wide `HIDD_BM_SetColors()` search found five maintained C call sites. `AllocBitMap()`, `internal_SetRGB32Colors()`, the generic display colormap-copy helper, Intuition pointer-color initialization, and SDL framebuffer copy-back all discard the returned Boolean. The internal caller paths therefore do not demonstrate a visible error response to GD9420; only direct HIDD clients that inspect the documented result can observe the false failure after colormap mutation. No new root cause or line credit. Source-only.

AArch64 Raspberry Pi fbgfx update/copy boundary recheck (GD9421 retained; no new GD; 2026-10-24): followed the HIDD `UpdateRect` entry from its `WORD x/y/width/height` API and a maintained Gallium rectangle caller into `fbDoRefreshArea()` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:5035-5060`; `workbench/libs/gallium/bltpiperesourcerastport.c:145-153`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/hidd/fbgfx/fbgfx_bitmapclass.c:208-218`). The wrapper passes the API's origin and extent as the helper's half-open endpoints; the helper applies scroll offsets and clips to display bounds before computing source/destination offsets. Reviewed `fbgfx` pixel-format tags as well: its format advertises 24 color bits in a 32-bit/four-byte pixel, so `FBGfxBM__Hidd_BitMap__SetColors()`'s `1 << data->bpp` uses a shift of 24 on the selected mode, not 32. No separate coordinate or shift defect was established. The firmware-depth mismatch remains GD9421 because its helper always copies four bytes per pixel while the bootstrap's accepted returned depth may differ. No display, blit, or firmware response was exercised; source-only.

MUI ARexx argument-buffer lifetime check (2026-10-24; no additional GD): checked whether freeing the temporary input string before `CallHookPkt()` leaves parsed string arguments dangling. DOS `ReadArgs()` copies `RDA_Source.CS_Buffer` into its own `strbuf` (`rom/dos/readargs.c:453-466`) and returns string argument pointers into that owned result storage (`:620-624,804-868`); the MUI hook runs before `FreeArgs(rdargsret)` releases it (`application.c:1746-1759`; `rom/dos/freeargs.c:50-64`). Thus freeing the original `arguments` buffer at `application.c:1749` does not invalidate parsed strings. No ownership finding added. This verifies only that lifetime concern; remaining `application.c` code and callers stay open.

MUI Area background-spec replacement failure-path check (2026-10-24; no additional GD): traced `MUIA_Background` replacement in `Area__OM_SET()` through `zune_image_spec_duplicate()`, old-spec/resource cleanup, `zune_imspec_setup()`, show, and draw (`classes/area.c:482-521,1338-1377`; `imspec.c:463-572,719-743`). If duplication fails, the old spec and initialized image are retained. If runtime setup fails after a successful replacement, the new spec remains and `mad_Background` becomes NULL; `zune_imspec_show()` and cleanup accept NULL, while the draw method falls back to `MUIM_DrawParentBackground` when there is no image. This is graceful loss of the selected background under allocation/setup failure, with no distinct correctness defect established by these paths. # Hyperlayers visibility-query failure follow-up (GD6186 expanded; no new ID; 2026-10-24)

Traced `IsLayerHiddenBySibling()`'s bounding-box prefilter and region query (`rom/hyperlayers/islayerhiddenbysibling.c:79-96`) against `SetRegion()` and `AndRegionRegion()` failure semantics (`rom/graphics/setregion.c:46-82`; `rom/graphics/andregionregion.c:53-87`). The query ignores both Boolean results and interprets any nonempty destination as an actual intersection. When the copy succeeds but the AND temporary allocation fails, the destination remains the copied sibling region and the query can return TRUE for non-intersecting visible shapes; a failed copy can likewise leave an incomplete destination. Traced its actual Intuition caller: `HandleSysGadgetVerify()` uses the result to choose WindowToFront versus WindowToBack for the system depth gadget (`rom/intuition/inputhandler_support.c:579-591`). The query resolves to the Layers vector outside MorphOS, where `rom/intuition/misc.c:171-210`'s local replacement is excluded. Corrected the detailed report's previous no-in-tree-caller qualification; the front/back decision gives a concrete caller consequence. Expanded existing GD6186; no duplicate finding was added. This targeted caller trace does not add whole-file credit. No allocation failure, layer query, or window-depth action was run; source-only.

Rechecked `BeginUpdate()` failure handling through the Intuition `Gad_BeginUpdate()` wrapper and its checked-in callers. `CheckLayerRefresh()` ignores the wrapper result and unconditionally calls `Gad_EndUpdate()` for GZZ border and requester refreshes (`rom/intuition/inputhandler_actions.c:66-95`); the wrapper holds GadgetLock around the call, while failed Layers `BeginUpdate()` releases its own layer lock before returning FALSE (`rom/intuition/inputhandler_support.c:1652-1661`; `rom/hyperlayers/beginupdate.c:67-92`). `EndUpdate()` then unlocks the layer again and, for a non-smart-refresh layer with a non-NULL clip list, frees the still-active list because `cr2` aliases `ClipRect` (`rom/hyperlayers/endupdate.c:59-88`). MUI legacy Application Input handler-mask recheck (GD5083 strengthened; 2026-10-24): compared `Application__MUIM_Input()` with `Application__MUIM_AddInputHandler()` and the `NewInput` callback gate (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1474-1504,1564-1586,1826-1835,1861-1889`) and the public node layout/flag definition (`application.h:315-339`). The old method ORs `ihn_Flags` into the returned handler mask; `NewInput` tests `ihn_Signals`, and non-timer handlers are linked into the list with their signal mask in that separate field. Therefore the legacy mask omits non-timer handler signals and the delegated `NewInput` call also receives a mask that will not intersect them. Timer handlers use the dedicated timer port and are outside this list. A checkout-wide direct-call search found five legacy Input callers (Wanderer filesystem utilities, BHFormat, VMM MUI, VMMUsage, and the desktop loader test); no checked-in same-application non-timer registration paired with those callers was established. Strengthened GD5083 with the implementation mismatch and explicit conditional reachability; no new ID or application.c body credit. No signal or application loop was run; source-only.

MUI Bitmap palette-allocation failure follow-up (GD9518 added; 2026-10-24): traced the failed `ObtainBestPenA()` result through the WORD cache entry and Cleanup release (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/bitmap.c:179-195,473-484`), then verified the selected Graphics API return and `ReleasePen()` behavior (`rom/graphics/obtainbestpena.c:45-48,119-148`; `rom/graphics/releasepen.c:57-80,147-155`). With no shared match and no free pen, `ObtainBestPenA()` can return -1; Bitmap stores that as nonzero -1 and later releases low-byte pen 255, even though it acquired no pen. On a 256-entry colormap this can make another client's exclusive pen available, or decrement a shared pen reference. Added GD9518 with the palette-exhaustion and pen-255 ownership conditions; distinct from GD9469's successful pen-zero reacquisition leak. This is caller/ownership follow-up only and adds no body-line credit; `bitmap.c` was already credited at 447/447 lines. No palette state or bitmap was changed; source-only.

GD2716/GD2726 withdrawal correction and ASCII subclass revalidation (2026-10-24): the prior withdrawal notes were incorrect because they traced only the superclass's non-datatype helper and missed the selected `ascii.datatype` subclass. `ascii.conf` declares `TEXTDTCLASS` as superclass and its manifest builds `asciiclass.c`; the class overrides `GM_LAYOUT` and dispatches `DTM_ASYNCLAYOUT` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/ascii/ascii.conf:1-23`; `mmakefile.src:6-12`; `asciiclass.c:165-181,224-225`). GD2726 is restored: the parent Text class's `LoadTextAsIFF()` allocates exactly `cn->cn_Size` bytes and reads exactly that many CHRS bytes (`workbench/classes/datatypes/text/textclass.c:363-390`); the ASCII subclass loop enters for `i < bufferlen` then reads `buffer[i+1]` when the final byte is CR (`asciiclass.c:315-325`), establishing a one-byte read past the allocation for an exact-size CHRS payload ending in CR. GD2716 is restored: the same selected subclass stores the ULONG `num` as `ln_TextLen` (`asciiclass.c:249,373-378`); at 32,768 input characters the shared text renderer assigns it to LONG and calls the graphics `Text()` API with WORD count (`textclass.c:538-539,663`; `textclass.h:34-39`; `graphics.conf:50`). On compiler behavior that narrows 32768 to signed WORD -32768, `Text()` passes that negative count to `BltTemplateBasedText(..., ULONG len, ...)`, and the eligible 8-pixel unstyled fast-font path scans `text[i]` up to that huge unsigned length (`rom/graphics/text.c:70-88,97-120`). The signed narrowing result is implementation-defined and was not tested; retain GD2716 as a conditional medium-confidence source candidate. GD2727 was traced through MultiView's toggle and `DoLayout(TRUE)` into the ASCII async layout: the wrap flag only gates rebuilding at `asciiclass.c:299-317`; line segments are emitted on input line/page/tab separators or end-of-buffer (`:319-368`) with no domain-width split, while the reported horizontal extent remains based on the longest line (`:491-522`). This confirms GD2727's behavior when the ASCII module is built and used. The earlier withdrawal notes are superseded. No build or runtime was run; default aggregate inclusion of the standalone ASCII target remains unverified.

GD2719 async-layout startup failure caller-path recheck (2026-10-24): traced the generic `DoAsyncLayout()` helper and its ASCII, binary, HTML, and picture subclass callers. The helper initializes `retval=FALSE`; if `AllocVec(LayoutMessage)` fails or `CreateNewProc()` fails, it frees any message, clears `DTSIF_LAYOUT|DTSIF_LAYOUTPROC`, and returns FALSE (`workbench/libs/datatypes/doasynclayout.c:146,172-213`). It does not send `DTA_Busy=FALSE` on either failure; that notification is in `AsyncLayouter()` after a worker actually runs (`:83-94`). Each of the four subclass GM_LAYOUT handlers notifies DTA_Busy TRUE before `DoAsyncLayout()` (`ascii/asciiclass.c:169-180`; `binary/binaryclass.c:175-191`; `html/htmlclass.c:357-373`; `picture/pictureclass.c:848-858`). Their superclass `datatypes.class` GM_LAYOUT sets `retval=TRUE` (`workbench/libs/datatypes/class.c:411,890-934`), and subclasses add the helper's FALSE result, so the dispatch still returns success while busy remains set and no layout runs. Retained GD2719, high-confidence source candidate for allocation or process-creation failure in any affected subclass. No failure was induced; module/default aggregate reachability remains configuration-dependent.

GD9520 async worker shutdown/restart flag race (new, 2026-10-24): traced the worker and API state transitions in `workbench/libs/datatypes/doasynclayout.c`. The worker clears `DTSIF_LAYOUT` under `SEM_ASYNC` and clears `DTA_LayoutProc` before releasing that semaphore (`:58-78`), then releases the object semaphore and performs completion notifications before clearing `DTSIF_LAYOUTPROC` under `Forbid()` (`:81-100`). A second layout request in this window enters the `DTSIF_LAYOUT`-clear branch because `DoAsyncLayout()` tests only `DTSIF_LAYOUT` (`:152-168`); it sets both flags, creates a second worker and publishes its process pointer (`:170-207`). The first worker then unconditionally clears the shared `DTSIF_LAYOUTPROC` bit, even though the second worker is active or waiting for `si_Lock`. `RemoveDTObject()` and `DisposeDTObject()` wait only on that bit (`removedtobject.c:68-79`; `disposedtobject.c:53-66`), so they can proceed while the second worker still references the object. The async subclasses in ASCII, binary, HTML and picture call the helper; MultiView's Word Wrap menu issues another `GM_LAYOUT` through `DoLayout(TRUE)` (`main.c:1681-1692`; `misc.c:593-617`). Candidate trigger is a repeated layout request during the worker's exit/notification window. Consequence is an unprotected async reference across remove/dispose, with possible use-after-dispose or task failure. Confidence medium-high from source ordering; no interleaving or runtime was exercised.

GD9520 synchronization-scope recheck (2026-10-25): compared the worker's terminal flag clear with the second worker's `SEM_ASYNC`-protected publication. The prior worker has already released `SEM_ASYNC` before the completion notification and its final `Forbid()`/`DTSIF_LAYOUTPROC` clear (`doasynclayout.c:78-100`); the new request sets the same flag while holding `SEM_ASYNC` (`:152-207`). Thus the final clear is not ordered by the semaphore. On single-CPU targets a task switch before `Forbid()` permits the second publication; on ExecSMP, `Forbid()` is explicitly processor-local (`rom/exec/forbid.c:55-59`) and cannot protect the shared flag from another CPU. The waiters still observe only the cleared bit and can proceed while B's queued/active message retains the object pointer. This strengthens the existing source-level synchronization premise without claiming a reproduced schedule; no new finding ID or body-line credit.


GD9520 maintained repeated-layout caller timing confirmation (2026-10-24): ASCII `GM_LAYOUT` calls `DoAsyncLayout()` and returns its result (`workbench/classes/datatypes/ascii/asciiclass.c:165-181`); successful helper startup only queues the message with `PutMsg()` and returns TRUE without joining the process (`workbench/libs/datatypes/doasynclayout.c:201-218`). MultiView's `HandleAll()` returns from the Word Wrap case after `DoLayout(TRUE)`, then resumes its outer event loop (`workbench/utilities/MultiView/main.c:1299-1306,1681-1693,1770-1772`). Thus a subsequent user layout request can be handled while the asynchronous worker is still in its completion window; the helper's existing in-progress branch is specifically intended to accept such repeated requests. This confirms the caller can overlap layout requests; the narrow exit-window interleaving remains source-inferred and unexercised.

HTML datatype constructor-failure candidate recheck (GD6278 detailed; 2026-10-24): re-read the `Html__OM_NEW()` failure branches through class-local `OM_DISPOSE` and the complete `layout_free()` helper. HTML tag/entity length-bound recheck (GD6279 detailed; 2026-10-24): re-read `parse_tag()` and `escape_to_char()` against the table-derived `MAX_Tag_Length`/`MAX_Esc_Length`. Each VLA has `MAX + 1` bytes, while the inclusive `i <= MAX` loop can store `MAX + 1` input characters and then writes the terminator at index `MAX + 1`. A name one character longer than the longest table entry therefore reaches a one-byte out-of-bounds terminator write. Expanded GD6279 with the distinct tag/entity paths and optional HTML-target scope. `parse.c` and `tables.c` already have full-body credit; no line total changed. No input was parsed; source-only.

FreeType `OT_WidthList` endpoint and loop-bound recheck (GD2839 added; 2026-10-24): followed `OT_GlyphCode`/`OT_GlyphCode2` storage into `GetWidthList()` and its `OT_WidthList` dispatcher (`workbench/libs/freetype2/setinfoa.c:207-215`; `kerning.c:35-40,76-107`; `obtaininfoa.c:117-124`). 8SVX sample-count wrap candidate re-review (GD6265 confirmed with bounded consequence; 2026-10-24): verified `ULONG` is unsigned 32-bit and traced `vh_OneShotHiSamples + vh_RepeatHiSamples` through BODY comparison, allocation/read, `SDTA_SampleLength` publication, and selected Sound playback length consumers. ASCII trailing-CR boundary candidate re-review (GD6267 confirmed with caller scope; 2026-10-24): followed the `buffer[i + 1]` read in `Ascii__DTM_ASYNCLAYOUT()` through both Text superclass buffer paths. `LoadText()` allocates one extra byte and writes a newline sentinel; by contrast `TDTA_Buffer` and `TDTA_BufferLen` setters store the caller's pointer and exact declared length without copying or extending the allocation. Thus an exact-length caller buffer ending in CR reaches a one-byte-past-extent read, while the standard file loader does not. No checked-in exact-length custom-buffer caller was found; kept GD6267 scoped to external clients of the public Text attributes. Consequence is limited to the read and possible fault/adjacent-data-dependent CR handling; no further effect is inferred. No custom buffer or layout was run; source-only.

ASCII empty-file candidate re-review (GD6268 retained at medium confidence; 2026-10-24): traced the zero-size file path through Text `LoadText()` and the subclass `OM_NEW` check. Text accepts size zero, allocates `len+1`, reads zero bytes, writes its newline sentinel at index zero, and returns a non-NULL buffer with length zero. ASCII rejects that pair solely because its condition requires both pointer and nonzero length, reports `ERROR_REQUIRED_ARG_MISSING`, and disposes the otherwise-created object. This confirms the behavioral mismatch; no explicit source contract promises that the ASCII subclass must accept an empty document, so GD6268 is retained as a low-impact, medium-confidence compatibility candidate rather than stated as an unconditional API violation. Binary datatype line-allocation abort candidate re-review (GD6269 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-24): reread the full expected-row calculation, initial line-list replacement, allocation loop and publication path in `binaryclass.c`; traced the resulting actual line list and published total into Text drawing and viewport calculations. The row count is computed from the full input length before construction. An `AllocPooled()` failure sets `abort`, but only the Ctrl-C signal value `bsig` gates completion; with no Ctrl-C, the method writes full `si_TotVert` and publishes full total/cleared busy despite the shorter new list. Old rows have already been removed. Expanded GD6269 with the confirmed full-height/partial-content mismatch and bounded memory-pressure trigger. Binary datatype large-buffer row arithmetic candidate re-review (GD6270 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-24): traced Text's size/addressability gate and optional DOS64 initialization into the Binary row-count, offset-width and iteration arithmetic. `ULONG` is unsigned 32-bit and `LONG` signed 32-bit. For a buffer above 0x7ffffff0 bytes, the rounded row count fits `LONG` but `lines * 16` in each offset-width threshold can overflow signed LONG; the chosen width controls how many high-to-low hex nibbles are written for each row address. For lengths above 0xfffffff0, `bufferlen + 15` wraps before division and undercounts rows; at buffer lengths above 0xfffffff0 the ULONG loop counter can wrap after the final partial row if allocation succeeds throughout. Text permits up to 0xfffffffe bytes when the size is addressable, and the selected Text module optionally opens dos64.library; this requires a 64-bit IPTR build, the DOS64 dependency, and enough memory. Expanded GD6270 with explicit bounds and kept output effects conditional on compiler/runtime behavior. No multi-gigabyte file, layout, or allocation was run; source-only.

PNM dimension-truncation candidate re-review (GD6271 confirmed with concrete Picture copy path; 2026-10-24): reread the PNM header parse, all row decoders and their `PDTM_WRITEPIXELARRAY` calls, then traced Picture's first-call source-buffer allocation and row-copy method. PNM parses dimensions in `long`, assigns them without bounds checks to 16-bit `BitMapHeader` width/height, but continues iterating and passing the original dimensions. Picture allocates from the truncated fields and copies the requested width/height without rectangle bounds checks. A P3 width 1/height 65,537 case produces a one-row Picture source allocation, then the second row copy starts at its end. Expanded GD6271 with this caller-to-consumer extent mismatch and exact trigger; other PNM parser findings remain separate. No image or allocation was exercised; source-only.

PNM ASCII-sample candidate re-review (GD6272 confirmed and bounded; 2026-10-24): reread `ReadNextInt()` and the P2/P3 loops through the successful `LoadPNM()` return. is not rejected before `c - '0'`, so the first missing sample returns -49; the loops scale/cast it into RGBBuffer and submit the row without checking stream state. A 1x1 P2 header with MaxVal 255 and no sample stores byte 207 and can complete the Picture write path. P3 applies the same unchecked conversion independently to each missing channel. The non-digit token arithmetic is noted as parser weakness but not promoted to a separate finding here. Expanded GD6272; binary P4/P5/P6 parsing is outside its scope. No file load was run; source-only.

PNM zero-MaxVal candidate re-review (GD6273 confirmed and scoped; 2026-10-24): traced `MaxVal` header parsing through every PNM decoder use. The only validation rejects values above 65,535; zero is retained. P2/P3 normalize ASCII samples by dividing by `MaxVal`, and P5 does the same for one- and two-byte samples, so any nonempty input in these formats reaches integer division by zero. P6 does not use `MaxVal` in its pixel conversion and is excluded from this finding. Expanded GD6273 and corrected the master-index summary to name the affected variants. No image was loaded; source-only.

PNM P6 MaxVal candidate re-review (GD6274 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-24): traced the accepted MaxVal range into the P6 read/forward path. The header permits 1..65,535, while P6 always reads `Width*3` bytes and sends those unchanged as RGB. Values below 255 are not normalized to the full channel range; values >=256 require two-byte big-endian samples, but the code still reads only one byte per channel and groups the stream as 8-bit RGB. Expanded GD6274 with both supported-range cases and updated the master-index summary. No P6 file was loaded; source-only.

GIF decoder-initialization failure candidate re-review (GD6275 confirmed and separated from decode-result handling; 2026-10-24): traced every `DecodeInit()` return path into its caller and the first decoder consumers. Codec `AllocVec()` failure stores NULL and returns -2; `LoadGIF()` ignores the result and immediately calls `DecodeLines()`, which dereferences `d->eof_code` from that NULL pointer. A short code-size read or out-of-range minimum code size also returns before `init_table()`, leaving the allocated codec fields uninitialized while the caller continues. `DecodeEnd()` is likewise called without checking prior status. Expanded GD6275 with these exact init-failure states and updated the index summary. The subsequent decode-error/full-image publication path remains GD6276 and is not duplicated. No allocation failure or GIF load was induced; source-only.

GIF decode-result and output-extent candidate re-review (GD6276 confirmed and separated from GD6275; 2026-10-24): traced line-buffer allocation, all three decoder status returns, both normal/interlaced Picture-copy paths, and decoder output accounting. `linebuf` is allocated without clearing; `DecodeLines()` can return errors after a partial prefix, and its normal end-code return does not require `linebufbytes == 0`. `LoadGIF()` ignores DecodeInit/DecodeLines/DecodeEnd results and submits the full `width*height` image (or full rows in interlaced mode) to Picture. GIF raw-save result-propagation re-review (GD6277 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-24): traced `SaveGIF()` from codec initialization through final buffer flush and `DTM_WRITE`. `EncodeInit()` allocation failure leaves `codecvars` NULL and the unchecked call proceeds to `EncodeLines()`; its output-buffer error can also return before the encoder table is initialized. `write_code()` signals subblock write failure, but both encoding loops discard it. The final `SaveGIF_EmptyBuf()` checks `Write()` length but its FALSE result is discarded, after which `SaveGIF()` returns TRUE and the raw method forwards that success. Expanded GD6277 to distinguish the allocation-failure NULL dereference from false success/incomplete file outcomes. No save, allocation failure, or destination I/O failure was induced; source-only.

BitMapScale scratch-allocation failure re-review (GD77 re-established, 2026-10-24): traced the function's planar and generic HIDD dispatch through each local scratch allocation and its public void signature. On planar bitmaps, failure to allocate `LinePattern` jumps to the common return before any scaled pixels are written (`rom/graphics/bitmapscale.c:250-270,396-400`). On generic HIDD scaling, failure of `srcbuf`, `dstbuf`, or `linepattern` makes `BM__Hidd_BitMap__BitMapScale()` return without writing the destination (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:4928-4949`); the graphics.library caller cannot observe that status and still calls `update_bitmap()` (`bitmapscale.c:211-220`). `BitMapScale()` returns void (`graphics.conf:155`; `bitmapscale.c:42-48`), so the caller cannot distinguish a completed scale from these allocation exits. Re-established GD77 as a conditional silent no-op / unscaled-destination result on scratch-allocation failure, including generic HIDD scaling; kept separate from GD5743's concrete pointer-construction caller consequence and GD5732's different buffered drawing operations. No allocation failure or scale call was induced; source-only.

ASL file-request multiselect allocation-failure re-review (GD2701 confirmed; 2026-10-24): followed selected-file counting and WBArg construction through the requester event loop to the public result. With `FRF_DOMULTISELECT` set and more than one list item selected, `FRGetSelectedFiles()` allocates room for the counted selections, then advances the output pointer/count only when `VecPooledCloneString()` succeeds (`workbench/libs/asl/filereqhooks.c:1802-1857`). A failed selected-name copy is silently skipped; if a prior or later copy succeeds, the method publishes only that subset via `fr_NumArgs = i` (`:1869-1876`). It then unconditionally returns `GHRET_FINISHED_OK` (`:1892`), which the file-request event hook converts to a finished event and `HandleEvents()` converts to TRUE (`filereqhooks.c:1415-1417`; `basicfuncs.c:795-804`); `AslRequest()` returns that success (`aslrequest.c:301-303,331`). `FileRequester.fr_NumArgs/fr_ArgList` are the public selected-file outputs (`compiler/include/libraries/asl.h:61-62`), and checked-in consumers iterate exactly `fr_NumArgs` (`workbench/c/RequestFile.c:179-193`). Confirmed the report summary: a temporary allocation failure while copying one or more selected names can make a multiselect request report success with a partial list. No allocation failure or requester was run; source-only.

ReadPixelArray8 clipped-offset and public-result re-review (GD2662/GD2663 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-24): re-read `readpixelarray8.c`, the clipping renderer, coordinate macro and vector configuration. `do_render_with_gc()` keeps the array source offsets in signed `WORD` locals and adds the clipped-away x/y distances into them (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:110-121,123-140,169-180`); `rp8_render()` converts those offsets directly into a byte offset from the caller array (`readpixelarray8.c:21-32`; `graphics_intern.h:295-296`). For `xstart=-32768,xstop=0` on a bitmap clipped to begin at x=0, the clipped source offset is 32768 and narrows to -32768; the render therefore starts before the caller array, although the documented allocation formula reserves the full requested width (`readpixelarray8.c:54-68,100-123`). Separately, the implementation accumulates and returns a `LONG` pixel count (`readpixelarray8.c:40,95,123-127`), but the public graphics vector configuration declares the result as `WORD` (`graphics.conf:175`). A fully read 256x128 rectangle returns 32768 from the body, which is not representable in signed WORD, so public callers cannot reliably receive the documented pixel count (`readpixelarray8.c:54-71`; `graphics.conf:175`). Reconfirmed the two distinct issues: the clipped pointer offset is a WORD intermediate in renderer clipping, while the count is a public return-width mismatch. No pixel read, clip operation or ABI build was run; source-only.

DataTypes NewDTObjectA internally obtained reference lifetime re-review (GD2747 confirmed; 2026-10-24): traced each `ObtainDataTypeA()` call in `NewDTObjectA()` through datatype-class open, engine lookup, object construction, returned-object disposal, and datatype replacement. A successful `ObtainDataTypeA()` increments the selected descriptor `OpenCount` (`workbench/libs/datatypes/obtaindatatypea.c:213-216`). `NewDTObjectA()` releases it on the explicit GroupID-mismatch paths only (`newdtobjecta.c:183-194,228-238`); after later failures such as datatype-class `OpenLibrary()`, engine lookup, or `NewObjectA()`, the NULL-object cleanup handles the file lock/IFF state but not the acquired DataType reference (`:273-349`). On success, `DisposeDTObject()` calls `DisposeObject()` and closes the datatype class library, while the base `OM_DISPOSE` frees the data handle/name but does not call `ReleaseDataType()` (`disposedtobject.c:53-67`; `class.c:961-1033`). The retained OpenCount is read by Workbench AddDataTypes, which refuses replacement of an existing descriptor when the count is nonzero (`workbench/c/AddDataTypes.c:1024-1034`). DataTypes NewDTObjectA class-library path boundary re-review (GD2749 confirmed and scoped; 2026-10-24): traced `DTA_BaseName` from the public datatype tag definition into the local library-name assembly and checked the selected in-tree ScreenGrabber caller. `NewDTObjectA()` accepts the tag at `workbench/libs/datatypes/newdtobjecta.c:131-135`, then copies `"datatypes/"` (10 bytes), appends the base name, and appends `".datatype"` (9 bytes) into `libname[120]` without a length check (`:276-286`). A 100-byte base name fits exactly with its terminator; 101 bytes makes the final terminator land at index 120, one byte past the array. The tag is defined as the datatype class base name (`compiler/include/datatypes/datatypesclass.h:99-100`). The selected ScreenGrabber caller uses the short literal `"png"` (`workbench/tools/ScreenGrabber/main.c:177-181`), so that maintained caller is not affected; the candidate applies to a call supplying a longer base name. A registered `dth_BaseName` also flows into this buffer, but no evidence was found that checked-in descriptors exceed the threshold. Confirmed GD2749 with this qualified source/API trigger. No object construction or long-name call was run; source-only.

DiskFont tagged-list UWORD count wrap re-review (GD2815 confirmed and bounded; 2026-10-24): followed tagged font conversion through both consumers. `ConvDiskFont()` counts each on-disk tag including `TAG_DONE` in a `UWORD`, allocates `numtags * sizeof(TagItem)`, then copies exactly `numtags` entries (`workbench/libs/diskfont/diskfont_io.c:402-440`). With 65,536 ordinary tag items plus the terminator (65,537 total), the count wraps to one; the allocation holds one tag and the copy loop omits the terminator. `AllocSegment()` allocates only the requested payload plus segment bookkeeping (`basicfuncs.c:20-39`). In the ordinary open path, `ReadDiskFont()` passes this one-item list to `ExtendFont()`, which clones it by `NextTagItem()` iteration until a terminator (`diskfont_io.c:508-525`; `rom/graphics/extendfont.c:92-103`; `rom/utility/clonetagitems.c:71-84`). In the contents path, `NewFontContents()` calls `ConvDiskFont(..., FALSE)` and then itself walks the list until `TAG_DONE` (`newfontcontents.c:152-167,190-222`). These consumers therefore read beyond the allocated tag payload when the first item is an ordinary tag. The trigger requires a very large tagged font; no valid-file maximum was found in the reviewed parser path. Confirmed GD2815 as a bounded source candidate; no font file was loaded or converted. Source-only.

DiskFont fixed-width filename parser bound re-review (GD2816 confirmed and qualified; 2026-10-24): checked the format declaration and every selected `ReadFontDescr()` caller. `MAXFONTPATH` is 256, matching `FontContents.fc_FileName[256]` (`compiler/include/diskfont/diskfont.h:22-27`); the parser's local `strbuf` is 257 bytes (`af_fontdescr_io.c:28-37`). Its byte loop has no 256-byte field limit and continues reading until NUL (`:110-124`). An unterminated filename field therefore causes parsing to consume the subsequent record fields; if no NUL occurs in the one-byte spare slot or following bytes, the loop writes past the local array. The following seek also uses the unbounded length to reposition within the record (`:136-143`). Traced the selected directory enumeration and direct lookup callers (`diskfontfunc.c:93-109,842-846,1345-1348`). Confirmed the missing parser bound as a malformed-descriptor robustness/correctness candidate; valid files are expected to NUL-terminate the fixed-width field, and no valid-file trigger was found. No font descriptor was loaded; source-only.

DiskFont NewFontContents caller filename-size re-review (GD2817 confirmed; 2026-10-24): read `NewFontContents()` from input setup through return and traced the selected Font datatype caller. The routine copies `fontName` into `name[MAXFONTNAME]` with `strcpy()` before validating the `.font` suffix (`newfontcontents.c:97-117`; `MAXFONTNAME` is 32 at `diskfont.h:52`). The Font datatype obtains `Name = FIB->fib_FileName` and passes it through `NewFC()` to `NewFontContents()` (`fontclass.c:197-209`; `otag.c:50-59`); DOS defines that FIB field as 108 bytes (`dos.h:57,81`). Thus a `.font` filename of 32 or more bytes including NUL overruns the 32-byte local array on the selected caller path. Also checked the subsequent directory-basename/child-name concatenation against the FIB field size; its combined maximum remains below the 256-byte `FontContents.fc_FileName` field, so no separate candidate was added there. No long-named file was opened; source-only.

DiskFont NewFontContents backward tag-pack boundary re-review (GD2818 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-24): traced allocation, list insertion, tag counting and packing against both ABI layouts. Each item is allocated as `contentsBuffer { Node; FontContents; }` (`newfontcontents.c:32-36,170-171`), then linked before tag packing (`:183-187`). `TagItem` has IPTR-aligned data and is 8 bytes on 32-bit, 16 bytes on 64-bit (`utility/tagitem.h:17-23`); the 256-byte pack endpoint starts at `&tfc_TagCount + 2`, and the start is moved backward by `nTags * sizeof(TagItem)` without a bound check (`newfontcontents.c:195-222`). Including TAG_DONE, 33 items on 32-bit and 17 on 64-bit first overlap Node fields; 34/18 reach the Node list links, and 35/19 start before the `contentsBuffer` allocation (Node size/layout from `exec/nodes.h:31-38`, with the FontContents member following Node). `ConvDiskFont()` supplies the converted tagged list and walks until the file's TAG_DONE (`diskfont_io.c:402-455`). Confirmed the count-dependent write and target-specific thresholds; no tag-count cap was found in the traced conversion path. No font was loaded; source-only.

DiskFont `.otag` tag-buffer end-bound re-review (GD2819 confirmed; 2026-10-24): traced `OTAG_GetFile()` from file-size acquisition through all tag scan/conversion paths and its selected `ReadFontDescr()` caller. It allocates `sizeof(OTagList)+l`, reads `l` bytes into `data`, and checks identifier/embedded size (`bullet.c:77-117`; `OTagList` layout in `diskfont_intern.h:78-83`). On 64-bit, the tag-count pass advances by tag/data pairs until TAG_DONE without comparing against `l` (`bullet.c:125-145`). Both 32-bit in-place conversion and 64-bit conversion read tag data for every non-DONE item and continue until TAG_DONE, also without checking the buffer end (`:154-180`). A matching declared-size field does not ensure a complete pair or terminating tag, so a malformed file can make these loops read past the allocated data; the 64-bit count scan does so before its converted-tag allocation. `ReadFontDescr()` uses this path for OFCH descriptors (`af_fontdescr_io.c:72-95`). Confirmed GD2819 as a malformed/truncated-file parser-bound issue. No `.otag` file was loaded; source-only.

DiskFont `.otag` indirect-offset and consumer-length re-review (GD2820 confirmed and bounded; 2026-10-24): traced indirect relocation from the file read into concrete outline-font consumers. `OTAG_GetFile()` converts `OT_Indirect` data to `otaglist->data + offset` without checking it against the actual `l` bytes (`bullet.c:77-117,154-180`). `ReadFontDescr()` obtains `OT_AvailSizes`, reads the pointed-to count, then reads that many additional UWORD entries without a buffer-end check (`af_fontdescr_io.c:72-85,211-223`). `OTAG_ReadOutlineFont()` obtains `OT_Engine`, calls `strlen()` on the pointer, and copies the value into a library path (`bullet.c:898-920`). The file header size equality does not validate these inner offsets or lengths. Confirmed GD2820 for malformed `.otag` payload bounds; kept distinct from GD2819’s missing tag terminator. No outline font was loaded; source-only.

GD2821 finding wording precision recheck (2026-10-24): the NULL dereference occurs in FreeType’s shared `GetGlyph()` helper, not in `ObtainInfoA()` itself. `ObtainInfoA()` dispatches the two selected glyph-map tag families to that helper; after a nonzero glyph code, `GetGlyph()` stores `AllocVec()` in `ge->GMap`, conditionally renders only on non-NULL, then unconditionally reads `ge->GMap->glm_Width` (`workbench/libs/freetype2/obtaininfoa.c:34-52,94-115`). Corrected GD2821’s report and master-index summary to name the actual dereference site. Existing caller/configuration analysis remains valid; source-only.

GD2823 scaling-divisor example correction (2026-10-24): the earlier `-750..750`, point-size-1 arithmetic example is invalid: `SetInstance()` computes `alt_point = 0` after its integer split (`a=d=0`), so `FT_Set_Pixel_Sizes(face, 0, 0)` returns through the checked error path before `RenderGlyph()` reaches the later divisor. Replaced it with custom bounds `0..1500`, UPEM 2048 and point size 1: `alt_point=1`, `a=1`, `d=0`, so the engine requests one pixel; the later divisor `(x_ppem * corrected_upem) / units_per_EM` is `(1*1500)/2048 == 0` in `glyph.c:285-290`. `GetWidthList()` calls `SetInstance()` first and uses the same integer formula after successful `FT_Load_Glyph()` (`kerning.c:44-47,96-107`). The UI accepts zero and positive bounds and passes these values through the custom bbox tag path; the module remains optional. This supersedes the earlier GD2823 example in this ledger. No font was rendered; source-only.

GD5908 display-info reader/removal and selected consumer recheck (2026-10-24): re-read `FindDisplayInfo()` and `NextDisplayInfo()` in full alongside the `GetDisplayInfoData()` handle path (`rom/graphics/finddisplayinfo.c:54-84`; `nextdisplayinfo.c:55-93`; `getdisplayinfodata.c:145-176`), and compared them with `display_Expunge()`'s exclusive-lock unlink, OOP disposal and `FreeVec(mdd)` (`graphics_display.c:221-275`). Traced the admitted removal path: `driver_ExpungeBootDisplay()` refuses only when `mdd->display` or `mdd->frontbm` is set, otherwise it calls `display_Expunge()` (`graphics_driver.c:262-283`); Nouveau's constructor uses the injected handover to find and expunge matching inactive firmware displays (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_hiddclass.c:420-440`). Followed the selected ScreenMode Preferences consumer: it gets IDs via `NextDisplayInfo()`, obtains one raw handle, then uses that same handle in separate name/display/dimension `GetDisplayInfoData()` calls (`workbench/prefs/screenmode/smselector.c:102-141`). Icon library duplication/layout full-body and failure-cleanup pass (GD9536 added; GD9535 caller evidence retained; 2026-10-24): read the complete `dupdiskobject.c` (311 physical lines; 208 `cloc 2.06` C lines) and `layouticon.c` (637 physical lines; 464 code lines), then traced `FreeDiskObject()`'s layout teardown, `GetIconTagList()` and Wanderer's AppIcon caller. `DupDiskObjectA()`'s ordinary allocation failures reach its `FreeDiskObject()` rollback; no separate duplication-body defect was established. In `LayoutIconA()`, bitmap/pen-map/chunky-buffer/mask allocation failures can occur after screen-specific state has been acquired or allocated, but error exits do not roll that partial state back and leave `ni_Screen` NULL. The mask branch uniquely returns before `FreeScreenDrawInfo()`; the other error exits free DrawInfo but only jump to the common return. `FreeDiskObject()` then calls `LayoutIconA(icon,NULL,NULL)`, which exits at the same-screen fast path and does not free the partial layout allocations; a retry with a screen dereferences the NULL saved screen for `ReleasePen()` if a partial image has a pen map. GD9536 now covers the complete missing-rollback family, with the mask-specific DrawInfo leak called out. Credited 672 full-body C lines. No allocation failure or icon operation was run; source-only.

Picture `PDTM_READPIXELARRAY` caller census and GD2849 scope confirmation (2026-10-24; no new finding): searched every checked-in `PDTM_READPIXELARRAY` reference and traced all 15 caller sites outside the Picture implementation. PNG, GIF, PNM, BMP, JPEG, WebP, MUI Dtpic, NBitmap, decorator, pointer preview, and the full-image datatype-cache paths request origin-zero full images or one full-width scanline. `workbench/libs/muimaster/datatypescache.c:936-945` is the only in-tree nonzero-left/partial-width request: the `.mim` renderer requests one state half at `Left=state*width`, `Width=width`, outputs ARGB, and allocates by the full sheet dimensions. Remaining uncertainty is external clients and uncommon format/source combinations; no pixel-array operation or image load was run. Source-only.

Volumelist `printSize()` capacity-narrowing pass (GD9604 added; 2026-10-24): read the complete helper and its volume-list callers (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/volumelist.c:20-36,180-216`) and reconciled the conditional `InfoData64` fields (`compiler/include/dos/dos.h:176-203`). Both used and free capacities are UQUAD before `printSize()`; after the GiB shift, conversion to `unsigned int` loses all bits above bit 31. Thus values at or above 2^62 bytes (4 EiB) wrap, with exactly 4 EiB formatted as `0G`, provided the block-count multiplication itself remains representable. Added GD9604 with DOS64-only and extreme-capacity conditions; practical volume availability was not established. No volume, formatting call, or display was run; source-only.

Volumelist DOS64 formatter/provider closure (GD9604 expanded; 2026-10-24): traced the optional NTFS `ACTION_INFO` path into `Volumelist__OM_NEW()`: NTFS `total_sectors` and `used_sectors` are UQUAD (`workbench/fs/ntfs/ntfs_fs.h:225-226`), startup loads the boot-sector `number_of_sectors` into `total_sectors` (`ntfs.c:1092`), and `FillDiskInfo()` returns that field as `InfoData.id_NumBlocks` (`disk.c:47-71`). The NTFS module is a standalone `workbench-fs-ntfs` target (`workbench/fs/ntfs/mmakefile.src:5-10`), while Volumelist is conditionally built in or external (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:323-329`). AmigaVideo GD5994 dummy interlace-list allocation and caller pass (confirmed; 2026-10-24): re-read `initvpicopper()` and both callers. `MakeViewPort()` sets `MaxCount` using a helper that returns at least 2,000 bytes and deliberately clears `CopSStart` for non-interlaced bitmaps. A later VBlank scroll reattachment or compositor stack rebuild can include that bitmap in the interlace list; the helper then allocates `MEMF_CHIP` storage, immediately calls `CopyMemQuick()` with it and derives list pointers without a NULL guard. `CopyMemQuick()` copies positive counts by dereferencing the destination. Confirmed GD5994; impact is limited to the allocation-failure and interlaced mixed-viewport condition, with the VBlank path running from interrupt context. No allocation failure, scroll, compositor rebuild or hardware update was run; source-only.


AmigaVideo GD5992 startup chip-allocation failure consequence trace (confirmed; 2026-10-24): calculated the requested block as 16 sprite bytes plus 184 copper bytes (46 UWORD pairs). On `AllocMem()` failure, `sprite_null` is NULL and `copper1` becomes integer address `0x10`; the `COPPEROUT` macro writes pairs through that address before the resulting pointers are stored in `GfxBase` and custom-chip registers and DMA is enabled. `initcustom()` is a `VOID` startup call and has no failure return/rollback. Kept GD5992 separate from GD5993: the former is direct null-derived CPU writes and invalid copper publication on the allocation failure itself; the latter is interrupt-handler lifetime after any later failed module initialization. No allocation failure or hardware access was run; the exact address-mapping effect remains target-specific; source-only.


AmigaVideo GD5991 VBlank reveal threshold caller recheck (confirmed and trigger narrowed; 2026-10-24): traced the bitmap position-change notification through `BitMapPositionChanged`/`setscroll` into the VBlank `gfx_vblank_doupdatescroll()` downward-move branch. Reconciled the conditions: `adjust` is assigned only for cross-interlace-mode cases, but a same-mode, higher-priority obscured bitmap can pass `toptmp < topvis`, be attached successfully, and reach `topvis = toptmp - adjust`; the indeterminate threshold can affect later hidden-screen decisions in the same loop. Narrowed the trigger to a successful same-mode reveal followed by at least one more candidate. No scroll or VBlank was run; source-only.

AmigaVideo GD5990 combined-signal and teardown recheck (confirmed; 2026-10-24): verified `DisplayServiceTask()`'s wait mask and exact-value switch against Exec `Wait()`'s returned-and-cleared mask.
