GD5908 runtime display-removal caller recheck (2026-10-24): verified the monitor Wrapper is a maintained dynamic registration path, not only a boot-time driver path. Its CLI accepts `CLASS=HIDD/A,LIBRARY=LIB`; Workbench launch reads those fields from icon tooltypes; when the class is absent it opens the requested library, finds the class and calls `AddDisplayDriverA()` (`workbench/devs/monitors/wrapper/wrapper.c:35-100`). `graphics_driver.c` supplies the temporary `DDRVA_Handover` to the HIDD constructor, and Nouveau's constructor calls `HIDDNouveauReleaseBootDisplays()` when that tag is present (`:340-352`; `workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_hiddclass.c:421-440`). Thus on-demand Nouveau registration through Wrapper can remove an inactive boot display while ScreenMode Preferences is querying mode handles, supporting the conditional race already recorded as GD5908. Wrapper is an explicitly buildable target with an optional aggregate edge; this does not establish that every default image ships it. No wrapper, mode query or registration was run; source-only.


## Optional Monitor Editor Preferences target

`workbench/prefs/MonEd/mmakefile.src` selects one C translation unit, `moned.c`, for the explicitly buildable `workbench-prefs-moned` target; its edge from the Preferences aggregate is commented out. `cloc 2.06` counts 764 C code lines in the body. GD5910 full-detail restoration and range-proof recheck (2026-10-24): matched the index-only GD5910 summary to the current selected bodies. `SetRGB32()` first calls the bounded `SetRGB32CM()` but then unconditionally invokes `internal_SetRGB32Colors()`; that helper calls HIDD `SetColors` and separately indexes the raw bitmap pixeltable using the original ULONG `first + i` without a bound (`rom/graphics/setrgb32.c:14-53,116-124`; `setrgb32cm.c:61-76`). For displayable HIDD bitmaps, `AllocBitMap()` allocates exactly `AROS_PALETTE_SIZE` (256) pixel entries or shares that same table with a friend bitmap (`allocbitmap.c:417-426`; `gfxfuncsupport.h:109-110`). A request for index 256 therefore passes the ColorMap no-op guard but reaches pixeltable entry 256. `LoadRGB32()`'s normal and allocation-fallback paths both reach the same unchecked setter (`loadrgb32.c:74-103`). Restored GD5910 as a confirmed source-level out-of-bounds write and replaced the report's index-only detail-gap stub. No palette call, bitmap, allocation failure or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

WiFi Preferences `WaitPort()` reply-consumer recheck (2026-10-24; GD6150 retained, no new finding): traced all three waits in `workbench/prefs/wifi/main.c` through `Send()`, `HandleReply()`, `WifiWorker()` and the worker's `ReplyMsg()` path (`main.c:84-98,304-360,394-400,642-664`; `worker.c:1334-1388`). `Send()` refuses a second command while `busy`, and the only normal reply-port consumer is the main task: startup synchronously consumes the device-list reply; the GUI loop drains replies through `HandleReply()`; cleanup drains any in-flight reply before sending and consuming the quit reply. No second `GetMsg()`/`WaitPort()` consumer for this reply port was found, so the generic WaitPort competing-consumer concern does not add a WiFi-specific race. The separately tracked GD6150 remains: cleanup disposes the MUI application before draining an outstanding command reply, while `HandleReply()` still updates MUI objects. No worker request or close interleaving was run; source-only.

Sound datatype `WaitPort()` startup/teardown caller recheck (2026-10-24; no new finding): traced the two `WaitPort(replyport)` sites in `Sound_NEW()` and `Sound_DISPOSE()` through both selected player implementations (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:866-892,1427-1445,PlayerProc:2927-2945,PlayerProcAHI:3727-3742`). Each handshake creates a private reply port, submits exactly one message to the child process port, waits for the child to `ReplyMsg()` that same message, and immediately dequeues it with `GetMsg()` before deleting the private port. The child receives the init message before later commands on its process port, and the player-port creation failure replies before exiting; the parent treats the NULL return data as failed startup and does not publish `PlayerPort`. The exit path replies before deleting the worker's own port and returning. No second consumer or outstanding reply on either private port was established. This closes only the WaitPort handshake caller slice; existing Sound findings and broader audio/AHI contracts remain tracked separately. The `workbench-datatypes-sound` manifest selects `dispatch.c` and `sound_init.c`, but its Workbench aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/mmakefile.src:4-13`). No player process or audio operation was run; source-only.

GD9612 shutdown-reply queue lifetime follow-up (2026-10-24; no separate finding): rechecked the static `msg` and `replyPort` lifecycle in all four clipboard workers. `ShutdownClipboardServer()` waits for the worker's reply but does not remove the reply message; the message node and port are static module data, and `mn_Node.ln_Name` retains the address of the shutdown caller's stack `ServerData`. No path reads that parameter after the shutdown case replies. If a later startup occurs, it reinitializes `replyPort.mp_MsgList` with `NewList()` before reusing the static message, detaching the stale queue entry; normal worker requests already remove their reply before returning. Thus the queued message and stale stack address do not establish an independent defect. The worker-tail/module-unload window remains GD9612. Source-only.

Screen-RastPort scroll upper-bound signedness follow-up (GD9613 added; 2026-10-24): rechecked both public scroll bodies and the shared `MoveRaster()`/`BltBitMap()` path (`scrollraster.c:105-108`; `scrollrasterbf.c:103-107`; `gfxfuncsupport.c:838-852`; `bltbitmap.c:142-153,244-255`). The reviewed maintained console/datatype examples use nonnegative bounds; no selected in-tree trigger was found. Added GD9613 for public callers, with the in-tree trigger gap stated. Raster scrolling overlap-copy failure pass (GD9614 expanded; 2026-10-24): rechecked both `MoveRaster()` branches against generic software `BltBitMap()` and both public scroll callers (`gfxfuncsupport.c:838-853,951-1031`; `bltbitmap.c:299-310`; `scrollraster.c:127-170`; `scrollrasterbf.c:124-165`). `BltBitMap()` destination-low-edge bounds pass (GD9615 added; 2026-10-24): re-read the full generic implementation and traced destination clipping through source clipping, extent checks, the row loop and `copyonepixel()` (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:244-318,341-363`). Negative source coordinates are corrected by advancing destination coordinates, but negative destination coordinates are not clipped or rejected. With `xDest=-1,xSize=2`, the size checks pass; unsigned pixel-index arithmetic feeds a huge x offset to the destination plane. Negative `yDest` similarly reaches row-pointer arithmetic without a low-edge check. Added GD9615 for the generic software backend; the HIDD branch has the same missing pre-dispatch low-edge clip, but backend response is left open. Checked-in direct `BltBitMap()` call expressions were searched; no maintained negative-destination call was established, so the confirmed trigger is public/external callers. Full-body credit for `bltbitmap.c` already exists; no new line credit. No bitmap operation was run; source-only.

GD9615 scroll-path caller follow-up (expanded existing finding; 2026-10-24): connected the negative-screen-rectangle case from GD9613 through both public no-Layer scroll paths to `MoveRaster()` and the generic software `BltBitMap()` path. `ScrollRaster()` changes a negative upper bound to the bitmap's far edge after the signed-to-unsigned comparison (`scrollraster.c:97-109`), then invokes `MoveRaster()` (`:127-128`); `ScrollRasterBF()` repeats the same clamp and call (`scrollrasterbf.c:95-108,124-125`). The intersection/translation in `MoveRaster()` can pass a negative destination coordinate (`gfxfuncsupport.c:838-852`). `BltBitMap()` advances destination coordinates only for a negative source, not for a negative destination, and its generic pixel loop feeds that negative destination into unsigned plane indexing (`bltbitmap.c:244-318,341-363`). Thus the reviewed public scroll APIs supply an in-tree call chain to GD9615 when the caller gives the GD9613 off-screen interval and the selected bitmap is generic planar software. This is distinct from a direct maintained `BltBitMap()` caller with negative coordinates, which was not found. HIDD backend effects and runtime outcome remain unverified; no scroll or blit was run.


GD9613/GD9615 interaction correction (2026-10-24): rechecked the negative screen-scroll example after adding GD9615. The signed-to-unsigned upper-bound comparison still expands the off-screen interval and the public scroll body still invokes far-edge fill/erase. However, `MoveRaster()` passes a negative destination to `BltBitMap()` after clipping a negative source; therefore the earlier GD9613 claim that this example predictably moves visible pixels is withdrawn. The generic software backend instead reaches GD9615's unchecked negative destination indexing; HIDD/backend handling remains unverified. GD9613 is retained for the independently proven range expansion and far-edge fill/erase, with blit consequence qualified.


`AllocBitMap()` HIDD header-only tag path (GD9616 added; 2026-10-24): followed `BMATags_NoMemory` from public definition and function documentation through extended-tag parsing and HIDD construction (`compiler/include/graphics/gfx.h:95-104`; `rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:133-135,196-217,242-246,331-349,381-390,454-474`). `BltBitMap()` HIDD result-count contract recheck (GD9617 retained; 2026-10-24): re-read the function's `RESULT` documentation (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:89-90`), its generic per-plane count (`:274-289`), and the HIDD implementation. No blit or HIDD acquisition failure was induced; source-only.

PaletteExtra signed-index boundary and pen-list caller pass (GD9620 added; 2026-10-24): read the full `rom/graphics/attachpalextra.c` body (54 `cloc 2.06` C lines), reconciled `ColorMap.Count`/`GetColorMap()` allocation widths and the public AttachPalExtra contract, then traced `pe_FirstFree` and `pe_FirstShared` through the selected `ObtainPen()` and `ReleasePen()` list walks. `ColorMap.Count` and list heads are `UWORD`, but `PalExtra_AllocList_Type` is signed `WORD`; with a 32,769-entry ColorMap and bitmap depth >=16, index 32,768 is valid in the allocated arrays but casts to -32,768 when a list walk initializes its index, so the next list access is before the allocation. Added GD9620, scoped to the public API trigger; no checked-in high-entry ColorMap caller was found and OpenScreen caps its normal palette at 256. Confirmed `GetColorMap(0)` fails its zero-byte allocations and therefore does not reach the sharable-count underflow initially suspected. This closes only AttachPalExtra's local body and pen-list interaction slice; other palette callers/configurations and public high-entry clients remain open. No ColorMap or pen operation was performed; source-only.

`ObtainBestPenA()` precision arithmetic and high-entry palette recheck (GD9621 added and trigger reconciled with GD9620; 2026-10-24): re-read all 63 `cloc 2.06` C code lines of the already body-credited `rom/graphics/obtainbestpena.c`, verified `color_distance()`'s 8-bit RGB squared-difference range and the fixed-width `ULONG`, and searched checked-in `OBP_Precision` callers. Replaced the earlier 65,535-entry illustration, whose setup was not independent of GD9620's signed-list boundary, with a reachable 32,769-entry sequence: reserve initial head 32,768 exclusively; then share pen 32,767 as black, leaving 32,767 free. Requesting RGB (105,244,246) under documented `PRECISION_GUI` produces distance 131,077; multiplication by `pe_NFree` is 4,295,000,059 and wraps to 32,763, below the 33,554,432 threshold. `ObtainBestPenA()` therefore increments the distant pen's shared count instead of calling `ObtainPen()` for a free one. In-tree GUI-precision callers were found, but not this large-colormap state, so the trigger remains public/external in practice. The nested semaphore path remains valid because the selected semaphore implementation supports same-task nesting. No palette was created or pen requested; source-only.

`FindColor()` negative-limit and unattached-map caller pass (GD9622 added and qualified; 2026-10-24): re-read the full `findcolor.c` loop and reconciled its signed `LONG maxpen` with unsigned `ULONG index`. For `maxpen=-1` and `cm->PalExtra==NULL`, the special-case does not normalize the limit; `maxpen >= cm->Count` is false, then the loop compares every index against converted `ULONG_MAX` and reads beyond the table after `Count`. Enumerated the checked-in direct call sites: ColorWheel uses the OpenScreen screen ColorMap, while MUI fallback paths use `MUI_RenderInfo.mri_Colormap`; maintained rendering setup obtains screen maps with PaletteExtra attached. The public documentation does not specify a negative maximum, so this is retained only as a low-to-medium-confidence candidate for callers relying on the implementation's -1 convention with unattached maps, or for missing validation of a negative limit. The earlier no-maintained-invalid-caller observation stands. No color search was run; source-only.

GD5908 `OpenScreen()` and display-ID bitmap caller follow-up (2026-10-24; existing finding strengthened, no new ID): traced Intuition screen creation from `FindDisplayInfo(modeid)` through separate dimension and display/monitor queries (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1104-1109`), then through its `BMATags_DisplayID` bitmap request (`:1225-1238`). `AllocBitMap()` saves `dh->drv` and `dh->id` from the unpinned result of `FindDisplayInfo()` (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:219-226`) and later passes `drv->display_obj` to `HIDD_Display_CreateObject()` (`:341-348`). Compared both uses with the unlocked lookup/query functions and the exclusive-lock removal path, which disposes the display object and frees the driver record (`rom/graphics/finddisplayinfo.c:54-84`; `getdisplayinfodata.c:140-176`; `graphics_display.c:218-275`). The selected on-demand Monitor Wrapper path reaches `AddDisplayDriverA()` and boot-display handover (`workbench/devs/monitors/wrapper/wrapper.c:60-100`; `rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:298-323,350-414`). If the queried mode belongs to the inactive boot display being removed, handover can overlap screen setup before bitmap construction completes. This extends GD5908 from display-info queries to a selected bitmap-construction path; no runtime interleaving is claimed. Rechecked PSI list creation: `DispIDlist_New()` enumerates IDs and `MUIM_List_InsertSingle()` invokes the class construct hook; that hook holds one display handle for three queries (`displayidlist_class.c:57-84,116-118`; selected MUI implementation `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/list.c:2983-3018,3070-3079`). The PSI class body was previously read and credited. The full `openscreen.c` body was previously read and credited; no additional body lines are added here. IntelGMA registration-failure handover trigger qualification (GD5229 retained, 2026-10-24): traced `G45_LoadState()` before `AddDisplayDriverA()` against the graphics registration return paths and IntelGMA `Root.New`. Confirmed `DD_NO_MEM` and `DD_ID_EXISTS` return before driver setup, while `DD_DRIVER_ERROR` follows failed `HW_AddDriver()`; all occur after the initial mode write. Although generic graphics registration can return `DD_IN_USE` when a driver refuses boot-display handover, IntelGMA does not consume `DDRVA_Handover` in its constructor; only the searched Nouveau class consumes this tag. Removed `DD_IN_USE` as an established IntelGMA trigger and qualified the candidate to pre-setup and class-instantiation failures. No registration failure, mode change or boot-display handover was run; source-only.

IntelGMA initial-mode allocation failure caller recheck (GD9602 retained; 2026-10-24): re-read the exact allocation fields and write paths. `initialState` is a `GMAState_t *`, and `G45_LoadState()` reads `state->htotal` before any guard, so its allocation failure reaches a definite NULL dereference independently of `G45_InitMode()` finding a PLL solution. `initialBitMap` is `intptr_t`; `AllocBitmapArea()` returns -1 on failure; `Card.Framebuffer` is a `char *`; the clear loop forms `initialBitMap + Framebuffer`, making the first 32-bit store start at `Framebuffer - 1`. Qualified the result to a likely first-store fault at the mapping edge or cross-boundary write if the preceding address is mapped, rather than claiming a general arbitrary framebuffer overwrite. The report cites these types and lines. The separate missing initial-state allocation and bitmap allocation remain in one finding because both are unchecked startup allocations on the same mode setup path; no allocation failure or hardware write was induced. Source-only.

IntelGMA caller added to graphics registration false-success finding (GD5906 expanded; 2026-10-24): traced `INTELG45::Root::New()` display allocation failure through the compositor constructor and graphics HIDD getter. A NULL display makes the compositor constructor dispose and return NULL; IntelGMA ignores that result and still returns its graphics HIDD, whose `DisplayDefault` getter returns `sd->display` (NULL). `driver_Setup()` logs/skips registration but reaches its unconditional TRUE return, so `AddDisplayDriverA()` reports `DD_OK`; G45 initialization then succeeds on the already assigned PCI pointer and startup makes the class resident. Added this concrete selected IntelGMA path to existing GD5906 alongside LinuxFB; no duplicate ID was added. No object allocation failure or registration was induced; source-only.

Display callback removal argument recheck (GD5907 detailed and qualified; 2026-10-24): distinguished the callback return object from registered userdata. `display_Enable()` passes the global registered userdata on add and stores the return object in that display node. `display_Expunge()` correctly passes the stored return object as callback argument 1, but also passes it as argument 3 instead of the global registered userdata required by the `SetDisplayDriverCallback()` contract. The sole in-tree callback is Intuition `DisplayDriverNotify()`, whose removal branch ignores argument 3 and disposes argument 1; therefore no current in-tree failure is established. Replaced the placeholder with a conditional private-API contract finding, updated the master index wording, and retained high confidence in the source mismatch with impact limited to clients consuming userdata during removal. No callback or display removal was run; source-only.

Font-extension unlinked-node failure recheck (GD5911 reconstructed; 2026-10-24): re-read `ExtendFont()`, hash-node allocation/insertion/deletion and `StripFont()` cleanup. Confirmed a new node from `tfe_hashnode_create()` remains unlinked until the extension, cloned tags and required color-font buffer all succeed; the three downstream failure paths free extension resources but not the new node. `StripFont()` looks up only linked nodes, so it cannot reclaim this allocation; retrying the same font repeats the new-node allocation. Traced selected diskfont conversion failure and `OpenFont()` resident-font matching behavior; those callers propagate extension failure, with a retained font match still possible in `OpenFont()`. Expanded GD5911 from its placeholder with exact failure edges and leak scope. Full-body credits already existed; no new line credit. No allocation failure or font operation was induced; source-only.

Region clipping head/chunk cleanup recheck (GD5912 reconstructed; 2026-10-24): traced `AndRectRegion()` unlink and head publication against RegionRectangle slot counters and `_DisposeRegionRectangleList()`. If a clipped-out first entry is followed by a retained entry in the same chunk, the retained entry becomes `RegionRectangle` with nonzero `Counter`; disposal then skips the chunk containing that start and frees only later chunks. `ClearRegion()`/`DisposeRegion()` use this list cleanup, and maintained `ScrollRegion()` applies `AndRectRegion()` to `cutRegion` before disposing it. Added the specific list-shape trigger and cleanup consequence; finding remains conditional on a region with the required multi-rectangle chunk layout. No region was built or clipped; source-only.

Cross-LayerInfo ClipBlit deadlock recheck (GD5913 reconstructed; 2026-10-24): re-read the full `ClipBlit()` lock/unlock sequence and `LockLayerRom()` wrapper. Confirmed the common `LayerInfo` ordering semaphore is taken only when both distinct layers share the exact same `LayerInfo`; distinct LayerInfo pointers skip it. Each call then blocks on source followed by destination and releases after the complete internal blit, establishing the opposite-direction two-task wait cycle for different screens. Rechecked the maintained direct ClipBlit call-site census: it does not establish an opposing cross-screen pair, so the report scopes this to concurrent public API clients rather than asserting a current in-tree trigger. No lock contention or blit was run; source-only.

TextFit extent-versus-numeric limit recheck (GD5914 reconstructed; 2026-10-24): reread the full selected implementation against its function contract. The header text specifies numeric bit width/height only when `constrainingExtent` is NULL, but the implementation always gates on `constrainingBitHeight >= tf_YSize` before inspecting extent and always applies `constrainingBitWidth` in its character loop. A sufficient non-NULL extent can therefore still yield zero or a truncated fit when numeric fields are smaller. Rechecked the direct in-tree call inventory: direct calls use NULL for `constrainingExtent`; `TextFitNew()` forwards its incoming extent and is the maintained wrapper surface, but this scan did not establish a non-NULL maintained call. Replaced GD5914 placeholder with the contract defect, concrete caller condition, and explicit no-in-tree-trigger qualification. No body or line credit added; no fit/render operation was run. Source-only.

BltClear odd-count behavior and API contract recheck (GD5915 reconstructed and qualified; 2026-10-24): compared generic and selected m68k-amiga implementations. Generic writes full ULONGs and then an optional UWORD, leaving a 1-byte tail; m68k-amiga converts to `bytecount >> 1` words and its blitter loop leaves any odd byte. The public flags description says bit 1 selects row mode, while the following bytecount paragraph reverses that mode description; documented even-byte requirement therefore makes the odd-count contract ambiguous. Reconciled all checked-in direct callers: bitmap setup uses even `RASSIZE()` row bytes, Flood uses `WIDTH_TO_BYTES()` rounded to an even byte stride, and the benchmark passes 32,000. Kept GD5915 scoped to odd counts in the implementation direct-count mode with no maintained in-tree trigger; confidence is high for behavior and medium for the public contract interpretation. No clear was run; source-only.

Color-font conversion allocation wrap and output-stride recheck (GD5916 reconstructed; 2026-10-24): recomputed the 32-bit `ULONG` product for `tf_Modulo=16385`, `tf_YSize=32767`: width 131,080, full product 4,295,098,360, allocated size after wrap 131,064. Traced that width through `InitBitMap(UWORD width)` to 8 pixels and `ReadPixelArray8(WORD xstop)` to xstop 7; its output modulo is 16 and the row callback writes 8 bytes per row. The final row writes through byte 524,263, beyond the wrapped allocation. Verified `ExtendFont()` reaches this helper only for real non-antialiased color fonts, and recorded the required roughly 512 MiB of source plane data per selected plane as a major practical reachability limitation; no maintained oversized font caller was found. Replaced GD5916 placeholder with exact arithmetic, type narrows, trigger and low-medium reachability caveat. No font, buffer or pixel transfer was created; source-only.

WeighTAMatch size narrowing and score-penalty recheck (GD5926-GD5927 detailed; 2026-10-24): reread the matcher and reconciled `TextAttr.ta_YSize` as UWORD with its signed WORD casts, size penalty and returned WORD. Added exact cases for 65535-vs-0 collapsing to distance one and 32767-vs-32768 expanding to 65535. Subtracting it raises the score; with an extra target style bit that clears bit 11, 30,719 becomes 30,847. Qualified the positive-score consequence to target narrowing behavior, the size range and an existing style penalty; without the latter, the final value may wrap negative. Traced the score into OpenFont and diskfont ranking comparisons. No font search was run; source-only.


User copper-list reinitialization and growth-failure recheck (GD5928-GD5929 detailed; 2026-10-24): reread `UCopperListInit()`, `CBump()`, `CMove()`/`CWait()` and both public macro variants. Confirmed reinit sets the first segment's Count to MaxCount, rewinds only its CopPtr, and leaves `ucl->CopList` and all extension segments' cursors/counts untouched. From the first segment, the next bump increments past capacity and misses the equality transition; from a previous extension segment, emission continues there. Separately traced both extension allocations in CBump: failure leaves Count at capacity and the current cursor on its last instruction; a later macro overwrites that instruction, then moves past the allocation without an error signal. Buffer-allocation failure additionally leaves an empty extension linked, but ordinary continuation advances the active Count past the equality check and does not select that node; FreeCopList safely traverses it and `FreeMem(NULL, 0)` is a no-op. Corrected GD5929 to remove the unsupported NULL-cursor retry consequence. No maintained C macro caller was found; both findings are scoped to external/public clients. Updated GD5928 summary in master index. No list or allocation failure was run; source-only.

The `IconEntry.ie_Flags` offset extends beyond the embedded `struct List`, so the write lands in adjacent `IconList_DATA` storage, with exact field dependent on ABI. Radeon I²C allocation and EDID transfer-result caller recheck (GD5934-GD5935 detailed; 2026-10-24): traced `RADEONDisplayDDCConnected()` through the selected I²C helper and generic HIDD. A NULL `OOP_NewObject()` result is passed to `HIDD_I2C_ProbeAddress()`; the helper's `OOP_DoMethod` macro dereferences the object's class. Separately, the local EDID array is uninitialized, `Hidd_I2CDevice::WriteRead` returns the generic `I2C_WriteRead()` BOOL, and Radeon ignores that return before reading `edid[0x14]`; generic address/byte failures return FALSE, including paths that leave the target byte unwritten. GD5934-GD5935 I²C failure-boundary refinement (2026-10-25): re-read generic `WriteRead()` and `GetByte()` failure exits (`workbench/hidds/i2c/i2cclass.c:286-327,330-369`) against the Radeon caller (`workbench/hidds/radeon/radeon_driver.c:1249-1296`). The uninitialized-byte condition is specifically a transfer that fails before the read reaches EDID offset `0x14`; if failure occurs while reading that byte, it may be only partially assembled, and if it occurs later the classification byte may already be valid although the overall operation failed. Radeon ignores the result in all three cases and always classifies from `edid[0x14]`. `RADEONQueryConnectedMonitors()` calls this routine during `RADEONInit()` (`radeon_driver.c:2422-2424`), and its discovered monitor result feeds primary/secondary monitor selection (`:1465-1515`); this pass found no separate maintained hotplug/re-detection caller. GD9625 generated relative-library cleanup qualification (2026-10-24): compared `graphics.conf`'s `rellib utility`/`rellib oop` entries with `_set_libinit()` rollback. The generated code closes declared relative-library references on INITLIB failure, but `driver_init()`'s direct `OpenLibrary("gfx.hidd")` is not declared there and has no matching close. `OOP_ObtainAttrBase()` increments the shared IID bucket reference count, and its documented paired `OOP_ReleaseAttrBase()` is not called by this failed-init path. `oop.conf` is `noexpunge`, so closing the generated OOP rellib does not destroy the OOP library's IID table or undo these separately counted acquisitions. Thus the direct gfx.hidd open and attrbase references survive their respective cleanup paths. No body-line credit.

GD9626 registered HIDD driver partial-cleanup trace (added 2026-10-24; supersedes the prior GD9625 note that called this node attached to an orphaned root): followed `HW_AddDriver()` into the driver's-list insertion and compared its contract/removal path against `driver_init()`'s direct `OOP_DisposeObject()` cleanup. GD9626 gfx.hidd expunge-path extension (2026-10-24): re-read `GFX_ClassFree()` and generated HIDD class expunge ordering. The parser creates the top-level `GFXHW` class in `cfg->classlist` for this `modtype=hidd` module (`tools/genmodule/config.c:464-489`); `writeoopinit()` therefore generates a shutdown which calls `OOP_RemoveClass()` and `OOP_DisposeObject()` (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:146-165`; `tools/genmodule/oopsupport.c:185-212`). The expunge sequence calls the module `EXPUNGELIB` hooks and then `_set_libexpunge()`/class shutdown (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1557-1573`; `compiler/autoinit/functions.c:75-84`). `GFX_ClassFree()` returns success without removing the `hw.gfx` singleton from `CLID_HW_Root`; the parent root is deliberately persistent and does not dispose it (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_init.c:319-320,334-351`; `gfx_hwclass.c:38-41`; `rom/hidds/hidd/initcode.c:45-53`). The only checked-in direct `OpenLibrary("gfx.hidd")` caller is graphics.library, which retains its reference; no selected in-tree last-close trigger was found. Expanded GD9626 with this qualified direct-open/close case, separate from the selected graphics.library failed-init stale child node. No library close/expunge or hardware enumeration was run; no body-line credit.

GD5924 selected Headless framebuffer reachability correction (2026-10-24): the prior mode-order census missed the RISC-V OpenSBI Headless HIDD. Reconciled the boot target and monitor loader with its default mode tags, generic mode enumerator order, inherited framebuffer type and graphics.library setup (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:51`; `rom/hidds/gfx/headless/mmakefile.src:4-24`; `headlessgfx_hiddclass.c:136-145,187-218,254-277`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_dmenumclass.c:175-256`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:756-770,861-870`; `rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:149-170,413-429`). Default Headless registration exposes 8/16/24-bit formats in that order at one resolution and inherits Direct framebuffer mode; `get_best_resolution_and_depth()` retains the 8-bit entry on equal areas while updating only its depth threshold, so default framebuffer creation selects 8-bit despite available 24-bit. Updated GD5924 from public-HIDD-only qualification to this concrete selected target. P96 and AmigaVideo lower-first format tables were checked but report no framebuffer; they do not reach the chooser. Generic `BltBitMap()` vertical-overlap and masked-copy candidate reconciliation (GD9627 added; GD4129 retained, duplicate GD6242 withdrawn; 2026-10-24): re-read the generic software row-copy loop and its public contract (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:55-95,291-319`). The same-bitmap API is documented, but the loop advances top-to-bottom and its temporary-row test only detects same-iteration scanline address overlap; for a vertical downward move, each corresponding source/destination scanline is adjacent and the test misses that later destination writes overwrite rows still needed as source. The graphics index now has 1,737 active links, with eight withdrawn headings. No bitmap or scroll was run; source-only.




Generic masked-blit unsupported draw-mode and public caller pass (GD4130 detailed; 2026-10-24): reread `copyboxmasked_impl()` from draw-mode save through return and traced the class wrapper and graphics.library caller (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1488-1492,1516-1590,1600-1654`; `rom/graphics/bltmaskbitmaprastport.c:24-38,127-141`). The implementation temporarily forces Copy for `PutImage`, supports only Or, Copy and AndInverted, and for other modes logs then writes the unmodified destination buffer with Copy before returning TRUE. The public minterm-to-GC conversion maps minterm zero to Clear (`gfxfuncsupport.h:84-89`; `hidds/gfx/include/gfx.h:369-385`), so a masked clear through the generic fallback is a concrete no-op despite the HIDD success result. The public library vector is void; no checked-in caller with a minterm outside those three modes was found, so the practical maintained-client trigger is not asserted. This remains a generic fallback/public API candidate; accelerated driver overrides are not covered. No copy was run; source-only.


`AreaEnd()` outline-mask geometry, narrowing, and caller recheck (GD4133 detailed; 2026-10-24): re-read `areaoutlinepolygonmask()` and the TmpRas allocation calculation in source order (`rom/graphics/areafill.c:189-220`; `rom/graphics/areaend.c:130-140`), then checked public `AreaDraw()` coordinate storage (`areadraw.c:63-75`). Refined the trigger to distinguish C semantics: with `dx=16384, dy=0`, `error << 1` promotes to `int` and 32768 is representable, but assigning it to signed `WORD twice` is out of range and implementation-defined; the later compound assignment to `WORD error` also narrows. On the usual two's-complement truncation, a horizontal edge from `(0,0)` to `(16384,0)` changes the next y step to -1; the routine then computes `ry=(UWORD)(y-bounds->MinY)` and indexes past the bounds-sized mask. This excludes an unsupported claim of signed-shift UB and scopes the memory-write consequence to the stated conversion. Repository `AreaDraw()` caller census found only small clock/colorwheel/drawlist/graph geometry and debug tests; none establishes this wide-edge trigger. The public signed-WORD interface remains the input surface. No polygon, compiler build, or TmpRas access was run; source-only.


`AreaEnd()` undersized-TmpRas error-exit and caller pass (GD5759 detailed; 2026-10-24): rechecked the function from state capture through all returns (`rom/graphics/areaend.c:71-85,101-140,259-281`). For a polygon, the MOVE record calls `Move()` before the polygon-mask size check; an undersized TmpRas returns -1 without restoring `cp_x/cp_y`, whereas normal completion and the invalid-record error restore both. The Area records are also not reset on this capacity return, consistent with retry. The ellipse branch's capacity check does not itself move the cursor. Repository `AreaEnd()` caller census includes ColorWheel, Reaction DrawList, Zune clock/graph, and graphics debug code; checked call sites ignore the result, and none established a cursor-dependent follow-up after an undersized-mask error. Kept the finding as a public RastPort state-restoration defect and limited in-tree impact claims accordingly. No error was induced; source-only.

GD4160 m68k GetExtSprite varargs-allocation claim recheck (2026-10-24): read `GetExtSprite()` and `GetExtSpriteA()` in full and checked `utility/tagitem.h` against `arch/m68k-all/include/aros/cpu.h`. m68k defines `AROS_SLOWSTACKFORMAT` but not `AROS_SLOWSTACKTAGS`; therefore the selected wrapper uses `&(tag1)` and performs no `GetTagsFromStack()` allocation. IntelGMA compositor viewport-stack allocation caller recheck (GD4197 detailed, 2026-10-24): reread `Compositor__Hidd_Compositor__BitMapStackChanged()` and its selected `INTELG45::ShowViewPorts()` caller (`intelgma_compositorclass.c:450-497`; `intelgma_hiddclass.c:909-919`). GD4200 32-bit plain interleaved raster-wrap arithmetic recheck (2026-10-24): traced the non-HIDD `AllocBitMap()` branch into `AllocRaster()` and the `RASSIZE()` macro (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:195-240,497-513`; `allocraster.c:43-57`; `compiler/include/graphics/gfx.h:43`). Worked the 32-bit case `sizex=262145`, `sizey=65535`, `depth=2`: combined width 524290 gives 65538-byte aligned row stride and `RASSIZE` wraps at 2^32 to 65534 bytes; the bitmap records a 32770-byte BytesPerRow and 65535 rows, while the second plane is placed 2,147,581,950 bytes after the base. Confirmed no overflow check or dimension-range rejection in the plain path. Kept this separate from GD1731's small-width per-row padding under-allocation. No maintained large-dimension plain interleaved caller was found; no bitmap or raster operation was run. Source-only.


GD4200 public raster-consumer reachability follow-up (2026-10-24): traced a returned plain two-plane bitmap into the non-HIDD `BltBitMap()` branch (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:240-315`). Its clipping uses the bitmap's stored dimensions, then its per-plane loop uses `Planes[plane]` and `BytesPerRow` without validating allocation spans. For GD4200's geometry, a one-pixel copy with plane mask selecting plane 1 addresses the plane pointer about 2 GiB past the small wrapped allocation. This establishes an ordinary public consumer for the invalid layout; no bitmap, blit, or allocation was performed. Source-only.

Intuition `ScreenPosition()` LONG-to-WORD clipping recheck (GD9391 detailed, 2026-10-24): checked the public parameter types and clipping contract against `compiler/include/graphics/view.h`, `screenposition.c`, `ScrollVPort()`, the generic bitmap setter, and native VGAGfx setter. The public LONG value is stored into signed-WORD viewport offsets before `ScrollVPort()` widens it to `IPTR` and calls the HIDD, so both selected setters receive the already-converted `WORD` value and only then apply their bounds; the exact out-of-range conversion is target/compiler-dependent, so the report no longer asserts universal wraparound. Rechecked `ScreenPosition()`/`MoveScreen()` in-tree callers: ordinary relative deltas are used and no extreme-value caller was established. Expanded GD9391's consequence and scope; no new body-line credit beyond the existing full-body entries. No screen movement or display operation was run. Source-only.


GD77 maintained icon-resize caller follow-up (2026-10-24): traced selected `LayoutIconA()` through its caller `GetIconTagList()`. The color-image scaling branch allocates the replacement with `BMF_CLEAR`, calls the void `BitMapScale()`, then frees and replaces the previous bitmap without observing scaler failure (`workbench/libs/icon/layouticon.c:82,392-454`; `geticontaglist.c:345-361`; `workbench/libs/icon/mmakefile.src:37`). The `LayoutIconA()` return remains success on this path. This makes a generic-HIDD scratch-allocation failure an observable blank resized icon with the prior bitmap discarded. Expanded GD77's caller consequence; no new root-cause ID or source-body credit. Caller inventory also covered the in-tree `BitMapScale()` call sites in hyperlayers, demos, graphics, printer, Wanderer, icon and cgfx; this does not close broader caller/platform review. GD77 sprite-generation caller follow-up (2026-10-24): traced `AllocSpriteDataA()`'s selected resize path and Intuition pointer construction. `AllocSpriteDataA()` allocates its output `AllocBitMap()` with `BMF_CLEAR`, invokes `BitMapScale()` and then publishes a non-null `ExtSprite` without checking scaler status (`rom/graphics/allocspritedataa.c:243-271`). `pointerclass.c` calls it and consumes the returned sprite bitmap (`rom/intuition/pointerclass.c:103-140`). A generic-HIDD scratch-allocation failure can therefore publish blank pointer image data as a successful sprite. Added this as a second maintained caller consequence of GD77; no new root cause or body credit. No pointer construction or scale was run; source-only.


GD77 printer graphics caller follow-up (2026-10-24): traced the selected printer scaling path after successful `PRS_INIT` (`workbench/devs/printer/gfx.c:544-545,601-640,668-671`). It allocates the destination with flags 0 (so `BMF_CLEAR` is not requested; `rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:76,193`), calls the void `BitMapScale()`, then reads every output row with `ReadPixelArray()` and transfers it. A generic-HIDD scratch-allocation failure leaves that bitmap unwritten, yet the path does not turn it into a printer error and retains the `PRS_INIT` result. Expanded GD77 with this conditional printed-output consequence; no new root-cause ID or source-body credit. No print, scale, or allocation failure was run; source-only.


GD77 `ScalePixelArray()` direct-HIDD caller pass (2026-10-24): traced the selected `cgfx` path from temporary HIDD bitmap allocation through `HIDD_BM_BitMapScale()`, `DoRenderFunc()` and `RenderHook` (`workbench/libs/cgfx/scalepixelarray.c:151-205`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:88-100,119-129`). The scaler returns void; the caller copies the temporary destination to the RastPort and reports the renderer's pixel count without a scaling-success signal. On generic scratch-allocation failure, it therefore copies whatever contents the temporary HIDD bitmap has after the no-write return; initialization is class-specific and remains unverified. Expanded GD77's caller map with this return-status gap, without claiming deterministic pixel contents or adding a new root cause. No scaling or render operation was run; source-only.


Printer source-hook result propagation pass (GD9630 added, 2026-10-24): traced `Printer_Gfx_DumpRPort()`'s source-hook initialization through transfer and return (`workbench/devs/printer/gfx.c:557-671`) and its selected device caller (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:638-659`). The function sets `err` to `PDERR_INTERNALMEMORY` before temporary row/bitmap allocation, never clears it after successful allocation and conversion, calls `PRS_CLOSE` without assigning a result, then returns that retained error for the device to publish as `io_Error`. The source hook is selected by the maintained `PRD_TPEXTDUMPRPORT` chunky/RGB modes or `DRPA_SourceHook`. Added GD9630; no new source-body credit because these bodies were already covered. No printer request or failure was induced; source-only.


Printer ordinary-path allocation error pass (GD9631 added, 2026-10-24): traced the no-source-hook path after successful `PRS_INIT` through transfer-row/destination bitmap allocation, the skipped rendering loop, `PRS_CLOSE`, and return (`workbench/devs/printer/gfx.c:544-545,590-671`). Confirmed `gfx.c` is selected by `workbench/devs/printer/mmakefile.src:3-10`. Added GD9631, separate from source-hook GD9630. No printer request or allocation failure was induced; source-only.

System requester MapRawKey overflow caller follow-up (GD9632 added; 2026-10-24): rechecked the one-byte `MapRawKey()` call in `rom/intuition/sysrequest_intern.c:216-247` against the keymap return and helper behavior (`rom/keymap/maprawkey.c:140-167,263-264`; `rom/keymap/support.c:29-37`). A multi-byte string mapping returns -1 before writing to the one-byte buffer; the caller's Boolean test treats that as success and reads `rawbuffer[0]` for requester response comparison. ScreenMode Test RastPort allocation failure recheck (GD6342 detailed; GD6343 kept distinct; 2026-10-24): followed the user Test method through successful timer setup and `OpenScreenTags()` to `CreateRastPort()` (`workbench/prefs/screenmode/smeditor.c:274-347`). The public helper's implementation returns NULL when its single `AllocMem()` fails (`compiler/arossupport/createrastport.c:35-43`); the next statement writes through `rp`, before any cleanup label, confirming GD6342's conditional fault and skipped normal test-screen/timer cleanup. The successful path's missing `FreeRastPort()` is the separate GD6343 allocation leak. No preview or allocation failure was run; source-only.

ScreenMode preview RastPort success-path ownership recheck (GD6343 detailed; 2026-10-24): traced `CreateRastPort()` at `smeditor.c:346` through all subsequent exits. The only successful-screen path closes the screen and timer/request/port (`:462-470`) but never calls the matching `FreeRastPort()`; the temporary RastPort is not owned by the screen, and its API explicitly requires the caller to free it (`compiler/arossupport/freerastport.c:18-46`). A successful Test action therefore leaks one RastPort allocation per preview. Kept this distinct from GD6342's failed-allocation dereference. No preview was run; source-only.

Pointer Preferences export sticky-success recheck (GD6344 detailed; 2026-10-24): traced both `MAXPOINTER` iterations through `PushChunk()` and `WriteChunkBytes()` (`workbench/prefs/pointer/prefs.c:155-212`; `prefs.h:14`). `retval` is set TRUE after any one `NPTR` write succeeds and is not cleared on later `PushChunk` or short/error write; the loop continues after a failed entry. `WriteChunkBytes()` returns actual bytes written or an error (`workbench/libs/iffparse/writechunkbytes.c:19-27`), and GUI `PTEditor__MUIM_PrefsEditor_ExportFH` returns the helper result (`pteditor.c:264-276`), confirming a success report for incomplete files. CLI persistence ignores the return independently (`prefs.c:258-283`), so it is not used as this finding's caller-visible success signal. No export or I/O failure was run; source-only.

Input Preferences empty-recognized-chunk import recheck (GD6345 detailed; 2026-10-24): traced successful `StopChunks()` registration into the `ParseIFF(IFFPARSE_SCAN)` loop (`workbench/prefs/input/prefs.c:291-356`). `retval` becomes TRUE before the loop, and a valid PREF FORM containing no recognized INPT/KMSW stop chunk reaches end-of-file without resetting it or applying either structure. The GUI import handler then refreshes unchanged globals and clears the Changed flag (`ipeditor.c:565-581`); the CLI ENV path treats the file as loaded and suppresses ENVARC fallback (`prefs.c:102-113,502-528`). No file or GUI import was exercised; source-only.

Input Preferences KMSW export failure recheck (GD6346 detailed; 2026-10-24): followed `Prefs_ExportFH()` after successful `INPT` serialization (`workbench/prefs/input/prefs.c:443-465`). `retval` becomes TRUE on INPT success; KMSW PushChunk failure has no error branch and KMSW write failure skips the `retval = retval && TRUE` assignment, leaving TRUE unchanged. `CloseIFF()` is unchecked (`:479`), and the GUI export method returns the stale helper result (`ipeditor.c:584-597`). Thus an INPT-only/incomplete file is reported successful after the specified KMSW failure. CLI save callers discard the result (`prefs.c:530-555`); no export or failure was run. Source-only.


System requester default-keymap trigger verification (GD9632 strengthened; 2026-10-24): checked the requester-synthesized `InputEvent` field values and the initialized default-keymap path (`rom/intuition/sysrequest_intern.c:216-230`; `rom/keymap/keymap_init.c:47-60`). The requester supplies `ie_Qualifier=0`; selected built-in keymap code `0x4c` is `ST|S`, and the unqualified string-table slot selects descriptor zero with length two (`rom/keymap/defaultkeymap.c:105-110,631-640,905-912`). Therefore cursor-up reaches the exact one-byte `MapRawKey()` overflow without relying on a hypothetical custom keymap. `WriteToBuffer()` rejects before copying, `MapRawKey()` returns -1, and the caller treats that as truth before reading `rawbuffer[0]`. Updated GD9632 with this concrete selected-input trigger. No requester or key event was run; source-only; no body-line credit.

System requester raw-key address handoff recheck (GD9632 retained; 2026-10-25): traced the `IntuiMessage.IAddress` pointer used to rebuild `ie_EventAddress` against the selected input-handler producer (`rom/intuition/sysrequest_intern.c:223-229`; `rom/intuition/inputhandler_support.c:144-170,189-212`). For `IDCMP_RAWKEY`, both message producers copy the original event address into the embedded `prevCodeQuals` field and set `IAddress` to that field's address; the requester dereference therefore restores the original pointer and is not a separate bad-indirection candidate. The `MapRawKey()` overflow/unwritten-byte defect remains confined to the one-byte capacity and truth-test described by GD9632. Message storage remains live while the handler processes it and is replied by its caller after dispatch. No input event or requester was used; source-only.

GD4228 HAM row-stride consequence narrowing (2026-10-24): checked the computed source-byte offset against the planar row allocation for non-byte-aligned widths. Because `bmh_Width <= BytesPerRow * 8`, `(i * bmh_Width + x) / 8` does not by itself advance beyond the allocated plane extent for valid dimensions; it does start later rows too early and reads wrong pixel bits. Removed the unsupported overread consequence from GD4228; the incorrect HAM output remains. No frame was decoded or accessed at runtime; source-only.

Under the documented sequence, the clear blocks until menu tracking ends, before `CloseWindow()` frees the window. GetGBuffers signed-size overflow re-review (GD5521 detail restored and qualified; 2026-10-24): re-read `getgbuffers.c` and `freegbuffers.c`, checked signed `WORD` dimensions in `graphics/gels.h`, and repeated the maintained C caller census. The positive geometry `Width=32767`, `Height=8194`, `Depth=8` makes the initial shadow extent 536,985,596 bytes and the depth-scaled extent 4,295,884,768, beyond 32-bit `LONG_MAX`; the source uses signed `long` multiplication without a range check for SaveBuffer and optional BufBuffer, and FreeGBuffers recomputes it. Corrected the earlier wrapped-size statement: signed overflow is undefined in C, so 917,472 is only the ordinary two's-complement wrap result, not a compiler-independent allocation size. No maintained direct caller was found; retained GD5521 as a conditional public API candidate, with actual undersized allocation/overrun dependent on selected compiler behavior and external reachability. Also traced `windecor_windowshape()`'s `BarRounded` result through the selected default shape hook (`:1867-1960`; `rom/intuition/intuition_misc.c:1192-1222`) into `ChangeWindowShape()`/layer shape update. The separate `BarMasking` branch returns a copied cached region and is not the GD6090 path. WinGDI native event-thread shutdown recheck (GD9637 added, 2026-10-25): traced `GDI_Init()`'s `CreateThread()`/immediate handle close through `gdithread_entry()`'s message loop and post-loop keyboard-hook removal, then followed `GDI_Shutdown()` from the selected HIDD expunge (`arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/gdi_native.c:241-264,364-454`; `wingdi_hiddclass.c:759-770`). GD9637 early worker shutdown-post race recheck (2026-10-25): re-read the host worker startup and cleanup in source order (`gdi_native.c:241-264,376-425,444-454`). `GDI_Init()` closes its thread handle without a readiness handshake; `gdithread_entry()` does not reach `GetMessage()` until after `SetWindowsHookEx()`. `GDI_Shutdown()` ignores the `PostThreadMessage(WM_QUIT)` result and immediately closes both acknowledgement events and frees all three IRQs. The Windows API contract says posting fails if the target thread has not created a message queue; thus the selected init rollback can lose the quit message if shutdown wins the worker-start race, leaving the worker and hook alive after teardown. This strengthens GD9637's documented trigger/consequence with an explicit lost-shutdown path. Updated the finding in `AROS-graphics-desktop.md`; its index link/ID is unchanged. The API contract is documented by [Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/desktop/api/winuser/nf-winuser-postthreadmessagea). No message queue, shutdown race, or host event was run; no body-line credit changed; source-only.

GD9538 DOS-name trigger recheck (no new GD; 2026-10-25): confirmed the 107-byte threshold fits DOS's accepted device-name representation. `MakeDosEntry()` allocates for the full C string and stores a BSTR length capped only at 255; `AddDosEntry()` checks duplicate names and appends without an additional length bound (`rom/dos/makedosentry.c:55-80`; `rom/dos/adddosentry.c:88-115`). A 107-byte name therefore reaches the icon caller; bytes 0–106 hold the name, byte 107 the colon, and byte 108 the NUL, one byte beyond its 108-byte array (valid indices 0–107). MUI font-preference parser and Configdata setter follow-up (2026-10-25; no new finding): traced `zune_font_get()`'s custom font string from `MUI_ConfigdataData.prefs.fonts[]` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/font.c:26-108`; `classes/configdata.c:305-342`) to the eight font fields and Zune Prefs `MUIM_Configdata_SetFont` callers (`classes/configdata.c:1056-1096`; `workbench/prefs/Zune/{windowp,listviewsp,groupsp,buttonsp,slidersp}.c`). The accepted string comes from Dataspace/IFF or the font requester; `zune_font_get()` allocates a private copy, parses the final path component with `StrToLong()` without checking its return, narrows the resulting `LONG` to `TextAttr.ta_YSize` (`UWORD`), then opens the corresponding `.font`. Non-numeric sizes become zero and overlarge values can narrow or overflow; an unsuccessful custom open follows the existing screen/system-font fallback path. No concrete in-tree malformed preference, independent user-visible consequence, or supported size contract violation was established, so this remains a parser follow-up rather than a finding. Also checked the apparent `MUIM_Configdata_SetFont` synchronization omission: Zune Prefs calls it on a temporary Configdata object solely to save its Dataspace; live applications obtain `mgi_Prefs` from their own initialized/reloaded Configdata object, so the omitted `Configdata_SynchronizeString()` call does not establish stale live font pointers. No preference was edited or font opened; source-only.


MUI gradient renderer angle/geometry follow-up (GD9657 corrected; 2026-10-25): re-derived the denominator from the actual quadrant setup in `FillPixelArrayGradient()`. The earlier 315-degree claim was incorrect: in quadrant four `yw = -height` and `vx = vy = -180`, making `t = -180 * (height + width)`, which cannot be zero for a nonempty rectangle. At 135 degrees, `vx = vy = 180`, quadrant two retains `yw = height`, and a square gives `t = 180 * (width - height) = 0` before the first pixel's `y1_mul_t_accu / t`. Confirmed the selected Zune Prefs slider permits 135 and serializes it into the image spec via `Gradient_Function()`; mode-0 scaled/tiled drawing on CyberGraphX truecolor reaches the division. Corrected GD9657 to the reachable 135-degree square case. No gradient was rendered; source-only; no file-body line credit.

CursorFB whole-operation bracket coordinate recheck (GD5731 detailed; 2026-10-25): re-read `CFB_REMOVE_ALL`, all six callers, and `GfxDisplay_CursorIntersects()` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_cursorfbclass.c:60-67,303-359`; `gfx_displayclass.c:294-307`), plus the public `InputEvent` and stored cursor-position types (`compiler/include/devices/inputevent.h:34-42`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_display.h:50-55`). The helper tests only `[-16384,16383]`, although signed `WORD` coordinates extend through 32767. Polygon draw/fill, text draw/fill, bitmap clear, and bitmap scale can therefore skip cursor removal when the cursor rectangle lies beyond that bound, then modify its pixels without the bracket restoring it. The consequence remains conditional on the selected display accepting those coordinates and the operation touching the cursor. No mode or drawing operation was run. Source-only.

WAV decoder input-span proof for GD6202 (2026-10-25): rechecked the retained zero/undersized `blockAlign` finding against the exact batch allocation and decoder loop. `SND_BUFFER_SIZE` is 16 KiB (`workbench/classes/datatypes/wav/include/wave_class.h:10`); mono float32 with `blockAlign=1` makes `numBlocks=16384`, allocates and reads 16,384 bytes, then the decoder processes the same 16,384 frames while advancing four bytes per frame (`wave_class.c:367-412`; `wave_ieee_float.c:28-40`), exceeding the allocation by 49,152 bytes. Stereo 8-bit A-law at the same alignment consumes two bytes per frame. This confirms a heap-buffer overread for sufficiently large data chunks; smaller partial batches may read zero-filled bytes within the oversized allocation instead. Zero alignment still divides by zero at the same parser sizing expression. Expanded GD6202's consequence with these exact spans. PCM has separate setup that recalculates alignment; no additional PCM issue established. No WAV was loaded or decoded; source-only.

MovePixelArray result and count arithmetic recheck (GD5745-GD5746 detailed, 2026-10-25): compared the public `UWORD` dimensions and documented count result with `movepixelarray.c:17-61`, then followed `ClipBlit()`'s void signature, clipping, same-RastPort overlap-region allocations, and failure exits (`rom/graphics/clipblit.c:27-41,130-158,201-216,263-275`). GD5744 coordinate-family trigger validation and promotion (2026-10-25): rechecked `AllocBitMap()` and the generic HIDD bitmap width attribute against the CyberGraphX entry points. `AllocBitMap()` accepts ULONG dimensions and `BMF_SPECIALFMT` forces HIDD allocation; HIDD width/height attributes are UWORD, so 32,769 pixels are representable. A one-row LUT8 bitmap at that width needs a 32,769-byte row, within `BytesPerRow`'s UWORD range. `WritePixelArray(RECTFMT_LUT8)` forwards x=32,768 through `WritePixels8()`'s signed-WORD coordinates; the bitmap clipping bound `width-1` also narrows to a negative WORD, causing the valid request to be rejected before drawing and returning zero. Promoted GD5744 from conditional/unconfirmed to a confirmed public API range mismatch; no maintained caller or large display mode is needed for this explicitly allocated offscreen HIDD bitmap. The ABI conversion and allocation were not run; source-only.

AllocRaster/FreeRaster public-width mismatch recheck (GD5741 detailed, 2026-10-25): compared the generated public vector declarations and complete implementations (`rom/graphics/graphics.conf:122-123`; `allocraster.c:16-23,54`; `freeraster.c:16-24,53`) with `RASSIZE()` (`compiler/include/graphics/gfx.h:43`) and Exec's zero-size `FreeMem()` path (`rom/exec/freemem.c:64-66`). A width of 65,536 allocates 8,192 bytes for height 1, but converts to UWORD zero at `FreeRaster()`, making its computed free size zero; `FreeMem()` then returns without releasing the block. Confirmed the checked-in direct callers use ordinary UWORD-sized dimensions; retained the finding for the public external API. No raster operation was run; source-only.

AllocBitMap extended displayability tag path recheck (GD5740 detailed, 2026-10-25): compared the public tag contract with every case in the extended parser and both downstream decisions (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:128-131,196-230,237-246,323-326`). `BMATags_Displayable` is not parsed; the tag-list true case therefore cannot force the HIDD path for an otherwise plain low-depth request, and the false case cannot suppress `BMF_DISPLAYABLE` or the HIDD attribute. ProcessPixelArray endian mapping recheck (GD5752/GD5753 narrowed, 2026-10-25): matched the documented `RECTFMT_ARGB` byte sequence (`workbench/libs/cgfx/writepixelarray.c:67-68`) against the `ULONG` unpack/repack in tint, blur, brightness, and SetAlpha.
