CGFX `DoCDrawMethodTagList()` no-direct-access fallback recheck (GD5754 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-25): reread `RenderHook()` and the public `CDrawMsg` layout. The fallback computes `max_tocopy_h` and `tocopy_h` from `PIXELBUF_SIZE / bytesperrow`, but passes `lines_todo` (the entire remaining height) to both `HIDD_BM_GetImage()` and `HIDD_BM_PutImage()`; it also leaves `cdm_ysize` at the original rectangle height for the hook. Thus a rectangle taller than the buffer capacity overruns the shared scratch buffer on the first `GetImage()`, with the hook and writeback also given oversized dimensions. Traced the default bitmap method returning FALSE and PlanarBM's inheritance; the selected ChunkyBM override returns TRUE, excluding its ordinary direct-access path. Traced the popup-shadow public caller, but did not establish that caller's bitmap/rectangle meets the trigger. No graphics operation was run; source-only.

Generic graphics renderer cached-GC draw-mode recheck (GD5755 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-25): re-read `int_bltbitmap()`, its `BltBitMap()` cache caller, and the pen-conversion fallback. The general CopyBox path saves `old_drmd`, sets `drmd`, then writes `drmd` again instead of the saved value; the special truecolor Clear path sets Copy and never applies its saved mode back. `BltBitMap()` returns the object to the shared GC cache. `bltbitmap_pens()` precomputes minterm results, then calls `HIDD_BM_PutImage()` without resetting the GC mode, so cache reuse can apply stale draw-mode semantics to those results when the selected HIDD honors that GC state. The source defect is confirmed; practical corruption depends on cache reuse and HIDD behavior. No blit or cache reuse was run; source-only.

`ClipBlit()` same-RastPort overlap minterm recheck (GD5756 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-25): reread the overlap branch and `MoveRaster()`. The selected overlap optimization calls `MoveRaster()` when either absolute displacement is less than half the requested width or height; `MoveRaster()` uses hard-coded `0xc0` Copy for unlayered and per-ClipRect blits and does not accept the caller's minterm. The other overlap route passes `minterm` into `internal_ClipBlit()`. The entry point documents non-Copy minterms, but the prior caller census found only maintained same-RastPort Copy uses, so the trigger is public/external API use. No blit was run; source-only.

`ScrollWindowRasterNoFill()` duplicate-move recheck (GD5757 confirmed and trigger narrowed; 2026-10-25): re-read the full vector and traced its `ScrollRaster()` call through `MoveRaster()`'s per-ClipRect loop. When both absolute displacement components are smaller than the requested rectangle dimensions, the function first `ClipBlit()`s the retained overlap. `scroll` remains TRUE if the translated rectangle is not wholly contained by one ClipRect or the layer is already marked `LAYERREFRESH`; that branch then calls `ScrollRaster()`, which moves the layer again. If either displacement consumes the full extent, the first ClipBlit is skipped, so that case is not claimed. Reconfirmed whole-tree C search found no maintained caller of this vector. No scroll was run; source-only.

Area polygon convex-fast-path slope recheck (GD5758 confirmed and trigger bounded; 2026-10-25): reread `areafillpolygon()`'s four-edge convex branch, `AreaDraw()` coordinate storage, and `AreaEnd()` TmpRas sizing. The fast path multiplies signed `LONG` `(x2-x1)` by 65,536 before dividing by vertical delta. On 32-bit signed-LONG targets, a valid convex quadrilateral edge from x=-16384 to x=16384 over one scanline produces 2,147,483,648, outside the representable range; the TmpRas size check does not constrain this intermediate. Recorded the overflow and unreliable fill result without assuming a particular wrap or asserting out-of-bounds access. Previously reviewed in-tree AreaDraw callers do not establish this wide-coordinate trigger. No render or target compiler check was run; source-only.

Ellipse midpoint overflow cross-implementation reconciliation (GD5760 confirmed and expanded; GD4064 withdrawn as duplicate; 2026-10-25): compared generic HIDD `DrawEllipse()`, Radeon and IntelGMA overrides, shared `areafillellipse()`, their public radius types and the AreaEnd dispatch. All four implementations use the same `t7 = rx * t5; t8 = t7 << 1` signed-LONG sequence. For radius 1000, t7 is 2,000,000,000 but t8 requests 4,000,000,000, beyond signed 32-bit range; larger radii can overflow t7 too. Thus the previous GD4064 1,025 threshold was not the earliest affected radius and described the same implementation family, so it is merged into GD5760; that finding additionally tracks the independent Area-fill copy. Stated only the range overflow and unreliable raster result, not a specific wrap or memory access. No target compiler or ellipse operation was run; source-only.

`Flood()` area-pattern decoder recheck (GD5761 confirmed and consequence refined; 2026-10-25): compared `pattern_pen()` with the actual `BltPattern()` convention and its pixel loop. `BltPattern()` treats every nonnegative `AreaPtSz` as monochrome, including exponent zero; Flood's helper uses `> 0`, routing zero to multicolor. The multicolor branch initializes `pen_mask` to zero and only shifts it left, so each plane contributes zero and `pixval` remains zero; it also advances the plane pointer only after the loop. Thus zero-exponent mono patterns are misinterpreted and all multicolor fill pixels use pen zero. Traced both planar-direct and ReadPixel/WritePixel paths through shared `putfillpixel()`; the decoding error applies to both. Maintained Flood callers found previously do not demonstrate patterned fill. No fill was run; source-only.

Graphics.library failed-init semaphore lifetime recheck (GD5762 confirmed and trigger enumerated; 2026-10-25): reread `GfxInit()` publication/failure order and traced the selected generated INITLIB cleanup through `_set_libinit()`, `_set_libexpunge()` and genmodule's `__freebase()` path. `fontsem` is added to Exec's public semaphore list before hash allocation and later fallible region-pool, ROM-font, graphics-root and driver initialization; no `RemSemaphore()` or `ADD2EXPUNGELIB` exists in graphics.library. On a false init result the generated path invokes the available expunge set then frees the embedded base, leaving the public list node stale. No failure was induced; source-only.

`DoCollision()` shifted one-word mask recheck (GD5763 confirmed and trigger specified; 2026-10-25): reread both shifted-comparison branches and mask setup. For a 16-pixel VSprite, `Width >> 4` is one word per row, and `InitMasks()` fills `Height * wordsperline` collision words. In the negative-scroll path, `_curindex` increments to `wordsperline`; the guard is `>`, so equality proceeds to read the next mask word. Two sorted one-row VSprites offset by one pixel provide the boundary case with `_i == 0`. Scoped the direct finding to the one-UWORD overread and left collision/fault effects conditional on adjacent contents. No maintained direct `DoCollision()` caller was found; no collision data was constructed or run. Source-only.

`AddVSprite()` internal-record allocation rollback recheck (GD5764 confirmed and separated from GD5765; 2026-10-25): reread list insertion, `_CreateIntVSprite()` allocation, DrawGList traversal and `_ValidateIntVSprite()`. The VSprite is linked before the internal record allocation; a NULL allocation result is stored without rollback. Later saved-background rendering dereferences `IntVSprite->SaveBuffer`, and the normal path passes the NULL field into `_ValidateIntVSprite()`, which dereferences the record. This is the missing-record publication defect; GD5765 remains the later unchecked bitmap replacement case after an internal record already exists. No allocation failure or list traversal was induced; source-only.

`_ValidateIntVSprite()` replacement-bitmap failure recheck (GD5765 confirmed and allocation cases separated; 2026-10-25): reread the dimension-change path and traced each replacement to its first use. Both old buffers are freed before unchecked `AllocBitMap()` calls; dimensions and source-data identity are then updated regardless of allocation results. Failed `ImageData` allocation flows immediately into `BltBitMap()`, whose `IS_HIDD_BM(destBitMap)` macro reads `bitmap->pad`, so NULL is dereferenced. Failed `SaveBuffer` allocation remains NULL for the DrawGList SAVEBACK capture path. The helper returns TRUE; callers receive no allocation-failure indication. The changed-size metadata also prevents an automatic retry from this same predicate. No allocation failure or list draw was induced; source-only.

`GetBitMapAttr(BMA_WIDTH)` chunky-HIDD bound recheck (GD5766 confirmed and caller consequence refined; 2026-10-25): compared the public attribute body with generic HIDD row-stride construction and its documented pixel-width attribute. The public vector always multiplies `BytesPerRow` by eight; chunky `BytesPerRow` is aligned pixel width times bytes per pixel (e.g. 640-pixel RGB32 gives 2,560 bytes and is reported as 20,480 pixels). Traced this result through `GetRPClipRectangleForBitMap()` and its unlayered render/pixel callers; the helper explicitly uses bitmap bounds to keep HIDDs without their own checks from accessing outside storage. Also rechecked SetRast/ClearEOL/ClearScreen endpoint consumers. Exact memory effects depend on HIDD bounds behavior, so the report claims the generic guard is defeated and qualifies out-of-bounds effects. No bitmap operation was run; source-only.

`GetDisplayInfoData(DTAG_NAME)` zero-capacity recheck (GD5767 confirmed and address claim qualified; 2026-10-25): re-read the size validation, temporary-record copy and final name terminator. The tag-size helper ignores the caller's size; zero survives the upper-bound clamp, the zero-byte CopyMem is followed by unconditional `buf[size - 1] = 0`, and `ULONG` is explicitly unsigned 32-bit. Thus the index underflows to `ULONG_MAX` and is outside the supplied zero-length destination. Removed the platform-independent “one byte before buffer” claim because the exact pointer result depends on target pointer width and compiler arithmetic. Maintained callers use structure-sized buffers; no zero-size call was made. Source-only.

`GetRGB4()` signed-index lower-bound recheck (GD5768 confirmed and caller scope stated; 2026-10-25): reread the public vector and checked the selected ColorMap allocation layout. `entry` is signed `LONG`; the only validation rejects NULL maps and `entry >= Count`, then directly indexes `ColorTable[entry]`. `GetColorMap()` allocates the color table as its own `entries * sizeof(UWORD)` block. Negative public inputs therefore read before that allocation. Re-searched maintained callers: reqtools and Palette Preferences use nonnegative iteration indices, with no local negative call established. No invalid call was made; source-only.

VGAGfx bitmap-construction cleanup recheck (GD5769 confirmed and trigger scoped; 2026-10-25): traced the `VideoData` allocation, ChunkyBM buffer tag, register-state allocation failure and constructor cleanup into custom Root.Dispose. The ChunkyBM tag explicitly marks the buffer non-owned, but VGAGfx frees `VideoData` before coercing Dispose, and Dispose unconditionally frees the same field again. The path requires a displayable bitmap and successful pixel-buffer allocation followed by failed register-state allocation; non-displayable construction returns before it. Confirmed the standalone all-native VGAGfx target manifest selects this bitmap class. No allocation failure or object construction was run; source-only.

VGAGfx reset callback erase-bound recheck (GD5770 confirmed and byte extent quantified; 2026-10-25): traced reset callback registration and dispatch into the visible bitmap dimensions, then through `vgaEraseArea()`'s physical pitch and unchecked `memset()` loop. The reset box uses `data->width/height`; the erase pitch uses `disp_width >> 3`, with no aperture cap. VGAGfx mode setup documents a 64-KiB VGA memory map, while its display enumerator advertises maximum dimensions 16,384. A 640×900 bitmap at 640-pixel pitch clears 80×900 = 72,000 bytes, extending 6,464 bytes past that mapped plane. Restricted the consequence to writes beyond the selected aperture and left resulting platform effect conditional. No reset or memory write was run; source-only.

`ScreenPosition(SPOS_MAKEVISIBLE)` implementation recheck (GD5771 confirmed; 2026-10-25): compared the public mode documentation and flag values with the complete implementation. The code has only an `SPOS_ABSOLUTE` branch; all other admitted modes are treated as relative, so `SPOS_MAKEVISIBLE` adds x1/y1 to current `LeftEdge`/`TopEdge` and never reads x2/y2. A non-draggable screen without SPOS_FORCEDRAG is gated out entirely; on eligible screens the requested rectangle is not made visible and the upper-left is interpreted as a movement delta. Reconfirmed no maintained C caller uses SPOS_MAKEVISIBLE. No screen operation was run; source-only.

`InitIIH()` partial-allocation failure-path recheck (GD5772 confirmed; GD9683 added; 2026-10-25): reread pool creation, the short-circuit cleanup scope and the common `IIHData` failure tail; traced InitIIH failure into OpenIntuition. If the first pool succeeds and the second fails, the success-only cleanup block is skipped and `InputEventMemPool` is lost when `iihdata` is freed, confirming GD5772. Separately, every post-IIHData setup failure reaches `FreeMem(iihdata)` followed by a write to `iihdata->MouseBoundsActiveFlag`; added GD9683 for that use-after-free, including port, pool and system-gadget construction failures. No allocation failure or Intuition open was run; source-only.

MorphOS Intuition ViewExtra retry candidate recheck (GD5773 confirmed and consequence expanded; 2026-10-25): re-read `IntuitionOpen()` from its graphics-base capture through ViewLord and ScreenFont setup (`rom/intuition/intuition_init.c:335-418`). Under `__MORPHOS__`, failed `GfxNew(VIEW_EXTRA_TYPE)` clears the stored graphics.library base and returns without closing the open reference (`:393-403`). A subsequent open that successfully allocates ViewExtra continues to `GfxBase->DefaultFont` through the cleared stored pointer (`:417-418`), so it dereferences NULL and cannot recover; the lost open reference also remains outstanding. Scoped to MorphOS and the failure-then-retry sequence. The body was already credited in full; no coverage percentage change. No allocation failure or retry was induced; source-only.

Intuition synchronous-action allocation-failure candidate pass (GD5774 and GD5813 rechecked and detailed; 2026-10-25): reread `DoSyncAction()` and traced its `CreateMsgPort()` failure behavior into both active-gadget synchronous callers. Outside the input-device task, a NULL port skips callback setup/queueing and returns without a failure result (`rom/intuition/inputhandler_actions.c:590-637`). `ActivateGadget()` then reads uninitialized `msg.success` (`activategadget.c:79-90`) for eligible custom/string gadgets. `RemoveGList()` leaves both result fields unset, retries based on `msg.success`, and returns `msg.count` after apparent success (`removeglist.c:142-160`); if the callback never runs, both the retry outcome and return value depend on prior stack contents. Kept GD5813 for the shared silently-dropped operation and GD5774 for the concrete caller result failures. Confirmed in-tree activation/removal callers exist, including ASL, Edit, datatype, and requester paths; whether each exact active-gadget/non-input-task condition occurs varies by caller. No port failure, gadget operation, or retry loop was induced; source-only.

Intuition/Layers failed-`BeginUpdate()` cleanup recheck (GD5775 confirmed and exact state sequence expanded; 2026-10-25): re-read `BeginRefresh()`, Layers `BeginUpdate()`/`EndUpdate()`, and `EndRefresh()`, then followed the previously tracked screen-bar, `WindowNeedsRefresh()` and `CheckLayers()` callers. In `BeginRefresh()`, outer layer locks are acquired before `BeginUpdate()`; the latter saves `ClipRect` to `cr2`, and on initial damage-region failure unlocks only its own lock and returns FALSE. `BeginRefresh()` nevertheless calls `EndUpdate()`: for non-smart-refresh layers with an existing ClipRect, this frees the list, restores the same pointer as active, and consumes the outer lock. It returns without setting `WFLG_WINDOWREFRESH`; paired `EndRefresh()` therefore skips EndUpdate but still unlocks the layer(s) and LayerInfo. Confirmed similar unchecked result/pairing in `renderScreenBar()`, `WindowNeedsRefresh()` and `CheckLayers()`; added their exact call sites to GD5775. Scoped freed-list consequence to an existing ClipRect on a non-smart-refresh layer; lock/state consequences require BeginUpdate failure followed by the unconditional cleanup path. No allocation failure or refresh was induced; source-only; no body-line credit changed.

Requester first-button allocation cleanup recheck (GD5776 confirmed and trigger/paths detailed; 2026-10-25): re-read `buildeasyreq_makegadgets()`, `intrequest_makegadgets()` and shared `intrequest_freegadgets()`. In both builders, failure of the first FRBUTTON `NewObject()` leaves `gadgetlist` NULL and passes it to the cleanup helper (`buildeasyrequestargs.c:581-588`; `sysrequest_intern.c:506-513`). The helper dereferences `gadgets->GadgetRender` before its NULL-terminating loop (`requesters.c:41-54`), so both public requester paths fault during failure cleanup rather than return a construction failure. Traced callers through the common BuildEasyRequestArgs / BuildSysRequest wrappers; no alternate NULL guard is present. The builder/helper bodies already have full-body credit; no percentage change. No allocation failure or requester was induced; source-only.

BuildEasyRequestArgs vertical-prop failure recheck (GD5777 confirmed and user-visible effect traced; 2026-10-25): re-read the long-body layout, gadget construction, returned list, text renderer and IDCMPUPDATE handling. When body height exceeds `disptextheight`, failed `PROPGCLASS` construction leaves the already-built button list non-NULL; the builder sets the IDCMPUPDATE flag and returns that list, so `BuildEasyRequestArgs()` opens the requester without a vertical prop (`buildeasyrequestargs.c:606-648,189-249`). `buildreq_draw()` clips the text to `disptextheight` and uses `dims->offy` as its vertical origin (`requesters.c:163-175`); the only selected mutation of `offy` comes from a vertical prop's IDCMPUPDATE (`sysrequest_intern.c:259-279`). Thus the requester displays only the initial clipped portion and cannot reveal the remainder. Scoped to over-height text plus prop failure after button creation; no allocation failure or requester was induced. Bodies already have full-body credit; no percentage change. Source-only.

BuildEasyRequestArgs later-button cleanup recheck (GD5778 confirmed and separated from first-button failure; 2026-10-25): traced successful `GetScreenDrawInfo()` at `buildeasyreq_makegadgets()` through button construction and both failure/normal exits. After at least one button exists, a later FRBUTTON `NewObject()` failure invokes `intrequest_freegadgets()` and returns without reaching the normal `FreeScreenDrawInfo(scr, dri)` (`buildeasyrequestargs.c:531,570-588,646-648`). The helper frees the gadget objects and shared frame but has no DrawInfo release (`requesters.c:41-55`). Scoped to successful DrawInfo acquisition and a later-button failure; the first-button case is GD5776's distinct NULL cleanup dereference. No allocation failure or requester was induced; source-only; bodies already have full-body credit, no coverage percentage change.

DisplayBeep timer/shared-state synchronization recheck (GD5779 confirmed and interleavings qualified; 2026-10-25): compared the selected `USE_NEWDISPLAYBEEP`/`USEWINDOWLOCK` configuration with `DisplayBeep()`, the input-handler timer scan, `CloseScreen()`, and `LockIBase()`'s contract. DisplayBeep and CloseScreen mutate `Screen.Flags`, `BeepingCounter`, and/or `BeepingScreens` while holding WindowLock; the timer reads/mutates the same state under IBaseLock, and neither lock is acquired by the other path. Traced feasible races: a timer decrement can overwrite a concurrent counter reset; count increments/decrements can lose updates, while the timer uses the count both as its entry guard and scan terminator. Qualified duration/count consequences as schedule-dependent and did not assert a deterministic corruption result. `USE_NEWDISPLAYBEEP` and `USEWINDOWLOCK` are both selected by `intuition_intern.h:225,285`. No beep, screen close, or interleaving was run; source-only; body-line credit unchanged.

ClearDMRequest delegate/active-request caller recheck (GD5780 confirmed and consequence expanded; 2026-10-25): traced `ClearDMRequest()` into the public `SetDMRequest()` entry guard and internal action. The delegate supplies NULL; `SANITY_CHECKR(dmrequest, FALSE)` returns before DoSyncAction under the selected non-debug macro, so the internal assignment of `window->DMRequest = NULL` is unreachable even when the existing requester is inactive. Compared with the documented retry-until-TRUE contract. Followed `EndRequest()`, which clears REQACTIVE and unlinks the active requester but leaves `window->DMRequest`, and the input-handler menu-button double-click path, which later invokes `Request(w->DMRequest,w)`. A caller therefore cannot detach the inactive requester, which remains eligible to reopen. No requester was installed, cleared or reopened; source-only; no body-line credit changed.

DOSBoot no-media animation partial-initialization recheck (GD5781 confirmed and target variants/consequences expanded; 2026-10-25): traced `banm_Init()` subordinate storage allocations through `anim_Init()` publication and the immediate initial draw. This clipping may hide the extra edge at a boundary, but does not correct the inclusive extra row/column when it lies inside the same visible cliprect. Non-layered mode instead calls inclusive `RectFill()` with the same endpoints. `CreateLayerTagList()` stores the supplied hook, and Intuition uses the sentinel for intentionally blank backfill. IconList appended-info width and buffer-resize ownership recheck (GD5875-GD5876 confirmed and scoped, 2026-10-25): re-read label rectangle width calculation and compared horizontal/vertical padding attributes and their preference loading. Confirmed the appended-size/date expansion uses vertical padding; narrowed underestimation to the case where vertical padding is smaller than horizontal and the extra text exceeds the current width (GD5875). Traced UPDATE_RESIZE's stale-size branch from old-buffer pointer replacement and DeleteLayer through the new buffer allocation, and compared DeleteLayer cleanup against RastPort/bitmap allocation ownership. Confirmed old off-screen RastPort and bitmap are lost without frees, whether or not replacement succeeds; scoped to caller-enabled buffering because Wanderer's compile-time switch is disabled (GD5876). No preference, rendering, resize or allocation failure was run; source-only.
IconList FmtSizeToString arithmetic candidate withdrawal (GD5879 withdrawn; 2026-10-25): rechecked `FmtSizeToString()` at `iconlist.c:328-369`. The earlier 500,000,000-byte example enters the megabyte branch (`num >= 1,048,576`), which widens multiplication to UQUAD. The kilobyte branch is restricted to 1,024 through 1,048,575, so `num * 10 + 512` remains below 10,486,262 and cannot overflow a 32-bit ULONG. The evidence does not support the alleged overflow; removed GD5879 from the candidate report and master index. No replacement example was established. No UI or file-size formatting was run; source-only.
AppIcon failed-clone candidate consolidation (GD5889 withdrawn as duplicate of GD9535; 2026-10-25): rechecked `iconwindow_volumelist.c:949-956` and the direct `LayoutIconA()` caller. This is the same unchecked `DupDiskObject()` result and NULL dereference already recorded in GD9535 (`layouticon.c:71-84`; duplication failure paths in `dupdiskobject.c:143-147,170-210,258-308`). Removed the duplicate GD5889 report section and index entry; GD9535 remains the canonical finding. No refresh or allocation failure was induced; source-only.

ScreenDepth hook notification source recheck (GD5954 confirmed; 2026-10-25): matched the public `ScreenNotifyMessage.snm_Code` contract to the `ScreenDepth()` call into `FireScreenNotifyMessageCode()`. The message-port path assigns `code`; the hook path leaves the stack message field unset before `CallHook()`. Scoped the finding to `SNA_Hook` subscribers and documented the indeterminate ScreenDepth flags; no UI/API operation was run. Source-only.

DisplayAlert encoded-record alignment candidate recheck (GD5955 confirmed; 2026-10-25): re-read `requester_makebody()` and the public DisplayAlert input layout. Its UWORD coordinate dereference is performed at each record start; parser advancement is `text length + 5`, so an even-length line makes the next coordinate odd-aligned when the first record is aligned. The m68k-amiga ROM manifest selects Intuition, and odd word access faults on classic m68k. Expanded the report with exact trigger, consequence, and architecture scope. No alert or fault was run. Source-only.

OpenScreen decorator-construction candidate recheck (GD5956 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced the selected non-SKINS OpenScreen call into `int_LoadDecorator()`, where `ScrDecorObj = NewObjectA(...)` is followed by unconditional `GetAttr()`. Verified `GetAttr()` invokes the `OOP_DoMethod` macro, which obtains `o_Class` through the supplied object pointer. A NULL constructor result therefore dereferences NULL before the failure can propagate to OpenScreen. Added explicit non-SKINS and constructor-failure scope to the report. No allocation failure or screen open was induced. Source-only.

X11 hardware cursor allocation candidate recheck (GD5957 confirmed; 2026-10-25): verified `X11SOFTMOUSE=0` in the local X11 header, the matching Xcursor function table and hardware-cursor capability advertisement, then traced `SetCursorShape()` from the returned `XcursorImageCreate()` pointer directly to `image->pixels` and hotspot writes with no NULL test. Scoped the finding to the default hardware-cursor path; the software-mouse compile-time branch bypasses it. No host allocation failure or cursor update was induced. Source-only.

X11 display visual-copy allocation candidate recheck (GD5958 confirmed; 2026-10-25): distinguished the checked host `XGetVisualInfo()` result from the separate unchecked `AllocMem()` for persistent `xsd->vi`. The latter is immediately used as the `memcpy()` destination, then as the source of later display setup state. Scoped the trigger to successful host query plus failed AROS allocation during hosted X11 initialization. No X11 startup or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

X11 host-library init rollback candidate recheck (GD5959 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced libc-load failure after `x11_handle` has been installed globally. The callback manually closes the handle and leaves the global non-NULL; the generic generated init failure path calls the EXPUNGELIB set, whose X11 host-library expunge callback closes that non-NULL handle again. Verified rollback ordering in `compiler/autoinit/functions.c` and `set_call_libfuncs()` failure semantics in `compiler/libinit/libinit.c`. HostLib behavior on the second close remains external and untested. Source-only.

X11 VidMode-list ownership candidate recheck (GD5960 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced the `USE_VIDMODE` query through `x11_fullscreen_supported()` and its startup caller. A successful mode-list query with count zero or one stores the allocated list in static `videomodes`, returns unsupported, and has no matching XFree path; source references show later consumption only on the supported path. Scoped the leak to successful queries returning fewer than two modes and noted repeated-check overwrite as conditional. No host VidMode query was run. Source-only.

X11 bitmap class-hint allocation candidate recheck (GD5961 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced successful window creation into the class-hint setup. `XAllocClassHint()` is followed by two field writes with no NULL check, before `XSetClassHint()`. Scoped the finding to successful X window creation plus failed class-hint allocation. No X11 window or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

X11 bitmap class-hint ownership candidate recheck (GD5962 confirmed; 2026-10-25): searched the complete `x11gfx_onbitmap.c` for the class-hint pointer and XFree calls. The allocated structure is populated and passed to `XSetClassHint()` but never freed. Checked the Xlib API contract: `XAllocClassHint()` storage is released with `XFree()`, and setting the property does not transfer ownership. Added the documented ownership and per-window trigger to the report. No host window was created. Source-only.

X11 framebuffer icon-pixmap ownership candidate recheck (GD5963 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced `init_icon()` creation through its local return value into `XSetWMHints()`, then followed framebuffer disposal. The pixmap ID is not stored in the instance layout, and disposal destroys windows plus the framebuffer drawable/colormap but does not free the icon pixmap. Scoped the leak to nonzero icon pixmap results and disposal while the shared X connection persists. No X11 window or disposal was run. Source-only.

X11 PseudoColor icon-cell ownership candidate recheck (GD5964 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced the PseudoColor icon pixel loop and checked the selected host-library function table. Successful `XAllocColor()` calls feed drawing but their pixel IDs are not accumulated or released; `XFreeColors()` is not loaded. Verified the Xlib contract that callers release allocated cells and that duplicate allocations by one client increment the shared-cell allocation count. Scoped the issue to PseudoColor icon creation and successful allocations. No host display or icon was used. Source-only.

X11 clipboard-port startup rollback candidate recheck (GD5965 confirmed, conditional; 2026-10-25): traced event-task startup ordering, clipboard `CreateMsgPort()`/`AddPort("HOST_CLIPBOARD")`, the parent `initclasses()` failure rollback, and task-exit cleanup. The worker signals ready before publishing the clipboard port; if the port is published before the parent signals kill, exit deletes only the notification port and leaves the named clipboard port in the system list. Recorded the race window and conditional no-consumer consequence in the report. No startup failure or client request was induced. Source-only.

X11 clipboard large-selection candidate recheck (GD5966 confirmed and refined; 2026-10-25): traced both XA_STRING and UTF8_STRING selection-request branches. XA_STRING calculates an XMaxRequestSize-derived threshold but comments out the comparison and hardcodes the one-request branch; the fallback is TODO. UTF8_STRING also sends one replacement. Both paths send SelectionNotify with the property after XChangeProperty without observing asynchronous property errors. Checked ICCCM selection-owner requirements for INCR and error-confirmed SelectionNotify. Replaced the older "larger than one property request" wording with server-limit-dependent trigger and consequence; no transfer was run. Source-only.

X11 shared-memory `shmat()` sentinel candidate recheck (GD5967 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced `shmget()` success into the `shmat()` result check. The code rejects NULL only, while the host API returns `(void *)-1` on failure; that value passes into `XShmAttach()` and is returned as accepted state if the server attach succeeds. Traced the stored address onward into `XShmCreateImage()`. Documented the POSIX/System V return contract and kept the final consequence conditional on XShmAttach behavior. No shared-memory failure or X11 image operation was induced. Source-only.

X11 shared-memory duplicate image-read candidate recheck (GD5968 confirmed; 2026-10-25): read `get_xshm_ximage()` and its bitmap image-read callers. Each helper call performs XSync followed by two identical XShmGetImage calls, discarding the first result; the helper is called once for each scanline chunk, including temporary-pixmap fallback. Scoped as redundant per-chunk server work and status loss; no performance benchmark or image read was run. Source-only.

X11 HIDD startup input-driver registration candidate recheck (GD5969 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced `X11_Startup()` object creation and both `HW_AddDriver()` calls against keyboard, mouse, Hidd_Input, and HW class/interface declarations. The passed objects are `CLID_Hidd_Kbd`/`CLID_Hidd_Mouse`, subclasses of `CLID_Hidd_Input` exposing `Hidd_Input`, while `HW_AddDriver` belongs to `CLID_HW`; neither consumer class declares the HW interface. OOP dispatch returns zero for missing methods, so keyboard registration yields NULL, mouse registration is skipped, and startup returns FALSE before display-driver registration. No startup was run. Source-only.

X11 keymap generator auto-repeat state candidate recheck (GD5970 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-25): searched all `XAutoRepeat*`, keyboard-control queries and exits in `makexkeytable.c`. The generator disables repeat without saving prior state, turns it on on normal completion and in the IO-error handler, and exits on output-open/short-write errors before that normal restoration. Confirmed the `change-x11keymaptable` target invokes the tool. Report now distinguishes prior-off state corruption from error exits that leave repeat disabled. No utility or host setting was run. Source-only.

X11 keymap generator final-stream-error candidate recheck (GD5971 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced the 256-byte `fwrite()` check through `fclose()` and process exit. Full `fwrite()` count is checked, but `fclose()` result is ignored before `exit(0)`, leaving delayed buffered write/flush/close errors unreported. Scoped the trigger to late stream errors after the complete count. No file error or generation was induced. Source-only.

X11 keymap generator build-target scope correction (GD5970/GD5971 retained; 2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): rechecked `arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/mmakefile.src:57-82` and the selected X11 HIDD dependencies. The ordinary `x11keymaptable` prerequisite copies checked-in mapping assets; it does not run `makexkeytable`. Only the explicit `change-x11keymaptable` target invokes the interactive host utility. GD5970 and GD5971 therefore apply when a user explicitly runs that target/tool, not during routine hosted-X11 HIDD builds. Both findings remain valid for that opt-in configuration; no host utility or setting was used.

WinGDI User32 host-resource expunge candidate recheck (GD5972 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced successful GDI, User32 and native interface/handle acquisitions into `gdi_hostlib_expunge()`. Expunge releases GDI and native globals but omits both `user_func` interface drop and `user_handle` close; no later cleanup reference exists on the successful path. Scoped to MinGW WinGDI expunge after successful initialization. No host DLL lifecycle was run. Source-only.

Cocoa keyboard callback argument candidate recheck (GD5973 confirmed; 2026-10-25): matched the Cocoa keyboard class callback type and `cocoa_input_poll()` invocation against the public Hidd keyboard IRQ handler contract and InputHW event forwarding. The poller passes a UWORD rawkey as the callback's second argument; consumers expect a pointer to `pHidd_Kbd_Event` and receive the value unchanged through `InputHW__CallBackFunc()`. Scoped to recognized key events with registered consumers. No Cocoa event was run. Source-only.

Cocoa input-poller process creation candidate recheck (GD5974 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced successful driver registration through `CreateNewProc(ptags)` and startup's unconditional continuation to resident success. The returned process pointer is ignored; the poller is the only selected path draining the host event ring and calling input callbacks. Scoped to process-creation failure after driver registration. No process failure or input event was induced. Source-only.

Cocoa poller DOS-open failure candidate recheck (GD5975 confirmed; 2026-10-25): re-read the full process entry and its creation caller. The task's own `OpenLibrary()` result is tested only to decide whether to call `Delay(1)`; when NULL, the unconditional infinite poll loop has no wait/backoff/exit. The creator's earlier DOS open is a separate reference and is closed after `CreateNewProc()`, so it does not ensure the worker's second open succeeds. No DOS open failure was induced. Source-only.

LinuxFB nested-display construction cleanup candidate recheck (GD5976 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced `LinuxFBGfx__Root__New()` from superclass object creation through `OOP_NewObject()` for the nested display. Failure cleanup unmaps framebuffer memory and closes the device but does not dispose the superclass-created graphics object. The nested constructor can return NULL when its input framebuffer metadata is absent or `get_pixfmt()` rejects a reported visual/storage format; OOP_NewObject propagates the method's NULL result without reclaiming unrelated partial objects, and HW_AddDriver frees only its failed DriverNode. Confirmed the leaked outer instance and conditional trigger; no framebuffer was opened. Source-only.

LinuxFB DirectColor gamma scaling candidate recheck (GD5977 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-25): traced `r_step/g_step/b_step` derivation into `SetGamma()` indexing and `FBIOPUTCMAP`. Components of 9–15 bits produce a zero step and repeatedly sample source index 255; a 16-bit maximum also makes `1 << bits` truncate into the UWORD `scale_size` as zero, skipping the write loop while returning TRUE. Recorded both arithmetic cases and the conditional framebuffer-format scope. No gamma operation or ioctl was run. Source-only.

LinuxFB console-mode restore and tty-lifetime candidate recheck (GD5978 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced console open/mode changes in `LinuxFBDisplay__Hidd_Display__CreateObject()` through nested bitmap failure and the registered reset callback. The failure return has no rollback. On display removal, `LinuxFBGfx__Root__Dispose()` removes the callback before cleanup; `cleanup_linuxfb()` unmaps framebuffer memory and closes only the framebuffer fd, not the console fd or modes. Confirmed the conditional leaked tty descriptor and lost restore path. No console ioctl or display removal was run. Source-only.

IntelGMA EDID failure-path candidate recheck (GD5979 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-25): traced both duplicated EDID consumers, `probe_monitor()` and `G45_parse_ddc()`. Each destination is uninitialized stack storage; each ignores the `WriteRead` BOOL and checks checksum/header anyway. Verified the I2C device wrapper returns the transaction status and the I2C master reports failed transfers as FALSE. A false-valid buffer changes VGA/LVDS selection in startup; the mode enumerator can also add timings from it. Kept false acceptance conditional on residual bytes after failed/partial transfer. No I2C or display path was run. Source-only.

IntelGMA solid-line narrow arithmetic candidate recheck (GD5980 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-25): re-read `DrawLine()` against the public `gfx.conf` signature (`WORD` endpoints). Confirmed 16-bit delta/error narrowing in the accelerated path, the 20,000-pixel slope-step overflow, horizontal/vertical exclusive-end loop boundary, and generic `WORD i <= dx` counter wrap at `dx == 32767`. Rechecked that clipping only rejects fully disjoint bounds and otherwise leaves rasterization loops at full span. Patterned and non-framebuffer paths dispatch to superclass. Target narrowing behavior remains unexecuted. Source-only.

IntelGMA displayable-bitmap fallback allocation candidate recheck (GD5981 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced `AllocBitmapArea()`'s `-1` sentinel into the displayable branch. The fallback stores `AllocMem()` directly in `bm->framebuffer`, sets `fbgfx = FALSE`, and returns the object without checking NULL; normal `OOP_NewObject()` therefore reports success. Disposal would pass the NULL pointer to `FreeMem()`, but no constructor rollback is attempted on this return path, so the object is exposed to subsequent bitmap operations. No allocation failure or bitmap operation was induced. Source-only.

IntelGMA DDC helper/bus ownership candidate recheck (GD5982 confirmed; 2026-10-25): traced the non-LVDS I2C bus and `CLID_Hidd_I2CDevice` helper through DDC parsing and `Root::New()` success/failure. The helper is only used by `G45_parse_ddc()` and is never disposed; the successfully created I2C bus transfers to `gfxdata->i2cobj` only after superclass graphics construction returns non-NULL, with no cleanup on the NULL return. Confirmed the helper object's normal OOP allocation path. No I2C device was created. Source-only.

IntelGMA mode-tag allocation candidate recheck (GD5983 confirmed; 2026-10-25): verified the two initial pool allocations are immediately dereferenced at mode-tag initialization, with no NULL test. Re-read `PUSH_TAG()` and its detailed-timing/LVDS callsites: it writes tag and data fields through the supplied current pointer; all temporary mode-description allocations are passed to `snprintf()` without checks. Confirmed the distinct failure triggers by branch; no allocation failure or DDC parse was induced. Source-only.

IntelGMA display-class startup gate and failure-unwind candidates recheck (GD5984-GD5985 confirmed; 2026-10-25): verified `IntelG45DisplayClass` creation is optional in the nested startup gates and is not part of the condition before `G45_Init()`/class registration. On later HIDD construction, `OOP_NewObject(NULL, NULL, ...)` returns NULL; graphics `Root::New()` still retains/returns the gfx object, and graphics registration logs a missing default display without failing driver setup. Separately traced the cleanup ladder: after display-class construction, later bitmap/I2C/compositor class or hardware-init failure disposes compositor, I2C, bitmap and gfx classes but omits the display class. No allocation failure or graphics startup was induced. Source-only.


MUI Application and Configdata IFF save failure re-review (GD5087/GD5088 fleshed out; 2026-10-25): traced both serializers from `MODE_NEWFILE` through PRHD/data chunk writes and CloseIFF, then through the selected DOS IFF hook and `WriteStream`/`WriteChunkBytes` error propagation. Confirmed Application Save ignores its PRHD/DataSpace/chunk/finalization results and always returns zero after truncating the destination (GD5087). Confirmed Configdata `SavePrefsHeader()` tests `WriteChunkBytes()` as a Boolean, so a negative `IFFERR_WRITE` is truthy; the outer Configdata serializer also ignores Dataspace, PopChunk and CloseIFF errors and always returns zero (GD5088). Traced selected Zune Preferences saves to ENV and ENVARC targets. No filesystem operation or I/O failure was run; source-only.


MUI Configdata parse/import failure and Zune apply/save caller trace (GD5089 fleshed out; 2026-10-25): followed `Configdata__OM_NEW()` ENV/ENVARC/global selection into `Configdata__MUIM_Load()`, `ParseIFF()`, and `MUIM_Dataspace_ReadIFF()`. Confirmed the load clears Dataspace before parsing, leaves `res` true for parser termination errors, and ignores ReadIFF allocation/error returns; the true result suppresses fallback. Traced Zune `main_open_menu()` through ConfigToGadgets and `test_prefs()` to `save_prefs(..., FALSE)`, which writes the resulting values to ENV. Documented this with Configdata getter/default initialization and the separate startup fallback consequence in GD5089. No file, parser error, allocation failure, UI action or save was run; source-only.


MUIScreen descriptor allocator failure-path and selected-caller pass (GD5090 confirmed, 2026-10-25): read the complete `MUIS_AllocPubScreenDesc()` body (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/allocpubscreendesc.c:47-102`). `AllocMem()` is unchecked; the non-NULL-source branch passes its result as the `CopyMem()` destination, and the NULL-source branch copies default strings and writes descriptor fields through it. Traced all in-tree calls: `MUIS_ReadPubFile()` (`readpubfile.c:93`), PSI palette preset (`editpanel_class.c:387`), screen copy (`screenpanel_class.c:152`), and List construct hook (`screenlist_class.c:63`). Their checks occur only after the helper returns, so none can recover from the internal dereference. Expanded GD5090 with both branches, triggers, consequence, callers, and confidence. This is a targeted failure-path/caller trace and does not add duplicate full-body credit to the already credited MUIScreen body. No allocation failure or caller was run; source-only.


Configdata public-screen descriptor list allocation failure and caller pass (GD5091 confirmed, 2026-10-25): re-read `Configdata_LoadPubScreens()` and descriptor cleanup (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/configdata.c:778-791,1316-1343`). It disposes the old list, opens the public-screen file, gets each allocated descriptor, then dereferences an unchecked `AllocVec(sizeof(struct Node), MEMF_CLEAR)` result at `:1333-1337`; on failure the task faults and the just-read descriptor is not released. Traced entry from successful preference load (`:1287-1289`) and filesystem notification setup (`:601-614`), and the later window fallback query (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:459-468`). Confirmed Configdata's selected builtin registration and its full-body review in the ledger. Expanded GD5091 with trigger, impact, selected callers, and confidence. This is a targeted failure-path/caller trace and adds no duplicate full-body credit. No allocation failure, public-screen file, or notification was exercised; source-only.


MUIS_OpenPubFile acquisition/unwind and selected-caller pass (GD5092 confirmed, 2026-10-25): read the full `MUIS_OpenPubFile()` body (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/openpubfile.c:47-93`) and `MUIS_ClosePubFile()` cleanup (`closepubfile.c:47-57`). Failure after `AllocIFF()`, after DOS `Open()`, after `OpenIFF()`, or during new-file FORM/PRHD/header setup returns NULL without releasing acquired resources. All in-tree callers (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/configdata.c:1331`; `workbench/prefs/PSI/screenlist_class.c:150,183`; `workbench/prefs/Zune/systemp.c:88`) perform normal close only for a non-NULL handle and cannot recover the hidden resources. Expanded GD5092 with staged resource ownership and selected callers; write-file truncation/content consequences remain separately covered by the save-path candidate. This is a targeted body/caller trace and does not add full-body credit because the MUIScreen body is already credited. No file, IFF, or failure path was exercised; source-only.


PSI public-screen save finalization status and GUI caller pass (GD5093 confirmed, 2026-10-25): traced `ScreenList_Save()` through `MUIS_ClosePubFile()` and both finish/Save As callers (`workbench/prefs/PSI/screenlist_class.c:174-202`; `workbench/libs/muiscreen/closepubfile.c:47-57`; `workbench/prefs/PSI/mainwindow_class.c:57-68,179-189`). `ScreenList_Save()` sets TRUE after open and successful descriptor writes, then invokes a void close helper; the helper ignores `PopChunk()` status, and both UI callers discard the method result. Thus a failure finalizing the outer IFF chunk can leave an incomplete file while the save method returns success and GUI flow gives no result. Distinguished this from per-descriptor write failure, which does clear the method result. Expanded GD5093; no finalization error or save was induced. Source-only.


MUIScreen fixed-width descriptor string validation and PSI list display pass (GD5096 re-established, 2026-10-25): traced IFF record size/read handling and `Name` copy (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/readpubfile.c:55-70`; fixed fields in `fileformat.h:31-39`) into PSI `ScreenList_Load()` and its registered `ScreenList_DisplayFunc()` (`workbench/prefs/PSI/screenlist_class.c:93-117,144-167,330-335`). The reader accepts a full record without checking that `Name` contains NUL; the display hook concatenates it with `strcat()` into `buf1[PSD_MAXLEN_NAME+2]`. For malformed records whose adjacent fixed-width fields also lack an early NUL, the scan and output exceed their respective bounds; display markers further reduce output capacity. Replaced GD5096's unrecovered placeholder with this source-supported conditional finding. Separate EditWindow title use of imported names (historical GD5167) remains to be independently reconciled. No file or GUI was loaded; source-only.


PSI EditWindow imported-name title construction and caller pass (GD5167 re-established, 2026-10-25): traced selected List entry through `ScreenPanel_Edit()`'s `MUIA_EditWindow_Title` tag to `EditWindow_New()` (`workbench/prefs/PSI/screenpanel_class.c:80-97`; `editwindow_class.c:24-28,59-63`). The constructor copies a localized prefix into the 148-byte `wtitle` and uses unbounded `strcat()` on the descriptor name. `MUIS_ReadPubFile()` copies all 32 fixed-width name bytes without termination validation (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/readpubfile.c:61-70`), and the adjacent title/font/background arrays can also be nonterminated, so a complete malformed record can extend the source past the destination capacity. Expanded GD5167 as the separate EditWindow consumer of the fixed-width input defect also recorded at GD5096; ordinary names fit, and the trigger requires malformed imported fields. No file or GUI was opened; source-only.


MUIScreen public-screen node lifetime and close caller pass (GD5098 confirmed, 2026-10-25): traced `MUIS_ClosePubScreen()`'s list lookup and post-unlock use (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/closepubscreen.c:58-98`) against Intuition `LockPubScreenList()`/`UnlockPubScreenList()` semaphore implementation (`rom/intuition/lockpubscreenlist.c:46-51`; `unlockpubscreenlist.c:44-48`) and `CloseScreen()` removal/free under that lock (`rom/intuition/closescreen.c:147-155,331-348`). After releasing the list semaphore, MUIScreen retains and dereferences `pubscrnode`; a concurrent successful close can remove/free it in that gap. Traced checked-in PSI close action and CLI callers (`workbench/prefs/PSI/screenpanel_class.c:217-221`; `psi.c:378-383`). Expanded GD5098 with the exact synchronization/lifetime edge and conditional trigger. No concurrent close or screen operation was run; source-only.


MUIScreen close failure/autoclose tracking and PSI caller pass (GD5097 confirmed, 2026-10-25): traced `MUIS_ClosePubScreen()` (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/closepubscreen.c:73-98`) to selected Intuition `CloseScreen()`'s documented/implemented FALSE return when windows remain (`rom/intuition/closescreen.c:105-113`). MUIScreen first marks the screen private and removes/frees its AutoClose tracking node (`closepubscreen.c:77-87`), ignores the close result, and returns TRUE. Its worker only closes no-window screens still in `muisb_autocScreens` (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/muiscreen_init.c:78-88`), so failed close leaves the screen private and untracked after its windows later close. PSI's button and CLI callers interpret/report the helper's TRUE result (`workbench/prefs/PSI/screenpanel_class.c:215-223`; `psi.c:378-383`). Expanded GD5097; this is separate from GD5098's stale PubScreenNode race. No screen/window was operated; source-only.


MUIScreen default-descriptor screen-lock release and PSI caller pass (GD5104 confirmed, 2026-10-25): traced `MUIS_AllocPubScreenDesc(NULL)` (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/allocpubscreendesc.c:55-72,98-102`) through PSI's Clone Workbench Palette menu action (`workbench/prefs/PSI/editpanel_class.c:376-402`). The allocator calls `LockPubScreen(NULL)` and returns without `UnlockPubScreen()`. Selected Intuition LockPubScreen increments `psn_VisitorCount` (`rom/intuition/lockpubscreen.c:130-150`); UnlockPubScreen decrements it and signals the owner on zero (`unlockpubscreen.c:83-107`). Thus each palette clone leaks one visitor lock and can block eventual close of an auto-close screen. Re-established GD5104 and distinguished it from GD5090's allocation-failure dereference. No palette action or screen close was run; source-only.

GD5421 detailed source and SMP scheduling recheck (2026-10-25): reconstructed the report entry from current source. `WaitTOF()` uses a stack node with `AddTail`/`Remove` under local-only `Disable()`; the VBlank `ForeachNode()` reads `ln_Succ` after calling `Signal()`. ExecSMP Signal can schedule an affinity-bound waiter on a different CPU, so the waiter may remove and return its stack node before CPU 0 advances the interrupt traversal. Concurrent callers can also interleave shared tail-link writes. Revalidated the selected Raspberry Pi package includes graphics.library and timer, its AArch64 kernel includes `kernel_execsmp`, and the BCM2711/2712 timer causes VBlank only on CPU 0 while other cores are schedulable. Kept default packaging of portable Workbench callers unconfirmed; the finding is scoped to public API use on this selected SMP configuration. No VBlank or schedule was run; source-only.


GD5422 pending DBufInfo queue interleaving recheck (2026-10-25): reconstructed the candidate from `internal_QueueDBufInfo()` and `TOF_VBlank()`. Queue insertion stores `dbi_Link1` then publishes the head; VBlank independently unlinks the head through `link`, clears its link/count, and replies both messages. Local-only `Disable()` does not serialize CPU 0 with another ExecSMP CPU. Traced Intuition `ChangeScreenBuffer()` into `ChangeVPBitMap()` and `FreeScreenBuffer()` waiting for `dbi_SafeMessage` before freeing the screen buffer. Identified interleavings that can overwrite the new head (losing its replies) or publish a new head linked to an already replied/cleared DBufInfo (allowing repeat traversal). The selected Raspberry Pi 4/5 package includes graphics.library and timer; the BCM2711/2712 scheduler drives VBlank on CPU 0. Replaced the report placeholder with exact source paths and qualified the trigger to concurrent SMP swaps. No screen-buffer operation or interrupt was run; source-only.

SDL bitmap color-expansion candidate recheck (GD5716/GD5717 retained; GD9692 added; GD5718 remains withdrawn; 2026-10-25): reread the complete `BlitColorExpansion` method and public HIDD contract (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdlgfx_bitmapclass.c:584-708`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:4220-4248`). SDL bitmap image-surface failure-contract scope check (no additional GD; 2026-10-25): traced `PutImage`, `GetImage`, and `PutAlphaImage` results from `SDL_CreateRGBSurfaceFrom()` into `SDL_BlitSurface()` and `SDL_FreeSurface()` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdlgfx_bitmapclass.c:430-455,501-523,717-735`). The selected graphics cursor caller invokes `HIDD_BM_PutAlphaImage()` during cursor draw (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:187`), and generic drawing helpers call `PutImage`/`GetImage` (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:435-459`). SDL `Native32` image-pitch caller reconciliation (GD9693 disposition: no new finding; 2026-10-25): re-read SDL bitmap `PutImage()` pitch construction and `Native32` post-creation `BytesPerPixel` override (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdlgfx_bitmapclass.c:376-449`), the public HIDD `PutImage` contract (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:2781-2818`), and all in-tree `HIDD_BM_PutImage()` expressions. Graphics Area scanline upper-bound follow-up (GD9698 added, 2026-10-25): rechecked the already body-read `areafillpolygon()` loops and `AreaEnd()` caller. `WORD` is signed 16-bit (`exec/types.h:58-62`); both scanline loops compare this variable with inclusive `bounds->MaxY` (`areafill.c:105-111,167-170`). `AreaEnd()` closes a four-vertex polygon, computes inclusive bounds, verifies TmpRas capacity, then calls the fill (`areaend.c:88-90,115-140`). A 2×2 rectangle spanning y=32766..32767 reaches the convex path with a 4-byte mask; after y=32767, increment conversion remains representable only as a `WORD`, so the inclusive comparison cannot become false. ### BoingIconBar screen-lock/remap failure and caller pass (GD5692 re-established; 2026-10-25)
Read `workbench/tools/BoingIconBar/iconbar.c` around `ReadPrefs()`, `OpenMainWindow()`, `ScreenResetRestore()`, `HandleScreenNotify()` and relevant open/reopen callers, plus the complete `LayoutIconA()` setup/cleanup portion in `workbench/libs/icon/layouticon.c`. Confirmed that an unsuccessful `LockPubScreen(NULL)` leaves `MyScreen` NULL; with `Icon_Remap` enabled, `OpenMainWindow()` still calls `LayoutIcon(icon, NULL, NULL)` and then tries `OpenWindowTags()` on the default public screen. `LayoutIconA()` releases cached remapped bitmaps/pen allocations, clears `ni_Screen`, and returns TRUE for a NULL screen. GD5692 is therefore retained at medium confidence, conditional on a transient lock failure coinciding with successful default-screen window creation. The source transition notification path was traced, but no rendering or timing was exercised. This pass closes this candidate's evidence gap only; broader Graphics/Desktop inventory and callers remain open.

### Zune Preferences Save As filename bound and helper pass (GD5690 re-established; 2026-10-25)
Reconciled `workbench/prefs/Zune/mmakefile.src`, the Save As menu hook in `zune.c`, and the selected helper `zunestuff.c`. `aslfilerequest()` documents 1,000-byte full-path output, copies directory/file components up to 498 bytes each, and joins them with `AddPart(..., 998)`; the Save As caller then uses unbounded `strcat(filename, ".prefs")` for paths lacking that substring. A near-capacity selected path can therefore overrun the 1,000-byte static destination; this append precedes the configdata allocation check. GD5690 is retained with medium-high source confidence; exact `AddPart()` boundary behavior and a file requester selection were not run. This is focused caller/helper coverage, not a full Zune Preferences target audit.

### GD5690 AddPart capacity contract follow-up (2026-10-25)
Checked the selected `rom/dos/addpart.c` implementation: `AddPart()` computes required bytes including the final NUL and accepts only when the result is `<= size` (`:119-143`). With caller size 998, output can be 997 path characters plus NUL. `main_saveas_menu()` then appends the six-character `.prefs` suffix and NUL into the 1,000-byte array, requiring up to 1,004 bytes. This confirms a concrete 4-byte overrun at the helper's maximum successful output; GD5690 confidence is raised to high. No requester was run.

### QuickPart Delete/AddFree allocation-failure caller pass (GD5689 re-established; 2026-10-25)
Reconciled selected `workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src`, `QP_ccApp.c`'s Delete action and `QP_ccPartitionContainer.c`'s AddFree method. Delete checks allocation of its bookkeeping node but not the free-space MUI object stored in `PCCN_ChildObj`, then passes the node into AddFree. In the non-merge case AddFree links the node and calls `OM_ADDMEMBER` with that possibly NULL object; the operation is still queued. In a merge case the passed node is neither linked nor freed after its extent is copied into an existing free node. GD5689 is retained at medium confidence; MUI's handling of a NULL member was not exercised, while model/UI inconsistency and merge-path allocation leak follow from selected source. No allocation failure or GUI was run.

### Generic gfx HIDD buffered-operation scratch sizing and caller pass (GD5687 re-established; 2026-10-25)
Re-read `DoBufferedOperation()` in `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c` and traced all five call sites. It sets 4,096 rows from `PIXBUFBYTES >> 2`, clamps only to request height, and multiplies rows by full-width 32-bit row size. Thus 1,920x1,080 requests allocate 8,294,400 bytes (7.91 MiB) in one scratch buffer, and 3,840x2,160 requests allocate 33,177,600 bytes (31.64 MiB), despite the nominal 16,384-byte constant. Allocation failure retries one row; the duplicate correctness effect when both allocations fail remains in GD5732. GD5687 is retained for avoidable large per-call memory consumption, high confidence in calculation and medium workload impact. No graphics operation or allocation was run.

### QuickPart storage attribute-base failure and enumeration pass (GD5688 re-established; 2026-10-25)
Read selected QuickPart startup/manifest and traced `OOP_ObtainAttrBases(storage_abd)` in `QP_Main.c` into `FindDisks()`/`unitenumFunc()` in `QP_FindDisks.c`. Caller ignores the Boolean result. In selected `rom/oop/obtainattrbases.c`, failed acquisition leaves the requested base zero and returns FALSE; subsequent unit type queries use that base, ignore `OOP_GetAttr()`'s return, and the supported-unit test accepts only fixed, SSD or RAID values. The generic root `Get` implementation writes zero to the output storage, so units are skipped; `FindDisks()` returns zero and startup continues as an empty device list. GD5688 is retained at medium-high source confidence. No attribute-base failure or GUI was run.

Read `LoadTextAsIFF()` and traced successful-load callers plus `LoadAsAscII()` and TDTA buffer getters. For each CHRS chunk, code records the declared full size, ignores `ReadChunkBytes()`'s returned byte count, and reports success when allocation exists. The loaded parser later consumes the full recorded span; public TDTA_Buffer/BufferLen getters expose it. Compared selected ILBM datatype code, which checks `ReadChunkBytes()` against the requested body length, confirming the API's count-based short-read contract. GD5684 is retained at high source confidence; no short read/truncated file was run. GD5683 allocation-failure candidate remains to be re-reviewed separately.

### Text datatype CHRS growth-allocation failure and subsequent-chunk pass (GD5683 re-established; 2026-10-25)
Re-read the full `LoadTextAsIFF()` CHRS loop and traced its DTF_IFF load caller. On growth `AllocVec(pre_size + add_size)` failure, the function frees the old allocation and clears only the pointer, retaining the old `buffer_allocated_len`. A later CHRS iteration then allocates only its own `add_size` but uses the stale nonzero `pre_size` as the destination offset and records the combined length. If that later allocation succeeds, `ReadChunkBytes()` writes past its end. GD5683 is retained at high source confidence; trigger requires a later chunk's growth allocation to fail and a subsequent smaller allocation to succeed. No allocation failure or IFF load was run. Distinct from GD5684's ignored short-read result.

### BoingIconBar oversize-icon range mutation and menu caller pass (GD5679 re-established; 2026-10-25)
Reconciled selected BoingIconBar target and `SetWindowParameters()` with `Show_Selected_Level()`/menu selection. A width overflow truncates the current range and assigns the next level's beginning to the current icon index. If that icon is first in its range, the next level begins on the same too-wide icon; its pass repeats the failure and moves the next boundary back to that index. This can propagate across later levels, leaving them empty; current-level display uses adjacent level beginnings as its bounds. GD5679 is retained at high source confidence. No preferences file with an oversized icon or GUI was used.

### Picture datatype chunky-buffer/PDTA_BitMap cache consistency pass (GD5672 re-established; 2026-10-25)
Traced selected `PDT_WritePixelArray()`, `PDTA_BitMap` OM_GET, and `ConvertChunky2Bitmap()`. Same-format writes update only `SrcBuffer` and set `Layouted = FALSE`; a prior lazy `SrcBM` is neither freed nor refreshed. The getter returns existing `SrcBM` without reconversion. Thus the supported sequence write → get source bitmap → same-format write → get source bitmap exposes stale bitmap pixels, while layout/read-pixel code uses current source buffer. Retain GD5672 at medium-high confidence, scoped to clients combining both interfaces; repository search did not identify an in-tree caller performing that exact sequence. No datatype or bitmap operation was run.

### Picture bitmap-to-chunky width narrowing and consumers (historical GD5671; consolidated into GD9804; 2026-10-25)
Traced AROS `ConvertBitmap2Chunky()` through `ReadPixelLine8()` to `ReadPixelArray8()` and its early invalid-range check. The source bitmap header width is ULONG/UWORD-sized at the caller, while the API width is signed WORD. At width 32,769 on the supported 16-bit signed representation, it narrows to -32,767; endpoint calculation produces -32,768 from xstart 0, so ReadPixelArray8 returns zero. The converter ignores the result, advances the destination offset, and returns success; its `AllocSrcBuffer()` allocation is not cleared. Both asynchronous layout and PDTM_READPIXELARRAY consume that buffer. This same picture caller was later included in GD9804 along with animation and MUI bitmap callers; GD5671 was a duplicate ID and has been removed from the report/index. No wide bitmap was converted.


### BoingIconBar preference notification wakeup recheck (GD5670 re-established; 2026-10-25)
Traced preference `StartNotify()` setup, `BIBport` draining at the top of the main loop, both visible-window and no-window branches, optional focus-timer setup failure, and timer rearming (`workbench/tools/BoingIconBar/iconbar.c:368-397,425-446,518-635`). The visible-window `Wait()` omits the preference port signal; if timer setup fails, the application still starts with `FocusMask == 0`, and no other event is required to arrive. A queued preference notification therefore remains pending until an unrelated selected event wakes the loop. Kept GD5670 with the timer-failure condition and unbounded idle delay stated explicitly; with the timer active the delay is ordinarily bounded by its 100 ms tick. No timer failure, notification or GUI event was induced. Source-only.

### NList temporary wrap-line insertion failure-path pass (GD9721 added; 2026-10-25)

Reviewed `NL_InsertTmpLine()` in `NList_func2.c` and its selected caller `NL_DoWrapLine()` in `NList_mcc4.c`. In-capacity insertion shifts pointers before `AllocTypeEntry()`; failure returns without restoring the array or changing the active count, so the active list can contain a duplicate and omit its former final row. Capacity-growth insertion likewise publishes `NList_First`/`LastEntry` before the entry allocation and leaves those values changed when the new pointer array is freed. Added GD9721 for this non-transactional failure path. This is a targeted function/caller pass only: no full-file line credit is claimed, and all other `NList_func2.c` methods and broader target coverage remain open. No allocation failure or GUI operation was run; source-only.

Wanderer drawer ToolType snapshot-allocation caller pass (GD9771 added; 2026-10-25): traced `IconWindow_StoreSettings()`'s array/string copy loop into `PutDiskObject()` and the selected icon serializer. `StrDup()` returns NULL on `AllocVec()` failure; because the destination array is cleared, an unchecked failed element becomes an early NULL terminator while the loop continues filling later slots. Both selected serialization formats stop at the first NULL: AOS `ProcessToolTypes()` counts and writes the prefix, while PNG `WriteIconChunk()` emits attributes until the NULL pointer. Normal `PutDiskObject()` output opens in `MODE_NEWFILE`, replacing an existing `.info` file. The selected Snapshot menu calls this store method for both snapshot-one and snapshot-all requests. Rechecked the append at `iconwindow.c:229-232`: failure to duplicate the new `WNDRRSRT` value also leaves an early terminator, so the successful save omits the updated sort preference even when every old ToolType copy succeeded. Expanded GD9771 to include both failure points; it requires a failed copy and a subsequently successful write; no allocation or write was induced. `iconwindow.c` already has full-body credit; this adds caller/serializer evidence only. Source-only.

PSI public-screen file descriptor ownership recheck (GD9479 confirmed and expanded; 2026-10-25): traced MUIS_ReadPubFile()'s allocated return through ScreenList_Load(), PSI's construct/destruct hooks, and selected muimaster List insertion. The hook duplicates the descriptor and List stores/destructs only the constructed copy; the original input is not freed. PSI loses it on successful insertion and on failed insertion (including List setup failure before construction or a NULL construct result). Each successfully read record therefore leaks one descriptor allocation per load; IFF close still occurs. Report now states the ownership boundary, failure cases, consequence, and caller-side fix. No file load or allocation failure was run; source-only.

Wanderer snapshot-all icon-position write-failure pass (GD9775 added; 2026-10-25): traced the snapshot-all loop into `PutIconTagList(ICONPUTA_OnlyUpdatePosition)` and its selected fast writer (`iconwindow.c:1620-1649`; `puticontaglist.c:124-133,152-155`; `support.c:335-348`). This path opens an existing icon with `MODE_OLDFILE`, seeks to X then writes four bytes, then seeks to Y and writes four bytes. The writer returns FALSE on either short write, while DOS `Write()` reports the actual byte count (`rom/dos/write.c:28-43`); Wanderer ignores each return, continues, and ultimately returns TRUE (`iconwindow.c:1661-1669`). The fast path discards `Seek()`'s return before writing coordinate bytes; DOS documents `Seek()` failure as `-1` (`rom/dos/seek.c:25-40`). If the initial seek fails without changing the file position but the handler still accepts the subsequent writes, the coordinate bytes land at the wrong offset and the writer can report success. CursorFB fixed-range candidate platform/mode recheck (GD5731 retained and qualified; 2026-10-25): traced hosted SDL and X11 mode construction into generic sync/display setup. GD9658 display-edge threshold correction (2026-10-25): rechecked CursorFB's caller condition against cursor_Draw() clipping (rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:158-173) and generic PutImage's pixel loop (gfx_bitmapclass.c:2852-2893). The earlier ledger wording implied a bitmap/display width of at least 32,776 pixels, but this is unnecessary: with a 32,768-pixel bitmap and cursor top-left at 32,760, cursor_Draw clips the cursor to the visible final eight pixels. Animation current-frame synchronization recheck (GD9416 detail restored; 2026-10-25): reread the complete `PM_TICK`/`PM_SHUTTLE` hook and tapedeck input update, then compared each access to `afd_FrameCurrent` and the only `afd_AnimFramesLock` critical sections. The player hook and playback task do not acquire that list lock for current-frame/tick access; the UI writes the scrub frame before calling `SetConductorState()`, which later dispatches `PM_SHUTTLE` without that lock. An in-flight `PM_TICK` can therefore overwrite the scrub before the UI snapshots the resulting frame for the conductor update. Expanded GD9416 with this interleaving and limited it to the explicitly buildable optional Animation module; no direct state synchronization was found in the reviewed path. No player, tapedeck, tick or interleaving was run; source-only.

GD9805 bitmap-size trigger confirmation (2026-10-25): traced MUI's LONG dimension tags through selected `AllocBitMap()` to the plain-bitmap metadata assignment. `struct BitMap.Rows` and `.BytesPerRow` are UWORD; `AllocBitMap()` stores the requested row count and computes byte stride from width. Thus a 16x32,768 bitmap is representable at 64 KiB per plane, and a 32,768x1 bitmap is also a modest-area case; both cross the corresponding signed-WORD loop bound in `remap_bitmap()`. This sharpens the previous broad availability caveat: trigger still requires successful source/destination allocation and target signed narrowing, but not a high-area bitmap. No body credit or finding ID changed; no allocation or remapping was run. Source-only.

GD5366 IntelGMA `PutImageLUT` detail restoration and caller-scope recheck (2026-10-25): reconstructed the missing detailed entry from the surviving coverage note and re-read `GMABM__Hidd_BitMap__PutImageLUT`, its method-table registration, generic superclass implementation and the checked-in graphics route (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_bitmapclass.c:1571-1695,2197-2199`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:3924-3991`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:67-85,696-731`). The IntelGMA override dereferences `msg->pixlut->pixels` on `fbgfx` bitmaps before its allocation fallback; for a NULL LUT structure this faults immediately, while the generic superclass handles a missing LUT/table as raw pixel values. A checked-in `WritePixelArray8()` on a plain bitmap obtains the generic cached PlanarBM object, and HIDD `AllocBitMap()` allocates the per-bitmap pixel table for displayable bitmaps; these paths do not establish the null-LUT call into IntelGMA. The explicit IntelGMA target exists, but its parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/mmakefile.src`; `workbench/devs/monitors/mmakefile.src:9`). No HIDD call or hardware operation was run. Source-only.

GD5367 `WritePixelArray8()` maximum-row width recheck (2026-10-25): re-read the public vector, `wp8_render()`, bitmap clipping and generic `PutImageLUT` method (`rom/graphics/writepixelarray8.c:16-45,64-76`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:101-140,680-731,1064-1088`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:3892-3893,3924-3940`). A 32,768-pixel row on a bitmap of that width can be requested with WORD endpoints 0 and 32767 and satisfies the documented array width. After clipping, `wp8_render()` computes 32768 but stores it in signed WORD before passing it to an HIDD method whose width is also WORD; that type cannot represent the positive extent. On low-word conversion targets the result is negative and the generic method returns without writing; exact conversion/manifestation is target-dependent. No in-tree call uses a bitmap this wide; PNG remap and FTManager dimensions are WORD-limited and their checked paths do not establish the trigger. Restored GD5367 from source with medium manifestation confidence and added the master-index summary. No wide bitmap or call was created; source-only.

ReadPixelArray8 width-boundary paired-path recheck (GD4030 retained; no duplicate; 2026-10-25): re-read `rp8_render()` and the generic `BM__Hidd_BitMap__GetImageLUT()` implementation against the corresponding WritePixelArray8 boundary candidate GD5367. A clipped inclusive rectangle x=0..32767 on a bitmap at least 32768 pixels wide retains a 32768-pixel row; `rp8_render()` stores that width in signed `WORD` before the HIDD call (`rom/graphics/readpixelarray8.c:21-32`; clipping in `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:123-140,1064-1085`). The inherited generic reader stores its x loop index in `WORD` and tests `x < msg->width` in both the temporary-line and allocation-fallback loops (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:4163-4214`); when the width narrows to -32768, neither loop copies row pixels. This is already GD4030's exact root and consequence, so no additional ID was added. The direct `ReadPixelArray8()` caller census finds `rom/graphics/fontsupport.c` and the `ReadPixelLine8()` wrapper; the generated m68k emulator entry is an ABI thunk, not a native C caller. No transfer or target-specific signed-conversion behavior was tested; source-only.

GD9803 selected MemList reader caller correction (2026-10-25; candidate strengthened): the previous VCGfx ledger note said no selected allocator walk concurrent with initialization had been found. A cross-resident pass now traces the actual reader: Raspberry Pi boot selects `kernel-input` and `hidd-vcgfx` (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:122,143`); `input.device` has resident priority 30 versus VCGfx 9 and the initial resident array is sorted descending by `krnRomTagScanner()` while building `ResModules` (`rom/devs/input/input.conf:4`; `vcgfx.conf:5`; `rom/kernel/kernel_romtags.c:311-339`; assigned in `rom/kernel/prepareexecbase.c:51`). `InitKickTags()` only sorts again if it adds KickTags (`rom/exec/initkicktags.c:273-275`). Input's init hook starts `ProcessEvents()` on a new task (`rom/devs/input/input.c:66-80`), whose pre-Wait setup allocates MsgPorts and I/O requests via AllocMem (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:157-194`; `rom/exec/createmsgport.c:48-52`; `createiorequest.c:59-69`). On ExecSMP the boot task stays on CPU0 while secondary cores are already released before COLDSTART (`arch/arm-native/kernel/platform_init.c:84-107`), allowing that task's shared-lock MemList walk to overlap the VCGfx unlocked AddTail. Updated GD9803's report evidence and qualification: the in-tree reader route is source-confirmed, but the exact simultaneous dispatch remains conditional and was not exercised. No boot, allocation, or scheduler operation was run; source-only.


GD9803 selected reader limitation and resident-order correction (2026-10-25; supersedes prior reader-overlap claim): the initial resident list is sorted in `krnRomTagScanner()` (`rom/kernel/kernel_romtags.c:311-339`) and installed as `SysBase->ResModules` (`rom/kernel/prepareexecbase.c:51`); `InitKickTags()` re-sorts only when it adds non-NULL KickTags (`rom/exec/initkicktags.c:273-275`). Added GD9834 for the selected color-channel mismatch case. No bitmap allocation, copy, render or build was run; source-only.


SDL unmapped-key delivery and Intuition caller closure (GD5724 strengthened; 2026-10-26; no new source-body credit): traced the `0xff` initialization for all unmapped SDL symbols (`keymap.c:139-150`), event-task dispatch of both key-down and key-up (`event.c:102-109`), and direct keycode copy plus conditional release-bit OR (`sdl_kbdclass.c:64-75`). The sentinel already contains `IECODE_UP_PREFIX`, so both event types are delivered as releases for `0x7f`. Traced Input HIDD callback routing and Intuition's `IECLASS_RAWKEY` handling through `IDCMP_RAWKEY` delivery (`rom/hidds/input/inputclass.c:94-114,187-204`; `rom/intuition/inputhandler.c:2208-2224,2587-2597`). `MapRawKey()` rejects codes >= `0x78`; the header reserves `0x78-0x7f` as communication codes. Expanded GD5724 to the demonstrated raw-key notification consequence; no in-tree consumer of `0x7f` or vanilla-character effect is claimed. No SDL event was injected; source-only.


EFI framebuffer attr-base leak reference-count implementation closure (GD9831 strengthened; 2026-10-26; no new path/LOC credit): re-read `OOP_ObtainAttrBase()` and `release_idbucket()`. Each successful obtain increments the shared IID bucket refcount under the IID-table semaphore (`rom/oop/obtainattrbase.c:130-136`); release decrements it and removes/frees the bucket only at zero (`rom/oop/support.c:181-205`). Therefore EFIFBGfx's failed `AddDisplayDriver()` path, after eight successful obtains and with no matching release, leaves persistent references; a retry increments the same buckets. GD9831's impact wording now reflects this exact storage/lifetime behavior. No module registration was induced; source-only.

The selected ATA, AHCI, NVMe, SCSI and VirtIO drivers include `IID_Hidd_StorageUnit` in their attr-base arrays and acquire the array before class/unit registration; initialization fails if acquisition fails (`rom/devs/ata/ata_init.c:138-145,243-249`; `ahci_init.c:55-65,163-167`; `nvme_init.c:44-54,128-134`; `scsi_init.c:116-124,220-225`; `virtio_init.c:43-53,118-123`). A first-time bucket-creation failure instead precedes active in-tree units, so no omitted supported unit was established.
