Picture source-buffer overflow and PNG scanline caller recheck (GD5707 source-revalidated; 2026-10-26; no additional body credit): verified `AllocSrcBuffer()` stores the 16-byte-aligned row stride and multiplies it by height for `AllocVec()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/colorhandling.c:316-331`). On 32-bit builds, width 65,535, four-byte pixels and height 16,385 produce stride 262,144 and a wrapped allocation request of 262,144 bytes. PNG publishes those UWORD-compatible dimensions into the Picture BMHD and sends decoded full-width scanlines through `PDTM_WRITEPIXELARRAY` (`pngclass.c:245-260,413-415,515-538`); Picture writes each row at the aligned destination stride without checking buffer extent (`pictureclass.c:1093-1150,1185-1207`). The second row begins at the end of the undersized allocation and writes past it. Confirmed both Picture and PNG are in the i386 PC floppy package (`arch/i386-pc/boot/floppy/mmakefile.src:55-60`). No image or allocation was exercised; source-only.


AreaEnd polygon WORD_MAX loop recheck (GD5708 qualified; 2026-10-26; no additional body credit): traced `AreaDraw()` coordinate narrowing (`rom/graphics/areadraw.c:67-75`), AreaEnd bounds and TmpRas size gate (`areaend.c:106-110,130-155,185-195`), both `WORD y <= bounds->MaxY` loops (`areafill.c:118,151`), and the final BltPattern caller (`areaend.c:149-169`). For MaxY 32767, signed-WORD increment is out of range; on ordinary two's-complement narrowing the counter wraps and the inclusive loop does not terminate. Since BltPattern follows the rasterizer return, the old claim of writing past the planar destination is unsupported and removed. No in-tree max-coordinate caller was found; public API boundary retained conditionally by compiler behavior. No AreaEnd or target build was run; source-only.

DiskFont short `.otag` header boundary recheck (GD5711 source-revalidated; 2026-10-26; no additional body credit): `OTAG_GetFile()` allocates `sizeof(OTagList)+l` for `l` file bytes and reads the two header words unconditionally (`workbench/libs/diskfont/bullet.c:85-112`). The identifier mismatch sets `ok` false but does not skip the next independent header comparison, so the read still occurs before failure cleanup. CGXVideo OOP attribute-descriptor failure-path closure (2026-10-26; no new GD, no body/LOC credit): resolved the `cgxvideo_init.c` row's open terminator/caller question by tracing its one active `IID_Hidd_BitMap` descriptor (`workbench/libs/cgxvideo/cgxvideo_init.c:11-16`) through `struct IntCGXVBase::attrbases[3]` (`cgxvideo_intern.h:32-37`), `OOP_ObtainAttrBases()`'s sentinel loop and failure cleanup (`rom/oop/obtainattrbases.c:49-65`), and `MakeLibrary()`'s `MEMF_PUBLIC|MEMF_CLEAR` base allocation (`rom/exec/makelibrary.c:126-145`). NListtree CopyToClip truncated-escape bounds pass (GD9843 added; 2026-10-26; targeted method/caller pass, no whole-body/LOC credit): re-read `_NListtree_CopyToClip()` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:10030-10085`) and traced its input through public Insert and the built-in context-menu choice (`:7064-7119,6568-6578`). Insert copies accepted node names to exactly `strlen(name)+1` bytes by default and performs no ESC validation. The clipboard parser skips two source bytes after every ESC, then advances again and reads/copies without checking for NUL. A name ending in ESC or ESC plus one byte therefore places the next read beyond the node-name allocation. Added GD9843, distinct from GD9816's valid bracketed-sequence mutation and GD9746's documented Active sentinel dereference. The custom CopyToClipHook path bypasses the built-in parser. No name or clipboard operation was run; source-only. The 10,702-line NListtree translation unit and broader Graphics/Desktop goal remain partial.

GD6251 report-detail restoration and failure/caller recheck (2026-10-26; existing finding, no new ID or LOC credit): re-read `HIDDCompositorRecalculateVisibleRegions()` and `HIDDCompositorRedrawVisibleRegions()` around both ignored calls. `AndRegionRegion()` computes into a temporary region and returns FALSE before clearing/replacing its destination when rectangle allocation fails; its caller has just seeded the destination with the full bitmap rectangle, then continues to treat any remaining rectangles as visible and redraw them. `ClearRegionRegion()` likewise leaves its destination unchanged on allocation failure; after the ignored subtraction, the redraw path enumerates the remaining display region and fills/backfills it, so bitmap-covered pixels can be repainted. Traced the stack-change dispatch through `graphics_compositor.h` and confirmed the monitor target is optional. Replaced the report's ledger-only placeholder with the two concrete triggers, consequences, target scope and confidence. No allocation failure or display operation was run; source-only.

GD6251 ignored region-operation inventory expansion (2026-10-26; existing root cause, no new ID or LOC credit): scanned all region-helper calls in the compositor's visible-region construction and redraw path. In addition to `AndRegionRegion()` and `ClearRegionRegion()`, it ignores `OrRectRegion()` results while seeding display, bitmap and alpha regions and `ClearRectRegion()` results while subtracting opaque/edge rectangles. The corresponding helpers return FALSE on temporary rectangle allocation failure without committing a replacement destination (`rom/graphics/orrectregion.c:64-101`; `clearrectregion.c:58-105`). Expanded GD6251's detail to include these same-state failures; no separate defect ID was added because they share the ignored allocation-failure contract and are consumed as one visibility/backfill calculation. No allocation failure or rendering was run; source-only.

GD6251 fallback reachability recheck (2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): traced ignored visibility-helper results to the normal `BitMapStackChanged()` error path. `HIDDCompositorRecalculateVisibleRegions()` and `HIDDCompositorRedrawVisibleRegions()` return void; `BitMapStackChanged()` updates `ok` from stack-node allocation and `HIDDCompositorToggleCompositing()`, not from any region operation. It calls `HIDDCompositorReset()`/`HIDDCompositorShowSingle()` only when that independent flag is false. Thus the region-allocation failure is not automatically converted to the documented single-bitmap fallback. Direct redraw callers likewise receive no region-operation result. Added this recovery-boundary evidence to GD6251; no allocation failure or view change was run; source-only.

`rom/graphics/areamove.c` explicit full-body, buffer-boundary and caller pass (GD9849 withdrawn as non-observable; 2026-11-01 recheck): the complete 130-line body / 51 `cloc 2.06` C code lines were already credited in the 198/198 graphics.library subtotal. Replacing the MOVE would therefore change stored start coordinates without changing any completed polygon or producing output. The implementation comment describes the intended replacement path when room remains, but the full-capacity rejection has no established observable consequence. GD9412 empty-region span and point-query recheck (2026-10-26; existing candidate qualified; no LOC credit): re-read the `OrRectRegion()` empty-destination branch and `IsPointInRegion()` comparisons (`rom/graphics/orrectregion.c:62,85-101`; `rom/graphics/ispointinregion.c:55-77`) against the public signed-WORD rectangle layout (`compiler/include/graphics/gfx.h:45-51`; `regions.h:19-30`). The API copies valid absolute endpoints but stores their difference into signed-WORD local maxima without a span-range guard. Such a conversion is implementation-defined when the span exceeds WORD_MAX; under low-16-bit narrowing, the local max becomes negative and the point query rejects points that passed the absolute bounds check. Kept the finding as a public API boundary issue because no maintained in-tree large-span caller was established, and qualified exact visible behavior by compiler conversion. Expanded GD9412 with these limits and source locations; no geometry operation was run and no body-line credit changed. Source-only.

GD9413 decorator removal lock/reference recheck (2026-10-26; existing candidate detailed; no LOC credit): traced `int_UnloadDecorator()`'s caller-held `ScrDecorSem` contract through `DoASyncAction()` and the input-device action queue (`rom/intuition/decoration.c:129-138`; `inputhandler_actions.c:642-674,678-712`). In the synchronous input-task branch the callback runs inline while the caller's lock is held; for ordinary callers the request is copied and queued, and the caller subsequently releases `ScrDecorSem`. The queued `int_removedecorator()` then unlinks the node and frees its pattern without taking that semaphore or rechecking the zero-reference condition (`decoration.c:103-126`). A later `int_LoadDecorator()` can find/increment the node under the lock before that callback executes, so removal can proceed despite the new reference; the callback also races the protected list traversal. Expanded GD9413 with the async-only trigger and conditional impact. No schedule or decorator operation was run; source-only.

GD9414 decorator unload allocation-failure recheck (2026-10-26; existing candidate detailed; no LOC credit): followed both allocation failure branches through `int_UnloadDecorator()` and the decorator service task (`rom/intuition/decoration.c:103-138`; `inputhandler_actions.c:642-674`; `workbench/c/Decoration/decoration.c:281-328`). `DoASyncAction()` returns FALSE if it cannot allocate the queued action, but the caller ignores that result. If queued, `int_removedecorator()` creates its reply port before `Remove()` or the `MAGIC_DECORATOR` message; if `CreateMsgPort()` fails, the callback exits without unlinking or notifying the service. GD9428 Group nested-disable propagation recheck (2026-10-26; both conditional imbalances retained; no LOC credit): reread Group's OM_SET tag rewriting and child dispatch (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:473-505,560-633,1004-1020`) against Area's high-bit local disabled flag and low-bit nested count (`classes/area.c:559-590,740-748`). Group suppresses the original local tag during superclass handling, restores it, then forwards every supplied `MUIA_Disabled` value as a child `MUIA_NestedDisabled` without comparing the previous local bit. Thus repeated TRUE increments each descendant's count even though setting the local high bit is idempotent; one later FALSE decrements only once. A Group receiving `MUIA_NestedDisabled=TRUE` from an ancestor retains a positive low count while its local high bit remains clear; a redundant local FALSE still forwards a child decrement and can remove the child's inherited contribution while the Group itself remains disabled. `Group_DispatchMsg()` visits children without an effective-state transition check. Reconfirmed Appearance Preferences uses runtime Disabled updates but does not establish either redundant sequence. No object state was changed; source-only.

NListtree Open/Close Active-list selector contract boundary (2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): re-read the complete `_NListtree_Open()` and `_NListtree_Close()` selectors and their method documentation (`NListtree.c:6670-6734,6866-6918`; `MCC_NListtree.doc:1158-1220,2423-2495`). Both methods can dereference `ln` before the later `if (ln && tn)` guard when callers combine `ListNode_Active` with Head/Tail; Close's Parent selector also reads `data->ActiveList->ln_Parent` directly. The general ActiveList attribute documentation explicitly returns `MUIV_NListtree_ActiveList_Off` when there is no active entry (`MCC_NListtree.doc:189-206`), and construction leaves `ActiveList` zeroed (`NListtree.c:5104-5115,5217-5222,5260-5268`). However, the Open/Close method contracts define which active list/node is used without defining behavior when none exists; their documented examples pair Active list with Active tree node, which safely no-op through the final guard. The selected keyboard Open/Close calls are additionally guarded by `data->ActiveNode` (`NListtree.c:5685-5715`). Thus this pass does not promote a defect based solely on an undocumented invalid selector combination. Keep Open/Close as an explicit contract/caller follow-up; no public caller using Active+Head/Tail or Parent without a selection was found in this search. No method or GUI was run; source-only.

NListtree no-active lookup and relative-entry helper follow-through (GD9848 candidate recheck; 2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): read complete `_NListtree_FindName()`, `_NListtree_FindUserData()`, `_NListtree_GetEntry()`, `FindTreeNodeByName()`, `FindTreeNodeByUserData()`, and `GetEntryByTotalPos()` bodies (`NListtree.c:1307-1335,2391-2429,2476-2514,8799-8840,8936-8977,9076-9147`). For FindName/FindUserData with the Active list selector, the public Active-Off state maps to `data->ActiveList == NULL`; each helper immediately forms `&ln->ln_List` for `GetHead()` (unless StartNode, which casts the NULL list as a node), so the NULL does reach an invalid list/node access. GetEntry has the same issue for Active plus Head/Tail, Next/Previous, and total-position paths; Parent routes the NULL through `GetParent()`. This confirms the source mechanism already described by GD9848. The method documentation defines Active as the list associated with the active entry but does not specify behavior when no entry is active, and no checked-in caller was found using these methods with Active while inactive. Thus this remains a conditional API-contract candidate rather than a new unconditional defect. Complete helper/method bodies are covered; no additional path or line credit because the NListtree translation unit is already counted. No method or GUI was run; source-only.

GD9836 compositor-construction failure caller/registration recheck (2026-10-26; retained; no LOC credit): traced both setup orderings again through `display_Register()` and `compositor_Install()` (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:366-404`; `graphics_compositor.c:23-59`). If the class is already registered, `display_Register()` calls the unchecked `compositor_Setup()` before `display_Enable()`; if the display registers first, it is enabled and inserted without an object, and later `compositor_Install()` ignores the failed object creation while returning `DD_OK`. In either order the failed compositor does not veto enabling/retaining the eligible display. Rechecked `display_LoadViewPorts()`'s fallback: when `ShowViewPorts` returns FALSE and `display_compositor` is NULL, the code submits only the front viewport bitmap with `HIDD_Display_Show()` (`graphics_display.c:511-565`). The concrete implementation provider is the optional Nouveau HIDD's `CLID_Hidd_Compositor` class (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau.conf:121-134`); this confirms the report's optional-module qualifier, not a default-image claim. No additional issue or caller path established. No allocation failure or display load was run; source-only.

GD9839 software-bitmap implementation path qualification (2026-10-26; no new ID or LOC credit): followed the signed `WORD` extent from `bltpattern_render()` through both software HIDD paths. The base `BM__Hidd_BitMap__PutPattern()` rejects nonpositive dimensions (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:3811-3822`); the generic chunky-bitmap class forwards those same signed fields to `HIDD_BM_PutMemPattern*()` (`gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:832-918`), and every pixel-width helper rejects a nonpositive width or height (`gfx_bitmapmemblit.c:829,974,1122,1328,1474,1736,1999,2332`). LinuxFB's bitmap class derives from `CLID_Hidd_ChunkyBM` and overrides only `SetColors` (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/linuxfbgfx.conf:25-35`), confirming the clipped 32,768-pixel span is also dropped on that selected software path. Other accelerated HIDD overrides may differ; no runtime draw or bitmap allocation was performed. Updated GD9839's target/consequence qualification; no finding count or body credit changed. Source-only.


GD9428 Appearance Preferences import sequence recheck (2026-10-26; no new GD): re-read the actual Theme option group construction and every runtime `MUIA_Disabled` setter in `appearanceeditor.c` (`:133-212,368-402,568-700,1028-1111`). DiskFont ReadFontDescr buffered-seek error-path trace (GD9852 added; 2026-10-26; no whole-body/LOC credit): followed both ignored `Flush()`/`Seek()` pairs through DOS read-mode `Flush()` and `Seek()` (`workbench/libs/diskfont/af_fontdescr_io.c:136-145,174-187`; `rom/dos/flush.c:73-84`; `rom/dos/seek.c:68-91`). `Flush()` clears the read-ahead bounds before its cursor-restoration seek can fail; `ReadFontDescr()` then ignores that failure and issues a relative seek with no buffer offset left to correct the physical cursor. It also ignores the relative seek result and continues parsing. Traced the returned descriptor into directory enumeration and direct font lookup callers (`diskfontfunc.c:93-145,842-860,1345-1370`). Added GD9852 for conditional mispositioned descriptor reads; retained the trigger on a failed restoration followed by subsequent I/O, without claiming a default-image module edge. No font file or I/O failure was used; source-only.

AmigaGuide node-position read-ahead error-path follow-up (GD9853 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): traced both AROS-only `Flush()` calls in `ScanFile()` through `ParseNodeLine()` and `CMD_ENDNODE` into `agn_Pos`/`agn_Length`, then followed those fields into `AllocAGObjectNode()`'s absolute seek and node-body read (`workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/file.c:109-115,403-410`; `util.c:383-407`). DOS read-mode `Flush()` can clear the buffered unread range and then fail to restore the logical cursor (`rom/dos/flush.c:73-84`); the ignored failure lets the subsequent position query observe the advanced underlying position, so the stored node range is wrong. Added GD9853, separate from GD9852's DiskFont parser consequence and GD6284's unterminated macro scan. The datatype is explicitly buildable but no parent aggregate edge is claimed. No guide or I/O failure was used; source-only.

NListtree clipboard escape parser recheck (GD9816 strengthened; 2026-10-26; no new ID or LOC credit): reread `_NListtree_CopyToClip()` and compared its pointer movement with NList's documented simple `ESC`+character formatting codes and built-in copy-hook contract (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:10051-10072`; `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NList.doc:415-445,466-481,656-665`). For an unbracketed code such as `ESC b` followed by `Hello`, the `s += 2` followed by unconditional `s++` drops the first ordinary character (`H`) before copying. The bracketed `ESC P[...]` case remains as documented in GD9816: `++*s` changes the opening bracket in the stored name and leaves sequence payload in clipboard text. Updated GD9816 to include the simple-code truncation; it is the same parser and finding, not a distinct defect. No name was copied or modified; source-only.

NListtree Exchange second-list selector consequence recheck (GD9813 strengthened; 2026-10-26; no new ID or body-line credit): reread the complete `_NListtree_Exchange()` selector and mutation path (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:7970-8125`) against the method contract (`:7838-7930`) and helpers `NLRemoveFromTable()`/`NLFindInTable()` (`:1080-1112`). NListtree full-capacity table-removal consequence qualification (GD9734 retained, confidence reduced to medium; no new finding or body credit): rechecked `NLCreateTable()`'s rounded exact allocation and the full-table `NLRemoveFromTable()` loop (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:987-1027,1080-1112`). AmigaVideo GD4763 repeated-swap rollback state recheck (2026-10-26; existing finding expanded; no body/LOC credit): traced `HIDD_ViewPortData.PreviousBitmap` through initial wrapping, successive `MakeVPort()` swaps, the failure rollback and `ChangeVPBitMap()` reload (`rom/hidds/gfx/include/gfx.h:130`; `rom/graphics/makevport.c:120-169,222-232`; `changevpbitmap.c:66-105`). `PreviousBitmap` is populated only while NULL and is not cleared on a successful swap; a later swap can dispose the currently wrapped bitmap while retaining the original saved bitmap. If that later `MakeVPort()` fails, rollback restores the original saved object instead of the bitmap that was displayed immediately before the request. The generic caller ignores the failure, reloads from VPD state and queues both DBufInfo replies; Intuition also updates its RastPort and returns TRUE. Expanded GD4763 with this stale-state sequence and kept the visible image consequence at medium confidence because backend behavior after failed rebuild was not exercised. No viewport, buffer swap, allocation failure or VBlank was run; source-only.


ChangeVPBitMap full-body and safe-reply/queue recheck (2026-10-26; GD4763/GD5422 retained; no new finding or LOC credit): reread all 109 lines of `rom/graphics/changevpbitmap.c`, then followed `internal_QueueDBufInfo()` and `TOF_VBlank()` in `rom/graphics/graphics_init.c:163-212`, the DBufInfo allocation/free contracts, and `FreeScreenBuffer()`'s wait-before-free caller. Confirmed `ChangeVPBitMap()` publishes `RasInfo->BitMap` and calls `MakeVPort()` before acquiring the viewport semaphore; it discards the rebuild result, reloads VPD state under the semaphore, and queues both replies if displayed. The non-displayed path replies immediately. The queue's local `Disable()`/`Enable()` critical section remains the already tracked GD5422 ExecSMP enqueue/removal race; the AmigaVideo failed-rebuild and stale `PreviousBitmap` path remains GD4763. `AllocDBufInfo()` is the documented constructor and `ChangeVPBitMap()` accepts a DBufInfo pointer; this pass did not treat invalid/null arguments as a separate defect. No allocation, swap, VBlank, or concurrent operation was run; source-only.


MUI Frameadjust preview allocation failure first-dereference correction (GD9512 refined; 2026-10-26; no path/LOC credit): checked the exact macro expansion after the earlier note established that `SetAttrsA()` rejects a NULL object. In `MakeFrameDisplay()`, `set(NULL, ...)` therefore returns safely, but each preview loop next calls `DoMethod(obj, MUIM_Notify, ...)` before `OM_ADDMEMBER`. The selected `DoMethod` macro evaluates `OCLASS(obj)` after `ASSERT_VALID_PTR(obj)`; muimaster's `debug.h` defines the assertion as empty. Thus the allocation failure reaches the invalid-object dereference at the notification call, and normally cannot reach `Group__MUIM_AddObject()`. Corrected GD9512 and the file row to describe this first failure site; Group's separate non-NULL assumption is not claimed as this caller's consequence. No failure was induced; source-only.


MUI Popframe/Popimage stale-popup candidate withdrawal (GD9513; 2026-10-26; no path/LOC credit): rechecked the missing `OM_REMMEMBER` in the owner `OM_DISPOSE` handlers against the normal selected owner teardown. `Application__OM_DISPOSE` removes the main Window before disposing it (`application.c:862-870`); `Family__MUIM_Remove` sends `MUIM_DisconnectParent` before unlink (`family.c:274-287`); Window propagates disconnect to its root Group and Group sends it to every child (`window.c:3595-3620`; `group.c:832-849`). Popframe/Popimage disconnect handlers call their CloseWindow methods, which remove and dispose the popup while the Application reference is still available (`popframe.c:156-185`; `popimage.c:180-211`). Therefore the normal application/window teardown path cannot leave the popup in the Application family for its later dispose loop. Directly disposing a still-connected owner could bypass this, but that lifecycle is outside the established parent-removal contract and no selected in-tree caller was found. Marked GD9513 withdrawn, removed it from `AROS.md`, and corrected the current file rows; older dated notes are superseded by this disposition. No GUI or window lifecycle ran; source-only.

MUI empty external-brush parser path recheck (GD9576 confirmed; 2026-10-26; no path/LOC credit): traced literal `4:` through the switch to `get_brush_imspec(s + 2)` and `3:` through `get_boopsi_imspec()`'s no-`.image` branch to the same helper (`workbench/libs/muimaster/imspec.c:179-186,325-405`). `StrDup("")` allocates `strlen+1` bytes and returns a one-byte NUL string (`compiler/alib/strdup.c:47-56`); `strlen(...) - 1` then underflows unsigned `size_t` before the helper indexes the string (`imspec.c:201-212`). NListtree selection-table allocation failure metadata/return recheck (GD9735 strengthened; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): re-read `NLCreateTable()`, `NLAddToTable()`, and every `TreeNodeSelectAdd()` caller. On `AllocVecPooled()` failure, `NLCreateTable()` has already enlarged `tb_Size` and the failed assignment sets local `newtable` to NULL; `NLAddToTable()` returns FALSE while leaving the stale enlarged capacity paired with the prior table pointer. Initial-table failure leaves NULL plus size 64, so the next add can skip allocation and write through NULL; growth failure can make a later add pass the old allocation's end. Selection callbacks ignore insertion failure and publish `TNF_SELECTED`, preserving GD9735's existing state mismatch. Corrected an initial misread: `newtable` is initialized by the assignment expression and is NULL on failure; no indeterminate-return claim remains. Expanded the finding to cover the exact subsequent-insert failure; no new ID, body or LOC credit. No allocation failure or selection was run; source-only.

GD9846 Move KeepStructure destination allegation withdrawn (2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): corrected the earlier recursion trace after checking the `cnt` value at each `CreateParentStructure()` frame (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:2660-2701,8323-8345`). ReAction DrawList full local source pass (GD9869 added; 2026-10-26): reconciled the explicit drawlist module manifest, class definition, public directive header and ReAction link-library auto-open entry; read all local C bodies and definitions (309 `cloc 2.06` C/header code lines). In `IM_DRAW()`, the local buffer is 320 bytes and `InitArea()` receives `320 / 5 = 64` vectors. A nonclosed polygon that fills all 64 records reaches `AreaEnd()`; its unconditional `areaclosepolygon()` violates the helper's `Count < MaxCount` precondition. At full capacity `VctrPtr` aliases the start of `FlagTbl`, so two closure coordinates overwrite flag bytes, and `FlagPtr[0]` writes one byte past the 320-byte array. DrawList ignores the AreaMove/AreaDraw and AreaEnd results; the ReAction autoinit set names the image library. Added GD9869; the earlier GD9849 repeated-MOVE candidate was later withdrawn because it has no established observable effect. No build, image render, allocation failure or stack-layout observation was performed; source-only.

Application PushMethod variadic ABI and caller inventory checkpoint (2026-10-26; no new GD): inventoried 83 textual `MUIM_Application_PushMethod` references in Workbench sources and verified the `DoMethod()` slow-stack form builds an `IPTR` vector (`compiler/include/clib/alib_protos.h:373-380`) against `MUIP_Application_PushMethod`'s fixed fields (`application.h:107-112`) and the method's count/argument extraction (`application.c:1900-1925`). MUI Configdata/Dataspace malformed-window-position length validation follow-up (GD9907 strengthened; 2026-10-26): rechecked the accepted property-length path in `Dataspace__MUIM_ReadIFF()` and `Dataspace__MUIM_Add()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/dataspace.c:93-126,193-243`), and the later `Configdata_GetWindowPos()` byte-swap call (`configdata.c:861-879`). Dataspace retains each property's actual `len`, but `Find` returns only its payload pointer; the window-position caller uses the embedded declared byte count and has no way to check the stored length before its first 4-byte read/swap. Confirmed `Add()` accepts 1-3 byte records, so a short positive-length property can reach the size-field read; oversized embedded values also control the swap loop and subsequent Application copy. This is distinct from GD5089's partial/default-settings false-success after parser/import failure: GD9907 concerns unchecked payload/destination bounds when the WindowPos property is consumed. No malformed preference was loaded; source-only.

Dataspace zero-length serialized-record loop pass (GD9911 added; 2026-10-26): traced `ReadIFF()`'s record cursor through `Dataspace_Add()` and the nested semaphore methods (`dataspace.c:100-108,221-240,293-326`; `semaphore.c:91-98`). Configdata StopChunk registration failure trace folded into GD5089 (2026-10-26; no new ID/LOC): checked `StopChunk()`'s error return through `EntryHandler()` (`workbench/libs/iffparse/stopchunk.c:52-64`; `entryhandler.c:73-99`): handler setup can fail when its local item cannot be allocated/stored. `Configdata__MUIM_Load()` ignores that result, clears the Dataspace, then enters `IFFPARSE_SCAN` (`configdata.c:1252-1268`). `ParseIFF()` returns to the caller on an entry handler's `IFF_RETURN2CLIENT`; with no installed StopChunk handler, the scan runs through the stream without yielding each `MUIC` chunk, then its terminal status is also ignored while `res` remains TRUE. ASL FontRequester large-font-count caller pass (GD9912 added; 2026-10-26; no new body/LOC credit): traced selected `FOGetFonts()` setup and rescan callers (`workbench/libs/asl/fontreqhooks.c:427,1292-1294`) through its repeated-buffer `AvailFonts(AFF_MEMORY | AFF_DISK)` request and `SortAvailFonts()` (`fontreqsupport.c:153-165,182-222`). The returned `afh_NumEntries` is UWORD (`compiler/include/diskfont/diskfont.h:90-93`), and diskfont increments the field for every fitting entry (`workbench/libs/diskfont/availfonts.c:210-219`); no 32,767-entry cap is present. At 32,768 entries the signed-WORD conversion in `SortAvailFonts()` is implementation-defined; under the conventional GCC/Clang AROS conversion, -32,768 is converted to a huge `size_t` for qsort, whose selected implementation computes out-of-array pointers (`compiler/crt/stdc/qsort.c:73-80`; `compiler/crt/stdc/__qsort.h:87-120`). If that returns, the WORD outer/grouping indices in `FOGetFonts()` cannot represent the remaining valid entries. Added GD9912, scoped to an exceptionally large available-font database and the stated toolchain conversion behavior. Existing `fontreqsupport.c` full-body credit remains; no font database or requester was exercised. Source-only.

DefaultMenuHandler failed-port ownership follow-up (GD5818 expanded, 2026-10-26): re-read the allocation branch at `rom/intuition/menutask.c:109-132` and matched it to Exec task cleanup (`rom/exec/remtask.c:167-181`). The requester-list semaphore remains held until after `PutMsg`, then is released before waiting, allowing the ASL task to finish cleanup; the stack message remains live until the reply is queued. MorphOS uses a separate asynchronous path. Concurrently freeing a requester while another task calls Abort remains an external API lifetime precondition. |

Matched the registry lookup/window lifetime to `aslrequest.c`; `ActivateWindow()` is called while the requester-list semaphore protects the published window pointer, and the lock is released on all non-NULL requester paths. `Popasl` is the only checked-in direct caller of Abort; no checked-in direct activation caller was found beyond the generated m68k compatibility thunk. No independent defect established. |

Zune Application membership/parent propagation recheck (2026-10-26; no new candidate or LOC credit): traced `Application__OM_ADDMEMBER()`/`OM_REMMEMBER()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1435-1465`) through the selected `Family` OM_ADDMEMBER/OM_REMMEMBER aliases and the `Window`/`Notify` connect/disconnect implementations (`classes/family.c:178-286,464-490`; `window.c:3574-3622`; `notify.c:768-800`). Family insertion connects a non-NULL child when already attached to an application; the Application wrapper then repeats the same parent connection. For Window and Notify the connection is an idempotent GlobalInfo propagation, so the duplicate dispatch does not establish a separate state defect. Removal similarly invokes disconnect in both wrapper and Family, but the first Window call closes and disconnects descendants; the second sees the window already closed, and Notify's disconnect intentionally retains GlobalInfo under its documented compatibility behavior. Family rejects a NULL child, but the application wrapper's subsequent method call would receive NULL; callers are required to pass a valid member object, and no selected in-tree NULL caller was found, so this was not elevated. No member mutation, window close or application tree was run. The membership slice is rechecked; full caller/build-variant coverage and the broader subsystem remain open; source-only.

Graphics.library AreRegionsEqual full-body and selected-vector caller pass (2026-10-26; no new GD): read all 71 physical lines / 22 `cloc 2.06` C lines in `rom/graphics/areregionsequal.c`, confirmed the vector is selected by `FUNCTIONS` in `rom/graphics/mmakefile.src:49` and declared in `rom/graphics/graphics.conf:229`. The implementation compares absolute region bounds, then each normalized RegionRectangle bound and list termination; the region-operation writer merges adjacent horizontal spans and vertically adjoining identical bands (`rom/graphics/intregions.c:280-358,432-465,611-746`), supporting the representation comparison for library-produced regions. Full-tree C search found no direct maintained caller; the generated m68kemu compatibility thunk forwards the two region pointers to the vector (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:4287-4293,7679`). No null/malformed public structure case was elevated because no such input contract is established. No region, graphics call, build or emulation was run. Graphics.library AskFont full-body and selected-caller pass (2026-10-26; no new GD): read all 56 physical lines / 15 `cloc 2.06` C lines in `rom/graphics/askfont.c`, confirmed it is selected by `FUNCTIONS` in `rom/graphics/mmakefile.src:50` and declared in `rom/graphics/graphics.conf`. The vector copies the current `RastPort->Font` name/size/style/flags into the caller's `TextAttr`. Both maintained callers establish a non-NULL font first: `OpenScreen()` calls `SetFont()` with its successfully selected `dri_Font` before AskFont and stores the resulting common-prefix layout as its `TTextAttr` (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:2124-2132`; `intuition_intern.h:726`; `graphics/text.h:72-88`); ASL sets its dummy RastPort to `GfxBase->DefaultFont` before the fallback AskFont (`workbench/libs/asl/basicfuncs.c:699-704`). Full-tree C search found no other direct caller; generated m68k vector dispatch is not a separate caller. The public routine assumes valid RastPort/font/output pointers, and no selected caller violates that precondition. No font or screen/requester operation was run. This adds one selected vector body to the Graphics ledger; wider public caller, ABI and subsystem closure remain open; source-only.

Graphics.library AskSoftStyle full-body and SetSoftStyle/public-caller pass (2026-10-26; no new GD): read all 59 physical lines / 12 `cloc 2.06` C lines in `rom/graphics/asksoftstyle.c`, confirmed manifest selection (`rom/graphics/mmakefile.src:51`) and the vector ABI (`rom/graphics/graphics.conf:54`). It returns zero for a RastPort with no Font and otherwise the complement of intrinsic `tf_Style`, matching the API note that undefined style bits are set. Traced the direct companion use in `SetSoftStyle()` (`rom/graphics/setsoftstyle.c:63`): its `enable & AskSoftStyle()` mask is stored into the UBYTE `AlgoStyle`, so high undefined bits are discarded by the instance field; supported style bits are filtered as intended. Searched all maintained C calls; they pair the query with initialized/window RastPorts or use the query as the `SetSoftStyle()` support mask. `InitRastPort()` installs `GfxBase->DefaultFont`, and `SetFont(NULL)` also selects that default (`rom/graphics/initrastport.c:34-49`; `setfont.c:53-72`). No selected caller with an uninitialized RastPort or null Font was established. No font or rendering operation was run. This adds one selected graphics vector body; exhaustive API clients and broader graphics/text closure remain open; source-only.

Graphics.library GetAPen/GetBPen paired vector bodies and consumer pass (2026-10-26; no new GD): read both selected implementations in full (11 `cloc 2.06` C lines each), confirmed `FUNCTIONS` inclusion (`rom/graphics/mmakefile.src:104,106`) and vector definitions (`rom/graphics/graphics.conf`). Each getter casts the signed-byte RastPort field to `UBYTE` before returning `ULONG`, preserving pen values 0..255 despite the storage type (`compiler/include/graphics/rastport.h:63-64`); paired SetAPen/SetBPen vectors accept `UBYTE` and store those values. Graphics.library GetDrMd/SetDrMd paired vector bodies and state-restore caller pass (2026-10-26; no new GD): read both selected implementations in full (13 `cloc 2.06` C lines combined), confirmed their manifest entries (`rom/graphics/mmakefile.src:109,175`) and ABI declarations. `DrawMode` is a signed byte in RastPort, but all defined public modes/flags occupy low positive bits (`compiler/include/graphics/rastport.h:66,99-105`); getter promotion therefore preserves supported values, and setter accepts the same UBYTE-width value, updates `linpatcnt`, and recomputes minterms. Traced selected save/restore uses in `graphics/text.c`, `bltpattern.c`, and `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/panelgroup.c`; these save the returned value in ULONG/UWORD and restore only documented low-bit draw modes. `graphics_misc.c` and `GetRPAttrsA()` consume the getter directly. No signed-width defect was established for valid public draw modes. No draw or RastPort operation was run. This adds two selected vector bodies; external invalid-mode callers and wider graphics drawing paths remain open; source-only.

Graphics.library GetOutlinePen/SetOutlinePen pair and previous-value contract pass (GD9930 added; 2026-10-26): read both selected vector bodies (28 `cloc 2.06` C lines combined), confirmed manifest inclusion (`rom/graphics/mmakefile.src:112,178`) and ABI declarations in `graphics.conf`. The RastPort field is signed `BYTE`, the getter casts it to `UBYTE`, but the setter assigns it directly to `ULONG oldPen` before storing the new value. Because the public setter documents “Previous outline pen” and its pen parameter is `ULONG`, a valid stored byte 128–255 is returned sign-extended rather than as its unsigned pen number. Added GD9930, scoped to callers consuming the return value; selected `SetRPAttrsA()` and the maintained Icon drawing caller ignore it. The latter obtains current outline color through the normalized GetOutlinePen path in `AreaEnd()`; no direct field consumer was found outside these implementation/support paths. No rendering or pen change was run. These two paths are now explicitly body-reviewed; external callers and wider graphics API closure remain open; source-only.

Graphics.library SetMaxPen/GetRPAttrsA pen-mask contract recheck (2026-10-26; no new GD or LOC credit): re-read both complete vector bodies and compared SetMaxPen's stated maximum-index contract with its mask calculation and `GetRPAttrsA(RPTAG_MaxPen)`'s power-of-two result. For a positive maximum pen `p`, SetMaxPen stores the low-bit mask through the next power-of-two boundary; the getter reports that boundary (256 when the mask is zero). This is consistent with the representable pen range implied by the mask, while SetMaxPen(0) intentionally leaves the mask unchanged. `SetRPAttrsA(RPTAG_MaxPen)` is a no-op, but the setter documentation does not list that tag as supported. The maintained C search found no SetMaxPen or RPTAG_MaxPen caller; only the public vectors are exposed. The wording does not establish a precise getter round-trip contract, so no off-by-one finding is promoted. Existing complete-body credits for `setmaxpen.c` and `getrpattrsa.c` stand; generated vectors/external clients remain outside the caller census. No RastPort operation was run; source-only.

### Graphics RGB4 palette vector recheck (GD5910 expanded; 2026-10-26)

| Selected source | Status and evidence |
|---|---|
| `rom/graphics/getrgb4.c` | Full 16 `cloc 2.06` C code lines reread. `entry` is signed `LONG`; the invalid-entry guard rejects only `entry >= colormap->Count`, then indexes `ColorTable[entry]` (`:53-61`). Negative indices therefore bypass the guard and read before the table. Checked-in GetRGB4 loops in `workbench/libs/reqtools/general.c:295` and `workbench/prefs/palette/paleditor.c:344,388` use nonnegative loop indices; no maintained negative-index caller was found. Retain as the existing external-invalid-index candidate; no in-tree trigger established. |
| `rom/graphics/loadrgb4.c` | Full 50 `cloc 2.06` C code lines reread. Positive signed `WORD count` controls both allocation and loops. On successful allocation the routine calls `internal_SetRGB32Colors(vp,...,0,count,...)` after converting every input color; on allocation failure it calls `SetRGB32(vp,t,...)` for each index (`:64-99`, `setrgb32.c:63-124`). Both paths reach GD5910's unchecked HIDD pixel-table write. `AllocBitMap()` creates exactly `AROS_PALETTE_SIZE` entries for displayable HIDD bitmaps (`allocbitmap.c:423-424`; constant 256 in `gfxfuncsupport.h:109-110`); counts above 256 therefore include index 256. Expanded GD5910 to include LoadRGB4's direct and allocation-fallback routes. |

Caller check: maintained Palette Preferences obtains `data->count` from its screen palette setup and uses it in the save/restore loops (`workbench/prefs/palette/paleditor.c:344-407`); the 2View demo uses image-derived `numColors` or a fixed 16 (`developer/demos/2View/Misc.c:235,465,480`). No checked-in call with count above 256 was established. Finding scope remains the public LoadRGB4 API on a displayable HIDD viewport when caller-provided `count > 256`; source-only, no palette operation or allocation failure induced. These are explicit path/body rows for the two RGB4 vectors; no subsystem completion is implied.

| Selected source | Review result |
|---|---|

The loop has no ColorMap/null/range guard and delegates direct indexed reads to `color_get()`; retained existing caller-specific GD9578 and GD4292, no separate API finding added in this pass. Out-of-range caller indices and destination table extent remain caller preconditions. |

Existing selected callers validate or derive indices, while failed-pen sentinel paths are already recorded under GD4292/GD9578. No additional independently triggered issue established. |

No separate allocation-failure defect established. |

Graphics.library shared-pen reference-count overflow pass (GD9931 added; 2026-10-26; no new file/LOC credit): re-read the complete `obtainpen.c`, `obtainbestpena.c`, and `releasepen.c` bodies, including the selected PaletteExtra locking and list transitions. `PalExtra_RefCnt_Type` is signed `WORD` (`graphics_intern.h:71,74`); both shared acquisition paths increment without saturation while holding the PaletteExtra semaphore (`obtainpen.c:135-145,185-191,230-256`; `obtainbestpena.c:92-106,119-154`). At 65,536 outstanding successful references on the 16-bit two's-complement target representation, the stored count wraps to zero. `ReleasePen()` tests zero as the exclusive case and links the pen into the free list without removing its still-live shared-list entry (`releasepen.c:57-85,147-155`). Added GD9931 for the resulting premature reuse, qualified to this high-count public-API condition; no checked-in individual caller establishes 65,536 live references. Existing lock recursion and regular list-membership checks remain as previously audited. Source-only; no pen operations or concurrency were run.

Graphics.library LoadRGB32 table/fallback pass (GD5910 retained; 2026-10-26; body/path already credited): reread all of `rom/graphics/loadrgb32.c` and `setrgb32.c`, the shared `internal_SetRGB32Colors()` helper, the RGB32 vector declarations, and all direct maintained C callers. The top-word count is at most 65,535, so the temporary `HIDDT_Color` byte-size multiplication itself does not overflow on the fixed 32-bit ULONG ABI; `first + count` likewise cannot overflow ULONG. The table format has no separate byte-length argument, so each nonzero record's three-component source extent remains the caller's responsibility. In both successful-allocation and allocation-fallback branches, a record range beyond the 256-entry HIDD pixel table reaches GD5910; the ColorMap setter's per-entry upper-bound rejection does not bound the subsequent HIDD translation-table write. Checked-in calls are OpenScreen initialization and ColorWheel's bounded palette table; no additional independently triggered defect was established. No table, allocation failure or display was exercised; source-only.

Graphics.library HIDD color-update backend consistency pass (GD9932 added; 2026-10-26; existing bodies/path credit, no LOC increment): traced `SetRGB32()`/`LoadRGB32()` through `internal_SetRGB32Colors()` and the generic HIDD bitmap SetColors method into the VESA, EFI framebuffer and SM502 overrides. Each override invokes the generic superclass first (which can update/extend its software ColorMap), then checks the mode palette limit and returns FALSE on an excessive range. The graphics helper ignores that result and still updates the 256-entry pixel translation table. OpenScreen's minimum 32-entry ColorMap combined with a 4bpp target supplies valid ColorMap indices 16-31 that exceed the 16-entry hardware limit. Added GD9932 for the resulting software/hardware palette divergence. The three backend paths are separately selected modules; no device or display operation was run. Source-only.

Graphics HIDD SetColors backend census follow-up (GD9932 expanded; SDL GD9933 added; 2026-10-26): searched all checked-in implementations of `Hidd_BitMap_SetColors`, then traced range checks and superclass ordering for each. Confirmed the capacity-reject/ignored-return pattern in VESA, EFI framebuffer, SM502, Raspberry Pi framebuffer, VGA, VideoCore, VMware SVGA and LinuxFB; the LinuxFB implementation rejects before its superclass update, while the others in this set perform or delegate generic color-map mutation first. This expands GD9932 to cover software translation-table divergence across those selected backend implementations where the HIDD bitmap range is narrower than the ColorMap. X11 and SDL do not use the same explicit `1 << bpp` rejection path. The SDL indexed-color path separately allocates an `SDL_Color` array, dereferences it without a NULL check, and omits freeing it after `SDL_SetColors()`; added GD9933 for optional hosted SDL builds. No HIDD or SDL display was run and no allocation failure was induced; source-only.

SDL HIDD selection and color-array ownership scope note (GD9933; 2026-10-26): checked `arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/mmakefile.src:3-20` and `arch/all-unix/boot/mmakefile.src:42-44`. The `kernel-hidd-sdl` target builds a standalone `SDL` monitor program; its option-controlled parent edge is commented in the Unix boot aggregate. GD9933 therefore applies to builds that explicitly select the SDL HIDD target, not by default to all hosted Unix images. The `SDL_Color` array is an implementation-local scratch buffer passed to `SDL_SetColors()`; the AROS function retains no pointer to that local array, and no free appears on the success path. SDL API documents `SDL_SetColors` as setting a portion of the surface colormap, consistent with synchronous palette update semantics ([SDL 1.2.15 SDL_SetColors documentation](https://www.libsdl.org/release/SDL-1.2.15/docs/html/sdlsetcolors.html)). No SDL target was built and no palette operation was run.

The current findings distinguish these routes and do not rely on one failure being proof of another. No GUI or allocation/window failure was induced; source-only.

ReadPixelLine8 32,768-pixel boundary refinement (GD9804 strengthened; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): traced the width-32,768 call through `ReadPixelLine8()` endpoint arithmetic, `ReadPixelArray8()` renderer callback, `rp8_render()` signed-WORD inclusive-width conversion, and the selected PlanarBM `GetImageLUT()` implementation (`rom/graphics/readpixelline8.c:59-66`; `readpixelarray8.c:21-32,97-123`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:662-704`). At this exact boundary, endpoint conversion may yield the valid stop coordinate 32,767, but the renderer and planar-reader signed WORD widths become negative and the selected `WORD x` loop copies no pixels; the returned count may itself be negative. Picture/animation callers ignore that result and consume the uncleared row. For widths 32,769–65,535, the wrapper can instead produce a stop before xstart and `ReadPixelArray8()` returns zero. Updated GD9804 to include the 32,768 boundary and distinguish the two paths. No build, bitmap, or pixel transfer was run; source-only.

Intuition pointer-color palette-base encoding trace (GD9938 added; 2026-10-26; no source-body/LOC credit): followed OpenScreen's depth-four `spritebase` calculation and packed `VTAG_SPEVEN_BASE_SET` value (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1406,1585,1588-1590`) through OpenScreen’s displayable HIDD bitmap allocation, VideoControl storage, SetPointerColors decoding, SetRGB32 and the HIDD bitmap translation-table allocation (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1225-1238`; `rom/graphics/videocontrol.c:128-130`; `rom/intuition/misc.c:267-271,331-358`; `rom/graphics/setrgb32.c:43-52,116-124`; `rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:423-426`). For depth four, base 8 is packed as `0x0800`, but the unmasked decoder returns `0x8008`, and the pointer update writes entries `0x8009..0x800B` past the 256-entry table even though SetRGB32CM rejects them against OpenScreen's minimum 32-entry ColorMap. Traced the maintained IPrefs pointer-preference caller (`setiprefs.c:176-178`). Added GD9938 as a caller-produced index defect distinct from GD5910's generic unchecked index and GD9937's separate palette offset error. Trigger requires pointer preference loading/update with a four-plane HIDD-backed screen on a mode with `dimensions.MaxDepth <= 8`; no pointer, screen, or palette operation was run. Source-only.

OpenScreen one-/two-plane sprite-base underflow trace (GD9939 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): checked the declared `UWORD spritebase`, low-depth calculation, bitmap mode/depth selection, and screen-initialization pointer-color loop (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:175,896,1225-1238,1585,1661-1683`). For one- and two-plane `ns.Depth`, `(1 << ns.Depth) - 8` is -6/-4 and converts to UWORD 65530/65532. When the selected mode maximum depth is at most eight, OpenScreen chooses minimum depth eight for mode lookup but requests the bitmap at `ns.Depth`, then calls SetRGB32 on `spritebase + 1..3` because those values exceed `numcolors`. Traced the `BMATags_DisplayID` request into HIDD allocation and the unchecked 256-entry translation-table write (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:219-226,242-250,423-426`; `rom/graphics/setrgb32.c:43-52,115-124`; `gfxfuncsupport.h:109-110`). CloseScreen/OpenWindow private-screen serialization recheck (GD9942 added; 2026-10-26; no body/LOC credit): traced CloseScreen's initial `FirstWindow` check before `WindowLock`, its later locked screen-membership-only check, and the private-screen close branch through screen unlink and resource teardown (`rom/intuition/closescreen.c:105-163,331-407`). Compared OpenWindow's ordinary-task `WindowLock` scope, final `FirstWindow` publication and lock release (`rom/intuition/openwindow.c:1048-1085,1618-1622`): an open that publishes after CloseScreen's initial check can complete first, after which CloseScreen acquires the lock but does not recheck `FirstWindow`. `int_closescreen()` checks `FirstWindow` only inside the `pubScrNode` branch, so private custom screens lack that guard. Confirmed `WA_CustomScreen` sets the supplied screen as `CUSTOMSCREEN` without a visitor lock (`openwindow.c:341-344,604-625`), while OpenScreen defaults `dowindowlock` true for ordinary tasks (`openscreen.c:146,2223-2231`). Private custom-screen CloseScreen/OpenWindow serialization recheck (GD9942 retained; 2026-10-26; no LOC credit): verified the precise ordinary-task interleaving against lock acquisition and publication: CloseScreen reads `FirstWindow` before `LOCKWINDOW` (`closescreen.c:108-124`); OpenWindow acquires that same semaphore, runs `int_openwindow()`, publishes `screen->FirstWindow`, then releases it (`openwindow.c:1048-1085,1621-1622`). CloseScreen subsequently owns the semaphore but its validation checks only that the screen remains in `FirstScreen` (`closescreen.c:125-143`); `int_closescreen()` repeats the `FirstWindow` guard only for screens with `pubScrNode` (`:331-346`), so a private custom screen still proceeds to unlink and teardown (`:360-407`, then `CloseScreen():168-253,273-300`). This confirms the race is not prevented by the global WindowLock; it requires the stated ordering and an ordinary task path that participates in the lock. Public-screen visitor references remain a separate guard. No window/screen operations were run; source-only.

GD9896 large-list reachability and consumer consequence recheck (2026-10-26; no new finding or LOC credit): re-read the selected `FRGetDirectory()` `Examine`/`ExNext` loop and node insertion (`workbench/libs/asl/filereqsupport.c:444-628`), `CountNodes()` (`basicfuncs.c:959-969`), list-view `ASLLV_Labels` count and `makenodetable()` (`listviewclass.c:149-174,493-518`), and file requester multi-select sizing/copy (`filereqhooks.c:1805-1860`). GD9912 selected-qsort behavior recheck (2026-10-26; finding retained and mechanism confirmed; no LOC credit): followed ASL's `WORD numentries` assignment into the selected C library `qsort()` implementation. `qsort` is present in the common and static function sets in `compiler/crt/stdc/mmakefile.src:500-540,840-865`; `qsort.c` emits the shared algorithm from `__qsort.h` (`compiler/crt/stdc/qsort.c:73-80`). Wanderer GD9924 initial-progress callback scope correction (2026-10-26; finding retained, trigger broadened; no LOC credit): reread `performDataCopy()`'s first `CallHook()` before `Open()`/`Read()` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:172-180`) against the selected `Wanderer__HookFunc_DisplayCopyFunc()` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/wanderer.c:162-178`). Wanderer GD9925 delete-success propagation recheck (finding retained; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): traced the `CombinePath()` failure branch in `deleteDirectoryContents()` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:352-377`) through `DeleteContent()` (`:807-830`) and `IsDirectoryEmpty()` (`filesystems_utilities.c:93-107`). A NULL child path is skipped without setting `stop`; subsequent `ExNext()` reaches normal end and leaves `stop == FALSE`, which is the helper's success value. The parent checks the directory, sees the skipped entry remains, avoids `deleteSingleFile()` on the nonempty parent, and returns `FALSE` as successful completion. `CombinePath()` returns NULL on its allocation failure (`filesystems_utilities.c:489-514`). This confirms GD9925's false-success consequence at the public operation boundary, not only the helper. No allocation failure or deletion was run; source-only.

Wanderer GD9926 recursive-copy null-path contract recheck (finding retained; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): traced `copyDirectory()`'s unchecked `CombinePath()` result into `CopyContent()` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:487-495,634-640`). On allocation failure `CombinePath()` returns NULL (`filesystems_utilities.c:489-514`). `infoFileSetup(NULL)` first calls `FileExists(NULL)`; the selected DOS `Lock()` explicitly returns `BNULL` for a NULL name (`rom/dos/lock.c:31-74`), so `FileExists()` returns FALSE, after which `infoFileSetup()` unconditionally calls `ConstructInfofileName(NULL)` (`filesystems.c:512-532`). That helper evaluates `strlen(path)` before its allocation check (`filesystems_utilities.c:577-588`), confirming the NULL dereference path. The caller then cannot reach its normal `CopyContent()` error return. No allocation failure or recursive copy was run; source-only.

GD9598 relaunch ordering recheck (finding retained; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-10-26): traced Find's Stop/Start path into Process.mui (`workbench/system/find/findgroup_class.c:768-787`): Stop's Kill writes `data->kill = 1` and does not clear it on worker exit; the worker only clears `data->task` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/process.c:41-53,152-185`). Relaunch calls `CreateNewProc()` before writing the returned task pointer and before resetting `data->kill` (`:193-220`). DOS process creation publishes the child through AddTask while Forbid is held, then calls Permit before returning; Exec documents that the child can finish and be freed before the creator resumes (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:543-564`). The execution window therefore permits the relaunched worker to read the stale kill flag and exit, with parent/worker writes racing on `data->task`. GD9598 already describes this ordering and the SMP/scheduling-dependent scope; no separate finding established. No process, stop/restart sequence or schedule was run; source-only.

Graphics.library `ReleasePen()` complete-body and shared-reference-count audit (GD9955 added; 2026-10-27): read the complete selected `rom/graphics/releasepen.c` body (66 `cloc 2.06` C code lines), confirmed it is selected by `rom/graphics/mmakefile.src:159`, and followed its free/shared-list mutation against `ObtainPen()` and `ObtainBestPenA()`. Both acquire paths hold the PaletteExtra semaphore and increment `PalExtra_RefCnt_Type` without a limit; this field is signed 16-bit `WORD`. ASL eraser allocation-failure ordering recheck (GD9873 retained; 2026-10-27; no body/LOC credit): re-read `AslEraser__GM_RENDER()` and the actual region/gadget-list operations (`workbench/libs/asl/eraserclass.c:85-129`; `rom/graphics/clearrectregion.c:74-105`; `rom/graphics/intregions.c:748-756`; `rom/intuition/gadgetclass.c:152-156`; `rom/intuition/refreshglist.c:147-162,239-263`). `ClearRectRegion()` commits its temporary result only on success; a failed `_DoOperationBandBand()` disposes the temporary list and leaves the input region untouched. `GA_Previous` links the eraser immediately after the referenced gadget, and the refresh iteration follows the linked order. Therefore a failed subtraction for a previously rendered gadget leaves its area available to the eraser's subsequent background fill; later gadgets can repaint only when they occur after the eraser. This confirms GD9873's order-dependent trigger without broadening it. No allocation failure or redraw was run; source-only.

Once `bo->map` is non-NULL, `PutPixel()` and `GetPixel()` skip the bitmap semaphore; neither takes `globalLock`, while accelerated methods take both locks and publish `gpu_dirty` only after queuing the operation (`nouveau_bitmapclass.c:244-278,288-329,382-423`; `nouveau_intern.h:254-261,300`; `nv04_exa.c:464-475`; corresponding NV50/NVC0 helpers). PNG icon ToolTypes `CopyMemQuick()` resize and cleanup caller pass (2026-10-27; no new GD or body/LOC credit): traced `diskobjPNGio.c`'s ToolTypes growth (`:535-572`) through `AllocMemIcon()`/`AddFreeList()` and `FreeDiskObject()`/`FreeFreeList()` (`support.c:495-510`; `addfreelist.c:30-69`; `freediskobject.c:59-69`; `freefreelist.c:35-55`). Each resize array, including superseded arrays, is registered in the DiskObject free list; the source TODO to free the old array is retained-memory overhead until object destruction, not a leak past `FreeDiskObject()`. `MEMF_CLEAR` on the replacement preserves the NULL terminator after copied entries. GD4292 failed-sentinel cleanup caller follow-up (2026-10-27; no new ID or body/LOC credit): traced the invalid `UBYTE` pen sentinel through both teardown loops. Picture increments `pd->NumAlloc` even when `ObtainBestPen()` returns -1, then `FreeDest()` releases every recorded entry (`colorhandling.c:1034-1044,416-423`). Animation increments `acd_NumAlloc` before the allocation and `DT_FreePens()` later releases every recorded byte (`animationclass.c:422-430,253-267`). With a ColorMap `Count >= 256`, the narrowed 255 passes ReleasePen's `n < cm->Count` guard; if another client owns pen 255, its shared reference can be decremented or its exclusive pen can be inserted into the free list (`rom/graphics/releasepen.c:57-85,147-155`). This extends GD4292's consequence beyond the existing `Count < 256` out-of-range `GetRGB32()` read to conditional release of a pen not acquired by the datatype. Caller cleanup bodies were already credited; no palette or teardown operation was run; source-only.

`MakeVPort()` temporary viewport failure-cleanup ownership recheck (existing finding retained; 2026-10-27; no new GD or LOC credit): re-read `rom/graphics/freevportcoplists.c` in full (93 physical lines / 41 `cloc 2.06` C lines) and the relevant `MakeVPort()` bitmap-state transitions (`rom/graphics/makevport.c:108-232`). For a new VPE, VPD allocation is stored in `DriverData[0]`; a successfully created planar wrapper is owned only when `VPXF_WRAPPED_BITMAP` is set. If subsequent display viewport setup fails before any `PreviousBitmap` exists, `MakeVPort()`'s rollback has no prior object to restore and its `own_vpe` branch calls `GfxFree()`; `GfxFree()` removes/frees the VPE without freeing DriverData, so the VPD and possibly the owned wrapper are lost, as documented in the existing MakeVPort failure-cleanup finding above. `FreeVPortCopLists()` disposes the current wrapper and any separately retained owned `PreviousBitmap`; tracing the transitions shows those represent distinct objects in the retained-previous case, so this pass did not establish a second disposal of one object. The selected `CloseScreen()` caller still ignores `RethinkDisplay()` failure before freeing coplists (existing compositor-staleness finding); the copper test directly frees only after its own setup path. Region rectangle operator selected caller pass (2026-10-27; no new GD or body/LOC credit): enumerated maintained callers of `AndRectRegionND`/`OrRectRegionND` and compared their copy-returning contracts with the destructive public wrappers. `ScrollRegion()` is the sole checked-in native C caller of `AndRectRegionND`; it checks the returned copy, clips the translated cut with non-failing `AndRectRegion()`, checks `ClearRectRegionND()` and `OrRegionRegion()` before swapping, and disposes temporary regions on all paths (`rom/graphics/scrollregion.c:58-92`; `andrectregion.c:48-145`; `clearrectregionnd.c:54-110`). No ownership or failure-path mismatch was established in that caller. `OrRectRegionND` has no checked-in native C caller; its maintained generated m68k-emulation thunk forwards the returned region pointer without changing semantics (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:4330-4335`). External callers and malformed/null API arguments remain outside this pass. No region operation was run; source-only.


Region band-operation one-sided and allocation-unwind recheck (2026-10-27; no new GD or body/LOC credit): read `_OrBandBand`, `_AndBandBand`, `_ClearBandBand` and `_DoOperationBandBand()`'s result cleanup (`rom/graphics/intregions.c:432-760`) against `AndRectRegionND`, `OrRectRegionND`, and `ClearRectRegionND` source ordering. Union copies either surviving band; intersection emits no rectangle when either operand is absent; clear preserves the minuend when only the region band remains, matching `ClearRectRegionND()`'s argument order (`:76-107`). NListtree table-growth failure caller recheck (GD9736 confirmed; 2026-10-27; no new finding or LOC credit): re-read `NLCreateTable()`/`NLAddToTable()` and traced both relevant callers (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:987-1053,2561-2586,7064-7253`). `InsertTreeNode()` ignores `NLAddToTable()`; `_NListtree_Insert()` likewise ignores the result after linking and adding visibility, then increments `NumEntries` and returns the node. This confirms failed growth does not roll back the inserted node or stop later insertions. At 64 allocated slots, a failed attempt to grow to 128 leaves `tb_Size == 128` with the original 64-slot `tb_Table`; the next insertion writes at index 64. At full capacity the final shift iteration reads `tb_Table[tb_Entries + 1]`, one pointer beyond the allocated table; the copied value lands in `tb_Table[tb_Entries]` and is immediately overwritten by the explicit NULL clear. NListtree selected-table allocation-failure caller recheck (GD9735 confirmed and scoped; 2026-10-27; no new GD or LOC credit): traced `TreeNodeSelectAdd()` through `_NListtree_SelectChange()`, `_NListtree_Select()`, and `MUIM_NListtree_NextSelected` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:987-1053,1492-1498,1513-1562,9710-9754,9828-9870,10510-10518`). On a visible selection, `_NListtree_SelectChange()` ignores the add result, sets `TNF_SELECTED`, and publishes `MUIA_NListtree_SelectChange`; `_NListtree_Select()` returns the requested selection state. NextSelected reads only the table, so the node is omitted despite its selected flag. If the first SelectedTable allocation fails, `tb_Size` remains 64 with `tb_Table == NULL`; the next add bypasses growth and writes through NULL. This is distinct from GD9736's sibling-list table growth failure. The NListtree full-body credit already exists; no path/LOC increment. No selection or allocation failure was run; source-only.

NListtree NextSelected maintained-caller correction (GD9838 strengthened; 2026-10-27; no new finding or LOC credit): searched the source tree for `MUIM_NListtree_NextSelected` and traced every selected direct caller. Generic chunky `PutTemplate` final-word overread recheck (GD9833 retained; 2026-10-27; no new finding or LOC credit): re-read `BltTemplate()` endpoint/modulo setup, `blttemplate_render()` clipping callback, `CBM__Hidd_BitMap__PutTemplate()` dispatch, and the final-pixel mask advancement in all four 8/16/24/32-bit helpers (`rom/graphics/blttemplate.c:17-27,93-110`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:756-817`; `gfx_bitmapmemblit.c:819-1463`). A 16-pixel row begins at bit 15 and the sixteenth iteration consumes that bit, advances the `UWORD *`, then loads the next word before the loop exits. `RASSIZE(16,1)` allocates two bytes (`rom/graphics/allocraster.c:48-53`), and the public `srcMod` contract permits a two-byte row. The direct `Text()` fallback uses `raswidth_bpr = raswidth16 / 8`, `RASSIZE(raswidth,rasheight)`, and calls `BltTemplate()` with `raswidth` (`rom/graphics/text.c:137-154,381-388`); a two-character fast-font run supplies the exact 16-pixel boundary. GD9833 remains supported across all four generic pixel-width helpers and this maintained caller. No drawing or allocation was run; source-only.

NListtree/NList rejected-row metadata follow-up (GD9862 refined; 2026-10-27; no new finding or LOC credit): rechecked the full failure handoff from `InsertNListEntry()` through NList's `MUIM_NList_InsertSingle` wrapper, `NL_List_Insert()` construct-hook branches, and `MUIM_NList_GetEntryInfo(-3)` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:1271-1285,1804-1815`; `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_func2.c:626-648,775-800,1798-1805`; `NList_func.c:1524-1565`). NList writes `NList_LastInserted` only after a non-NULL constructed entry and resets the value to -1 on Clear; a rejected construct therefore leaves the previous successful index intact. With a prior row, NListtree's unchecked `-3` query binds the new tree node to that row's private NList entry. Without any previous row, the query returns a NULL entry and sentinel position; the report's wrong-prior-row consequence is correctly scoped to a populated NList. GD9862 remains one inherited-construct-hook defect. No insertion, hook, allocation failure or GUI was run; source-only.

GD10086 in-flight OpenScreen/handover overlap recheck (2026-11-01; trigger strengthened; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read the caller timeline rather than only the successful final state. `OpenScreen()` resolves the mode, allocates the `BMATags_DisplayID` bitmap (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1104-1109,1225-1238`), and only later calls `DoSyncAction()` to run `int_openscreen()` (`:2297-2303`); that action performs `MakeVPort()` and `int_RethinkDisplay()` before the viewport is loaded (`:2418-2486`; `rethinkdisplay.c:105-162`; `loadview.c:55-65`). `mdd->display` and `mdd->frontbm` are assigned only in the subsequent `display_LoadViewPorts()` path (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:511-518,574-611`). `OpenScreen()` does not hold `displaydb_sem` during bitmap allocation or setup, while handover takes it for registration/removal; no shared lock spans these two paths. `display_Expunge()` calls `DriverNotify` directly, and the selected Intuition `DisplayDriverNotify()` does not route removal through the same `DoSyncAction()` (`graphics_display.c:218-252`; `rom/intuition/monitorclass.c:50-76`). Therefore an overlapping handover can pass the empty viewport/front-bitmap guard after the new bitmap has captured the raw display pointer but before viewport publication. This is a selected in-tree race window; it does not claim deterministic scheduling or that a completed OpenScreen leaves a persistent no-viewport bitmap. It supersedes the prior conclusion that no maintained caller establishes an in-flight setup overlap. No screen open, driver handover, or schedule was run; source-only.

Generic HIDD `MapColor()` 65,536-entry loop recheck (GD4631 promoted from summary to detailed candidate; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): re-read `BM__Hidd_BitMap__MapColor()` and traced the count's type and creation/attachment route. Wanderer AppIcon split-label overread candidate recheck (GD9402 detailed and condition narrowed; 2026-10-27; no path/LOC credit): re-traced `AppIcon_GetLabel()` through volume-list `MUIM_IconList_CreateEntry()`, its `strlen+1` pool copy, and multiline label creation into `IconList__LabelFunc_SplitLabel()`. Graphics.library M68K thunk/vector coverage recheck (2026-10-28; no new candidate; no body/LOC credit): compared the `graphics.conf` public/private function declarations with the generated graphics thunk set and the separately registered manual thunk vectors, then traced dispatch in `M68KEmu_SetupLibBase()` and Moira `willExecute()`. MUI Application window-position restore and remaining OM_SET/GET slice (GD10124 added; 2026-10-28; targeted review, no body/LOC credit): inspected the remainder of `Application__OM_SET()`/`Application__OM_GET()` and traced saved-position restore through `Configdata_GetWindowPos()`, `windowpos_swapbytes()`, `MUIM_Dataspace_Find()` and `MUIA_Application_CopyWinPosToApp`. MUI Application `MUIA_ShowMe` mutation-safe window iteration recheck (2026-10-28; no new GD or LOC credit): tested the loop's stated reentrancy case against its exact restart logic (`application.c:1153-1204`). After each child Set returns, `lastwin` is set to that current window; on the next iteration the code reacquires the Family list and searches for that still-present node before selecting its successor. Consequently insertion/removal of other windows during Setup/Cleanup is handled without retaining the invalidated list cursor. The code explicitly assumes the current window does not remove itself; under that stated contract, a self-removal counterexample is out of scope. No separate iteration defect was established. Window ShowMe can open/close the native window and cause Setup/Cleanup (`window.c:3177-3198,3849-3875`), matching the reason for re-reading the list. No window or callback was run; source-only.

Graph per-source capacity multiplication overflow recheck (GD9781 expanded; 2026-10-28; no path/LOC credit): re-read `Graph__UpdateSourceEntries()`, `Graph__OM_SET()`, the timer consumer, `IPTR` typedef and CPU pointer-size fallback (`workbench/classes/zune/graph/graph.c:76-100,357-373,924-963`; `compiler/include/exec/types.h:83-85`; `compiler/include/aros/cpu.h:88-90`). On 32-bit builds, `count=0x40000001` makes `sizeof(IPTR) * count` wrap to four bytes; if that allocation succeeds, the helper installs one-element storage while `OM_SET` commits the much larger count. Periodic sampling eventually supplies an out-of-capacity slot to the source hook. Repository search found no checked-in `MUIA_Graph_EntryCount` caller supplying an extreme count; this is scoped to external/future 32-bit clients. Kept this under GD9781 because it has the same incorrect per-source capacity versus published global count invariant. No allocation, timer, client call or build was run; source-only.

MUI Application config-change window-state failure-path caller recheck (GD5636/GD5637 retained; 2026-10-28; no body/LOC credit): re-read `Application__CloseWindows()`, both configuration-change callers, `OpenWindows()`, and `PushMethod()` allocation/queue handling (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:2106-2143,2146-2164,2261-2268,2276-2316,1893-1925`). Confirmed the list-allocation NULL is ambiguous: it means either no child list or snapshot allocation failure, while each open window is still closed; OpenWindows(NULL) then opens every child, including ones previously closed. If a per-window node allocation fails, the non-NULL list reopens only the successfully recorded windows. Separately, after a successful snapshot, both callers ignore PushMethod's return; CreateMQNode failure means no callback is queued, so OpenWindows cannot reopen/free the snapshot. SetConfigdata has already disposed the old configdata and installed the new one before this queue attempt. These are the distinct state and ownership consequences already tracked by GD5636 and GD5637; no additional defect established. No allocation failure or GUI operation was induced; source-only.


MUI Application generated Base truncation caller recheck (GD9927 expanded; 2026-10-28; no path/LOC credit): re-read the non-single-task branch of `Application__OM_NEW()` and checked the public `MUIA_Application_Base` declaration (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:419-446`; `application.h:202-203,232-233`). The 255-byte `portname` buffer stores at most 254 characters; for a Base length of 253 or more, `snprintf("%s.%d")` truncates the varying numeric suffix, making every `.1` through `.999` availability probe identical. Since the new tracking node is not published until after resource initialization, a later constructor with the same long Base misses the already-used string during all probes and duplicates it when the loop exhausts. Also checked the apparent nested `ZuneSemaphore` acquisition in the single-task branch: Exec `InternalObtainSemaphore()` increments `ss_NestCount` when the current task already owns the semaphore (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:101-112`), so this is not a self-deadlock. No maintained caller with a Base this long was found. Expanded GD9927 with this sequential trigger alongside its concurrent check-to-publish and suffix-exhaustion cases; no separate finding or file credit. No MUI startup was run; source-only.


MUI Application config-notification message lifetime recheck (no new GD or body/LOC credit; 2026-10-28): traced `Application_SetupConfigNotify()` and its failure cleanup through `Application__OM_DISPOSE()` and `Application__MUIM_NewInput()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:346-374,957-964,1800-1815`). On successful setup the request uses `NRF_SEND_MESSAGE` and points to the app-owned port; setup failures free the duplicated name and delete/reset the port. During normal input handling the app replies to every queued `NotifyMessage`. On teardown it calls `EndNotify()` before deleting the port; DOS `EndNotify()` removes and replies any still-queued messages for that request when `nr_MsgCount > 0` (`rom/dos/endnotify.c:64-100`). No separate app-side queued-message leak or port-lifetime defect established for this selected path. This is a caller/ownership check only; no notification or teardown was run. Source-only.


Intuition system-gadget DrawInfo lifetime caller recheck (2026-10-28; no finding or coverage credit): traced `CreateWinSysGadgets()` through selected `GetScreenDrawInfo()`, `FreeScreenDrawInfo()`, each `WDM_LAYOUT_BORDERGADGETS` dispatch, and the caller in `OpenWindow()` (`rom/intuition/intuition_misc.c:211-217,532-560`; `rom/intuition/openwindow.c:1575`). A repository-wide C search found only the Mesa swap-buffer caller of `BltPipeResourceRastPort()`; it passes the context offsets and framebuffer dimensions (`workbench/libs/mesa/mesa3dgl_glaswapbuffers.c:63-65`). Those offsets originate in public `GLA_Left`/`GLA_Top` tags or window borders, and the API docs require geometry to fit the RastPort but do not define numeric bounds (`mesa3dgl_glacreatecontext.c:53-76`). The separate Raspberry Pi V3D/VC4 source and build selection is recorded with GD10138; this local wrapper slice does not by itself close all Gallium backends or Mesa dependencies.

StringGadget numeric input conversion boundary recheck (2026-10-29; no new GD or body/LOC credit): followed the complete `DoSGHKey()` numeric-edit branch in `rom/intuition/strgadgets.c:1148-1225` through `atol()` to the selected C runtime `compiler/crt/stdc/atol.c:48-50` and `strtol.c:106-147`. The input filter permits only a leading minus and decimal digits for `GACT_LONGINT`; `strtol()` detects `ULONG` accumulation overflow and returns the signed LONG endpoint, including negative overflow, so long digit strings do not wrap into an unrelated in-range value in this implementation.
