VGAGfx cursor aperture consequence recheck (GD6140 retained and narrowed; no body/LOC credit; 2026-10-29): rechecked the fixed VGA mode table and cursor address calculation in `arch/all-native/hidd/vgagfx/vgagfx_displayclass.c:37-42,338-389` against `vgaRefreshArea()` clipping in `vgagfx_support.c:445-480`. The selected 640×480 mode uses an 80-byte planar row, so active display rows occupy 38,400 bytes of the standard 64 KiB VGA aperture. The cursor loop lacks a `disp_height` guard and erasure clips at that height, establishing writes/stale contents beyond the active framebuffer. The checked-in code does not establish an ordinary cursor shape large enough to reach beyond the VGA aperture; narrowed GD6140 to stale off-screen aperture memory and removed the unsupported implication of host-memory/aperture overrun. No cursor, VGA memory, or hardware operation was run; source-only.


VGAGfx cursor hotspot and physical-versus-bitmap dimension contract recheck (GD6141–GD6142 retained; no body/LOC credit; 2026-10-29): traced `PointerClass__OM_NEW()` and `MonitorClass__MM_SetPointerShape()`/`SetPointerPos()` (`rom/intuition/pointerclass.c:48-169`; `rom/intuition/monitorclass.c:81-100,1916-1960`) against the public display method contract (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:461`). Intuition creates the pointer bitmap from the supplied bitmap dimensions, passes the pointer x/y hotspot offsets to `SetCursorShape()`, then sends the logical pointer position unchanged to `SetCursorPos()`. The VGA shape method consumes bitmap width/height and pixels but not the offsets; its position method clamps against the visible bitmap width/height. The VGA bitmap constructor stores requested bitmap dimensions separately from the selected mode dimensions and does not require equality (`arch/all-native/hidd/vgagfx/vgagfx_bitmapclass.c:48-91`); its displayable-buffer setup also clears physical rows/columns outside a smaller bitmap (`:265-317`). This supports the stated nonzero-hotspot and dimension-mismatch triggers for GD6141/GD6142. The public method text says hotspot offsets are generally needed for hosted cursor implementations, so GD6141 remains framed as ignored supplied hotspot data and visual displacement, without asserting a universal hit-test consequence. No new independent defect or body credit; no pointer, bitmap, or display operation was run. Source-only.


VGAGfx nested `HW_acc` acquisition recheck (no new finding; no body/LOC credit; 2026-10-29): traced `SetCursorShape`, `SetCursorPos`, `SetCursorVisible`, and the `Show`/bitmap-refresh callers into `draw_mouse()` (`arch/all-native/hidd/vgagfx/vgagfx_displayclass.c:228-385`; `vgagfx_bitmapclass.c:300-321`). Several callers hold `HW_acc` while invoking `draw_mouse()`, which obtains the same semaphore. This is not a self-deadlock: Exec `InternalObtainSemaphore()` treats an already-owned semaphore as recursive and increments `ss_NestCount` (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:90-113`); each nested `ReleaseSemaphore()` decrements the count, and only the final release clears ownership (`rom/exec/releasesemaphore.c:80-88`). No lock-reentrancy finding is added. The independent unsynchronized `mouseVisible` assignment in `SetCursorVisible()` was inspected, but no selected concurrent reader/writer interleaving with a distinct user-visible consequence was established beyond the subsequent semaphore-serialized erase/draw; not promoted. GD6229 embedded-GC initialization consequence recheck (existing finding strengthened; 2026-10-29; no new ID or coverage credit): traced `RPTAG_PenMode=FALSE` and color tags through `SetRPAttrsA()`, `GetDriverData()`, `InitRastPort()` and `WritePixel()` (`rom/graphics/setrpattrsa.c:128-160`; `graphics_inline.h:68-89`; `initrastport.c:59-68`; `writepixel.c:65-69`). <a id="vulkan-funcs-pipeline-partial-creation"></a>Vulkan-Hpp batch pipeline partial-success ownership trace (GD10225 added; no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-29): compared the enhanced compute-pipeline wrappers (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:3764-3802,3846-3898`), graphics-pipeline wrappers (`:4916-4954,4998-5050`), and beta AMDX execution-graph wrappers (`:16561-16605,16652-16708`) with the Khronos Multiple Pipeline Creation contract. Each enhanced batch wrapper calls `detail::resultCheck()` immediately after dispatch and before returning the raw vector or converting the output handles to `UniqueHandle`s. The Vulkan contract permits a failing batch to retain successfully created non-null handles and directs the application to destroy those handles. In exception-enabled mode, a mixed-success batch therefore throws before those handles are returned/adopted, leaking the successful subset. Kept the finding to vector batch overloads and excluded one-item convenience wrappers, where partial success cannot arise. The beta path is guarded by `VK_ENABLE_BETA_EXTENSIONS`; no in-tree C++ caller of these wrappers was found. `vulkan_funcs.hpp` remains under review and receives no file/LOC credit. No pipeline creation, build, or runtime was performed; source-only.

Each dispatches into a raw `std::vector<VkPipeline>`, then calls `resultCheck()` before constructing/adopting the output RAII vector; exception-enabled error returns therefore throw while non-null partial-success handles remain unowned. Vulkan-Hpp memory-map pointer error-contract follow-up (GD10223 rechecked; targeted only, no path/LOC credit; 2026-10-29): traced enhanced `Device::mapMemory()`, core `mapMemory2()`, its KHR alias, and `getMemoryMetalHandleEXT()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:1110-1129,8465-8480,22599-22613,31976-31993`). Each declares an uninitialized local pointer, passes its address to dispatch, calls `detail::resultCheck()`, and then moves the pointer into `createResultValueType()`. `ResultValue<T>` construction stores/copies that value before the caller can inspect the result (`vulkan.hpp:7527-7544`). The official Vulkan `VkResult` reference states that output parameters have undefined contents for runtime errors unless a command specifies otherwise; `vkMapMemory` and `vkMapMemory2` document memory-map, host-memory and device-memory failures ([vkMapMemory](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkMapMemory.html), [vkMapMemory2](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkMapMemory2KHR.html), [VkResult](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkResult.html)). With `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` and assertions disabled, `resultCheck()` continues on those errors and the wrapper moves the undefined output. This directly corroborates the existing GD10223 pointer-output case; it does not establish a separate root cause or broaden the finding to unrelated commands. The wrapper header remains partial and receives no file/LOC credit. No API call or build was run; source-only.

**GD10268 — DataTypes startup leaks a held NamedObject on a global name collision:** if an existing global `DataTypesList` object has no user area, `GetDataTypesList()` retains its `FindNamedObject()` reference while the replacement is rejected as a duplicate; DataTypes initialization fails and the old object's use count remains elevated. Conditional on a prior exact-name collision. See [GD10268](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10268) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L10226). No path or LOC credit changed.

**GD10269 — AddDataTypes updates shared datatype lists without their semaphore:** its initial built-in list population occurs before it takes `dtl_Lock`, while DataTypes API readers traverse those lists under the shared lock. Concurrent readers or another AddDataTypes invocation can observe/interleave list changes. Applies when AddDataTypes is included and run; no path or LOC credit changed. See [GD10269](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10269) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

**EK9101 — OpenSBI FDT missing `#size-cells` default (2026-10-30):** restored and rechecked the conditional interoperability finding. DTSpec requires compliant boot programs to provide the property but tells clients to assume one when it is absent. No matching in-tree DTB was found. **EK10215 — RISC-V large-range unmap can exhaust the page-table pool (2026-10-30):** the OpenSBI unmap walker splits each touched 2 MiB leaf into an L0 table; a 256 MiB unmap needs 128 such tables, exceeding the fixed pool once existing root/intermediate tables are counted. Exhaustion halts in the allocator. No in-tree `KrnUnmapGlobal()` caller was found, so the finding is limited to public/external API use. No path or LOC totals changed. See [EK10215](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10215) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md).

**EK10205 — task launch callback duplicate scope and caller path confirmed (2026-10-30):** manifest reconciliation limits the generic-scheduler/architecture-dispatcher pair to Sam440 and RISC-V OpenSBI. ARM-native, AArch64-native, and native RISC-V use their own scheduler implementations; Efika uses its custom scheduler. The only checked-in callback assignment is Efika's and remains outside the affected paths, so the trigger is external/future use on the two affected targets. No path or LOC totals changed. See [EK10205](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10205) and the [dispatch coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L9885).
**EK10216 — truncated PC Multiboot2 EFI64 tag supplies a bogus system-table pointer (2026-10-30):** x86-64 parsing reads the 64-bit pointer even when the tag declares only its 8-byte header. Conditional on malformed external boot metadata; no in-tree producer was found. No runtime boot test was performed. See [EK10216](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10216) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L9886).

**EK10217 — i386-PC dispatcher skips pending task exceptions (2026-10-30):** Exec sets TF_EXCEPT and forces scheduling, but i386-PC cpu_Dispatch has its Exception() call commented out. Tasks with an exception callback resume without delivery, leaving the flag set for later scheduler decisions. Applies to the explicit pc-i386 kernel target; the current boot aggregate edge is commented out. No build or runtime test was performed. See [EK10217](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10217) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md).
**EK10218 — concurrent BOOPSI class registration can publish duplicate IDs (2026-10-30):** MakeClass checks for an existing ID under a shared lock, but publication occurs later through AddClass, which unconditionally inserts under the exclusive lock and documents duplicate IDs as undefined. Two overlapping registrations for the same public class ID can both succeed; later FindClass selects by list order. Conditional on client ID collision and overlapping registration; no in-tree duplicate-ID pair was found. See [EK10218](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10218) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md).
**EK10219 — m68k `AllocNamedObjectA()` leaks its native allocation if shadow creation fails:** the thunk allocates the native object, then returns NULL from failed guest-shadow allocation/registration without freeing the native object. Conditional on shadow heap/table exhaustion on the optional 64-bit-host m68k emulator. See [EK10219](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10219) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only; no allocation failure was induced.
**EK10224 — detached-stream conversion failure loses I/O and can leak its copied lock (2026-10-30):** `detach.o` passes unchecked `OpenFromLock(DupLockFromFH(...))` results to `CreateNewProc()`. NIL is accepted, so the child can start without inherited I/O and null input suppresses argument injection; if lock duplication succeeded but filehandle conversion failed, the unconsumed lock is not freed. Conditional on filesystem/allocation failure. See [EK10224](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10224) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only; no handle failure was induced.
**EK10223 — TLSF bucket search shifts a signed negative mask (2026-10-30):** `FIND_SUITABLE_BLOCK()` shifts `~0` before combining it with unsigned bitmaps, which is undefined for the negative signed `int` operand. This affects ordinary allocation searches on TLSF-backed configurations; the compiled effect is compiler-dependent. See [EK10223](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10223) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only; no build or allocation was run.
**EK10222 — 32-bit TLSF rounding can map large requests to zero or invalid buckets (2026-10-30):** near-4-GiB aligned sizes wrap during `MAPPING_SEARCH()`: one maps the request to zero and can return a zero-size block after managed-pool autogrowth; a nearby value produces a negative first-level index and negative shift count. Applies to 32-bit TLSF configurations such as i386-PC and ARM-native; no in-tree near-limit request was found. See [EK10222](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10222) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only; no allocation or runtime operation was performed.
**EK10221 — 64-bit TLSF pooled allocations can index past the bucket tables (2026-10-30):** a request near 126 GiB maps to first-level bucket 31, but the tables contain indices 0–30. `AllocPooled()` forwards its `IPTR` size into a TLSF-managed pool before any bounds check. Applies to TLSF-backed 64-bit configurations such as default x86-64 PC and RISC-V64 OpenSBI startup; no literal near-boundary call appeared in a 503-call source census; dynamic sizes remain untraced. See [EK10221](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10221) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only; no allocation or runtime test was performed.
**EK10220 — m68k `RawDoFmt()` returns output length instead of the remaining DataStream pointer:** guest callers receive a character count where the API promises the unconsumed stream cursor. Applies to the optional m68k emulator when the result is used. See [EK10220](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10220) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L10351). **OD10293 — VMware failed probe leaks its initialized devm DRM device (2026-10-30):** after `devm_drm_dev_alloc()` succeeds, a `vmw_driver_load()` or `drm_dev_register()` failure returns without dropping the DRM device's initial reference. The VMware AROS `devm_add_action_or_reset()` stub reports success but does not register the cleanup, and the direct AROS probe wrapper does not run driver-core devres release. This extends the VMware probe failure-path review; it is distinct from OD4211's partial `drm_dev_init()` cleanup. No allocation failure or probe was run. **OD10294 — GK20A IOMMU instance memory cannot be CPU-mapped when it spans multiple pages (2026-10-30):** GK20A allocates IOMMU-backed instance-memory pages separately, but AROS `vmap()` requires adjacent addresses. The failed map feeds unchecked GPU-object accessors; retries can corrupt the LRU, destruction can leave a dangling LRU node, and reclamation subtracts bytes never added to the mapping counter. Conditional on the GK20A/Tegra IOMMU path and a CPU-accessed allocation larger than one page. No hardware or build was exercised. See [OD10294](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10294) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#L27350).
**OD10296 — GK20A partial instance-memory construction dereferences a NULL owner during error cleanup (2026-10-30):** after the node has initialized its destructor, backing-allocation failure returns a partial object; the common wrapper unreferences it before `node->imem` is set, and both destructors dereference that field before checking construction state. Conditional on allocation or mapping failure on either GK20A instmem backend. No failure was induced. See [OD10296](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10296) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#L27358).

Both the SDHCI peripheral IRQ and its created bus worker are routed/affined to CPU 0, confirming that an interrupt can preempt the task while it holds the shared spinlock and deadlock in the IRQ callback. The affected configuration remains AArch64 Raspberry Pi SMP; no hardware or IRQ was exercised. See [OD9573](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9573) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). No path/LOC credit; the full review remains open. Source-only.
**GD10275 — Buffered IconList setup leaks its RastPort on layer setup failure:** if buffering is selected and bitmap/RastPort allocation succeeds but layer-info or layer creation fails, fallback overwrites the new RastPort pointer without freeing it. See [GD10275](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10275) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md). No allocation failure or GUI operation was induced; source-only.
**GD10274 — Vulkan-Hpp latency timing wrappers can return unwritten records:** RAII and enhanced vector helpers return storage sized from the first maximum-count query without trimming it to the fill call's actual `timingCount`. Conditional on fewer records being written on the second call; no non-generated in-tree consumer was found. See [GD10274](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10274) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md). No Vulkan query or build was run; source-only.
**GD10273 — Generic bitmap row alignment wraps at the UWORD width limit:** with default 16-pixel alignment, widths 65,521–65,535 round to 65,536 in a `UWORD` and wrap to zero. Generic chunky bitmap creation requests a zero-byte buffer; generic planar creation requests zero-byte planes, so both fail for positive height and planar depth. A framebuffer switched to a custom mode of that width also receives a zero row stride, but the resulting generic display-copy behavior is unverified at these dimensions. The mode-change trigger depends on a driver exposing such a mode; no allocation or mode switch was run. See [GD10273](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10273) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md). Full-body source credit recorded; source-only.
**GD10272 — AddDataTypes can lose a refresh after scan setup fails:** `DateScan()` stores a changed `DEVS:DataTypes` timestamp before `ScanDirectory()` allocates traversal state. If that allocation fails, the command still reports success and a later refresh sees the stored timestamp and skips retrying. Conditional on low-memory failure during `REFRESH`; applies when the optional command is built and run. See [GD10272](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10272) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md). No path or LOC credit changed.

The reply is an independent allocation with no destructor tracking; a failed device init leaves it leaked, and a later init retry can leak another. The R570 table uses the R535 implementation. **EK9439 — m68k `GetColorMap()` guest shadows lose palette-table pointers:** restored after checking the native allocator, shadow layout and pointer-conversion path. The native ColorMap has ColorTable and LowColorBits arrays, but both fields become NULL in the guest shadow; direct guest structure access is affected, while native accessor vectors still resolve the native object. No maintained emulated caller was found. See [EK9439](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9439) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No palette operation or build was run; source-only.


**EK9440 — m68k Region mutations are not reflected in the guest shadow:** restored after checking the layout and generated/native mutator paths. The layout omits `bounds`, and wrappers do not synchronize `RegionRectangle` after mutation; direct guest structure inspection can therefore be stale, while calls that resolve the native shadow remain functional. No maintained emulated guest caller was found. See [EK9440](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9440) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No Region operation or build was run; source-only.


**EK9891 — m68k generated lifecycles retain guest shadow mappings:** restored and reconciled against the current wrappers/native owners. Confirmed cases cover MsgPort, DevProc, GadTools Menu and messages, Utility NamedObject, and borrowed DrawInfo. Repeated successful calls retain guest heap blocks and bounded table entries; only native-free cases are described as leaving mappings to freed storage. DeleteIORequest and Graphics free pairs remain separately tracked. See [EK9891](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9891) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No guest operation or build was run; source-only.


**EK9441/EK9442 — console completion counter wrap and ignored scan errors:** restored after rechecking the match counter, chooser branch, `ExNext()` contract, DOS error propagation and selected FAT handler. EK9441 is conditional on a 32,768+ match set and compiler narrowing; EK9442 can mis-insert one result as unique only when a scan error follows it and another matching entry remains. Both are selected in ARM/AArch64 Raspberry Pi packages. See [EK9441](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9441), [EK9442](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9442), and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No scan or build was run; source-only.


**EK9443 — Unix-hosted and MinGW reject Wanderer’s warm-only shutdown action:** restored after rechecking both `ShutdownA()` switches and the selected Ctrl-Reboot caller. The call returns before dispatching warm reset, so Wanderer reports unsupported; Unix and MinGW have separate `ColdReboot()` restart paths, whose actual host behavior remains untested (MinGW RAM marker caveat: EK9517). See [EK9443](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9443) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No reboot was run; source-only.


**EK9444 — Unix startup continues after `core_Start()` fails:** restored after tracing the early failure returns, signal setup, startup caller and HostLib cleanup contract. `kernel_startup()` ignores FALSE and proceeds into cold-start residents without the signal/trap/IRQ/syscall setup; unresolved-symbol failure also leaks the allocated interface array. Later failure is conditional and untested. See [EK9444](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9444) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No boot or build was run; source-only.


**EK812 — `ChildStatus()` has an unlocked live-child scan on ExecSMP:** restored after rechecking both list mutations and the POSIX `waitpid(pid, ...)` caller. A scan can miss a notifying child between list transfer and return `ECHILD`, or race an unnotified sibling's removal/free while traversing. Both require cross-CPU overlap. See [EK812](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek812) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No task or wait was run; source-only.

**EK10341 — POSIXC `waitpid()` counts exited children without the message-port lock:** its unconditional `ListLength()` walk can overlap the ExecSMP child-exit publisher's locked append. Scoped to ExecSMP builds selecting POSIXC `waitpid()`; the unlocked exited-list walk is separate from EK812's live-child reader. See [EK10341](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10341) and the [caller/lock trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-waitpid-exited-child-count-list-lock-pass-ek10341). Source-only; no wait or interleaving was run.

**EK10342 — POSIXC `wait()` and `waitpid(-1)` omit `ECHILD` when no children exist:** `waitpid(-1, ..., WNOHANG)` returns 0; the blocking forms enter `ChildWait(0)` and wait indefinitely. The no-child result differs from the POSIX `ECHILD` contract. See [EK10342](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10342) and the [no-child path trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-waitpid-any-child-no-child-echild-pass-ek10342). Source-only; no wait call was run.

**EK10343 — POSIXC `WEXITSTATUS` mishandles compound arguments:** the public macro masks an unparenthesized argument, so conditional or bitwise expressions may leave selected high bits unmasked. No in-tree precedence-sensitive caller was found; scope is external or future clients. See [EK10343](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10343) and the [macro/caller census](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#posixc-wexitstatus-precedence-and-caller-census-ek10343). Source-only; no caller or build was run.



**EK427/EK9907 — VMM Rexx `MEMTYPE` dispatch and syntax:** restored after rechecking the command switch, numeric parser, cache resize path and guide. Numeric low-bit values fall through into `WRITEBUFFER` and can replace a nonzero write cache with a zero-size cache; documented FAST/CHIP/ANY tokens instead fail parsing and return an argument error. Both findings are scoped to an operating optional VMM loop; the checked-in startup limitation EK9906 remains relevant. See [EK427](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek427), [EK9907](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9907), and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No command or cache resize was run; source-only.


**EK428 — optional VMM library startup dereferences null `CxParams`:** restored after tracing the library's `StartupParams = 0` message through manager initialization. `Init_VM_Manager()` then evaluates `PrefsPath` through the null pointer before the manager replies, so the `OpenLibrary()` handshake can fail to complete. This is an optional library path, not a default-image finding; it precedes the separate EK9906 MUI-start failure. See [EK428](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek428) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No library open was run; source-only.


**EK429 — VMM `ShowGUI()` formats a 198–199-character path into a 200-byte command buffer:** restored after tracing the MUI path builder through `AddPart()` and the manager formatter. Quote wrapping requires 201–202 bytes including NUL, so the write exceeds the buffer by one or two bytes when the preferences process is not running and console open succeeds. Optional VMM targets only; EK9906 remains a startup caveat. See [EK429](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek429) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No GUI process was run; source-only.

**EK05 — `ChildWait()` can clear the child signal after a child has already queued its completion (ExecSMP):** after the locked completion-list scan, a child can be queued and signal the parent before `SetSignal(0, SIGF_CHILD)` clears that signal; `ChildWait()` may then sleep with the completion still pending. The detailed report identifies the race as EK05; earlier coverage notes call it EK811. This is the same finding, not an additional candidate. See [EK05](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek05) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No task or SMP interleaving was run; source-only.

**OD10308 — PoPo GUI cleanup waits on an unsubmitted timer request after MUI startup failure:** if MUI class or application construction fails after timer.device opens but before the first SendIO, cleanup calls WaitIO on the never-enqueued request; its zeroed list links are dereferenced by Remove. Conditional on the optional Poseidon GUI startup failure path. See [OD10308](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10308) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). No allocation failure, GUI, timer request, or build was run; source-only.

**EK8875 — Concurrent ExecSMP `Cause()` calls can insert the same soft-interrupt node twice:** the queued-state check is outside the per-priority spinlock; a second CPU can pass it, then append the already-queued node after acquiring the lock. The duplicate insertion self-links the node and can make `SoftIntDispatch()` invoke it repeatedly without draining the list. Conditional in-tree caller examples include RTL8139 interrupt paths and PCIUSB concurrent transfer submissions sharing one completion node; both require explicit optional-target selection, and no default-image reproducer is claimed. See [EK8875](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8875) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No interrupt or SMP interleaving was run; source-only.


**EK8877 — PC startup ignores required exception-handler allocation failures:** the i386/x86-64 syscall and common PC APIC error/IPI registrations discard KrnAddExceptionHandler() results. If node allocation fails during startup, the gate remains installed without its handler; later delivery reaches cpu_Trap()'s unhandled-exception halt path. The spurious vector is excluded. See [EK8877](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8877) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No allocation failure, boot or trap was induced; source-only.


**EK8883 — Raspberry Pi boot LED diagnostics read a third GPIO cell from an eight-byte property:** both ARM32 and AArch64 loops accept two cells, then print data[2]. Their GPIO behavior separately checks for a third cell, so the confirmed impact is limited to an out-of-property diagnostic read and misleading log output. Requires firmware to supply an enabled LED gpios property with one argument; no checked-in DTB establishes that input. See [EK8883](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8883) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No boot or DT input was exercised; source-only.


**EK8891 — PC ExecSMP scheduler-state macro references the wrong local:** FLAG_SCHEDDISPATCH_ISSET declares __tls but reads undeclared __schd and never uses the TLS value. An expansion without a caller-local __schd is ill-formed; with one, it reads the wrong object. No checked-in expansion was found, so this remains a conditional interface defect without a current in-tree build failure. See [EK8891](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8891) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No macro expansion or build was run; source-only.


**EK515 — Failed Android bootstrap retries retain module state and host allocations:** pre-start GetKernelSize or LoadKernel failures skip module-list and host-memory cleanup; a later size-change retry can append duplicate modules and overwrite prior allocation pointers. Scoped to a failure followed by a pre-start retry. See [EK515](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek515) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No Android run or failure injection was performed; source-only.


**EK529 — Parthenope's ext2 factory dereferences a failed boot-object allocation:** after a successful ext2 probe mount it allocates the boot-device object, then initializes fields without checking NULL. The caller's DOS/SFS fallback has already been exhausted and its NULL check occurs only after return. Conditional on explicitly building the optional Parthenope Sam440 target and allocation failure; the parent boot manifest comments out that target. See [EK529](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek529) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No allocation failure or boot was induced; source-only.


**EK530 — Parthenope accepts most SFS checksum mismatches:** its helper zeros the stored field and returns the checksum that should be stored, but directory and extent-tree readers only reject a zero return instead of comparing it with the original field or checking the full block sum. Corrupt metadata with a nonzero recomputed checksum passes; a valid block whose expected checksum is zero is rejected. Applies to explicitly built optional Parthenope Sam440 on SFS media; its parent boot edge is commented out. See [EK530](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek530) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No media or boot was used; source-only.


**EK532 — Parthenope file readers can overrun fixed-size boot buffers:** the callback has no capacity argument, while the local DOS, SFS, ext2 and CD readers copy/read the complete file length. Callers supply fixed buffers from 64 KiB to 18 MiB for menus, kernels, initrds and modules. A larger file overruns its destination before parsing; TFTP is excluded because its transfer bound is external. Applies to the explicitly built optional Parthenope Sam440 target. See [EK532](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek532) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No large file or boot was used; source-only.


**EK536 — Parthenope's CD file loader masks missing and failed reads:** missing files return zero, while a failed read after finding a nonempty file still returns its positive advertised size. Kernel/module callers reject only negative results and continue with unwritten or incomplete buffers; menu lookup treats zero as a miss but parses a positive failed read. The Linux initrd case remains EK9235. Applies to explicitly built optional Parthenope Sam440. See [EK536](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek536) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No media or boot was used; source-only.
**EK9227 — Parthenope treats a positive short multi-block CD read as a complete file:** the U-Boot callback returns a block count, but the reader accepts any nonzero count and the file loader returns the advertised full size. Menu and image consumers then parse the incomplete destination. The actual selected firmware driver's short-count behavior is not confirmed. Applies only to explicitly built optional Parthenope Sam440. See [EK9227](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9227) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L12071). No media or boot was used; source-only.


**EK728 — OpenSBI debug-console writes discard partial-completion counts:** the DBCN helper returns only the error field, and string/character output callers never retry an unwritten suffix or failed write. Applies when OpenSBI selects DBCN and reports a short or failed write. See [EK728](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek728) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK715 — i386 alert disassembly can overrun its stack padding array:** alert formatting subtracts an unsigned instruction-hex length from a 16-character width; a decoded instruction longer than eight bytes wraps the bound and writes beyond the 17-byte local array. Applies to i386 debug builds with disassembly enabled. See [EK715](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek715) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK672 — MinGW host timer expirations coalesce while AROS interrupts are disabled:** each expiration sets a Boolean pending byte, so multiple timer-0/1 periods dispatch once after interrupts resume. EClock and VBlank counters can lag after a long masked interval. Applies to Windows-hosted MinGW32. See [EK672](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek672) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only; separate from EK674 timer-period truncation.

**EK8921 — `C:Mount` leaks a constructed node when its filesystem type has no FileSystem.resource entry:** with no explicit handler, `PatchDosNode()` leaves the segment list empty; Mount skips insertion and returns without disposing the node or its owned allocations. Applies to a filesystem mount whose DOS type is not registered. See [EK8921](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8921) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK8925 — FileSystem.resource registration races across ExecSMP CPUs:** partition `AddFS()` and selected PFS3 `AddToFSResource()` use processor-local `Forbid()` around shared duplicate checks and list insertion. Concurrent same-type registrations can duplicate entries or interleave list updates. Applies to concurrent PFS3 initialization or other overlapping registration producers on ExecSMP. See [EK8925](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8925) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK8957 — concurrent `C:Mount` shutdowns can leave a synchronous packet unanswered:** two callers can snapshot the same AUX console-handler port; the first successful `ACTION_DIE` is replied to and exits the handler loop, leaving a second queued request without a reply. Applies to overlapping REMOVE requests for a running handler with no open handles. See [EK8957](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8957) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK684 — `C:Mount` double-frees its handler string and leaks a rejected device node:** after `AddDosEntry()` rejects a same-name entry, Mount frees `HandlerString` without clearing the global pointer, then caller cleanup frees it again; the unregistered node and owned strings/startup/environment allocations are also abandoned. Applies to a rejected load-handler node followed by normal `FreeStuff()` cleanup. See [EK684](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek684) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK683 — `C:Mount` can loop forever after a mount source file shrinks:** `readfile()` snapshots the file size, then subtracts each DOS `Read()` result; zero-byte EOF leaves the remaining count unchanged and bypasses cleanup. Applies to a mountlist or mountfile truncated before the measured byte count is read. See [EK683](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek683) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK679 — `C:Mount` can scan an uninitialized error buffer after formatter allocation failure:** `VSNPrintf()` leaves the destination untouched when its scratch allocation fails, then `ShowFault()` calls `strlen()` on the stack buffer. Five Mount error paths call the reporter. Applies when that formatter allocation fails during error reporting. See [EK679](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek679) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK609 — a failed concurrent `pthread_create()` can damage a reused thread slot:** failure cleanup runs after releasing `thread_sem`, so another creator can reuse the empty slot; the first caller can clear the new parent pointer or report the second task as its own successful creation. Applies when task creation fails during overlapping create calls. See [EK609](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek609) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK608 — `pthread_join()` does not deliver deferred cancellation while waiting:** it checks cancellation before its `SIGF_PARENT`-only wait, which `pthread_cancel()` cannot wake with its Ctrl-C signal; after target completion join returns without checking again. Applies when a thread is canceled while blocked in `pthread_join()`. See [EK608](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek608) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK607 — `sem_unlink()` frees a named pthread semaphore still used by open handles or waiters:** `sem_close()` does not track references, and unlink destroys/frees the shared object immediately; destruction also ignores a busy condition-variable result. Applies when a named semaphore is unlinked while another caller retains its handle, particularly with a waiter. See [EK607](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek607) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK604 — concurrent lazy use of a static pthread condition can access its waiter list before initialization:** initialization marks the semaphore valid before `NEWLIST()` initializes the waiter list; another first-use wait or signal can skip initialization and use null sentinels. Applies to concurrent first use of one `PTHREAD_COND_INITIALIZER`. See [EK604](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek604) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK603 — pthread condition waits clear a pending Ctrl-E signal if private signal allocation fails:** the wait path falls back to the task's Ctrl-E bit and clears it before waiting, consuming any already-pending event on that bit. Applies when all allocatable task signals are unavailable and Ctrl-E is pending at entry. See [EK603](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek603) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK600 — failed per-task POSIXC `OpenLib` skips close-hook rollback:** generated `OpenLib` frees its duplicate base after a later `OPENLIB` hook fails, without calling completed `CLOSELIB` hooks. A partial vfork/exec descriptor copy can therefore leak copied descriptors and FCB references. Applies to task-local POSIXC base initialization when a later hook fails; relative-library-open failures are tracked separately as EK8934. See [EK600](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek600) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK592 — POSIXC `flock()` can return success without recording its lock for expunge cleanup:** `AddToList()` returns failure when its node allocation fails, but `flock()` ignores that result after acquiring the semaphore. A later explicit `LOCK_UN` still works; without it, expunge cleanup has no record of the semaphore. Applies when lock-record allocation fails after a successful shared or exclusive lock. See [EK592](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek592) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK591 — closing the final POSIXC descriptor leaves its `flock()` semaphore held:** `close()` closes the DOS handle and frees the FCB but does not release or unlink the semaphore-only lock record. While the locking task remains alive, conflicting callers for the same path can continue to block. Applies to a locked file whose final descriptor is closed without `LOCK_UN`; task-exit semaphore behavior is not asserted. See [EK591](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek591) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK590 — POSIXC `flock()` initialization dereferences a failed list allocation:** `__init_flocks()` calls `NEWLIST()` immediately after `AllocMem()` without checking for NULL, so low memory can fault during library initialization. Applies when the selected POSIXC link library initializes and its list allocation fails. See [EK590](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek590) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK589 — concurrent POSIXC `flock()` calls mutate the shared lock-record list without synchronization:** `AddToList()` and `RemoveFromList()` change one process-shared list without a cross-CPU lock. Concurrent calls can corrupt it or lose semaphore records needed by cleanup. Applies to POSIXC on ExecSMP under concurrent lock/unlock calls. Separate from EK592 allocation-failure bookkeeping. See [EK589](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek589) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK588 — concurrent first `flock()` calls can create duplicate named semaphores on ExecSMP:** `Forbid()` is CPU-local, and the semaphore lookup and insertion use separate list-lock intervals. Two CPUs can both miss the same path, create different semaphores, and both obtain exclusive locks. Applies to POSIXC on ExecSMP under concurrent first use for one file. See [EK588](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek588) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK570 — `pthread_exit()` uses an unset jump buffer on the initial thread:** the initializer registers the main task but only worker startup calls `setjmp()`; initial-thread exit therefore longjmps without a matching jump point. Applies to clients linking the selected AROS pthread library that call `pthread_exit()` from the initial thread. See [EK570](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek570) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK569 — detaching a pthread can leave a stale task pointer and hang process exit:** both detach-after-completion and a detach racing the worker completion branch can leave the slot marked detached with a non-NULL task pointer; the exit hook then waits forever. Applies to clients linking the selected pthread library. See [EK569](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek569) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK567 — `pthread_mutex_timedlock()` acquires an available mutex twice:** a successful `trylock()` falls through to timed `Procure()`, which increments the owner nest count again; one unlock leaves the mutex held. Applies to callers using the selected AROS pthread link library with an available normal or recursive mutex and a valid deadline. See [EK567](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek567) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only; no mutex call or contention was run.
**EK565 — `pthread_setschedprio()` rejects every priority:** its range predicate compares against max and min in the wrong direction, so it returns `EINVAL` before looking up the thread or changing its priority. Applies to clients linking the selected AROS pthread link library; no checked-in caller was found. See [EK565](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek565) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK560 — PowerPC privilege helpers can demote an already-supervisor caller:** CHRP/Efika and Sam440 `Supervisor()` wrappers unconditionally call `UserState()`, and Efika MMU vectors call `goUser()` which also sets `MSR_PR` instead of restoring the saved mode. Subsequent privileged work can fault. These remain conditional public-API cases; no ordinary in-tree supervisor-mode caller was found. See [EK560](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek560) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK554 — m68kemu AUTOINIT size overflow can overrun a guest allocation:** adding jump-table bytes to a near-maximum 32-bit `dataSize` can wrap to a small allocation, while writes check only the overall guest arena. Malformed disk-library input can corrupt guest-arena state beyond that block; no host-memory impact is claimed. Applies to explicit hosted m68kemu builds using disk-library fallback. See [EK554](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek554) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK553 — rejected disk libraries retain loaded hunks until the m68kemu context ends:** after successful hunk parsing, later Resident/AUTOINIT rejection returns failure without releasing hunk blocks. Repeated guest attempts can consume the finite emulation heap; context teardown eventually reclaims it. Applies to explicit hosted m68kemu builds using disk-library fallback. See [EK553](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek553) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK552 — m68kemu returns disk-loaded AUTOINIT libraries without applying their initialization:** it reads but does not apply `dataInit` or call `initFunc` before exposing the library base. Libraries that rely on either step can operate with missing required state. Applies to explicit hosted m68kemu builds using disk-library fallback. See [EK552](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek552) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK551 — repeated m68kemu opens reload disk libraries and CloseLibrary retains them:** disk-loaded bases are not cached in the context name map, so each open allocates another hunk copy; CloseLibrary is a no-op. Repeated guest open/close cycles can exhaust the emulation arena. Applies to explicit hosted m68kemu builds using disk-library fallback. See [EK551](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek551) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK550 — m68kemu disk-library fallback ignores `OpenLibrary()`’s minimum version:** the thunk discards D0 and returns a loaded library without comparing the caller’s requested version with its resident version. Guest code can use an incompatible older library. Applies to explicit m68kemu builds on supported hosted targets when disk fallback is used. See [EK550](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek550) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK546 — Parthenope SFS probing dereferences three unchecked allocation results:** failure to allocate the device, initial block buffer, or copied root object reaches a NULL write/read. The DOS-to-SFS-to-ext2 factory sequence cannot reach ext2 fallback in these cases. Applies only to explicitly built optional Parthenope Sam440; the parent boot manifest comments it out. See [EK546](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek546) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK545 — Parthenope SFS loading reports an early-ended extent chain as a successful short read:** when the chain ends before the object’s declared size, `sfs_loadfile()` returns the positive bytes copied; menu parsing and OS4 module loading accept that count. Applies only to explicitly built optional Parthenope Sam440; the parent boot manifest comments it out. See [EK545](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek545) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK544 — Parthenope SFS loading dereferences a missing extent-tree node:** `get_bnode()` returns NULL for a missing key, invalid checksum or failed block read; `sfs_loadfile()` immediately accesses the returned node. Corrupt extent metadata or a tree-block I/O error can fault menu, kernel or module loading. Applies only to explicitly built optional Parthenope Sam440; the parent boot manifest comments it out. See [EK544](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek544) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK543 — Parthenope SFS lookup and destroy paths leak retained block buffers and the copied root:** directory/object searches and extent-tree lookups return pointers into allocated buffers without an ownership release, and `sfs_destroy()` omits the separately allocated root object. Repeated menu/file lookups accumulate leaks. Applies only to explicitly built optional Parthenope Sam440; the parent boot manifest comments it out. See [EK543](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek543) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK541 — AArch64 CPU startup can leave sparse online IDs while Exec and processor.resource assume dense IDs:** after CPU 1 fails but CPU 2 registers, the CPU count is 2 for online IDs `{0,2}`. Topology and idle tasks use IDs 0 and 1; affinity accepts offline CPU 1 and omits online CPU 2, and its load query returns zero. The previous claim that AArch64 processor.resource starts a pinned probe and hangs was incorrect: that probe is only selected on 32-bit Raspberry Pi. Applies to AArch64 BCM27xx ExecSMP under the stated partial-start condition. See [EK541](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek541) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**EK537 — Parthenope's CD path splitter exceeds its component array:** the local array has nine pointer slots, but splitting a ten-component path writes a tenth pointer without a depth check; lookup then consumes that out-of-range entry. Triggered by a deep path from the CD-backed boot menu. Applies only to explicitly built optional Parthenope Sam440. See [EK537](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek537) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). No path or boot was run; source-only.
**EK9228 — Parthenope reads ISO directory identifiers and SUSP data without record bounds checks:** malformed record lengths can make lookup consume bytes outside the record or directory extent and accept a wrong file extent. Limited to explicitly built optional Parthenope Sam440; malformed-media consequences depend on the bytes. See [EK9228](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9228) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L12074). No image or boot was used; source-only.
**EK9229 — m68kemu accepts a Hunk file that ends before all hunks are complete:** EOF exits the record loop but still returns the first hunk address, and `RunFile()` executes any nonzero result. A truncated file can therefore start with missing or partial hunk contents. Applies to optional hosted m68kemu `RunFile()` use. See [EK9229](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9229) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L12077). No Hunk file or guest was loaded; source-only.
**EK9231 — m68kemu argument-size arithmetic can under-allocate before copying:** a near-maximum 32-bit argument length wraps the guest allocator's rounding to a tiny block, then `CopyMem()` still uses the original length and can write past the 32 MiB emulator arena. No checked-in caller provides such a valid buffer/length; this is a low-reachability public API boundary candidate. Applies to explicitly built optional `m68kemu.library`. See [EK9231](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9231) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L12083). No large buffer or copy was used; source-only.
**EK9233 — Parthenope's ELF loader reads section metadata and payloads beyond the loaded file:** it has no file-length input and trusts section-table offsets/counts and section offset/size fields; the boot caller discards the loaded length. Malformed ELF input can make it read past the file image before module/kernel handoff. Applies to explicitly built optional Parthenope Sam440; default aggregate inclusion is not claimed. See [EK9233](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9233) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L12089). No ELF or boot was used; source-only.
**EK9234 — Parthenope ELF placement can produce a zero or wrapped Sam440 low-memory MemHeader:** if read-only kernel/module placement reaches or passes 16 MiB, startup's `0x01000000 - memLowest` size is zero or wraps, but the MemHeader and first MemChunk are still written and later Fast RAM is added at 16 MiB. Threshold/default-image reachability is unverified. Explicit optional `parthenope-sam440` only. EK9265 is consolidated here as duplicate. See [EK9234](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9234) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5284). No image or boot was used; source-only.
**EK9235 — Parthenope ignores Linux initrd load failure:** with a configured initrd, `testboot_linux()` passes its allocated buffer to U-Boot `bootm` even when `load_file()` reports failure or incomplete data. Applies to explicit optional `parthenope-sam440` Linux boot entries with initrds; backend trigger is conditional. See [EK9235](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9235) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5084). No load failure or boot was exercised; source-only.
**EK9236 — PC bootstrap does not bound GNU ar long-name offsets:** `/offset` references are added to the `//` table and scanned for a delimiter without a table or module extent. A malformed boot archive can make the bootstrap read beyond the name table. Applies to selected i386/x86-64 PC bootstrap archive modules. See [EK9236](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9236) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5087). No archive or boot was parsed; source-only.
**EK9237 — 32-bit Raspberry Pi boot can map the kernel at the wrong physical offset:** image placement preserves a 4 KiB endpoint offset, but section mapping drops the lower 20 physical-address bits. Conditional on firmware memory ending between 1 MiB boundaries. Applies to `arm-raspi`. See [EK9237](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9237) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5132). No firmware or boot was used; source-only.
**EK9238 — RISC-V OpenSBI consumes some ordinary `ebreak` traps:** any saved `a7 <= 0x100` is classified as a scheduler syscall, but the shared dispatcher handles only IDs 0–3. An unsupported admitted value such as `SC_CLI` is stepped over with no breakpoint handling. Applies to RISC-V OpenSBI; no ordinary in-tree `ebreak` producer was found. See [EK9238](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9238) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5135). No trap was run; source-only.
**EK9244 — POSIXC `ftruncate()` can move a RAMFS descriptor to EOF while returning success:** shrinking below the saved offset clamps the RAMFS opening; the wrappers ignore the failed attempt to restore the old position. Applies to both `ftruncate()` and `ftruncate64()` on RAMFS. See [EK9244](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9244) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5164). No file operation was run; source-only.
**EK9245 — AArch64 Raspberry Pi can advertise unmapped RAM above 4 GiB:** a `/memory/reg` tuple crossing 4 GiB takes the low mapping path, skips upper blocks, but publishes the full range to TLSF. Conditional on firmware using one crossing tuple; checked-in device-tree shape is unknown. See [EK9245](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9245) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5169). No FDT or boot was used; source-only.
**EK9250 — Shell drops an alias argument byte inside backticks:** embedded input reaches alias expansion without a newline, but the splice unconditionally subtracts one byte as if it were present. An alias using `[]` can lose the final argument character. Applies to selected Shell targets. See [EK9250](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9250) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5213). No command was run; source-only.
**EK9251 — Shell init reports success when resident segment setup fails:** `CreateSegList()` and both `AddSegment()` results are not propagated; the library initializer returns TRUE even if command registration is absent. Applies to targets selecting the Shell library; allocation/duplicate-name trigger is conditional. See [EK9251](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9251) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5993). No failure was induced; source-only.
**EK9252 — Realtime LOCATE can remain blocked after an unready player is deleted:** the barrier waits for `PLAYER_Ready`, but `DeletePlayer()` neither removes the participant from the wait protocol nor signals the barrier task. Applies to external callers of the optional Realtime API; no maintained LOCATE caller was found. See [EK9252](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9252) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5222). No wait was run; source-only.
**EK9253 — Parthenope CD lookup leaks temporary names on read errors:** failed directory-record reads leak the copied path; failed entry-name reads leak both path and name. Repeated failures can consume memory, though exhaustion on the selected boot path is unproven. Explicit optional `parthenope-sam440` only. See [EK9253](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9253) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5227). No media error or boot was exercised; source-only.
**EK9254 — Parthenope leaks AOS module staging allocations after a failed module load:** the negative-result return bypasses cleanup for the 16 MiB buffer, list, and any accumulated module records/payloads. Explicit optional `parthenope-sam440` AOS path only; exhaustion is not established. See [EK9254](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9254) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5230). No load failure or boot was induced; source-only.
**EK9257 — Parthenope reads SUSP CE fields without checking the entry or remaining-buffer length:** the fixed 28-byte structure is consumed even for a shorter or truncated CE record. Malformed Rock Ridge media can cause reads beyond the SUA buffer or use adjacent bytes as continuation coordinates. Explicit optional `parthenope-sam440` only. See [EK9257](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9257) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5235). No media was parsed; source-only.
**EK9260 — Parthenope writable ELF placement can descend into the bootloader image:** writable sections move down from `0x00800000` without a lower-bound check, while the bootloader is linked from `0x00200000`. Overlap depends on aggregate section sizes and is unverified for checked-in images. Explicit optional `parthenope-sam440` only. See [EK9260](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9260) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5249). No image or boot was used; source-only.
**EK9261 — `TimeDelay()` stores its signal-disable sentinel as 255:** `mp_SigBit` is unsigned, so assigning -1 makes `DeleteMsgPort()` call `FreeSignal(255)`, which shifts by an out-of-range count. Exact signal-mask effect depends on target code generation. Applies to targets selecting `compiler/alib/timedelay.c`. See [EK9261](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9261) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5255). No timer or signal path was run; source-only.
**EK9259 — Parthenope maps a zero-alignment ELF section at address zero:** the placement mask formulas collapse to zero when `sh_addralign` is zero, then copy or clear the section there. Applies to explicit optional `parthenope-sam440` AROS ELF loads. See [EK9259](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9259) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5246). No ELF image or boot was used; source-only.
**EK9262 — `TimeDelay()` inverts its documented return status:** successful `DoIO()` returns 1, while message-port or timer-device setup failures return 0; the `DoIO()` result is ignored. The two checked Intuition callers ignore the value. Applies to targets selecting `compiler/alib/timedelay.c`. See [EK9262](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9262) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5255). No timer request was run; source-only.
**EK9263 — PC IRQ traversal is not synchronized with handler add/remove on ExecSMP:** the dispatcher walks without `kb_IntrSpinLock`, while generic removal locks only around unlink/free and the PC add path has no shared lock. Concurrent teardown can invalidate a node in use. Applies to ExecSMP PC targets; overlap is conditional. See [EK9263](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9263) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L7503). No interrupt or concurrent removal was run; source-only.
**EK9264 — PC APIC calibration enables its heartbeat timer if handler allocation fails:** registration can return NULL, but calibration still configures an unmasked periodic vector; the next heartbeat is unhandled and follows the system-halt path. Allocation failure is required. See [EK9264](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9264) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5278). No APIC event or allocation failure was induced; source-only.
**EK9256 — Parthenope `list_new()` initializes a failed allocation:** its head/tail writes immediately dereference the result; AROS debug metadata and AOS module loading call the helper. Explicit optional `parthenope-sam440` only; trigger requires allocation failure. See [EK9256](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9256) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5233). No allocation failure or boot was induced; source-only.
**EK9255 — Parthenope `strdup()` dereferences a failed allocation:** the helper unconditionally copies into the allocation result, and menu parsing uses it for configured paths, labels and options. Applies to explicit optional `parthenope-sam440`; trigger requires allocation failure. See [EK9255](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9255) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5233). No allocation failure or boot was induced; source-only.
**EK9267 — m68kemu passes a guest argument stream to native `VNewRawDoFmt()` as a host `va_list`:** m68k 32-bit big-endian slots do not implement the supported 64-bit host varargs ABI, so formatted guest calls can consume the wrong values. Applies to optional x86_64, AArch64 and RISC-V m68kemu targets and external guest clients. See [EK9267](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9267) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5232). No guest program was run; source-only.
**EK9268 — m68kemu passes a guest `VNewRawDoFmt` callback through as a native callback:** the formatter calls the translated containment address as a host function; guest SERIAL/COUNT sentinels are translated as addresses and miss native sentinel checks. Applies to optional m68kemu targets and external guest clients using these modes. See [EK9268](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9268) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5232). No guest callback was run; source-only.
**EK9269 — m68kemu returns a host buffer address from `VNewRawDoFmt` string mode:** native formatting advances the translated host pointer, then the thunk returns it without converting back to a guest address. Guest callers using the returned pointer receive an invalid/truncated address. Applies to optional m68kemu targets and external guest clients. See [EK9269](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9269) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5235). No guest formatter was run; source-only.
**EK9270 — m68kemu passes guest `AllocEntry` `MemList` bytes to native code without layout conversion:** the guest and 64-bit host structure offsets/strides differ, so native Exec reads the wrong count and entries. Optional 64-bit m68kemu targets; external guest callers. See [EK9270](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9270) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5238). No allocation was run; source-only.
**EK9271 — m68kemu returns a native `MemList` pointer from `AllocEntry` to the guest:** D0 receives a truncated host address, and passing it to guest `FreeEntry` translates it as a guest address. Optional 64-bit m68kemu targets; external guest callers. See [EK9271](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9271) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5238). No allocation or free was run; source-only.
**EK9272 — m68kemu routes guest `AllocAbs` to native Exec’s free-list allocator:** the translated address lies inside the already allocated containment block, so native Exec cannot reserve that range through the emulator’s separate guest heap. Optional m68kemu targets; external guest callers. See [EK9272](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9272) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5241). No allocation was run; source-only.
**EK9273 — m68kemu applies native 64-bit list layouts to guest 32-bit lists:** generated list operations dereference/write native pointer offsets and strides, corrupting or misreading containment-backed guest lists. Optional 64-bit m68kemu targets; external guest callers. See [EK9273](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9273) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5244). No guest list operation was run; source-only.
**EK9274 — m68kemu returns host node pointers from `RemHead`/`RemTail` to guest code:** D0 gets a truncated host address instead of a guest node address. Separate from list input layout; applies when a native/shadow-backed list is used. Optional 64-bit m68kemu targets; external guest callers. See [EK9274](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9274) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5244). No guest list operation was run; source-only.
**EK9277 — m68kemu passes guest `Task` records to native `AddTask` without field conversion:** ordinary guest task structures are 92 bytes, while the checked-in x86_64 native layout uses different offsets; task setup reads and writes the wrong fields. Optional x86_64 m68kemu; external guest callers. See [EK9277](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9277) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5247). No task was created; source-only.
**EK9278 — `AllocVec()` and unmanaged `AllocVecPooled()` can wrap a near-maximum request to one byte:** if that small allocation succeeds, the API returns a pointer without the requested backing extent. Managed pools are excluded; no selected in-tree near-limit caller was found. See [EK9278](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9278) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5316). No allocation or payload access was run; source-only.
**EK9471 — `AllocVecPooled()` can call a NULL managed-pool callback:** it checks `mhe_Alloc` but invokes the separate `mhe_AllocVec`; a custom managed provider with only the ordinary allocator faults on nonzero vector allocation. Selected in-tree providers do not establish this trigger. See [EK9471](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9471) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1861). No pool operation was run; source-only.
**EK9279 — PC write-lock priority donation can restore an intermediate priority:** repeated donations overwrite the saved original priority, so acquisition restores only the most recent intermediate value. Requires a waiter to observe successively lower-priority owners; selected PC NVMe queues provide task-context contention. See [EK9279](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9279) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1261). No lock contention was run; source-only.
**EK9280 — OpenSBI virtual-IRQ count arithmetic can wrap before bitmap scanning:** an extreme public count passes both range checks, then the scan can index past the 1,024-byte bitmap. Applies to RISC-V64 OpenSBI; selected PCIDT requests are bounded. See [EK9280](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9280) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5322). No IRQ allocation was attempted; source-only.
**EK10154 — OpenSBI virtual-IRQ allocation does not synchronize bitmap reservation:** overlapping callers can both select and return the same free range, then share one handler chain. Requires concurrent RISC-V64 OpenSBI callers; no selected in-tree overlap was found. See [EK10154](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10154) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8556). No IRQ operation was run; source-only.
**EK9300 — Sam440 retries an unhandled TLB fault at the unchanged PC:** the handler tests the exception-chain result backwards and returns without advancing SRR0 or entering the generic fatal path. Applies to data/instruction TLB faults with no matching handler. See [EK9300](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9300) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#5327). No exception was run; source-only.
**EK9301 — Sam440 DOS boot loading ignores sector-read errors:** failed or partial reads can be consumed as file data and the reader can return the declared file size. Applies to optional Parthenope DOS loading; exact stale-buffer behavior depends on the external callback. See [EK9301](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9301) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L846). No disk read or boot was run; source-only.
**EK9302 — Sam440 DOS boot loading trusts OFS `data_size`:** zero-length payloads leave the file byte count unchanged, and oversized lengths can make the copy read beyond the block scratch payload. Requires malformed/corrupt OFS block metadata and an extending chain or sufficiently large remaining file. See [EK9302](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9302) and [coverage](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5338). No partition or file was read; source-only.

## Exec/Kernel detailed report restorations (2026-10-30)

- [EK745](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek745): ordinary generated library vectors perform unsynchronized open-count and delayed-expunge flag updates on ExecSMP; ASL is a selected standard-vector example. Expunge consequences remain conditional on a delayed expunge request.
- [EK752](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek752): 32-bit `AllocAbs()` endpoint wrap can pass a standard MemHeader bounds check and corrupt its free-chunk chain; the extreme caller request remains unestablished.
- [EK769](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek769): zero root DTB cell counts make the OpenSBI memory tuple loop make no progress before startup fallbacks.
- [EK772](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek772): overflowing FDT cell counts can pass a wrapped tuple-width check before `read_cells()` walks beyond a short property.
- [EK871](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek871): failed TLSF control-state initialization is ignored before AArch64 extra-range publication or managed `CreatePool()` allocation.


**[EK872](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek872) — Sam440 startup can register a zero-sized region at the 16 MiB boundary:** the decoded total is reduced by the reserved 16 MiB, then passed to `AddMemList()` without a zero check; the generic routine writes and publishes a header with underflowed free size. Actual board register values and boot reachability remain unverified. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**[EK873](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek873) — A late reset-callback completion can release the wait for a later callback:** after timeout, the prior callback continues in a support task; its eventual completion uses the same signal and task-pointer fields as the currently awaited callback. Applies to the non-supervisor path when timer.device is available and callbacks overlap as described. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**[EK8774](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8774) — IRQ-handler data updates do not synchronize with ExecSMP dispatch:** the modifier uses only local `Disable()`, while selected generic/PC dispatch paths on Raspberry Pi and x86-64 PC read the data on other CPUs without matching synchronization. Old-data lifetime consequences remain conditional; no direct in-tree modifier caller was found. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**[EK8779](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8779) — Concurrent IFMeta construction can collide method IDs:** IFMeta increments the shared method-base counter before taking the IID-table semaphore; simultaneous distinct interface registrations can receive the same numeric base. The trigger remains conditional on concurrent dynamic IFMeta construction, with no selected in-tree sequence established. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

EK8780 disposition (2026-10-30): withdrew the OOP_GetMethod out-of-range-offset candidate. The documented input is a method ID obtained from OOP_GetMethodID(); no malformed in-tree caller or contract requiring invalid-offset rejection was found. It is no longer an active indexed bug. See the disposition in the [Exec/Kernel report](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8780) and [coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**[EK8784](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8784) — `OOP_GetMethodID()` lookup is unpinned against final interface release:** lookup traverses the IID hash without its semaphore while final attr/class release unlinks and frees the bucket and copied ID. Scope remains conditional on an ExecSMP client overlapping these operations; checked in-tree callers did not establish such an overlap. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**[EK8790](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8790) — SMP task-setup failure can leak caller-allocated CPU masks:** PC and ARM/AArch64 callers pass heap masks through `TASKTAG_AFFINITY`, but task/context setup can fail before `PrepareContext()` adopts them; selected callers then release their own task records without freeing the mask. Scope is limited to non-NULL masks and the documented failure paths; EK8918/EK8976 cover distinct successful ARM and non-ExecSMP i386 cases. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**[EK8792](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8792) — Security can miss task lifecycle events during owner-list initialization:** task.resource checks for an empty hook list outside its registration semaphore; a creator can be absent from both notification and Security's snapshot, or a remover can evade notification after inclusion in the snapshot. This can leave a live task untracked or a stale owner node. Applies when security.library/task.resource are selected and lifecycle overlaps initialization; no overlap was run. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**[EK8793](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8793) — task.resource can omit a live task from task listings:** if its prelaunch `TaskListEntry` allocation fails, the hook silently skips insertion while Exec still launches the task. task.resource enumerators, including selected `C:TaskList`, then miss it for its lifetime. Trigger is conditional on that allocation failure. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.
**[EK8798](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8798) — Task-list clients can dereference task data after concurrent removal:** task.resource locks iterator entries, but does not pin returned tasks. SysMon and optional TaskTrace retain or use raw task pointers; the optional VMM preferences task page reads process CLI/BSTR fields that DOS frees before `RemTask` removes the task. Applies to ExecSMP when refresh/lookup overlaps teardown; VMM and TaskTrace are explicit optional targets, not claimed in the default image. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only; no SMP interleaving was run.

**[EK8796](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8796) — Debug disassembly assumes CPU alert context:** the synchronous `AT_NONE` system-alert path can pass NULL while selected i386/RISC-V debug libraries enable disassembly, causing a secondary fault during alert formatting. The user “More” path also treats non-CPU alert union data as an exception context, with wrong output conditional on its contents. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**[EK9455](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9455) — SysMon task details duplicate the task name in the Status row:** both UI objects are assigned to the Name-object field, and refresh writes the task name through the overwritten pointer; no task state is displayed. The Name row can become stale if the name changes while the detail window is reused. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**[EK8806](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8806) — RISC-V64 diagnostics truncate saved register values:** `%016lx` asks RawDoFmt to fetch 32-bit `ULONG` values from 64-bit GPR/SP/RA/PC fields, so their upper halves are omitted in CPU alerts and the `RI` debugger display. The saved context is unchanged. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**[EK8813](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8813) — Raspberry Pi ARM32 ELF loading has no image-length bounds:** the helpers read section tables, payloads and relocation metadata from a pointer alone, while selected standalone/package callers know the extent but do not pass it. Scoped to malformed or truncated ELF input; the embedded generated core is not claimed malformed. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**[EK8816](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8816) — AArch64 post-DMA cache maintenance can overwrite device data in a shared edge line:** selected Raspberry Pi AArch64 NVMe and xHCI read paths clean whole cache lines after DMA. If adjacent bytes are modified during transfer, stale bytes can be written over the device result. The overlap is conditional; source-only. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md).

**[EK8818](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8818) — Low-memory allocation retries can reuse a detached handler cursor:** a handler removing itself before `MEM_TRY_AGAIN`, or freeing the successor cached before callback invocation, can leave traversal with stale node state. No checked-in handler demonstrates the sequence; conditional public API candidate. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**[EK8820](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8820) — ExecSMP task creation can lose CPU affinity when mask allocation fails:** the task is still launched with NULL affinity; ARM32/AArch64 treat that as unrestricted, while PC/APIC treats it as CPU 0 only. Trigger requires the per-task mask allocation to fail after ETask allocation. Distinct from caller-owned mask leaks and idle-task accounting. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only.

**[EK8823](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8823) — AArch64 range mapping can fail after partial descriptor edits:** a later page-table allocation failure returns without rollback; selected RP1 cleanup then frees the backing storage. Residual hardware visibility and current target buildability remain unverified (see EK8902). Trigger requires a large, partially aligned mapping and a later allocation failure. Source-only. See the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md).

**[EK8824](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8824) — Concurrent AArch64 page-table splits can lose a successful mapping:** callers splitting the same L2 block can publish competing L3 tables, leaving the later table installed and the earlier caller’s edit absent.
