**EK10232 — M68040 CAS/CAS2 failed comparisons skip required memory writeback:** the selected Moira handlers update compare registers but omit the M68040 destination writeback on a failed comparison. This suppresses mapped-device writes as well as the specified locked-access transaction; a CAS.W to the bridge's VPOSW mapping demonstrates an observable emulated-state difference. Applies to explicit `m68kemu.library` execution. See [EK10232](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10232) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L10570). No instruction or build was run; source-only.

**EK10233 — CHK2/CMP2.B/W truncate address-register values before range checking:** the selected handler clips An to the operation size before checking the bounds, although M68040 byte/word forms compare the full 32-bit An against sign-extended bounds. With bounds 1–2 and A0=`0x00010001`, CHK2 incorrectly suppresses its enabled exception; CMP2 also returns the wrong C/Z flags. Applies to explicit `m68kemu.library` execution. See [EK10233](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10233) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L10572). No instruction or build was run; source-only.
**GD4784 — FTManager replaces a valid font preview after grayscale allocation failure:** an unchecked pixel-buffer or destination-bitmap failure can still produce a non-NULL blank preview, which the caller installs over the old one. Glyph-info allocation failure also reaches signed-overflowing bounds arithmetic. Applies to explicit `workbench-system-ftmanager` builds. See [GD4784](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd4784) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#ftmanager-font-bitmap-allocation-failure-recheck). Source-only; no allocation failure or preview was run.


**OD3372 — Closing PCI xHCI frees active DMA/private state before quiescing the controller and interrupt; workers that reached their wait loops remain blocked with resources open.** Applies to selected Raspberry Pi AArch64 and RISC-V OpenSBI packages. See [OD3372](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3372) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pci-xhci-close-teardown-reconciliation). Source-only; no controller close or interrupt was run.


**OD10348 — PCI xHCI ignores failure to mark a parent slot as a hub and proceeds to address a downstream device.** Applies to selected Raspberry Pi AArch64 and RISC-V OpenSBI PCI xHCI packages when a parent Configure Endpoint command fails during child enumeration. See [OD10348](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10348) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#xhci-parent-hub-slot-programming-caller-pass). Source-only; no enumeration or command was run.

**OD10349 — UHCI reset shifts by an unchecked public port number after its range-checked reset helper fails.** Port 0 or a port at least 33 reaches an invalid C shift in the reset bitmap update; the selected USBHub worker supplies ports 1–2, so the trigger is limited to invalid or external HIDD calls. See [OD10349](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10349) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#uhci-root-hub-reset-port-range-recheck). Source-only; no controller or method was run.

**OD10350 — UHCI reports reset-change in the wrong status field and leaves a sticky reset bit.** The flag is placed in `wPortStatus`, and the wrapper also sets it after a reset timeout; the selected stack bypasses the generic clear path. Applies to UHCI root-hub status queries; the worker does not currently branch on the flag. See [OD10350](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10350) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#uhci-reset-status-word-reconciliation). Source-only; no reset or controller was run.

**EK10234 — M68040 CLR reads a custom-register destination before clearing it:** the selected Moira CLR path reads `$DFF02A` before writing zero, but only 68000/68008 CLR requires that read. The bridge's read callback advances the emulated beam, so later VHPOSR reads can shift by two color clocks. Applies to explicit `m68kemu.library` execution. See [EK10234](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10234) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L10595). No guest instruction or build was run; source-only.

**EK10235 — M68040 RTE uses incompatible frame formats:** the selected RTE parser rejects valid formats 3 and 7 but accepts format B, a long bus-cycle frame for M68020/M68030. The bridge has no checked-in producer for these frames; the trigger requires a guest-supplied or restored frame. Applies to explicit `m68kemu.library` execution. See [EK10235](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10235) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L10617). No frame or instruction was executed; source-only.

**EK10236 — M68040 master-mode interrupts keep both exception frames on the master stack:** the selected Moira handler does not clear SR.M or switch to the interrupt stack before pushing the format-1 throwaway frame. This applies when an interrupt reaches the selected M68040 core while it is in supervisor master mode; the checked-in AROS bridge has no `setIPL()` caller, so current in-tree reachability is unestablished. See [EK10236](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10236) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L10613). No interrupt was run; source-only.

**EK10237 — M68040 CINV/CPUSH variants raise Line-F:** the selected model registers these cache-maintenance instructions, but their handlers use the generic Line-F exception path. Supervisor execution should perform the maintenance (a no-op in the cacheless emulator); user execution should raise a privilege violation. Applies to explicit `m68kemu.library` execution. See [EK10237](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10237) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L10623). No guest instruction was run; source-only.

**EK10238 — M68040 MOVE16 variants raise Line-F instead of copying a 16-byte memory line.** All five selected addressing forms reach Line-F; expected transfer and postincrement never occur. Applies to explicit `m68kemu.library` execution. See [EK10238](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10238) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L10625). No guest instruction was run; source-only.

**EK10239 — CHK2/CMP2.B interprets PC-relative bounds as unsigned:** the selected byte handlers sign-extend Dn but leave PC-relative bounds zero-extended, so D0=`0x80` with bounds `0x80–0x81` reports out-of-range instead of equality. CHK2 can take a false exception; CMP2 returns wrong C/Z. Applies to PC-relative displacement/indexed forms in explicit `m68kemu.library` execution. See [EK10239](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10239) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L10643). No guest instruction was run; source-only.

**EK10240 — PC ExecSMP can link a stack-rejected task into both Running and Wait:** the dispatcher adds a selected task to Running, then queues an invalid-stack task on Wait without unlinking it. Its recovery path removes/requeues the same node under assumptions that leave Running's intrusive links inconsistent. Applies to x86-64 PC SMP when a ready task fails the saved-stack bounds check. See [EK10240](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10240). Source-only; no scheduler operation was run.
**EK10303 — PC ExecSMP can requeue a task while dispatch publishes it as Running:** `SetTaskPri()` trusts `TS_READY` while the PC dispatcher has dequeued the task and may already have linked it to `TaskRunning`. Concurrent priority change can link one task into both scheduler lists or corrupt Running. Scoped to x86-64 PC ExecSMP. See [EK10303](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10303) and the [scheduler/SetTaskPri trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#pc-execsmp-settaskpri-dispatch-list-race-ek10303). Source-only; no interleaving was run.
**EK9025 — Failed CDFS handler startup leaves its shared semaphore published:** first-handler device or cache setup failure returns without removing the new singleton or closing `utility.library`. Applies to the explicit optional `kernel-fs-cdfs` target. See [EK9025](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9025) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L3704). No failure was induced; source-only.

**EK10241 — CDFS can use its shared state after the last handler frees it:** a starting handler receives an unpinned pointer from `FindSemaphore`; the last existing handler can remove and free the empty singleton before device registration uses it. Applies to overlapping CDFS handler startup/shutdown on preemptive targets. See [EK10241](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10241) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#cdfs-shared-semaphore-lifetime-caller-pass). No interleaving was run; source-only.

**EK10242 — Bifteck reports success after an interrupted or failed log write:** ignored `FPutC()`/`Close()` failures and an overwritten Ctrl-C error allow a truncated debug log to return `RETURN_OK` and clear `IoErr`. Applies to the explicit optional `debug-tools-bifteck` target. See [EK10242](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10242) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#remaining-named-findsemaphore-caller-census-closure). No command or output failure was run; source-only.

**EK10243 — PosixC pthread workers can leak an opened library base after task-slot allocation failure:** the enter hook ignores a failed task-storage write; the exit hook then cannot recover or close the base. Repeated affected workers retain per-task bases and library open references. Applies to builds selecting both `linklib-pthread` and per-task-base PosixC. See [EK10243](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10243) and the [PosixC thread-hook coverage row](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L593). No allocation failure or worker was run; source-only.


**OD3776 — EMU10kx register transactions and interrupt-mask updates are not serialized across CPUs:** the AHI lock aliases are local interrupt masking only. On ExecSMP, overlapping calls can misdirect PTR/DATA or AC97 ADDRESS/DATA transactions, or lose independent INTE bit updates. Conditional on cross-CPU overlap. See [OD3776](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3776) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md).

**OD10351 — EMU10kx MIDI IRQ can call cleared CAMD callbacks:** after close clears the hook pointers, a still-pending or in-flight MIDI interrupt can pass NULL to `CallHookA`; timing is conditional and was not reproduced. See [OD10351](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10351).

**OD10352 — EMU10kx CAMD open ignores MPU reset failure:** if reset lacks its expected `0xfe` acknowledgement, OpenCAMDPort still reports success and CAMD accepts the port. See [OD10352](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10352).

**EK9335 — A cyclic RDB LSEG chain can hang table discovery:** the synchronous filesystem-size pass follows `lsb_Next` without cycle detection, including when reached by DOSBoot's partition scan. See [EK9335](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9335).

**EK9336 — New RDB partitions return zero PT_GEOMETRY:** the required DosEnvec tag makes the only geometry-initialization branch unreachable; the generic query copies the zeroed structure. HDToolBox performs this query after adding a partition. See [EK9336](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9336).

**EK9341 — Closing an open RDB root table can leak its generic wrapper:** root close calls the backend close callback but omits freeing `PartitionTableHandler`. Checked in-tree callers close tables first; the public precondition remains ambiguous. See [EK9341](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9341).

**EK9338 — An RDB open-pass read failure can leak the backend metadata record:** if the initial header rescan fails after the check callback recognized the table, `PartitionRDBOpenPartitionTable()` frees its scratch buffer but loses its unlinked `RDBData` allocation. The trigger is conditional on a later/transient read error. See [EK9338](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9338).

**EK9339 — RDB metadata-chain failures can lead to truncating writeback:** failed reads, invalid records, or allocation failures stop BADB, PART, or FSHD loading while the backend still returns success; later serialization rebuilds each chain from the in-memory prefix. HDToolBox can write the partial table, while the optional `C:Partition` tool can also size a new partition against the incomplete list and overlap an omitted extent. See [EK9339](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9339).


**EK9340 — RDB can expose a selectable filesystem with a missing or partly read LSEG image:** read/validation/allocation failure leaves the FSHD node linked; later load dereferences a NULL image on m68k and non-m68k paths, while a second-pass short read can feed incomplete storage to the loader. See [EK9340](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9340).


**EK9342 — Optional QuickPart reopens a live partition table:** its disk scan leaves the first open active, then the container constructor opens the same handle again; generic open overwrites the first table pointer, and the later single close only disposes the replacement. See [EK9342](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9342).


**EK9344 — DOSBoot's m68k-only mouse-menu and PAL/NTSC blocks use a mismatched guard:** `#ifdef mc68000` excludes them under AROS's `__mc68000` spelling; the key action remains advertised but does nothing. See [EK9344](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9344).


**EK9345 — Concurrent synchronous `SystemTagList()` calls can corrupt a shared console break target:** with the same interactive FileHandle, one caller can restore the original task while another is running, then the latter can restore an exited child's task pointer. The overlap is conditional; no in-tree same-handle caller sequence was established. See [EK9345](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9345).


**EK9346 — ARM32 BCMGENET may read stale RX data from reused slots:** the selected ARM32 `CachePostDMA()` is a no-op, and the driver reuses slots without another pre-DMA operation. The consequence is conditional on noncoherent GENET DMA; AArch64's override is excluded. See [EK9346](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9346).


**EK9347 — Optional QuickPart leaks each root partition handle opened during disk scan:** the disk and container disposal paths close table/UI state but never call `CloseRootPartition()`. See [EK9347](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9347).


**EK9348 — Optional QuickPart leaves its constructor-time device open outstanding:** the scan's extra open/close pair balances only itself, then disposal deletes the still-open IO request without `CloseDevice()`. See [EK9348](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9348).


**EK9349 — QuickPart can pass a null IO request to `OpenDevice()`:** it does not check the message-port or request allocations; Exec returns NULL on failure and dereferences the request in OpenDevice. See [EK9349](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9349).


**EK9350 — Optional QuickPart writes through a failed disk-name allocation:** both the supplied-name copy path and identify/fallback path use unchecked allocations; the separate verbose-name allocation is guarded. See [EK9350](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9350).


**EK9351 — Optional QuickPart's fixed-width name trimmer can underflow or truncate:** its trim pointer starts two words early, reads before the buffer on all-space/all-zero identify data (and may write there), and can terminate before a nonblank final word. See [EK9351](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9351).


**EK9352 — Optional QuickPart reads SCSI Inquiry product bytes at offset 32 instead of 16:** it displays revision/vendor-specific bytes after a successful fallback. See [EK9352](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9352).

**EK9353 — Optional QuickPart reverses SCSI Inquiry characters in pairs on little-endian targets:** its ATA helper applies big-endian word conversion to the raw Inquiry byte string. See [EK9353](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9353).


**EK9354 — Optional QuickPart drops the free extent after an interior partition:** it shrinks the free node's end before checking whether a post-partition range remains, so later placement cannot use that omitted range in the editor session. No on-disk data loss is claimed. See [EK9354](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9354).


**EK9356 — QuickPart leaks its separately allocated partition-container bookkeeping nodes:** consuming free-space nodes unlinks without freeing them, and container disposal never drains the remaining list. See [EK9356](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9356).


**EK9357 — QuickPart dereferences a failed partition bookkeeping-node allocation:** `InsertPartEntry()` proceeds to `AddTail()` with `newPartNode == NULL` after `AllocVec()` fails. See [EK9357](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9357).


**EK9358 — QuickPart dereferences a failed initial free-space-node allocation:** the container constructor immediately initializes `contSpacerNode` without checking `AllocVec()`. See [EK9358](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9358).


**EK9359 — QuickPart can overflow a 64-byte stack buffer while formatting a DOS device name:** an eligible DOS BSTR name of at least 63 characters places the colon or terminator beyond the buffer. See [EK9359](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9359).


**EK9360 — QuickPart under-reports displayed partition size by one sector:** its inclusive block count subtracts one before conversion to bytes; partition endpoints are unaffected. See [EK9360](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9360).


**EK9361 — QuickPart passes a failed size-string allocation to `%s`:** the NULL `StrDup()` result reaches `sprintf()` unchecked; manifestation depends on libc behavior. See [EK9361](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9361).


**EK9362 — QuickPart leaks duplicated partition strings on object disposal:** the type, size, label and optional DOS-device strings are not released; the container label can alias the type allocation. See [EK9362](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9362).


**EK9363 — QuickPart passes a failed `NewRegion()` result to `OrRectRegion()`:** drawing the active partition can dereference NULL on region allocation failure before the later clip-region guard. See [EK9363](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9363).


**EK9364 — QuickPart's Apply and Undo controls are unwired:** delete operations can be staged in the pending group, but the controls have no notification and `SaveDisk` is a stub, leaving no selected commit/rollback path. See [EK9364](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9364).


**EK9365 — QuickPart appends `unknown>` after every displayed GPT partition UUID:** the UUID formatter falls through to the default description case. This is a label-only issue. See [EK9365](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9365).


**EK9366 — QuickPart omits the “primary” label for ordinary MBR partitions:** the formatter tests an empty string pointer for NULL, so the ordinary-label branch never runs. See [EK9366](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9366).


**EK9367 — QuickPart leaks an unattached delete-operation object when replacement free-space allocation fails:** the handler has already cleared the active selection and leaves the newly created object undisposed. See [EK9367](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9367).


**EK9368 — QuickPart divides by zero when no discovered drive has nonzero capacity:** failed root probes retain zero-sized entries while scaling divides by the still-zero largest capacity. See [EK9368](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9368).


**EK9369 — QuickPart can call `UUID_Unparse()` with a NULL UUID library base:** startup ignores failure to open `uuid.library`, and the later GPT details path calls the vector. See [EK9369](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9369).


**EK9370 — QuickPart does not release custom classes, its UUID library reference or its storage attribute base:** normal exit and partial class initialization lack corresponding cleanup. See [EK9370](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9370).


**EK9371 — RISC-V CPU alerts treat saved `s0` as a frame chain despite frame-pointer omission:** alert formatting reads two words before saved s0, while selected RISC-V builds omit frame pointers; traces can be invalid, with a conditional boundary read. See [EK9371](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9371).


**EK9372 — Hosted emergency-console startup leaks DOS resources on failure paths:** early resident failures retain `dos.library`; later failures can leak allocated input/output FileHandles before returning or removing the process. Applies to hosted targets with the emergency-console resident enabled. See [EK9372](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9372).


**EK9373 — Sam440 can lose 50 Hz VBlank/timer.device ticks during `Disable()`:** UIC masking does not stop the decrementer, its handler skips VBlank while `IDNestCnt` is nonnegative, and `Enable()` does not replay skipped events. See [EK9373](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9373).


**EK9374 — SAD's `ST` command walks PC ExecSMP task lists without their read locks:** concurrent scheduling/removal can invalidate traversal links or task data. See [EK9374](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9374).


**EK9375 — SAD's `RA` and `RC` loops wrap at count `FFFFFFFF`:** the 32-bit unsigned counter wraps if the entire requested range remains readable, so completion is not guaranteed. See [EK9375](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9375).


**EK9376 — m68k `ChangeDecoration` passes guest-layout storage to native Intuition without converting `NewDecorator`:** its private vector can misread and overwrite guest structure fields on 64-bit native hosts; no maintained guest caller was found. See [EK9376](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9376).


**EK9377 — m68k screen-notification creation returns a native pointer that the guest cannot pass back reliably:** the start thunk does not translate the returned handle, while the end thunk translates its input as a guest address. No maintained guest caller was found. See [EK9377](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9377).


**EK9378 — Android Exec selects missing `ucontext` APIs and retains a freed HostLib interface after init failure:** the Android option set still enables `newstackswap`, Exec ignores platform-init failure, and the later selected `RunCommand()` caller reaches the stale interface. See [EK9378](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9378).


**EK9379 — `CONDSTATE_METRIC` can call a conducted player's NULL optional hook:** the public tags allow `PLAYER_Conducted` without `PLAYER_Hook`, and the metric path dispatches without checking; no checked-in metric caller was found. See [EK9379](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9379).


**EK9355 — QuickPart leaves a trailing free-space node spanning a later partition:** while scanning an ordered multi-partition table, it appends partition 2 at the first nonmatching child and never splits the trailing free node that contains it. The node and proportional layout continue to count partition 2 as free. Applies to explicit optional QuickPart builds. See [EK9355](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9355).

**EK9018 — Concurrent x86-64 PC ExecSMP signals can mutate Ready under the stale Wait lock:** concurrent callers can both observe a waiting task before either local reschedule syscall changes its state; the later handler can remove/re-enqueue it while holding the old list lock. Target affinity need not include both caller CPUs. See [EK9018](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9018). Source-only; no schedule was run.

**GD10293 — ReAction Scroller arrow frames can draw outside small gadgets:** with arrows enabled, a vertical gadget whose width exceeds its height or a horizontal gadget whose height exceeds its width generates frame coordinates beyond its bounds; the selected Intuition render path removes the layer clip region, allowing visible overdraw. Applies to explicit optional `scroller.gadget` builds. See [GD10293](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10293) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#reaction-scroller-arrow-frame-geometry-and-render-clipping-pass). Source-only; no render or build was run.


**GD10294 — Android graphics startup reports success after display registration fails:** `agfx_Startup()` ignores `AddDisplayDriverA()`'s error, returns `TRUE`, and leaves its self-open count and input drivers active without a display. Latent at this commit because GD14340’s missing `androidgfx_bitmap.c` manifest prerequisite blocks the module build; if repaired, it requires a display-registration failure. See [GD10294](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10294) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#android-graphics-startup-registration-result-pass). Source-only; no failure or build was run.


**OD10353 — Nouveau and VMware PCI glue leak OOP attribute-base references on PCI object creation failure:** both copies obtain two attribute bases before constructing the PCI bus object and bypass their release routine if construction fails. Applies to explicitly selected optional Nouveau/VMware DRM HIDD targets. See [OD10353](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10353) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-vmware-pci-glue-init-failure-cleanup-pass). Source-only; no PCI operation or failure was induced.


**GD10295 — SysExplorer PCI tree misclassifies non-PCI-to-PCI bridge devices:** the PCI enumerator tests base class `0x06` but ignores the subclass, so host and other bridge-class devices can appear as PCI-to-PCI bridges. Applies to the explicitly selected optional PCI support module. See [GD10295](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10295) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sysexplorer-pci-enumerator-class-filter-pass). Source-only; no PCI enumeration or GUI was run.


**OD10354 — GH100 FMC section-name parsing can read beyond the firmware image:** FMC validation bounds section payloads but not section-name offsets or termination; `elf_section()` uses the unchecked offset with `strcmp()` before firmware verification. Applies to explicit optional Nouveau GH100-family builds with malformed or damaged local FMC firmware. See [OD10354](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10354) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#gh100-gsp-fmc-section-name-validation-pass). Source-only; no firmware or GPU was used.

**OD10355 — Nouveau HS-v2 loaders divide by a zero signature count from malformed firmware:** selected bootloader readers use unchecked `num_sig` as a divisor before rejecting the blob. Applies to optional GA10x GSP and shared GA100 ACR/scrubber firmware paths. See [OD10355](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10355) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-hs-v2-zero-signature-count-pass). Source-only; no firmware or GPU was used.

**OD10356 — Nouveau GSP FRTS setup leaks a local firmware object on late initialization errors:** FRTS creates a stack-local Falcon firmware object, then returns on initialization failure without destroying it; later GSP teardown cannot reach that local object. Applies to optional TU102/GA100/GA102/AD102 GSP paths using the shared FRTS callback. See [OD10356](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10356) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-gsp-frts-local-firmware-cleanup-pass). Source-only; no failure or GPU operation was run.

**OD10357 — Nouveau GSP FWSEC app-interface metadata can direct out-of-bounds reads and writes:** the selected patcher trusts VBIOS/firmware offsets, entry counts and DMEM command offsets without checking the allocated image extent. Applies to optional TU102/GA100/GA102/AD102 GSP FWSEC paths with malformed or mismatched local metadata. See [OD10357](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10357) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#nouveau-gsp-fwsec-app-interface-bounds-pass). Source-only; no firmware or GPU was used.

**OD10358 — BTCtrl can use a hardware record after concurrent removal:** the command retains a raw hardware pointer after releasing the list lock, while Bluetooth Preferences can remove and free that record. See [OD10358](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10358) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#btctrl-hardware-lookup-removal-lifetime-pass). Source-only; no removal or build was run.

**OD10359 — `BEHMB_REMHARDWARE` delivers a freed hardware pointer:** `btRemHardware()` frees the record before queuing the event whose documented parameter is that record. The in-tree Preferences handler ignores the pointer; impact is conditional on a client dereferencing it. See [OD10359](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10359) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-hardware-removal-event-pointer-lifetime-pass). Source-only; no event or build was run.
**OD10360 — Bluetooth can restore a device as bonded without loading its credentials:** if canonical device-ID allocation fails, restore still publishes registered/bonded state while skipping saved key loading. Classic authentication or LE re-encryption then lacks the saved key for that boot. See [OD10360](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10360) and the [Bluetooth restore ID-allocation pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-restore-id-allocation-failure-pass). Source-only; no allocation failure or connection was run.
**OD10361 — Bluetooth channel waits race on the device health counter:** unlocked waiter updates can overlap the hardware task’s locked counter/dead-flag updates, losing increments or causing delayed/duplicate dead-state notifications. See [OD10361](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10361) and the [Bluetooth channel health-counter pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-channel-health-counter-race-pass). Source-only; no channel or interleaving was run.
**OD10362 — Bluetooth restore reads a short registration chunk as a full device record:** a bounded but undersized DREG chunk is accepted and then read at the full structure size, potentially creating a phantom registered device or faulting. See [OD10362](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10362) and the [typed config-chunk length pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-short-registration-chunk-pass). Source-only; no malformed config was loaded.
**OD10363 — Bluetooth accepts bond flags without their saved key bytes:** a bounded KEYS payload can set a link-key flag while omitting the key; restore retains the flag and the HCI path can return zero-filled key material. See [OD10363](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10363) and the [key-chunk flag/length pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-key-chunk-flag-length-pass). Source-only; no malformed key chunk was loaded.
**OD10364 — Bluetooth unregistration can leave class bindings active if its cleanup event allocation fails:** the hardware task reports success, but the broadcaster silently drops the event on allocation failure and retained bindings block clear-old cleanup. See [OD10364](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10364) and the [event-note allocation-failure pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-device-unregistration-event-allocation-failure-od10364). Source-only; no allocation failure or unregister was run.
**OD10365 — Bluetooth class removal can free a class still bound during radio teardown:** hardware removal moves the device to a dead list before releasing bindings, but class removal searches only live devices and frees the class after its cleanup scan misses that binding. See [OD10365](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10365) and the [dead-device class-release race pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-dead-device-class-release-race-od10365). Trigger requires overlapping class and radio removal; source-only, no removal was run.
**OD10366 — Concurrent Bluetooth radio removals can strand one caller:** both calls overwrite the hardware task’s single shutdown-waiter slot, and the worker signals only the last one. Applies when removal overlaps before the radio is unlinked. See [OD10366](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10366) and the [concurrent radio-removal waiter pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-concurrent-radio-removal-waiter-od10366). Source-only; no removal was run.
**OD10367 — Bluetooth GATT completion can leave queued endpoint reads undispatched:** after a control GATT operation fails or is aborted, its callback can return without draining queued notification reads. This can strand a HOGP input report channel during overlapping CCCD setup and output/feature activity; generic clients can also wait indefinitely. See [OD10367](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10367) and the [GATT callback queue-drain pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-gatt-callback-queue-drain-od10367). Source-only; no ATT operation or abort was run.
**OD10368 — Bluetooth channel timeout setting is never enforced:** `BCHA_Timeout` is stored through the public attribute packer but no request or wait path reads it. A pending read may outlive its configured timeout. No in-tree caller sets this attribute; intended per-request semantics are inferred from its public comment. See [OD10368](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10368) and the [channel-timeout attribute census](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-channel-timeout-attribute-od10368). Source-only; no channel operation was run.
**OD3715 expanded — Bluetooth name updates free the prior display name before checking replacement allocation:** a failed copy can erase a custom name and later persisted setting; the hardware remote-name path can also leave the display name NULL after a successful response. See [OD3715](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3715) and the [remote-name allocation trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#bluetooth-device-name-second-copy-failure-od3715-expanded). Source-only; no allocation failure or remote-name response was run.

**OD3718 (expanded) — Bluetooth Preferences’ Add Device worker can use a radio after removal:** its background process retains a raw discovered-device pointer while Preferences can remove and free the radio. See [OD3718](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3718). Source-only; no removal or worker was run.
**GD10297 — RequestString leaks its parsed argument block on repeated Shell runs:** its successful `ReadArgs()` handle is never freed, and Shell executes the command on its long-lived process. Applies to the optional standalone `workbench-c-requeststring` target. See [GD10297](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10297-requeststring-leaks-its-readargs-allocation-on-every-shell-invocation) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#requeststring-full-body-and-readargs-lifetime-pass). Source-only; no command was run.
**GD10298 — RequestChoice leaks its gadget-label buffer on a body-allocation failure:** if the escaped body allocation fails after the gadget-label allocation succeeds, the early return skips `FreeVec(GadgetText)`. Repeated Shell runs can retain the allocation until Shell exits. Applies to the optional `workbench-c` target. See [GD10298](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10298-requestchoice-leaks-its-gadget-label-buffer-if-body-formatting-allocation-fails) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#requestchoice-full-body-and-allocation-failure-pass). Source-only; no failure was induced.

**GD10299 — RequestFile passes an unparsed accept/reject filter when pattern allocation fails:** the tag retains the raw argument, which ASL passes to the parsed-pattern matcher. Applies to an explicit `workbench-c` build when allocation fails. See [GD10299](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10299-requestfile-silently-drops-accept-reject-filters-when-pattern-allocation-fails) and the [RequestFile pattern/cleanup pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#requestfile-parser-allocation-and-cleanup-ownership-recheck). Source-only.

**GD10300 — Search reads beyond its indentation buffer in deep directory trees:** `ALL` traversal derives indentation length from nesting depth and passes it to `WriteChars()` beyond the fixed 161-byte buffer at depth 32 or greater. Applies to explicit `workbench-c` builds with normal name output. See [GD10300](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10300-search-reads-beyond-its-indentation-buffer-in-deep-trees) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#search-command-full-body-and-depth-bounds-pass). Source-only; no traversal was run.

**GD10301 — Search loops forever building its KMP table for a 256-byte literal query:** its 8-bit loop counter wraps while compared with the 16-bit query length. Applies to a 256-byte query without `PATTERN` or `FILE`. See [GD10301](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10301-search-can-loop-forever-while-building-the-prefix-table-for-a-256-byte-query) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#search-command-kmp-counter-width-pass). Source-only; no long query was run.

**GD10302 — SetClock leaves its Shell process with DOS requesters disabled:** after setting `pr_WindowPtr` to `(APTR)-1`, the command never restores it; later volume-error requesters in that Shell are suppressed. Applies when run from a long-lived Shell. See [GD10302](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10302-setclock-leaves-the-callers-requesters-disabled) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#setclock-full-body-and-process-state-pass). Source-only; no requester was run.

**GD10303 — SetDate leaks parsed arguments on invalid date/time or `AnchorPath` allocation failure:** both post-`ReadArgs()` exits skip `FreeArgs()`, so repeated Shell invocations retain argument storage. Applies to explicit `workbench-c` builds. See [GD10303](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10303-setdate-leaks-its-parsed-arguments-on-validation-and-allocation-failures) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#setdate-full-body-and-argument-cleanup-pass). Source-only; no failure was induced.

**GD10304 — SetDefaultFont can write past its 256-byte font-name buffer:** after copying the supplied name, it appends `.font` without checking capacity; `ReadArgs`'s `?` prompt accepts dynamically growing lines. Applies to a name of at least 251 characters without `.font`. See [GD10304](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10304-setdefaultfont-appends-font-past-its-fixed-name-buffer) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#setdefaultfont-full-body-and-name-bounds-pass). Source-only; no long name was entered.

**GD10305 — SetPSM reports both public-screen modes when only one was previously enabled:** logical `&&` tests treat any nonzero old mode mask as both flags, returning 15 instead of 5 or 10. Applies to explicit `workbench-c` builds. See [GD10305](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10305-setpsm-reports-both-modes-when-either-old-mode-bit-is-set) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#setpsm-full-body-and-return-code-pass). Source-only; no mode was changed.

**GD10306 — Sort ignores its NUMERIC option:** numeric requests still use the lexical string comparator. See [GD10306](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10306-sort-ignores-its-numeric-option) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sort-command-full-body-and-comparator-pass). Source-only; no sort command was run.

**GD10307 — Sort CASE comparisons repeatedly compare the first selected character:** later characters do not participate in lexical comparison, so equal-prefix lines can remain misordered. See [GD10307](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10307-sort-case-comparisons-repeatedly-compare-the-first-selected-character) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sort-command-full-body-and-comparator-pass). Source-only; no sort command was run.

**GD10308 — Sort COLSTART comparison reads beyond line boundaries:** comparator lengths are not reduced after the column offset, and the case branch applies the offset twice. See [GD10308](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10308-sort-colstart-comparison-reads-beyond-line-boundaries) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sort-command-full-body-and-comparator-pass). Source-only; no sort input was run.

**GD10309 — Sort reads one byte past input when the final line lacks a newline:** its parser checks the byte at `pos` before testing whether `pos` equals the input length. See [GD10309](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10309-sort-reads-one-byte-past-input-when-the-final-line-lacks-a-newline) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sort-command-full-body-and-line-boundary-pass). Source-only; no file was sorted.

**GD10310 — Sort mishandles empty lines and reads before the input buffer:** zero-length records cause a `len - 1` access and blank lines can be omitted. See [GD10310](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10310-sort-mishandles-empty-lines-and-reads-before-the-input-buffer) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sort-command-full-body-and-line-boundary-pass). Source-only; no file was sorted.

**GD10311 — Sort silently omits lines when a record allocation fails:** allocation failure discards the current line without setting an error. See [GD10311](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10311-sort-silently-omits-lines-when-a-record-allocation-fails) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sort-command-full-body-and-allocation-pass). Source-only; no failure was induced.

**GD10312 — Sort reports success when OpenFromLock fails:** the output can remain empty while the command returns success. See [GD10312](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10312-sort-reports-success-when-openfromlock-fails) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sort-command-full-body-and-io-cleanup-pass). Source-only; no failure was induced.

**GD10313 — Sort leaks its opened Locale reference on every invocation:** repeated Shell runs retain locale references because no `CloseLocale()` occurs. See [GD10313](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10313-sort-leaks-its-opened-locale-reference-on-every-invocation) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sort-command-full-body-and-resource-cleanup-pass). Source-only; no command was run.

**GD10314 — Sort leaks the output filehandle when FIB allocation fails:** the allocation error skips the only `Close(file_out)` path. See [GD10314](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10314-sort-leaks-the-output-filehandle-when-fib-allocation-fails) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sort-command-full-body-and-io-cleanup-pass). Source-only; no failure was induced.

**GD10315 — Sort treats short output writes as complete:** a partial line write can leave truncated output while returning success. See [GD10315](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10315-sort-treats-short-output-writes-as-complete) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sort-command-full-body-and-io-cleanup-pass). Source-only; no output was written.

**GD10316 — StackSnoop writes past its output buffer when the report is large:** unchecked appends can write beyond the static 20,000-byte buffer when formatted output exceeds its capacity. Applies to explicit `workbench-c` builds. See [GD10316](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10316-stacksnoop-writes-past-its-output-buffer-when-the-report-is-large) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#stacksnoop-full-body-and-output-bounds-pass). Source-only; no operation was run.

**GD10317 — StackSnoop traverses scheduler lists without SMP locks:** local interrupt disabling does not protect shared task lists against remote SMP list mutations. Applies to explicit `workbench-c` builds on SMP systems. See [GD10317](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10317-stacksnoop-traverses-scheduler-lists-without-smp-locks) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#stacksnoop-full-body-and-smp-list-lifecycle-pass). Source-only; no operation was run.

**GD10318 — StackSnoop omits tasks running on other SMP CPUs:** tasks on the SMP running and spinning lists are absent from the report. Applies to explicit `workbench-c` builds on SMP systems. See [GD10318](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10318-stacksnoop-omits-tasks-running-on-other-smp-cpus) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#stacksnoop-full-body-and-smp-list-lifecycle-pass). Source-only; no operation was run.

**GD10319 — SymbolDump emits a NULL end address for zero-length symbols:** `EnumerateSymbolsA()` calculates a fallback end address but passes the original zero value to the hook, which SymbolDump writes to `SYS:symbols.out`. See [GD10319](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10319-symboldump-emits-a-null-end-address-for-zero-length-symbols) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#symboldump-full-body-and-debug-api-pass). Explicit `workbench-c` target; source-only.
**GD10320 — SymbolDump calls EnumerateSymbolsA when debug.library failed to open:** if the output file opens but `debug.library` does not, the command calls the library vector through a NULL base. See [GD10320](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10320-symboldump-calls-enumeratesymbolsa-after-debug-library-fails-to-open) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#symboldump-full-body-and-debug-api-pass). Explicit `workbench-c` target; source-only.

**GD10321 — TaskList reports success with an incomplete AROS task snapshot:** the AROS path ignores a failed task-list handle and treats a per-task copy allocation failure as a successful partial list. See [GD10321](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10321-tasklist-reports-success-when-its-aros-task-snapshot-is-incomplete) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#tasklist-full-body-and-allocation-failure-pass). Explicit `workbench-c` target on AROS; source-only.
**GD10322 — TaskList derives a pointer from NULL before checking allocation failure:** `addtask()` computes the destination pointer after `AllocVec()` but before the NULL check. See [GD10322](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10322-tasklist-performs-pointer-arithmetic-on-a-failed-allocation-result) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#tasklist-full-body-and-allocation-failure-pass). Explicit `workbench-c` target; source-only.

**GD10323 — Touch can truncate an existing file after SetFileDate fails:** on multi-user AFS, a non-owner with group write/delete access but no property-access relation is denied the date update, then `MODE_NEWFILE` deletes and recreates the file; Touch reports success. See [GD10323](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10323-touch-truncates-an-existing-file-when-timestamp-update-fails) and the [AFS permission trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#touch-afs-property-vs-replacement-gd10323). Explicit `workbench-c` plus `kernel-fs-afs`; source-only.

**GD10324 — UUIDGen leaks ReadArgs storage on every successful parse:** it never frees the parsed argument block, so repeated Shell calls retain memory. See [GD10324](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10324-uuidgen-leaks-its-readargs-allocation-on-every-successful-parse) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#uuidgen-full-body-and-count-validation-pass). Explicit `workbench-c` target; source-only.
**GD10325 — Negative UUIDGen amounts become billions of iterations:** `/N` accepts a signed negative value, which is read as `ULONG` and used as the loop count. See [GD10325](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10325-a-negative-uuidgen-amount-becomes-billions-of-iterations) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#uuidgen-full-body-and-count-validation-pass). Explicit `workbench-c` target; source-only.
**GD10326 — UUIDGen reports success when argument parsing or uuid.library setup fails:** both no-output failure paths fall through to `RETURN_OK`. See [GD10326](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10326-uuidgen-reports-success-when-parsing-or-uuid-library-setup-fails) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#uuidgen-full-body-and-count-validation-pass). Explicit `workbench-c` target; source-only.

**GD10327 — Version reads before its buffer on files shorter than `$VER:`:** the marker scanner preserves five bytes even when fewer bytes were read. See [GD10327](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10327-version-reads-before-its-buffer-on-files-shorter-than-ver) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#version-full-body-file-scanner-and-elf-pass). Explicit `workbench-c` target; source-only.
**GD10328 — Version's ARM attribute parser trusts malformed section lengths:** truncated metadata can be read beyond its loaded section because nested lengths are not bounded. See [GD10328](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10328-versions-arm-attribute-parser-trusts-malformed-section-lengths) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#version-full-body-file-scanner-and-elf-pass). Explicit `workbench-c` target with ARM `ARCH` parsing; source-only.
**GD10329 — Version reads an uninitialized status while parsing library ID strings:** the status determines whether valid parsed version information is retained or replaced with fallback values. See [GD10329](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10329-version-reads-an-uninitialized-status-while-parsing-library-id-strings) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#version-full-body-file-scanner-and-elf-pass). Explicit `workbench-c` target; source-only.

**GD10330 — Wait converts a negative duration into a very long delay:** signed `/N` input is read as unsigned and multiplied into timer ticks without range validation. See [GD10330](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10330-wait-turns-a-negative-duration-into-a-very-long-timer-request) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wait-full-body-and-duration-pass). Explicit `workbench-c` target; source-only.

**GD10331 — WaitForPort can free its timer request with I/O pending:** Ctrl-C/D exits its wait loop without aborting and waiting for timer.device before freeing the request and port. See [GD10331](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10331-waitforport-frees-a-timer-request-while-it-may-still-be-active) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#waitforport-full-body-timer-lifecycle-and-timeout-pass). **GD10332 — WaitForPort exceeds its documented ten-second timeout:** strict `>` comparison after one-second increments causes an eleventh timer interval. See [GD10332](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10332-waitforport-exceeds-its-documented-ten-second-timeout) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#waitforport-full-body-timer-lifecycle-and-timeout-pass). Explicit `workbench-c` target; source-only.

**GD10333 — Automount can leave a handler registered but not started:** on startup-buffer allocation failure, it has already added the DeviceNode to the DOS list, then exits without rolling it back; later passes skip it. See [GD10333](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10333-automount-leaves-a-dos-entry-registered-when-startup-buffer-allocation-fails) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#automount-full-body-configuration-and-mount-lifecycle-pass). **GD10334 — Automount returns success after preference or mount setup errors:** it preserves failures in `res` but unconditionally returns `RETURN_OK`. See [GD10334](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10334-automount-returns-success-after-preference-or-mount-setup-errors) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#automount-full-body-configuration-and-mount-lifecycle-pass). Explicit `workbench-c` target; source-only.

**GD10335 — Break can signal a task after lookup locks are released:** NAME and PROCESS results are raw task pointers; PORT handling retains `mp_SigTask` after the port-list lock ends. Local `Forbid()` does not prevent teardown on another SMP CPU. See [GD10335](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10335-break-can-signal-a-task-after-lookup-locks-are-released) and the [full-body caller review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#break-full-body-task-lifetime-and-allocation-pass). **GD10336 — Break dereferences unchecked task-list node allocations:** allocation failures in its process, port, and task-name paths are followed by immediate member writes. See [GD10336](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10336-break-dereferences-unchecked-task-list-node-allocations) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#break-full-body-task-lifetime-and-allocation-pass). Explicit `workbench-c` target; source-only.

**GD10337 — ChangeTaskPri reads `/N` priority at pointer width:** ReadArgs provides a `LONG *`, but the command dereferences it as `IPTR *` on 64-bit builds. See [GD10337](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10337-changetaskpri-reads-its-n-priority-at-pointer-width) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#changetaskpri-full-body-and-readargs-number-width-pass). Explicit `workbench-c` target on 64-bit; source-only.
**GD10338 — Break reads `/N` process ID at pointer width:** a valid 32-bit `LONG` is dereferenced as `IPTR` on 64-bit builds, altering the queried process ID. See [GD10338](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10338-break-reads-a-n-process-id-at-pointer-width) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#changetaskpri-full-body-and-readargs-number-width-pass). Explicit `workbench-c` target on 64-bit; source-only.

**GD10339 — ConClip OFF starts the service when none is running:** the absent-port branch creates the rendezvous port without honoring `off`, then enters the service loop. See [GD10339](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10339-conclip-off-starts-the-service-when-it-is-not-already-running) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#conclip-full-body-options-and-hook-lifecycle-pass). Explicit `workbench-c` target; source-only.
**GD10340 — ConClip reads its `/N` clipboard unit at pointer width:** on 64-bit builds it loads `CLIPUNIT` as `IPTR` though ReadArgs stores a `LONG`. See [GD10340](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10340-conclip-reads-its-n-clipboard-unit-at-pointer-width) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#conclip-full-body-options-and-hook-lifecycle-pass). **GD10342 — Date overflows signed arithmetic when setting dates after 2046:** its 32-bit `LONG` day count is multiplied into seconds before conversion to the timer's unsigned seconds field. **GD10349 — GPIO PULL uses the BCM2711 register layout on legacy Broadcom GPIO:** the non-RP1 resource path always writes GPPUPPDN at `+0xE4`, while legacy BCM2835 uses the GPPUD control sequence at `+0x94..0x9c`. See [GD10391](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10391-eval-divides-by-zero-while-evaluating-or-mod) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#eval-command-full-body-expression-and-output-format-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-eval` target; source-only.

**GD10392 — Eval evaluates out-of-range shift counts without validation:** direct signed shifts accept counts outside the `int` width. See [GD10392](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10392-eval-evaluates-out-of-range-shift-counts-without-validation) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#eval-command-full-body-expression-and-output-format-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-eval` target; source-only.

**GD10393 — Eval parses `08` and `09` as zero instead of decimal numbers:** `%i` parses a leading-zero token as octal while the lexer consumes the remaining decimal digits. See [GD10393](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10393-eval-parses-08-and-09-as-zero-instead-of-decimal-numbers) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#eval-command-full-body-expression-and-output-format-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-eval` target; source-only.

**GD10394 — Eval accepts a hex prefix with no digits using a stale value:** failed `sscanf` conversion still returns a numeric token without updating `yylval`. See [GD10394](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10394-eval-accepts-a-hex-prefix-with-no-digits-using-a-stale-value) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#eval-command-full-body-expression-and-output-format-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-eval` target; source-only.


**GD10395 — LoadWB returns success when Workbench does not start:** it ignores the StartWorkbench result and exits zero if startup prerequisites fail. See [GD10395](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10395-loadwb-returns-success-when-workbench-does-not-start) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#loadwb-command-full-body-start-result-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.


**GD10396 — SetKeyboard changes the system default instead of the current shell:** its docs promise per-shell behavior, but the implementation calls a systemwide default-keymap API. See [GD10396](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10396-setkeyboard-changes-the-system-default-instead-of-the-current-shell) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#setkeyboard-command-full-body-scope-and-keymap-lifetime-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.


**GD10397 — Play reports success when playback is interrupted with Ctrl-C:** it ignores which wait signal arrived and returns success after interruption. See [GD10397](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10397-play-reports-success-when-playback-is-interrupted-with-ctrl-c) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#play-command-full-body-signal-and-interruption-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.


**GD10398 — GfxControl reports the direct-bitmap-access transition before it completes:** PDBA only waits for process creation and ADBA only queues a message, with no completion acknowledgement. See [GD10398](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10398-gfxcontrol-reports-the-direct-bitmap-access-transition-before-it-completes) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gfxcontrol-command-full-body-transition-and-options-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.

**GD10399 — GfxControl mishandles simultaneous PREVENT and ALLOW switches:** it reuses one stale port lookup when processing both operations. See [GD10399](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10399-gfxcontrol-mishandles-simultaneous-prevent-and-allow-switches) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gfxcontrol-command-full-body-transition-and-options-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.


**GD10400 — Print returns success when a requested file cannot be opened as a datatype:** it emits a per-file error but leaves the command result successful. See [GD10400](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10400-print-returns-success-when-a-requested-file-cannot-be-opened-as-a-datatype) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#print-command-full-body-per-file-result-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.


**GD10401 — AROSMonDrvs skips all monitor drivers if icon.library fails to open:** its NULL-base priority fallback is unreachable because the caller gates the whole scan on a successful open. See [GD10401](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10401-arosmondrvs-skips-all-monitor-drivers-if-iconlibrary-fails-to-open) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#arosmondrvs-command-full-body-monitor-discovery-and-execution-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.

**GD10402 — AROSMonDrvs leaks DiskObjects with other icon types:** GetDiskObject results are freed only for WBTOOL/WBPROJECT icons. See [GD10402](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10402-arosmondrvs-leaks-diskobjects-with-other-icon-types) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#arosmondrvs-command-full-body-monitor-discovery-and-execution-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.

**GD10403 — AROSMonDrvs ignores failures to find or start the requested drivers:** Execute results are captured only in DEBUG code and never affect the command status. See [GD10403](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10403-arosmondrvs-ignores-failures-to-find-or-start-the-requested-drivers) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#arosmondrvs-command-full-body-monitor-discovery-and-execution-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.


**GD10404 — BindDrivers truncates wildcard product IDs before device matching:** a `PRODUCT=<manufacturer>` tooltype's `0xffff` wildcard narrows to product 255 at the `FindConfigDev()` call, so other products from that manufacturer are not matched. See [GD10404](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10404-binddrivers-truncates-wildcard-product-ids-before-device-matching) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#binddrivers-shell-command-full-body-tooltype-and-binding-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.

**GD10405 — BindDrivers leaks icon objects for drivers without a valid PRODUCT tooltype:** the `DiskObject` returned by `GetDiskObject()` is not released on missing/invalid tooltype or node-allocation failure paths. See [GD10405](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10405-binddrivers-leaks-icon-objects-for-drivers-without-a-valid-product-tooltype) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#binddrivers-shell-command-full-body-tooltype-and-binding-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.

**GD10406 — BindDrivers reports success after driver binding failures:** `LoadSeg()`/resident lookup failures break the product loop, but their status is discarded and the command returns `RETURN_OK`. See [GD10406](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10406-binddrivers-reports-success-after-driver-binding-failures) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#binddrivers-shell-command-full-body-tooltype-and-binding-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.


**GD10407 — Assign returns success when startup or argument parsing fails:** failed required-library opens and `ReadArgs()` failure leave its result at `RETURN_OK`; a successful RDArgs allocation is also leaked when parsing fails. See [GD10407](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10407-assign-returns-success-when-startup-or-argument-parsing-fails) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#assign-shell-command-full-body-initialization-and-output-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.

**GD10408 — Assign drops deferred list output on short/failed writes, failed flushes, or output-buffer allocation failure, while still returning success.** See [GD10408](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10408-assign-discards-short-or-failed-writes-while-printing-lists) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#assign-shell-command-full-body-initialization-and-output-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.


**GD10409 — Dir treats pattern-enumeration errors as successful completion:** nonzero `MatchNext()` results, including interruption and filesystem errors, exit the loop without changing the success result. See [GD10409](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10409-dir-treats-pattern-enumeration-errors-as-successful-completion) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#dir-shell-command-full-body-enumeration-and-allocation-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.

**GD10410 — Dir uses the pattern buffer without checking allocation success:** the result of `AllocMem()` is passed to `ParsePattern()` without checking for NULL. See [GD10410](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10410-dir-uses-the-pattern-buffer-without-checking-allocation-success) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#dir-shell-command-full-body-enumeration-and-allocation-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.


**GD10411 — Copy DIRECT DELETE ignores deletion failures:** its direct-delete loop discards every `KillFile()` result and returns success. See [GD10411](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10411-copy-direct-delete-ignores-deletion-failures) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#copy-shell-command-full-body-mode-and-error-path-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.

**GD10412 — Copy silently skips soft-link directories when its link buffer allocation fails:** recursive link traversal leaves the entry unprocessed and does not report failure. See [GD10412](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10412-copy-silently-skips-soft-link-directories-when-its-link-buffer-allocation-fails) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#copy-shell-command-full-body-mode-and-error-path-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.

**GD10413 — Copy can dereference a NULL device procedure while examining a soft link:** it uses `GetDeviceProc()`'s result without checking the allocation-failure return. See [GD10413](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10413-copy-can-dereference-a-null-device-procedure-while-examining-a-soft-link) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#copy-shell-command-full-body-mode-and-error-path-pass). Explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target; source-only.

**GD10414 — AmigaGuide navigator installs an empty clip region after rectangle allocation failure:** `InstallClipRegionSafe()` ignores `OrRectRegion()` failure and proceeds to install the empty region before drawing. See [GD10414](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10414-amigaguide-navigator-installs-an-empty-clip-region-after-rectangle-allocation-failure) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-library-clearregion-full-body-and-amigaguide-caller-pass). Optional AmigaGuide datatype caller; allocation-failure path is source-only.

**GD10415 — Compositor dereferences a missing alpha region after allocation failure:** it calls `OrRectRegion()` after `NewRegion()` can fail without checking the result. See [GD10415](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10415-compositor-dereferences-a-missing-alpha-region-after-allocation-failure) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-clearregion-compositor-visibility-caller-pass). Compositor monitor with alpha bitmaps; allocation-failure path is source-only.

**GD10416 — Compositor treats a failed display-region build as an empty display:** it ignores the initial `OrRectRegion()` failure, then removes all bitmap nodes from visibility and redraws the display void. See [GD10416](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10416-compositor-treats-a-failed-display-region-build-as-an-empty-display) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-clearregion-compositor-visibility-caller-pass). Compositor monitor full redraw under region allocation failure; source-only.

**GD10417 — Failed alpha-region expansion suppresses later alpha recomposition:** a failed union leaves the alpha tracking region incomplete, so incremental opaque bitmap updates can skip overlapping alpha redraws. See [GD10417](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10417-failed-alpha-region-expansion-suppresses-later-alpha-recomposition) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-clearregion-compositor-visibility-caller-pass). Compositor alpha regions under allocation failure; source-only.

**GD10418 — Compositor can paint the display background over a bitmap after region subtraction fails:** it ignores `ClearRegionRegion()` failure, then treats the still-unsubtracted bitmap area as display void and backfills over it. See [GD10418](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10418-compositor-can-paint-the-display-background-over-a-bitmap-after-region-subtraction-fails) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-clearregion-compositor-visibility-caller-pass). Compositor opaque bitmap redraw under region allocation failure; source-only.

**GD10419 — Compositor redraws an unclipped bitmap region when display intersection fails:** `AndRegionRegion()` failure leaves the full bitmap region in place, which is later passed to a CopyBox API requiring in-bounds coordinates. See [GD10419](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10419-compositor-redraws-an-unclipped-bitmap-region-when-display-intersection-fails) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-clearregion-compositor-visibility-caller-pass). Compositor partially off-display opaque bitmap under region allocation failure; backend consequence varies; source-only.

**GD10420 — Failed opaque-region subtraction lets lower Compositor bitmaps overwrite upper ones:** ignored `ClearRectRegion()` failure leaves overlapping pixels visible in lower layers, which draw later in the same top-to-bottom traversal. See [GD10420](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10420-failed-opaque-region-subtraction-lets-lower-compositor-bitmaps-overwrite-upper-ones) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-clearregion-compositor-visibility-caller-pass). Compositor overlapping opaque bitmaps under region allocation failure; source-only.

**GD10421 — NList demo image drawing loops can wrap at the signed coordinate limit:** signed `WORD` loop counters advance by two through inclusive coordinates; on wrapping targets, the optional custom-image renderer can fail to terminate at the coordinate limit. See [GD10421](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10421-nlist-demo-image-drawing-loops-can-wrap-at-the-signed-coordinate-limit) and the [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#nlist-demo-custom-image-renderer-full-body-and-caller-pass). Optional NList demo/custom image tag and extreme geometry; medium confidence, source-only.

**OD10421 — DRM EDID-to-SAD helper returns descriptors from only the first audio block:** it stops after the first CTA audio block, omitting any later SADs. See [OD10421](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10421-drm-edid-to-sad-helper-returns-descriptors-from-only-the-first-audio-block) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#vmware-nouveau-drm-edid-sad-extraction-pass). Optional VMware/Nouveau DRM cores; no in-tree caller found, so impact is limited to external/future clients; source-only.

**OD10422 — DiskImage Expat allocator can wrap the private-header size:** adding its `size_t` header to a near-maximum allocation request can wrap to a small `AllocPooled()` size while recording the original large request. Affects the default allocator in x86-aros and ppc-aros `expat.library` when the public `XML_MemMalloc()` API receives such a request; undersized-allocation consequence depends on the wrapped small allocation succeeding. See [OD10422](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10422-diskimage-expat-allocator-can-wrap-the-private-header-size) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-expat-pool-allocator-full-body-and-size-overflow-pass). Source-only.

**OD10423 — MountHDF divides by zero for zero geometry parameters:** `BLOCKSPERTRACK` or `SURFACES` can be supplied as zero, making the computed cylinder size zero before the DOS-node cylinder-count division. Affects the x86-aros and ppc-aros DiskImage `MountHDF` commands. See [OD10423](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10423-mounthdf-divides-by-zero-for-zero-geometry-parameters) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-tooltypes-and-mounthdf-geometry-parameter-pass). Source-only.

**OD10424 — MountHDF leaks its DOS node when a duplicate name is rejected:** `MakeDosNode()`'s allocation is not freed when `AddBootNode()` fails because `IHD<unit>` already exists. Repeated attempts retain one allocation each in x86-aros and ppc-aros DiskImage builds. See [OD10424](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10424-mounthdf-leaks-its-dos-node-when-a-duplicate-name-is-rejected) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-tooltypes-and-mounthdf-geometry-parameter-pass). Source-only.

**OD10425 — DiskImage AROS fallback truncates 64-bit file offsets:** the AROS DOS64 stub falls back to `Seek()` after narrowing a `QUAD` offset to `LONG`. Selected DMG parsing passes 64-bit plist/resource offsets through this path, so sections above `LONG_MAX` can be read from the wrong position or fail. Affects x86-aros and ppc-aros DiskImage builds; source-only. See [OD10425](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10425-diskimage-aros-fallback-truncates-64-bit-file-offsets) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-dos64-helper-and-dmg-offset-caller-pass).

**OD10426 — DiskImage image-name allocation failure is reported as success:** `DITAG_GetImageName` tests the output-slot address instead of the `ASPrintf()` result, so allocation failure leaves a NULL name without setting `ERROR_NO_FREE_STORE`. The optional Zune list then labels the still-mounted image “no disk” and uses empty-drive controls. Affects x86-aros and ppc-aros DiskImage builds; source-only. See [OD10426](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10426-diskimage-image-name-allocation-failure-is-reported-as-success) and the [DiskImage GetImageName caller recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-getimagename-error-result-and-gui-caller-reconciliation-2026-11-06).

**OD10427 — Reaction GUI dereferences a failed reload-hook allocation:** after `CreateExtHook()` can return NULL, startup checks the unrelated non-NULL disk-change hook and then dereferences the reload-hook pointer. Affects x86-aros and ppc-aros Reaction GUI builds with DiskImage library version 52.22 or newer under hook-allocation failure; source-only. See [OD10427](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10427-reaction-gui-dereferences-a-failed-reload-hook-allocation) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-extended-hook-allocation-and-reaction-caller-pass).

**OD10428 — DiskImage reply port signals reserved bit zero:** the custom no-signal port leaves `mp_SigBit` zero, then synchronous unit operations enable `PA_SIGNAL`; Exec sends and waits on reserved `SIGF_ABORT`, consuming or spuriously raising that signal. Affects x86-aros and ppc-aros DiskImage device/library builds; source-only. See [OD10428](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10428-diskimage-reply-port-signals-reserved-bit-zero) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-no-signal-port-reply-signal-bit-and-callers-pass).

**OD10429 — CUE CDDA byte swapping uses unaligned word accesses on PowerPC:** the Motorola-track path passes the caller's `scsi_Data` buffer to `swab2()`, which dereferences it as `ULONG *`/`UWORD *`. Affects ppc-aros CUE CDDA reads with unaligned buffers; source-only. See [OD10429](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10429-cue-cdda-byte-swapping-uses-unaligned-word-accesses-on-powerpc) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-swab2-alignment-and-cue-cdda-caller-pass).

**OD10430 — DiskImage extraction overwrites a predictable temporary-file collision:** DMS/XAD/XPK extraction writes `unit_<unit>.<ext>` with `MODE_NEWFILE` in the configured temp directory or `T:`; an existing same-named file is replaced, then normal cleanup deletes it. Affects x86-aros and ppc-aros DiskImage plugin builds; source-only. See [OD10430](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10430-diskimage-extraction-overwrites-a-predictable-temporary-file-collision) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-temporary-file-name-collision-and-extraction-callers).

**OD10431 — DiskImage reports successful abort for a request already in progress:** `LibAbortIO()` searches only the queued requests and defaults to success; once the unit worker dequeues a request, abort reports success without setting `IOERR_ABORTED`, while the operation continues to normal completion. Affects x86-aros and ppc-aros DiskImage device requests; source-only. See [OD10431](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10431-diskimage-reports-successful-abort-for-a-request-already-in-progress) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#diskimage-beginio-abortio-queue-and-completion-pass).

**OD9710 — USB HID report-descriptor debug dump reads past the final partial line:** `nDebugMem()` always evaluates 16 byte arguments, even when the final row contains fewer bytes, so a descriptor length not divisible by 16 causes reads beyond its exact-sized report buffer. The binding GUI and selected parser-error paths reach this diagnostic. Affects explicit builds selecting Poseidon's ROM USB HID class; source-only. See [OD9710](AROS-other-drivers.md#od9710) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-parser-error-dump-and-partial-source-pass).

**OD10433 — USB HID report parser reads truncated item payloads past the descriptor:** short-item payloads and long-item headers/payloads are read without checking the remaining report-descriptor length. Affects builds selecting Poseidon's ROM USB HID class when a descriptor ends partway through an item; source-only. See [OD10433](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10433-usb-hid-report-parser-reads-truncated-item-payloads-past-the-descriptor) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-hid-report-parser-item-boundary-pass).
**OD10434 — CDFS closes the I/O-request pointer slot instead of its request:** normal device teardown passes the address of `bp_IOStdReq` to `CloseDevice()` and leaves the successful request/port allocations unreleased. Affects optional CDFS builds; source-only. See [OD10434](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10434-cdfs-buffer-cache-deletion-closes-the-pointer-slot-instead-of-its-io-request).

**OD10435 — ISO9660 volume dates use the wrong ASCII digit base:** decimal conversion subtracts `'9'` instead of `'0'`, so mounted volume dates do not reflect the descriptor. Affects optional CDFS builds mounting ISO9660 media; source-only. See [OD10435](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10435-iso9660-ascii-date-conversion-subtracts-the-wrong-digit-base).

**OD10436 — Rock Ridge NM names and AS comments are mishandled:** fitting fields are skipped, and a long ISO identifier can make the NM copy size negative before conversion to unsigned `IPTR`. Affects optional CDFS builds on media with those extensions; source-only. See [OD10436](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10436-rock-ridge-nm-names-and-as-comments-are-skipped-unless-they-exceed-remaining-capacity).

**OD10437 — ISO9660 locate leaks a lock record on a non-directory intermediate component:** one failed multi-component path shape returns without freeing the allocated lock. Affects optional CDFS builds; source-only. See [OD10437](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10437-iso-path-traversal-leaks-a-lock-record-for-a-non-directory-intermediate-component).

**OD10438 — ISO9660 unmount leaks path-table storage:** normal unmount frees the volume structure but omits its separately allocated table bytes and entry array. Affects optional CDFS builds on media with a path table; source-only. See [OD10438](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10438-iso9660-unmount-leaks-separately-allocated-path-table-storage).

**OD10439 — ISO9660 directory lookup applies its offset twice:** after selecting the cache block for a directory offset, the code indexes that block using the full directory offset. Affects optional CDFS builds on media with directories spanning multiple blocks; source-only. See [OD10439](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10439-iso9660-directory-lookup-applies-the-full-directory-offset-twice).

**OD10440 — ISO9660 path-table lengths and parent indexes are unchecked:** incomplete entries can be retained and invalid parent indexes later address beyond the table. Affects optional CDFS builds using ISO path tables; source-only. See [OD10440](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10440-iso9660-path-table-entry-lengths-and-parent-indexes-are-not-validated).

**OD10441 — ISO9660 directory and Rock Ridge record lengths are not bounded:** declared record and extension sizes are consumed before being checked against their enclosing record and block.
