See [OD10498](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10498). Source-only; no session or credential call was run.

**OD10499 — Security-backed `getcredentials()` substitutes effective IDs for remote real IDs:** querying another task with distinct real/effective credentials reports the effective IDs in both fields. See [OD10499](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10499). Source-only; no credential query was run.

**OD10500 — Security-backed group lookup hides allocation failure as an empty member list:** failed user-info allocation skips member collection while returning a successful group. See [OD10500](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10500). Source-only; no allocation failure was induced.


**OD10501 — Security-backed `getcredentials()` rejects a valid task owned by nobody:** the security API returns NULL for a valid nobody-owned task, and UserGroup maps that to EINVAL. A quiet logout supplies the in-tree trigger. See [OD10501](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10501). Source-only; no logout or credentials call was run.


**OD10502 — `getgroups()` rejects a valid nobody-owned current task:** after `Logout QUIET`, security-backed enumeration returns -1/ENOENT before checking the requested count; the precise expected group count is unresolved. See [OD10502](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10502). Source-only; no logout or group query was run.

**OD10504 — AHIRecord ignores FLAC output-file close errors:** `SaveSlave()` discards `fclose(BufferedFile)` after FLAC finalization; a DOS handler `ACTION_END` error is ignored; a RAMFS write-protect request between successful FLAC finish and close supplies a conditional in-tree path. The write-protect interleaving is narrow and conditional; this is separate from OD9773's finish-time encoder callback failures. See [OD10504](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10504) and the [FLAC output close review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ahirecord-flac-output-close-result-pass-od10504). Source-only; no file or close failure was induced.

**OD3036 — RTL8139 and Etherlink III receive paths can traverse freed list nodes on ExecSMP:** RTL8139 RX can overlap opener Close or final multicast-range removal; Etherlink III RX can overlap opener Close. The lists use CPU-local `Disable()` for mutation without a shared SMP lock in the readers. Cross-CPU placement and timing are required. See [OD3036](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3036) and the [RTL8139 multicast-list recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#rtl8139-multicast-range-list-concurrency-pass). Source-only; no device or race was run.

**GD10453 — X11 framebuffer disposal can free an object still referenced by the event task:** if the temporary reply-port allocation fails, disposal skips `NOTY_WINDISPOSE` but the OOP object is still freed. The event task retains its `bmobj` pointer and may dereference it for a later Expose; X11 resources also leak. Applies to hosted X11 under that allocation failure. See [GD10453](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10453) and the [X11 disposal failure-path review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#x11-framebuffer-dispose-reply-port-failure-gd10453). Source-only; no allocation failure or event was induced.

**EK10291 — Unmapped m68k guest A-line instructions can loop forever:** the optional m68kemu bridge redirects unknown vector-10 exceptions to RTE without changing the saved opcode PC, so RTE resumes at the same A-line. See [EK10291](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10291) and the [Moira A-line exception recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#moira-a-line-bridge-exception-recheck-ek10291). High confidence; no guest or emulator was run.

**OD2840 recheck — NVMe sparse-NSID enumeration is retained as a conditional startup-scalability concern, not a protocol violation.** The NVMe Base Specification permits both per-NSID probing and the active-NSID-list command. Practical reachability remains conditional because the selected controller path fails bus construction under OD2876 and no maintained direct NVMe `AddBus` caller was found. See [OD2840](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2840) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only; no controller was run.


GD5421 security.library removal-entrypoint recheck (2026-10-31): the selected root-only `secKill()` calls `RemTask(task)` for non-process targets, establishing an in-tree API entry point to the existing WaitTOF stale-stack-node path. No `secKill()` client or caller targeting a blocked WaitTOF task was found, so the trigger remains public-API conditional. The finding and queue code are unchanged; no path/LOC credit. See [GD5421](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd5421) and the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

WaitTOF fixed-signal early-wakeup candidate check (GD5421 rechecked; no new GD or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-01): `WaitTOF()` clears and waits on `SIGF_SINGLE` while its waiter node is queued (`rom/graphics/waittof.c:51-63`; `SIGF_SINGLE` is bit 4, `compiler/include/exec/tasks.h:141-149`), so another producer of that bit for the same task could return it before VBlank. Checked all direct maintained `WaitTOF()` callers: Blanker waits on separately allocated `actionmask`/`cxmask` and then checks those masks; popupmenu and 2View wait on their own message-port bits; Jed, the graphics test and m68k bootstrap show no concurrent same-bit producer in their local bodies (`workbench/tools/commodities/Blanker.c:241,336-343,479,583`; `workbench/libs/popupmenu/pm.c:463,603-617,750-762`; `developer/demos/2View/2View.c:636,675`; `workbench/tools/Edit/Jed.c:266`; `developer/debug/test/graphics/truecolorpens.c:190`; `arch/m68k-amiga/c/AROSBootstrap.c:1257-1258`). No selected in-tree WaitTOF caller establishes this early-wakeup path, and the fixed reserved single-signal convention does not provide a local isolation guarantee for an external caller. Kept it as an external/API contract question rather than splitting GD5421. No signal, VBlank or GUI operation was run; source-only.


**OD3248 — USB Audio can report a successful binding after AHI rejects a mode registration:** `nAddAudioModes()` ignores `AHI_AddAudioMode()` failure, while `nAllocAudio()` still publishes the class as ready, leaving one or more formats absent from AHI. Conditional on AHI failing to acquire its database or allocate a copied mode node. See [OD3248](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3248) and the [Other Drivers coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md). Source-only; no database failure or device was exercised.


**OD3887 — USB mass-storage change-interrupt removal can race notification and leave a stale soft-interrupt pointer:** the change-interrupt list is modified under processor-local `Forbid()` while the worker traverses raw request links and queues callbacks with `Cause()`; `DoIO(TD_REMCHANGEINT)` does not drain either lifetime, and callers such as FAT, NTFS and PFS3 release storage after removal completes. Conditional on the ExecSMP overlap. See [OD3887](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3887).

**OD3330 — Workbench USB MassStorage change-interrupt removal can race the unit-task traversal:** `usbmss.device` handles add/remove directly in `BeginIO` under local-only `Forbid()`, while the unit task traverses the same list; FAT can return from `DoIO(TD_REMCHANGEINT)` and free its request before that traversal finishes. Scoped to selected AArch64 Raspberry Pi ExecSMP builds. See [OD3330](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3330).




**GD10454 — Volumelist reads past non-terminated BCPL DOS-list names:** on m68k, `AROS_BSTR_ADDR()` returns the payload of a length-prefixed BSTR, but Volumelist passes it to `strncpy()` without using the stored length. A short valid BSTR without a C terminator can be read past its allocation. Current in-tree trigger reachability is unconfirmed. See [GD10454](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10454).

**EK9463 — `AllocMem()` can dereference a freed Diskfont low-memory handler on ExecSMP:** `AllocMem()` snapshots the priority-1 Diskfont handler before taking `LowMemSem`; a concurrent failed-allocation reclaim can reach LDDemon, expunge an unopened Diskfont library, and free that embedded handler before the snapshotting CPU acquires the lock. Conditional on list order, allocation failure, and cross-CPU timing. See [EK9463](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9463) and the [LDDemon caller-path strengthening](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ek9463-lddemon-caller-path-strengthening). Source-only; no allocation failure or interleaving was run.

**OD3136 — Poseidon can parse BOS bytes beyond a successful short transfer:** `pFetchBosCaps()` parses the requested length rather than the controller's actual byte count, so an uninitialized buffer tail can be treated as capability data. The only checked-in callers enumerate controller root hubs; the PCI xHCI root-hub handler stalls BOS requests, so no in-tree successful-short-BOS trigger is confirmed. Retain as an external/custom HCD or exported-vector candidate. See [OD3136](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3136) and the [root-hub reachability correction](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#od3136-root-hub-reachability-correction). Source-only; no transfer was run.


**GD10455 — HostGL dereferences a null X11 display after connection failure:** its initialization stores `XOpenDisplay(NULL)`'s result and reports success even when it is NULL; a later `glACreateContext()` passes it to `DefaultScreen()`. Conditional on the optional hosted HostGL library being used while no X11 connection is available. No in-tree client was established. See [GD10455](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10455) and the [HostGL display-init caller recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hostgl-display-initialization-failure-pass-gd10455). Source-only; no display or context was used.


**GD10456 — HostGL dereferences a null context in allocation-failure cleanup:** `glACreateContext()` jumps to cleanup when its initial context allocation fails, but cleanup reads fields through `ctx` before checking it. It faults instead of returning the documented NULL failure result. Conditional on allocation failure in the optional hosted HostGL library; no in-tree client was established. See [GD10456](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10456) and the [HostGL context-allocation cleanup pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hostgl-context-allocation-failure-cleanup-pass-gd10456). Source-only; no allocation failure or context was induced.


**GD10458 — HostGL debug builds dereference NULL while detaching a context:** `glAMakeCurrent(NULL)` is used by the checked-in EGL backend, but its debug log reads `ctx->glXctx` before the NULL-aware detach branch. This faults only when HostGL debug logging is enabled. See [GD10458](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10458) and the [HostGL make-current review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hostgl-make-current-and-destruction-pass-gd10458). Source-only; no build or context was run.


**GD10457 — HostGL can return a context after its pbuffer buffers fail to allocate:** the pbuffer renderer ignores pixel/line-buffer allocation results, and context creation only checks the GLX context. A later swap passes those pointers to GL and copy/draw operations; resize repeats the unchecked allocation after freeing old storage. Conditional on the optional hosted HostGL pbuffer path and an allocation failure. No in-tree client was established. See [GD10457](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10457) and the [HostGL buffer-allocation and swap pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hostgl-buffer-allocation-and-swap-pass-gd10457). Source-only; no allocation failure or rendering call was run.

**GD10459 — Sound datatype indexes four-entry sample-format tables with unchecked public `SDTA_SampleType`:** values outside 0–3 are stored and used as array indices in AHI playback and sample-size calculations. Trigger is conditional on an invalid public attribute and reaching those paths; no checked-in invalid-value caller was found. See [GD10459](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10459) and the [sample-format review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sound-datatype-sample-format-bound-pass-gd10459). Source-only; no playback or malformed attribute was run.


**GD10460 — Sound datatype uses an unchecked signal-bit number as a shift count:** `SDTA_SignalBitNumber` is stored without range validation and later shifted for the mask getter and playback notifications. Values outside 0–31 either shift out of range on 32-bit targets or truncate to an empty `ULONG` mask on 64-bit targets; bit 31 itself also uses a signed shift on 32-bit targets. Trigger is conditional on an invalid public attribute; the checked-in `Play` caller uses a valid signal bit. See [GD10460](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10460) and the [signal-bit range review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sound-datatype-signal-bit-range-pass-gd10460). Source-only; no object or signal was exercised.


**GD10461 — Sound datatype’s waveform scaling guard overflows on long samples:** `DrawWaveform()` shifts a signed 32-bit sample length left by eight. Above 8,388,607 frames this overflows and can make the renderer return without drawing; the checked-in 8SVX reader can supply a valid sample above that limit when allocation succeeds. This is separate from GD6199’s underflow for small draw rectangles. See [GD10461](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10461) and the [long-sample waveform pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sound-datatype-long-sample-waveform-pass-gd10461). Source-only; no sample was drawn.


**GD6264 — Sound datatype divides by zero for an unchecked zero sample rate or period:** a zero-rate 8SVX VHDR reaches division during construction; public Sound clients can also supply a zero period/frequency and reach conversion/getter divisions. See [GD6264](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd6264) and the [zero-frequency pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sound-datatype-zero-frequency-pass-gd10462). Source-only; no malformed file or conversion was run.

**EK10293 — m68k dispatch fast path skips AMMX restore when a detected 68080 has no FPU flag:** affects AC68080 cores before GOLD2.7, whose FPU was not yet available; ordinary task dispatch bypasses the AMMX restore gate. See [EK10293](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10293) and the [m68k context coverage trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1498). Source-only; hardware behavior was not tested.


**EK9485 — EfikaMX startup copies an unchecked ATAG command line into a 200-byte buffer:** the bootstrap forwards the full `ATAG_CMDLINE`; an argument of 200 bytes or more overruns `CmdLine[200]` before startup parks in its separate loop. Limited to explicit EfikaMX targets; the checked-in boot script uses only `use-tlsf`, and the aggregate target edges are commented. See [EK9485](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9485) and the [Efika command-line caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6692). Source-only; no boot or firmware input was used.


**EK9486 — EfikaMX bootstrap copies an ATAG command line through a failed allocation:** a single 524,288-byte command line rounds to a 524,304-byte request against the 512 KiB bump arena, returns `NULL`, then reaches unchecked `strcpy()`. Larger arguments or prior arena use can fail earlier. Explicit EfikaMX bootstrap only; the checked-in argument is short and aggregate target edges are commented. See [EK9486](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9486) and the [Efika bootstrap caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6702). Source-only; no boot was run.


**EK9487 — the console paste path passes an unchecked work-buffer allocation to ConClip:** if the 16 KiB allocation fails and ConClip has nonempty clipboard text, its copy/read path uses the null buffer before replying. The console handler may then remain blocked waiting for that reply. Conditional on ConClip running, allocation failure, and nonempty clipboard content. See [EK9487](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9487) and the [ConClip caller recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L2457). Source-only; no allocation failure or paste was induced.


**EK9488 — VMM startup can wait forever when its manager cannot allocate the startup reply:** the manager signals the starter port but queues no message, then exits; both the library and selected preferences client use `WaitPort()`, which keeps waiting while the port is empty. Conditional on startup-message allocation failure. See [EK9488](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9488) and the [VMM reply-allocation trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6742). Source-only; no allocation failure or startup was induced.


**EK9489 — Shell's optional memory diagnostic can print a huge false leak count:** with `__debug_mem` enabled, it subtracts unsigned `AvailMem()` samples and prints the result as leaked bytes; an increase in free memory wraps the subtraction. This affects only the diagnostic and can also reflect unrelated task activity. See [EK9489](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9489) and the [AvailMem caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6746). Source-only; no command or memory change was run.


**EK9490 — Exec `allocmem` diagnostic can report success after allocation checks fail:** the final pooled-test result overwrites prior errors, and failed `CreatePool()` calls do not set an error result. An initial allocation failure also feeds a NULL-derived address to `AllocAbs()`. This affects the developer test only. See [EK9490](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9490) and the [allocation-test review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6748). Source-only; no allocation test was run.


**EK9491 — `runtests` reports a wrapped memory increase as a huge loss:** its unsigned `AvailMem()` samples are subtracted whenever they differ; an increase wraps, and a decrease cannot be attributed to the command from global samples alone. Diagnostic-only. See [EK9491](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9491) and the [test-harness memory sample](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6748). Source-only; no test script was run.


**EK9492 — Installer can misreport large memory totals to scripts:** its `GRAPHICS_MEM` and `TOTAL_MEM` database values are stored in signed `long`; on 32-bit targets values above `LONG_MAX` are not representable and can be formatted incorrectly. See [EK9492](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9492) and the [Installer `AvailMem()` trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6752). Conditional on a script query and more than 2 GiB in the requested memory class. Source-only; no Installer script or high-memory system was run.


**EK9494 — PC APIC TSC calibration can spin after the startup PIT stops:** startup configures PIT channel 0 in one-shot terminal-count mode, while the fallback calibration requests ten 10 ms waits. Once the roughly 55 ms counter reaches zero, `pit_wait()` can observe zero elapsed ticks forever. Conditional on taking the PIT-based calibration fallback. See [EK9494](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9494) and the [PC timer calibration trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1234). Source-only; no PIT or APIC behavior was run.


**EK9495 — UserGroup timezone fallback writes past its buffer on a full read:** if locale data is unavailable and `ENV:TZ` returns ten bytes, the code writes the terminator at `zone[10]` for a ten-byte array. Conditional on the fallback path during UserGroup initialization. See [EK9495](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9495) and the [UserGroup timezone trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6794). Source-only; no environment file or library initialization was used.


**EK9496 — PC Multiboot2 boot stalls on a zero-sized tag:** the early console scan advances by rounded tag size without rejecting zero; a zero-sized non-END tag makes the pointer stop advancing before main parsing. Conditional on malformed boot metadata. See [EK9496](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9496) and the [Multiboot2 console parser trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1159). Source-only; no boot record was parsed.


**EK9497 — PC dead-end alerts can emit an enormous border on a one-column text framebuffer:** the renderer computes `scr_Width - 2` as an unsigned count; width 1 underflows and makes the character loop run excessively. The selected Multiboot path accepts the reported width without a minimum check. See [EK9497](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9497) and the [alert-width caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L7074). Source-only; no framebuffer or alert was exercised.


**EK9498 — Android bootstrap passes a function pointer to `%p` in debug logging:** the selected `D(x)` call passes `EntryPoint` (a function pointer) through a variadic logger to Android's `%p` formatter, which expects `void *`. The exit-status `%08X` site was rechecked and dropped because the value fits the corresponding unsigned type. Diagnostic-only; practical output impact is ABI-dependent. See [EK9498](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9498) and the [Android logger caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6909). Source-only; no Android process or logger was run.


**EK9500 — `FindNamedObject(NULL)` returns list nodes and sentinels as objects:** its NULL-name branch returns the embedded list node without converting it to a `NamedObject` or acquiring a reference; empty/end enumeration returns the tail sentinel instead of NULL. Releasing or reusing these values can access the wrong object state, and concurrent removal can invalidate the node. No in-tree NULL-name C caller was found; public/external API use is affected. See [EK9500](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9500) and the [Utility enumeration recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L9016). Source-only; no enumeration or removal race was run.


**EK9501 — `CheckDate()` accepts February 29 in non-leap years:** it validates only that February's day is at most 29; `Date2Amiga()` then maps the invalid date to the same day count as March 1. The selected PTP class uses that result to form a `DateStamp`. See [EK9501](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9501) and the [CheckDate/PTP caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6993). Source-only; no PTP device or date was exercised.


**EK9502 — concurrent `AddNamedObject()` calls can corrupt namespace lists:** membership is checked before taking only the destination namespace lock, then the same intrusive node can be enqueued under separate locks. Concurrent cross-namespace adds can overwrite its links; duplicate-enabled same-namespace adds also lack a locked recheck. The sole in-tree caller adds a fresh object to the global no-duplicates namespace, so impact is conditional on external/concurrent API use. See [EK9502](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9502) and the [AddNamedObject membership trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6996). Source-only; no interleaving was run.


**EK9503 — 32-bit `AllocateTagItems()` can under-allocate for extreme counts:** `numTags * sizeof(struct TagItem)` wraps before `AllocVec()` when the count exceeds the 32-bit multiplication limit; callers can then use a smaller allocation as the requested array. No in-tree caller near the threshold was established. See [EK9503](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9503) and the [tag-allocation review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6999). Source-only; no allocation was attempted.


**EK9504 — ExecSMP `GetUniqueID()` can return duplicates:** it increments a shared counter under `Disable()`, but Exec documents that `Disable()` is CPU-local on ExecSMP and shared state needs a spinlock. Concurrent calls on different CPUs can return the same ID. No in-tree caller was established. See [EK9504](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9504) and the [Utility ID serialization review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L7005). Source-only; no concurrent calls were run.


**EK9505 — ExecSMP `RemNamedObject()` can lose a deferred reply:** two CPUs can pass the empty `no_FreeMessage` check under CPU-local `Forbid()` and overwrite the shared message slot; one waiting caller may never receive its reply. In-tree callers pass NULL, so the trigger is external concurrent API use. See [EK9505](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9505) and the [deferred-removal caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L7210). Source-only; no message interleaving was run.

**EK9506 — ExecSMP named-object removal can race with a new lookup:** the remover checks for zero users before taking the namespace lock and unlinks without rechecking, while a concurrent finder can increment the still-linked object's count under that lock. The owner may then free an object with a new outstanding reference. See [EK9506](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9506) and the [lookup/removal interleaving trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L7272). Source-only; no namespace interleaving was run.


**EK9481 — `AddBootNode()` can allocate an undersized name buffer for long BSTRs:** in the post-DOS handler-start path, a signed `BYTE` truncates names above 127 bytes. A 255-byte name becomes `len == -1`, yields a one-byte allocation, then passes the negative length to unsigned `CopyMem()`; the DOS entry was already published. Conditional on `ADNF_STARTPROC` and a long name. See [EK9481](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9481) and the [BSTR narrowing trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6709). Source-only; no long BSTR or copy was used.


**EK9480 — m68k Amiga `debugmmu` can leave VBR on an invalid page:** if the aligned vector-page allocation fails, setup still invalidates address zero and enables the MMU without moving VBR. A later exception cannot reliably fetch its vector. Conditional on `debugmmu` and allocation failure; `pmmu` is a separate path. See [EK9480](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9480) and the [VBR allocation trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6620). Source-only; no boot or allocation failure was induced.


**EK9482 — ARM/AArch64 ExecSMP `Signal()` can keep a task pointer across an unpinned IPI-pool wait:** the affinity path reads task state before locking, then claims an IPI entry before locking/rechecking; `RemTask()` can reclaim the standard task allocation during that gap, and its sweep cannot see a claimed but uncommitted entry. `NewCreateTaskA()` puts the task descriptor in `tc_MemEntry`, and `RemTask()` frees that list after the cancellation sweep. If removal completes while the sender is stalled after claiming an IPI entry, it resumes to a stale task pointer. Conditional on cross-CPU signal/removal overlap. See [EK9482](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9482) and the [call-IPI lifetime trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6657). Source-only; no interleaving was run.


**EK9483 — POSIXC `flockfile()` and `funlockfile()` are no-ops:** individual stdio calls lock only for the duration of each operation, so clients cannot hold the stream across a multi-operation sequence as the API promises. No maintained direct caller was found; impact is conditional on external concurrent stream use. See [EK9483](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9483) and the [POSIXC stream-lock review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L6679). Source-only; no stream or task interleaving was run.


**EK9052 — ARM32/AArch64 `SuperState()` returns a restore token for already privileged callers:** ARM32 changes such callers to User mode on paired `UserState()`; AArch64 forces EL1t task mode from EL1h. Both violate the documented NULL-token convention. The trigger is conditional public-API use from privileged mode; no checked-in caller was established. See [EK9052](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9052) and the [Exec/Kernel coverage ledger](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md). Source-only; no privilege transition was run.
**EK9064 — `TaskTag_CPUAffinity` can leave stale bits in a reused output mask:** the query adds each allowed CPU bit but never clears caller storage; all selected CPU-mask helpers are additive. The in-tree test clears its buffer, so the trigger is a client reusing a nonzero buffer. See [EK9064](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9064) and the [caller/output-buffer contract pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L34). Source-only; no query was run.


**EK9066 — MinGW processor initialization leaks allocated HostLib error strings:** both DLL-open and symbol-lookup failures omit `HostLib_FreeErrorStr()`; the Windows backend allocates the message with `FormatMessage` and releases it with `LocalFree`. Conditional on either loader failure in the MinGW processor module. See [EK9066](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9066) and the [MinGW HostLib ownership trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4055). Source-only; no Windows host or loader failure was run.


**EK9067 — generic MMU absolute allocations leave free-byte accounting too high:** `mm_AllocAbs()` marks pages allocated but does not reduce `mh_Free`, while `KMS_Free` reports that field and `mm_Free()` adds freed bytes. This can misreport free memory and mislead later prechecks; the page map still guards actual allocation. Conditional on initialized generic `USE_MMU` use. See [EK9067](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9067) and the [linear allocator trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L3984). Source-only; no allocation or statistics query was run.


**EK9068 — the shared RISC-V FDT reader does not bound header blocks or token payloads:** `FDT_Open()` trusts magic-valid offsets and sizes, while node/property traversal scans token and string data without checking those extents. Malformed firmware DTBs can disrupt boot or hardware discovery. Limited to selected OpenSBI consumers; the optional DWMAC target is not in the default network aggregate. See [EK9068](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9068) and the [shared FDT caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L3991). Source-only; no malformed DTB or boot was used.


**EK9069 — x86-64 EFI can interpret an EFI32 system table with 64-bit offsets:** if Multiboot2 supplies EFI32 without EFI64, the bootstrap publishes the 32-bit pointer unchanged and the native EFI resource reads fields using the 64-bit layout. Runtime and configuration-table pointers are then at different offsets. See [EK9069](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9069) and the [EFI32 handoff trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4009). Source-only; no firmware handoff or boot was tested.


**EK9071 — Exec semaphore's signed 16-bit counters can wrap:** 65,536 successful same-owner obtains or attempts turn the queue count back into the free sentinel while the lock is still held, admitting another owner; 32,769 queued bids can make `ReleaseSemaphore()` skip its waiter queue and leave requests unanswered. Requires extreme acquisition/waiter counts. See [EK9071](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9071) and the [obtain/attempt paths and exact counter thresholds](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#ek9071-attemptsemaphore-counter-recheck). Source-only; no semaphore operation was run.


**EK9070 — OpenSBI advertises failed CPU nodes in the processor inventory:** both the early kernel count and the selected processor-resource enumeration omit a `status = "fail"` filter. The claim is limited to public inventory; it does not establish a runnable or schedulable hart. Conditional on external firmware containing such a node. See [EK9070](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9070) and the [FDT CPU inventory recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L28). Source-only; no boot or CPU query was run.


**EK9072 — Workbench Logger can drop a new log broadcast after dequeuing a timer reply:** Logger calls `GetMsg()` on the timer reply, then `WaitIO()` on the already dequeued request. If that timer was the only queued message and a broadcast arrives before `WaitIO()`'s second `Remove()`, stale links can detach the new message. See [EK9072](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9072) and the [Logger/GetMsg/WaitIO trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L2017). Source-only; no timer or listener interleaving was run.


**EK9073 — TLSF can zero its control block beyond a small managed region:** the size check omits the `MemHeaderExt` prefix even though TLSF is placed after that prefix in the same chunk. A region just above the accepted threshold can pass and the control-block clear can cross its end. Conditional on a selected TLSF startup receiving such a range. See [EK9073](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9073) and the [TLSF threshold trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4076). Source-only; no boot or memory map was run.


**EK9074 — Efika ignores idle-task creation failure and keeps its allocation:** after allocating the task, stack, and MemList, `Kernel_Init()` ignores `NewAddTask()`'s NULL result and stores the task pointer anyway. ETask/context setup failure leaves the caller allocations unreclaimed and publishes an unregistered idle-task pointer used by idle-time accounting. See [EK9074](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9074) and the [Efika idle-task failure trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L3734). Source-only; no allocation failure or boot was run.


**EK9075 — POSIX `flock()` can use a freed named semaphore:** a concurrent final `LOCK_UN` can free it after another task's `FindSemaphore()` returns but before that task obtains it. ExecSMP permits remote overlap; on UP, a pending reschedule at `Permit()` can expose the same gap. See [EK9075](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9075) and the [lookup/removal lifetime pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4088). Source-only; no `flock()` call or interleaving was run.


**EK9076 — Optional VMM can assign the pre-pager priority 127:** with a partition paging task at priority -127, subtracting two requests -129; on AROS GCC targets where signed-byte narrowing wraps, `SetTaskPri()` stores 127. This reverses the intended worker/device priority ordering. Active Workbench:System edges select the VMM app and handler; VMM startup has separate limitations. See [EK9076](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9076) and the [priority caller trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4113). Source-only; no priority change or paging operation was run.


**EK9077 — A 2–4 GiB allocation can hang the standard allocator:** on selected 64-bit standard-allocator paths, the request narrows to a negative `LONG`; arithmetic right shift reaches -1 and the index loop never terminates. On ExecSMP it holds allocator locks while spinning. Requires `notlsf` (for the checked x86-64 PC path), a MemHeader reporting enough total free bytes and a caller requesting that size. See [EK9077](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9077) and the [allocator size-index trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4115). Source-only; no large allocation was attempted.


**EK9078 — DOS `RunHandler()` can dereference a failed process creation:** after `CreateNewProcTags()` returns NULL, successful reply-port and packet allocations lead to `PutMsg()` through `process->pr_MsgPort` before callers can report the startup failure. See [EK9078](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9078) and the [RunHandler failure-path review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4121). Source-only; no handler or allocation failure was run.

**EK9079 — DOS can strand a started handler process before its startup packet:** if reply-port or packet allocation fails after process creation, `RunHandler()` returns without stopping the child. Selected RAM, FAT, and AUX handlers wait indefinitely for that packet, retaining process resources. See [EK9079](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9079) and the [post-spawn failure review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4123). Source-only; no allocation failure or handler was run.


**EK9081 — TLSF can under-report free memory to Exec's allocator prefilter:** TLSF frees and in-place shrinks increase its private free count without updating `mh_Free`; Exec may skip the header before calling TLSF, even when a request fits the largest free block. `AvailMem()` can report the larger TLSF count meanwhile. Conditional on a stale snapshot and no alternate matching header. See [EK9081](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9081) and the [TLSF free-count/prefilter recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4119). Source-only; no allocation was run.


**EK9082 — Native AArch64 `CacheClearE()` truncates lengths above 4 GiB:** the public vector takes pointer-sized `IPTR`, but the selected AArch64 wrapper forwards `ULONG`; a 4 GiB range becomes zero and larger ranges are reduced modulo 4 GiB, so only a prefix may be maintained. No selected in-tree range above 4 GiB was found. See [EK9082](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9082) and the [AArch64 wrapper/SVC width trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1029). Source-only; no cache operation was run.

**EK9083 — PC SMP CPU load can be misreported after an extended sample interval:** the idle counter is subtracted from a fixed one-second baseline while the divisor covers the full elapsed interval; above-baseline sleep time underflows and can produce nonsensical load, which feeds the frequency governor and CPU-load attribute. See [EK9083](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9083) and the [heartbeat/ACPI counter trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1198). Source-only; no timer or frequency transition was run.

**EK9084 — PC SMP task CPU-usage conversion overflows on long samples:** the x86-64 path accumulates 64-bit TSC ticks, then shifts the sample left by 32 in the same 64-bit type before division; above `UINT32_MAX` ticks the Q32 numerator wraps, corrupting `TaskTag_CPUUsage`. Trigger requires a long heartbeat interval and a task with more than about 2.15 seconds of runtime at 2 GHz in that sample. See [EK9084](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9084) and the [heartbeat and task-switch counter trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1198). Source-only; no scheduling interval was induced.

**EK9085 — ARM/AArch64 SMP CPU-load sampling loses full 32-bit timer periods:** the getter narrows a 64-bit microsecond clock and idle counter to 32 bits; after a gap of about 71.6 minutes, elapsed periods are lost, and an exact-wrap gap reports 0% load. See [EK9085](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9085) and the [ARM/AArch64 load-reader and timer trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1048). Source-only; no long sampling gap was induced.

**EK9086 — OpenSBI's RISC-V ACPI fallback reads recognized MADT entries beyond the declared table end:** a final RINTC or PLIC record may pass the structure-size check without fitting inside `header.length`; its fields are then read and may feed PLIC initialization when device-tree PLIC data is absent. See [EK9086](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9086) and the [MADT bounds/startup trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8410). Source-only; no malformed firmware or boot was used.

**EK9087 — OpenSBI reads the RSDP XSDT pointer without checking its declared length:** a malformed revision-2+ RSDP can end before `xsdt_address`, yet both live lookup and ACPI diagnostics read that field and may use adjacent bytes as the root address. See [EK9087](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9087) and the [RSDP/root lookup trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4158). Source-only; no malformed firmware or boot was used.

**EK9088 — OpenSBI does not bound ACPI root/child table reads to retained EFI regions:** it trusts RSDT/XSDT addresses and table lengths before dereferencing root entries and child headers/spans; malformed firmware can trigger unmapped reads or feed unrelated data into PLIC setup. See [EK9088](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9088) and the [EFI-region mapping and ACPI traversal trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4160). Distinct from EK9086's MADT-internal entry bounds and EK9087's RSDP field extent. Source-only; no malformed firmware or boot was used.

**EK9090 — Sashimi `RECOVER` can read beyond a memory region while matching a stale cookie:** its scan checks a cookie at the final in-range word, then conditionally reads backlink/time words past `mh_Upper` before the loop tests the exclusive end. Requires matching stale marker data at the boundary; confidence is low for occurrence. See [EK9090](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9090) and the [RECOVER scan and MemHeader bound trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L676). Source-only; no recovery scan was run.

**EK9091 — `BUFFERSIZE=-1` can underallocate Sashimi's FIFO on 32-bit builds:** `/N` accepts `-1`, which is cast to `ULONG`; the allocation length wraps to near the resource-structure size while `sr_FIFOTotalSize` remains `0xffffffff`, so later captured output can write beyond the buffer. Requires allocation success and subsequent output. See [EK9091](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9091) and the [ReadArgs/allocation/FIFO trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4795). Source-only; no invalid input or output was run.

**EK9092 — Unix `KrnMayGetChar()` can wait on a blocking stderr descriptor:** the implementation calls `read()` directly; only `KrnObtainInput()` sets `O_NONBLOCK`. Built-in SAD performs that setup, but public raw/debug polling wrappers do not. See [EK9092](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9092) and the [Unix input contract/setup trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1323). Source-only; no host read was run.

**EK9093 — `GetPlayerAttrsA()` overcounts unsupported tags:** it increments the documented success count even when no switch case stores the requested value, so callers may trust untouched output. Its only selected direct caller requests supported `PLAYER_Ready`; practical impact remains conditional on external/future use. See [EK9093](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9093) and the [getter/caller check](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L155). Source-only; no player query was run.

**EK9094 — Console paste can use a freed ConClip port during shutdown:** the console handler retains a `FindPort()` pointer while preparing the request, then sends without holding a port-lifetime reference; ConClip can process OFF and delete the port in between. Distinct from EK9529's already-queued request that misses the final drain. See [EK9094](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9094) and the [console paste/port teardown trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4195). Source-only; no paste or shutdown race was run.

**EK9099 — `OpenDevice()` can call a freed dynamic device base on ExecSMP:** it drops the DeviceList read lock after lookup, before calling the Open vector, while `RemDevice()` runs expunge under CPU-local `Forbid()`. The per-unit printer device adds a concrete publish-then-startup-failure caller: another CPU can open its newly published node while failed worker startup removes/frees it. Also applies to the selected USB and Bluetooth class paths already traced in the detailed report. See [EK9099](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9099) and the [printer caller/lifetime recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#printer-per-unit-opendevice-expunge-caller-recheck-ek9099). Source-only; no concurrent open or worker failure was run.

**EK9095 — x86-64 PC can advertise usable RAM above its 512-GiB identity map:** MMU setup clamps mapping at 512 GiB, while the later high-memory map builder accepts reported RAM through the address-space limit. An above-limit chunk can fault during MemHeader construction or later use, depending on map fragmentation and allocation order. See [EK9095](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9095) and the [MMU/map/allocator trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L1756). Source-only; no high-RAM boot was run.

**EK9096 — x86-64 PC `KrnMapGlobal()` ignores `MAP_Supervisor`:** the leaf and parent entries are marked user-accessible regardless of the flag, so callers requesting supervisor-only mappings do not receive that protection. The maintained in-tree caller set does not pass the flag; impact is external/future conditional. See [EK9096](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9096) and the [leaf/parent permission trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L4217). Source-only; no mapping or privilege access was performed.

**EK9097 — RISC-V OpenSBI maps and reserves only the first 2 MiB of the device tree:** startup captures the DTB's declared size but uses a fixed 2 MiB for its later mapping and separately added RAM-bank exclusion. A larger DTB can have an unmapped tail when outside already mapped regions, or a reusable tail in a separately added RAM bank. Selected in-tree FDT consumers run before those later banks are published; effects remain conditional on firmware placement/size and a later reader or allocation. See [EK9097](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9097) and the [extent and consumer-order recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8478). Source-only; no DTB or boot was used.

**EK9098 — AArch64 Raspberry Pi boot tags can exceed the fixed tag buffer:** the bootstrap reserves 64 `TagItem`s, while each nonzero `/memory/reg` tuple emits two entries with no capacity check; 27 tuples plus mandatory later tags already exceed the buffer and reach adjacent stack storage. No checked-in normal firmware tree establishes that range count, so reachability and resulting stack effect remain conditional. See [EK9098](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek9098) and the [capacity/tag-producer recheck](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L5770). Source-only; no DTB or boot was used.


**GD10462 — Hyperlayers omits resize backfill strips when rectangle union fails:** `MoveSizeLayer()` ignores `OrRectRegion()` failures while combining newly exposed strips, so the resize can skip the selected Intuition default backfill clear for a strip. Conditional on allocation failure; a later client redraw may repair the display. See [GD10462](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10462-hyperlayers-omits-resize-backfill-strips-when-rectangle-union-fails) and the [resize/backfill caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#movesizelayer-growth-backfill-union-result-recheck). Source-only; no resize or allocation failure was induced.


**GD10463 — ChangeLayerShape installs an empty layer bound when rectangle allocation fails:** the replacement `Region` can allocate successfully while its `OrRectRegion()` bounds insertion fails. The unchecked failure leaves an empty outer shape, which then clears the derived visible shape before Intuition recalculates layers. This is distinct from GD6179's failed `NewRegion()` dereference. See [GD10463](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10463-changelayershape-installs-an-empty-layer-bound-when-rectangle-allocation-fails) and the [shape-bound caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#changelayershape-outer-bound-union-failure-recheck). Source-only; no shape or allocation failure was induced.


**GD10464 — Hyperlayers can omit exposed simple-refresh areas after damage insertion fails:** `_CopyClipRectsToClipRects()` ignores two `OrRectRegion()` results while adding backup/revealed clip areas and an `OrRegionRegion()` result while adding backfill damage to `DamageList`; later simple-refresh clipping is derived from that list. An allocation failure can therefore omit an area from client redraw, even though reveal invokes the backfill hook. See [GD10464](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10464-hyperlayers-can-omit-exposed-simple-refresh-areas-after-damage-insertion-fails) and the [DamageList insertion trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hyperlayers-damage-insertion-failure-recheck). Source-only; no allocation failure or refresh was induced.


Hyperlayers clip-install shape-mask caller recheck (GD6186 strengthened; 2026-10-31; no new finding or coverage credit): re-traced `_InternalInstallClipRegion()` through the public `InstallClipRegion()` wrapper. If the initial ND intersection succeeds but the ignored in-place `AndRegionRegion(l->shape, r)` fails, the preserved region proceeds to `_CreateClipRectsFromRegion()` for the first visible ClipRect partition, allowing clip rectangles outside a nonrectangular layer shape. Added this callsite-specific consequence to GD6186; `AndRegionRegionND()`'s separate NULL failure remains GD6173. Existing body credit unchanged. No allocation failure or clip install was run; source-only.


Hyperlayers simple-refresh backfill mask caller recheck (GD6186 strengthened; 2026-10-31; no new finding or coverage credit): the final unchecked `AndRegionRegion(l->visibleshape, dr)` in `_CopyClipRectsToClipRects()` can leave the already bounds/VisibleRegion-clipped damage region unmasked, after which the code calls the layer backfill hook for each retained rectangle (`rom/hyperlayers/basicfuncs.c:967-1004`). The `_ShowPartsOfLayer()` caller reaches this mode during reveal (`:1109-1120`). Added this conditional callback consequence to GD6186; no separate ID or body credit. No allocation failure or layer operation was run; source-only.


**GD10233 continuation — nested Vulkan-Hpp rendering structures:** the enhanced `ArrayProxyNoTemporaries` constructors/setters in five copied rendering/resolve structure wrappers narrow container sizes to `uint32_t` while retaining the original array pointer. Added `RenderingAreaInfo`, `RenderingAttachmentLocationInfo`, `RenderingInfo`, `RenderingInputAttachmentIndexInfo`, and `ResolveImageInfo2` to GD10233. This is the same oversized-container root cause; no new ID or source-body credit. See [GD10233](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10233-vulkan-hpp-array-proxies-truncate-large-container-sizes) and the [contiguous struct review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L11966).


**GD10233 continuation — inline-uniform byte extent:** the `PushConstantsInfo` constructor/`setValues()` and `WriteDescriptorSetInlineUniformBlock` constructor/`setData()` narrow byte extents above `UINT32_MAX` while retaining the original data pointers; e.g. a `2^32 + 16` byte range becomes a 16-byte push-constant update. Added these same-root-cause paths to GD10233 (core Vulkan 1.4 / `VK_KHR_maintenance6` and core Vulkan 1.3 / `VK_EXT_inline_uniform_block`; no checked-in C++ caller). See [GD10233](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10233-vulkan-hpp-array-proxies-truncate-large-container-sizes) and [coverage entry](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L11971). Source-only; no Vulkan call or build was run.


**Exec/Kernel Moira continuation:** reviewed the selected M68040 BRA/Bcc/BSR/DBcc handler and opcode-registration slice against the Motorola instruction definitions. Displacement base/extension selection, BSR return address and DBcc termination matched; the apparent odd-target check before loop exhaustion is inactive because selected `MOIRA_EMULATE_ADDRESS_ERROR` is false. No new finding or body/LOC credit; `MoiraExec_cpp.h` and `MoiraInit_cpp.h` remain partial. See [coverage entry](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L11590). No guest instruction or build was run; source-only.

**Exec/Kernel Moira continuation:** audited the selected M68040 MOVE SR/CCR/USP handler family, opcode masks, privilege checks and status-register stack-bank transition against the 68040 manual. No independent selected-path defect was established; the distinct C68000 branch was not treated as active AROS behavior. No new finding or body/LOC credit; Moira opcode files remain partial. See [coverage entry](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L11592). No instruction or build was run; source-only.

**GD10465 — BoingIconBar can leave its static toolbar hidden after window creation fails:** static startup and Workbench screen restoration ignore `OpenMainWindow()` failure, while idle retry is limited to the bottom activation strip. See [GD10465](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10465-boingiconbar-can-leave-its-static-toolbar-hidden-after-window-creation-fails) and the [full-body/caller recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#boingiconbar-full-body-and-static-window-retry-pass-gd10465). Source-only; no window failure or screen reset was induced.


**EK10294 — ARM32 accepts IRQ IDs beyond the BCM2708 dispatch range:** `HW_IRQ_COUNT` defaults to 240 although the selected controller dispatches only 0–71. Unsupported ID 96 is accepted and enables the register bit for IRQ 64, but its handler is stored at list 96 and is never called. Trigger requires an external/future caller; standard ARM32 Pi builds have no checked-in such caller. See [EK10294](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10294) and the [ARM32 IRQ coverage review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L11612). Source-only; no IRQ was registered or delivered.


**EK10295 — ARM32 secondary bootstrap leaks its CPU context if ETask allocation fails:** context creation succeeds before `Exec_InitETask()` fails, but that cleanup frees the task, stack, and MemList without deleting the unattached context. Conditional on reaching the low-memory path after EK153 is corrected. See [EK10295](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10295) and the [full bootstrap cleanup review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L11621). Source-only; no allocation failure or boot was run.

**EK10296 — Moira reverses Z after successful DIVS.W/DIVU.W:** the selected word-divide helpers assign the quotient directly to Boolean Z, so zero and nonzero quotients report the wrong condition flag and can misdirect guest branches. Applies to explicit M68040/Musashi-compatible m68kemu.library builds. See [EK10296](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10296) and the [Moira divide-family review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#moira-selected-m68040-word-divide-pass-ek10296). Source-only; no guest instruction or build was run.

**EK10297 — Moira executes MULL/DIVL with nonzero reserved extension bits:** both execution handlers ignore bit 15 and bits 9–3 of the extension word instead of taking the illegal-instruction exception required for invalid M68040 encodings. Conditional on malformed MULL/DIVL guest code in an explicit `m68kemu.library` build. See [EK10297](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10297) and the [extension validation review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#moira-mull-reserved-extension-validation-ek10297). Source-only; no instruction or build was run.

**EK10298 — Moira executes instructions with invalid extension fields:** selected CAS/CAS2, CHK2/CMP2 and bit-field handlers do not enforce reserved-zero fields; the shared full-format indexed-EA decoder also accepts reserved BD SIZE and I/IS combinations. Conditional on malformed guest instruction encodings in an explicit M68040 `m68kemu.library` build. See [EK10298](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10298) and the [extension validation pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#moira-extension-word-validation-families-ek10298). Source-only; no instruction or build was run.



**EK8873 — BCM2708 timer allocation failure silently omits VBlank delivery:** allocation failure skips timer-3 registration and the startup caller ignores the returned handle. This removes the `INTB_VERTB` source used by Exec, the selected Raspberry Pi timer.device, and graphics TOF/VBlank services. Applies to ARM32 Raspberry Pi and AArch64 Raspberry Pi 3/BCM2837; Pi 4/5 use different timer initializers. See [EK8873](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8873) and the [timer initialization and consumer trace](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#L8580). Source-only; no allocation failure, interrupt, timer, boot, or build was exercised.

**GD6198 — Sound datatype DTM_COPY dereferences a NULL IFF handle after allocation failure:** `Sound_WRITE()` records `ERROR_NO_FREE_STORE` when `AllocIFF()` fails, then its `DTM_COPY` cleanup dereferences `iff->iff_Stream`. MultiView advertises and invokes `DTM_COPY` for supported datatypes; the Sound module is explicitly buildable, though not selected by its parent aggregate edge. See [GD6198](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd6198) and [the Sound dispatcher caller/cleanup pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sound-dtm-copy-caller-scope-reconciliation-gd6198). Source-only; no allocation failure or clipboard copy was induced.


**OD10505 — FDisk leaves `io_Error` stale for `TD_GETDRIVETYPE`:** it sets `io_Actual` to `DRIVE_NEWSTYLE` without clearing the request error, and `DoIO()` returns that stale field. The common `workbench-devs-fdsk` target is selected through `workbench-devs-common`. See [OD10505](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10505) and the [FDisk full-body and command pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#fdsk-device-full-body-and-command-contract-pass-od10505). Source-only; no request or build was run.


**OD10506 — Ramdrive range checks can wrap before `CopyMem()`:** its read/write helpers test `offset + size` in 32-bit arithmetic, so a wrapped sum can pass and address beyond the fixed disk buffer. The common Workbench device target includes Ramdrive. See [OD10506](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10506) and the [Ramdrive full-body and range-check pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#ramdrive-full-body-and-range-check-pass-od10506). Source-only; no request was issued.

**OD10507 — Atheros5000 copies oversized management frames past its DMA slot:** S2_WRITEMGMT accepts an unchecked length; the unit task narrows it and copies into a fixed 3,060-byte DMA buffer. Conditional on an oversized request to an explicitly selected optional Atheros5000 target. See [OD10507](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10507) and the [management TX review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#atheros5000-management-tx-length-and-unit-body-recheck-od10507). Source-only; no request or device was used.
OD10507 reachability qualifier (2026-10-31): the HAL's declared legacy IEEE 802.11 maximum is below the 3,060-byte DMA slot, and the checked-in WirelessManager bridge has no demonstrated standards-sized overlength caller. The unchecked copy remains a conditional malformed/overlength SANA-II request defect; in-tree trigger unproven, overall confidence medium. No new finding or LOC credit.

**OD10508 — IntelGMA Gallium context creation dereferences failed allocations:** the Mesa i915 constructor uses assertions for fallible draw-context and blitter allocations, then immediately dereferences the results. Conditional on allocation failure while an explicitly built IntelGMA screen creates a Gallium context. See [OD10508](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10508) and the [external Mesa i915 coverage review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). Source-only; no build or allocation failure was run.


**OD10509 — IntelGMA i915 supplies vertex position as `gl_FrontFacing`:** the selected shader path binds the fragment FACE input to the vertex POSITION slot for filled polygons, so front/back-dependent shading is wrong. See [OD10509](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10509) and the [i915 vertex-layout review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). Source-only; no shader or GPU was run.


**OD10510 — IntelGMA i915 loses empty scissor bounds:** with the supported framebuffer-flip extension set to bottom-origin, zero scissor maxima underflow and encode as 65535, so the driver no longer clips all fragments. See [OD10510](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10510) and the [dynamic-state review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). Source-only; no render was run.


**OD10511 — IntelGMA i915 ignores the selected depth mip/layer offset:** framebuffer setup computes a nonzero offset for the attached depth subresource but emits the depth buffer relocation at offset zero. See [OD10511](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10511) and the [framebuffer-state review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). Source-only; no FBO or draw was run.


**OD10512 — IntelGMA i915 render copies leak temporary views:** when `I915_USE_BLITTER=0`, each supported render-copy path retains its temporary surface and sampler view. See [OD10512](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10512) and the [surface-helper review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review).

**OD10513 — IntelGMA i915 render copy dereferences failed view allocations:** the same optional path passes unchecked allocation results to the generic blitter, which dereferences them. See [OD10513](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10513) and the [surface-helper review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). Source-only; no copy or allocation failure was run.


**OD10514 — IntelGMA Gallium glFinish() does not wait for GPU completion (conditional manual target):** if IntelGMA/i915 is explicitly linked against a compatible Gallium stack, its flush callback queues work without returning a fence, so Mesa skips the wait. Its monitor and Mesa-version dependency edges are currently commented out, and Mesa 26 API compatibility is unverified; this is not a default-build claim. See [OD10514](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10514) and the [screen/fence review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). Source-only; no GL call or GPU operation was run.

**OD10515 — IntelGMA i915 shifts by 32 when emitting the maximum fragment-constant range:** the translator accepts constant slot 31 and the screen advertises 32 vec4 constants, reaching undefined behavior in `(1 << nr)` when `nr == 32`; the resulting register mask may be wrong. Conditional on the explicit 32-bit IntelGMA Mesa 26.0.0 path using all 32 constants. See [OD10515](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10515) and the [i915 state-emission review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). No shader or GPU was run.

**OD10516 — IntelGMA i915 state constructors dereference failed allocations:** blend, sampler, depth/stencil and rasterizer constructors write through unchecked `CALLOC_STRUCT` results. Conditional on allocation failure in an explicit IntelGMA Mesa 26.0.0 build. See [OD10516](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10516) and the [i915 state-management review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). No allocation failure or GL call was run.


**OD10517 — IntelGMA i915 dereferences a failed framebuffer-surface allocation:** failed surface-wrapper creation stores NULL in the color attachment cache, which the framebuffer-state setter immediately dereferences. Conditional on allocation failure during a color framebuffer update in an explicit IntelGMA Mesa 26.0.0 build. See [OD10517](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10517) and the [i915 state-management review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). No allocation failure or framebuffer update was run.


**OD10518 — IntelGMA i915 aliases fragment varyings after slot eight:** the screen advertises ten varying vectors, but the translator has eight mappings and sends any overflow to T_TEX0. See [OD10518](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10518) and the [i915 fragment-program translator review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). No shader or GPU was run.


**OD10519 — IntelGMA i915 writes past shader immediate arrays:** more than 32 TGSI immediate vectors index beyond the compiler's fixed arrays before the constant limit is handled. See [OD10519](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10519) and the [i915 fragment-program translator review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). No shader compilation was run.


**OD10520 — IntelGMA i915 fragment-shader compilation dereferences failed allocations:** compiler-context, error-string and final-program allocations are used without checking for failure. See [OD10520](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10520) and the [i915 fragment-program translator review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). No allocation failure or shader compilation was run.


**OD10521 — IntelGMA i915 compiles fragment derivatives as zero:** TGSI DDX/DDY are translated into zero-valued results even though the selected Mesa interface exposes GLSL 1.20 derivatives. See [OD10521](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10521) and the [i915 fragment-program translator review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). No shader or GPU was run.


**OD10522 — IntelGMA i915 silently drops fragment instructions at the program limit:** the 192-dword buffer holds 64 three-dword instructions, but advertised ALU and texture limits permit a longer program; later instructions are skipped without a compile error. See [OD10522](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10522) and the [i915 fragment-program emitter review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). No shader or GPU was run.
**OD10523 — IntelGMA i915 fragment optimization treats every temporary as dead:** both liveness arrays retain their `-1` sentinels, so the MOV-forwarding pass may remove a copy even when later shader instructions still read that temporary. See [OD10523](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10523) and the [i915 optimizer review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). No shader or GPU was run.
**OD10524 — IntelGMA i915 can install a missing render stage after allocation failure:** the unchecked stage allocation is stored by the draw pipeline and its validator later calls through the missing terminal stage. See [OD10524](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10524) and the [i915 primitive-emitter review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). No allocation failure or draw was run.
**OD10525 — IntelGMA i915 maps a NULL vertex buffer after allocation failure:** the selected AROS winsys returns NULL on allocation failure, but the vbuf renderer maps it before checking. Conditional on the optional `DBG_VBUF` path. See [OD10525](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10525) and the [i915 primitive-vbuf review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). No allocation failure or draw was run.
**OD10526 — IntelGMA i915 dereferences a failed vbuf-render allocation:** the optional `DBG_VBUF` context path initializes the newly allocated renderer without a NULL check. See [OD10526](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10526) and the [i915 primitive-vbuf review](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#mesa26-i915-gallium-source-review). No allocation failure or context creation was run.





**GD10466 — V3D can keep a framebuffer page as its render target after scanout detach allocation fails:** the detach helper clears scanout bookkeeping even when its private replacement BO allocation fails, so later windowed rendering can continue through the framebuffer-backed resource. Applies to the optional Raspberry Pi AArch64 V3D Gallium target; default-image inclusion is not claimed. See [GD10466](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10466-v3d-can-keep-a-framebuffer-page-as-its-render-target-after-scanout-detach-allocation-fails) and the [targeted presentation-path review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#v3d-scanout-detach-allocation-failure-gd10466). Source-only; no allocation failure or GPU operation was run.

**GD10467 — V3D can display a render job discarded by timeout recovery:** the sequence wait ignores its failure result, and overlay presentation continues after recovery has dropped the queued job. The queued BO can be shown with stale or incomplete pixels. Applies to the optional Raspberry Pi AArch64 V3D Gallium target; default-image inclusion is not claimed. See [GD10467](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10467-v3d-can-present-a-frame-discarded-by-timeout-recovery) and the [timeout/recovery caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#v3d-wait-recovery-overlay-result-gd10467). Source-only; no GPU timeout or display was induced.

**EK10299 — Moira bit-field width calculation overflows signed `int`:** a valid register-width operand with its high bit set can become `INT_MIN`, then overflow on subtraction before modulo-32 width handling. Results depend on compiler/optimization. Applies to explicit `m68kemu.library` builds, not default ROM inclusion. See [EK10299](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10299) and the [bit-field arithmetic pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#moira-register-width-bit-field-signed-overflow-ek10299). Source-only; no instruction or build was run.


**EK10300 — Moira executes MOVES with nonzero reserved extension bits:** the selected handler ignores the extension's zero-required low eleven bits and performs the transfer instead of taking an illegal-instruction exception. Conditional on malformed MOVES encodings in an explicit M68040 `m68kemu.library` build. See [EK10300](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10300) and the [MOVES extension validation pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#moira-moves-reserved-extension-validation-ek10300). Source-only; no instruction or build was run.

**EK10302 — CHRP Exec bootstrap cannot preprocess its `InitETask` call:** the architecture override passes three arguments to the only checked-in two-argument macro, so explicit CHRP PPC `kernel-exec` builds fail before link. Default Efika image inclusion is not claimed. See [EK10302](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek10302) and the [CHRP macro-arity pass](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#chrp-exec-bootstrap-source-and-macro-arity-pass-ek10302-and-ek8842-reconciled-no-pathloc-credit-2026-10-31). Source-only; no build was run.

**EK8842 — CHRP Exec continues after required allocation failures:** several bootstrap allocations only log failure before null dereferences or publication, risking early boot failure under memory exhaustion. It is conditional on the CHRP override being made buildable; no default-image claim. See [EK8842](AROS-exec-kernel.md#ek8842) and the [CHRP allocation-failure review](AROS-exec-kernel-coverage.md#chrp-exec-bootstrap-source-and-macro-arity-pass-ek10302-and-ek8842-reconciled-no-pathloc-credit-2026-10-31). Source-only; no allocation failure or boot was run.


**GD10468 — V3D job state is not serialized against interrupts in ExecSMP:** the optional AArch64 RasPi driver registers GIC SPI 74, which BCM2711 targets at CPU 0, while SMP tasks without affinity can run on any CPU; local interrupt disabling and the task-side semaphore do not serialize the IRQ handler against task service on another core. Limited to an explicit `raspi-aarch64` `smp` build of the optional V3D HIDD; default UP and default-image inclusion are not claimed. See [GD10468](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10468-v3d-job-state-is-not-serialized-against-interrupts-in-execsmp) and the [IRQ-route confirmation](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#v3d-smp-irq-route-confirmation-for-gd10468). Source-only; no IRQ interleaving or build was run.


**OD3228 — USB Audio capture reuses one buffer for multiple in-flight isochronous IN requests:** xHCI, OHCI and UHCI can have two input transfers targeting the same recording buffer, so a later packet may replace an earlier packet before its completion callback consumes it. EHCI is excluded because it calls the completion hook before scheduling the next one-packet request. The USB Audio class is optional; default RasPi package inclusion is not claimed. See [OD3228](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3228) and the [host-controller callback reconciliation](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-audio-capture-buffer-overlap-build-graph-and-host-controller-reconciliation-od3228-retained-2026-10-31-no-new-finding-or-pathloc-credit). Source-only; no device or transfer was exercised.

**OD4300 reachability recheck:** the legacy m68k `CAMDDriver.c` array also stores `Flags=0` in its `MDEV` record; AROS CAMD would reject it through the same format gate if that branch were packaged. The class manifest has no m68k CPU alias, so the affected selected targets remain the declared i386, x86_64, ARM, AArch64 and PPC variants. See [OD4300](AROS-other-drivers.md#od4300) and the [embedded-driver loader reconciliation](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#usb-midi-embedded-camd-bridge-loaderbuild-gate-reconciliation-od4300od4301od4459-rechecked-2026-10-31-no-new-od-or-loc-credit). Static source only; no binary was loaded or build performed.

**OD3521 — OpenSBI PCIDT can report success after allocating fewer MSI vectors than requested:** the backend always programs one vector and ignores the requested minimum. Checked-in callers request one vector; the defect is conditional on a future or external PCIDT client requiring more. See [OD3521](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3521) and the [PCIDT contract and caller census](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#opensbi-pcidt-vector-contract-and-caller-census-refresh-od3521-retained-conditionally-2026-10-31-no-new-finding-or-fileloc-credit). Source-only; no vector request or interrupt was run.

**OD10527 — OpenSBI PCIDT can report successful initialization after a bridge registration fails:** its init loop uses the legacy PCI registration method, which discards generic `HW_AddDriver()`'s NULL failure result. A failed bridge may therefore be absent from PCI enumeration, and successful later registrations can repeat an earlier bridge. Conditional on allocation or setup failure during RISC-V OpenSBI PCIDT startup. See [OD10527](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10527--opensbi-pcidt-reports-initialization-success-when-a-bridge-driver-was-not-registered) and the [bridge-registration trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#opensbi-pcidt-bridge-driver-registration-failure-trace-od10527-added-2026-10-31-no-pathloc-credit). No boot or registration failure was induced.

**OD10528 — PCI enumeration silently omits devices whose HIDD object construction fails:** `InsertDevice()` returns NULL, but `PCI__HW__SetUpDriver()` ignores the result and reports setup success. On PCIDT, the constructor masks endpoint interrupts before the failed superclass construction. Conditional on selected device-object construction failure during PCI scanning. See [OD10528](AROS-other-drivers.md#od10528--pci-bus-setup-succeeds-after-a-discovered-device-object-failed-to-construct) and the [PCI device-construction failure pass](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#pci-bus-device-construction-failure-od10528). No allocation failure or enumeration was induced.
**LDDemon Open serialization review correction (2026-10-31):** OD9568, OD9923, OD9931 and OD9965 are withdrawn because their triggers require concurrent same-name public `OpenDevice()` callbacks, which LDDemon serializes through each device's Open vector. OD3115 is narrowed to Open overlapping final Close, because the `CloseDevice()` wrapper does not take the per-name semaphore. See the [corrected findings](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3115) and [coverage ledger](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md).

**GD10469 — ChangeLayerShape ignores custom-shape intersection failure:** if region allocation fails during `AndRegionRegion()`, the rectangular destination survives, and the update proceeds with a bound broader than the requested custom shape. See [GD10469](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10469-changelayershape-ignores-custom-shape-intersection-failure) and the [intersection failure trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#changelayershape-custom-intersection-failure-recheck). Source-only; no allocation failure or shape update was induced.


**GD10470 — Palette Preferences cannot restore a client-installed very large color map through LoadRGB4:** its unsigned `ColorMap->Count` snapshot narrows to signed `WORD`; 32,768 entries become a nonpositive count and `LoadRGB4()` skips restoration on affected targets. `SA_ColorMapEntries` cannot produce this size because OpenScreen narrows it to signed `WORD`; the scoped trigger requires a client-installed map returned by `GetColorMap()`. See [GD10470](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10470-palette-preferences-cannot-restore-very-large-color-maps-through-loadrgb4) and the [caller and count-type trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#palette-preferences-large-colormap-restore-recheck). Source-only; no screen or palette update was run.
**GD10472 — OpenScreen reduces large `SA_ColorMapEntries` requests to 32 entries:** the tag is stored in signed `WORD numcolors`; on affected targets, 32,768 becomes negative and the minimum-size expression selects 32. No checked-in caller was found; the trigger is external-client use, and the undocumented maximum keeps reachability confidence medium. See [GD10472](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd10472-openscreen-reduces-large-sa_colormapentries-requests-to-32-entries) and the [tag-to-ColorMap trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#openscreen-large-colormap-tag-narrowing-gd10472). Source-only; no screen was opened.


**OD3298 — keyboard.device clears a freed open-unit flag after replying the final queued read:** on ExecSMP, the reply owner can consume the message and close the unit before `kbdSendQueuedEvents()` clears `KBUF_PENDING` through the replied request. See [OD3298](AROS-other-drivers.md#od3298) and the [keyboard handler lifetime recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#keyboard-final-queued-read-unit-lifetime-od3298-recheck). Source-only; no request or device was used.


**OD2389 — keyboard.device can leave a read queued after publishing its event:** on ExecSMP, a key callback can publish an event and skip draining the queue just before BeginIO inserts its pending request, leaving input blocked until another key arrives. See [OD2389](AROS-other-drivers.md#od2389) and the [empty-check/enqueue recheck](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#keyboard-pending-read-empty-check-enqueue-race-od2389-recheck). Source-only; no event or interleaving was run.


Text.datatype public-header and AmigaGuide caller review (2026-10-31): completed the 40-line `textclass.h` API/field crosswalk.
