<a id="smp-smallpt-raydepth-stack-size-overflow-gd10576"></a>
## SMP-SmallPT RAYDEPTH stack-size boundary follow-up (GD10576; 2026-11-01; no body/path/LOC credit)

Rechecked the numeric argument path from `RAYDEPTH/N` in `main.c:85,152-157` through `ReadArgs()` (`rom/dos/readargs.c:843-845,879-881`) and `StrToLong()` (`rom/dos/strtolong.c:35-37`), whose comment explicitly says it does not check excessive values. The resulting `int maximal_ray_depth` has only a lower clamp. In `renderer.c:59`, the expression `AROS_STACKSIZE + maximal_ray_depth * 1000` is evaluated in signed `int` before assignment to `ULONG`. For x86-64's `AROS_STACKSIZE=40960`, depth 2,147,443 makes the mathematical sum 2,147,483,960, exceeding `INT_MAX` by 313; larger valid LONG arguments also overflow the multiplication. The calculated value is passed to `TASKTAG_STACKSIZE` (`renderer.c:155-163`). Added GD10576 for the undefined signed-overflow stack request, scoped to the explicitly buildable optional target; worker creation failure overlaps the startup wait already described by GD10571. No compilation, task creation, or runtime operation was performed.


<a id="smp-smallpt-height-clamp-order-gd10577"></a>
## SMP-SmallPT HEIGHT argument ordering follow-up (GD10577; 2026-11-01; no body/path/LOC credit)

Re-read `main()`'s command-line argument parsing around the previously reviewed full-body pass. The intended `req_height < 128` clamp occurs at `main.c:176-177`, before `HEIGHT/N` is loaded into `req_height` at `:179-181`, so the comparison always sees the initial zero for this argument. The value then reaches `createMainWindow()` (`:194`), whose screen path rounds any smaller requested height down to a multiple of 32 (`:44-47`); e.g. 127 becomes 96 and 1–31 become zero. Added GD10577 for the skipped minimum constraint and resulting undersized/zero window request. The consequence of zero inner height depends on Intuition's OpenWindow handling and is qualified in the finding. This is an additional gap found during a targeted post-pass review; it does not change the full-body coverage counts. No GUI or build was run; source-only.

## GD10438 LinuxFB explicit-pitch condition refinement (no new finding or coverage credit)

Completed the selected LinuxFB producer trace: `linuxfbgfx_hiddclass.c:117-120` stores `fsi.line_length` as the framebuffer pitch and `vsi.xres` as its width; `linuxfbgfx_displayclass.c:227-228` uses `vsi->xres` for the mode width and `:339-348` passes the pitch as explicit `aHidd_BitMap_BytesPerRow`. With the generic bitmap default 16-pixel alignment, the constructor rejects a framebuffer when `line_length < ceil(xres / 16) * 16 * bytes_per_pixel`, even when `line_length >= xres * bytes_per_pixel` and thus covers the actual unpadded row. This establishes the precise selected configuration condition but not that any supported Linux framebuffer reports it; the candidate remains conditional. GD10438 was updated with this trigger boundary. No framebuffer was opened and no display mode or build was exercised; source-only.


## Masked-blit row-stride candidate and alignment-producer recheck (GD10439 retained; no body/path/LOC credit)

Rechecked `copyboxmasked_impl()`'s mask pitch against its HIDD contract and row indexing (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1361,1442-1448,1511-1526,1569`). With source width 9 and alignment 4, the existing bitmap round-up produces 12 pixels correctly, but `12 >> 3` gives a 1-byte mask row where the full 12-pixel row requires 2 bytes; each later source row is then indexed at the wrong mask offset. This is independent of GD10438 because alignment 4 is a valid power of two. The generic wrapper dispatches driver-owned/cursor-wrapped bitmaps to their method path and uses this implementation for ordinary software bitmaps (`:1600-1643`). The graphics.library `BltMaskBitMapRastPort()` bridge passes the mask pointer directly to `HIDD_Gfx_CopyBoxMasked()` without a stride (`rom/graphics/bltmaskbitmaprastport.c:28-38,73`); its public autodoc only says the mask has the same size as the source, while the HIDD method's own contract explicitly includes source bitmap alignment (`gfx_hiddclass.c:1358-1362`). Consequently the byte-pitch defect is established for the generic HIDD contract; legacy-call reachability depends on the caller's mask allocation honoring the aligned source row pitch, which the public autodoc does not spell out. The full source search for `aHidd_BitMap_Align` producers found only byte-multiple values: 16/64 AmigaVideo, 16/32 Picasso96, 32 Nouveau, 32 IntelGMA and 32 WinGDI planar. Picasso96 sets `data->align` to 16 for off-screen and 32 for displayable bitmaps (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/p96gfx/p96gfx_bitmapclass.c:330-332`); its selected `CopyBoxMasked` method delegates to its superclass (`p96gfx_hiddclass.c:1098-1110`), so this is a generic-fallback consumer with a byte-multiple producer, not an in-tree sub-byte trigger. Thus the source-level arithmetic defect remains, while in-tree triggering still requires direct HIDD use/configuration not evidenced in maintained callers. No mask operation or build was run; source-only.

## MUI Window sleep/wake minimum-width caller and Intuition contract recheck (GD5170 promoted from summary-only; 2026-11-01; no body/LOC credit)

Rechecked `Window__OM_SET()`'s `MUIA_Window_Sleep` transitions against selected `WindowLimits()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:3282-3335`; `rom/intuition/windowlimits.c:74-80,105-106`). The first sleep transition stores native `MaxWidth` in both sleep-width fields; the final wake transition passes the saved `wd_SleepMinWidth` as `WindowLimits()`'s minimum and ignores its return. Intuition leaves the minimum unchanged if current width is below that requested value, so the temporary sleep minimum remains; if current width is large enough, the former maximum becomes the new minimum. Both outcomes fail to restore the original lower bound. The Window class is in the default muimaster class list (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:60-89`), and application sleep iterates the window list and forwards the attribute (`application.c:1204-1217`). Repository search found checked-in direct callers in TextEditor's SpellChecker, VMM, HDToolBox, syslog, diskimage GUI and QuickPart, plus application-level wrappers in PSI. Confirmed the field mismatch and API behavior; the practical resize restriction depends on the window's original limits and current dimensions. Promoted GD5170 from an unverified legacy summary to a confirmed source finding with conditional user-visible impact. No source-body or LOC credit changes; no window, GUI, build or runtime operation was exercised. Source-only.

Vulkan preferred-GPU reselection loader-to-callback recheck (GD10214 retained; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): followed the copied loader entry points `vkCreateDevice()` and `vkGetDeviceQueue()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/vulkan_loader.c:554-608`) into their distinct OOP methods and the `GET_GPU` selection (`vulkan_class.c:177-229`; `vulkan_intern.h:314-339`). The loader forwards the opaque device/physical-device handles without a provider token; successful CreateDevice increments the selected entry count, changing an equal-priority tie for the next selection. Thus a second registered equal-priority provider can receive another provider's device handle at GetDeviceQueue/DestroyDevice. Re-searched the checked-in source tree: `VulkanHidd_RegisterGPU()` has no implementation callsite outside its own export/header and the probe comment, so current provider reachability is still unverified and remains explicit in GD10214. This confirms and sharpens the existing conditional API finding; no new root cause or coverage credit. No GPU registration, Vulkan method, build or runtime operation was exercised; source-only.

<a id="vesa-zero-framebuffer-pci-selection-gd14327-added-2026-11-02"></a>VESA zero-framebuffer PCI selection pass (GD14327 added; 2026-11-02): traced the selected PC VESAGfx init fallback from bootloader `VesaInfo.FrameBuffer` through `Find_PCI_Card()` and the PCI class enumerator. `bootloader_init.c` leaves the field zero for VBE mode-info versions below 2.0; VESAGfx then enumerates all interface-0 display/VGA devices and maps each BAR0 into one shared field. `PCI__Hidd_PCI__EnumDevices()` continues its `ForeachNode` after every callback. VESAGfx PCI fallback ownership/cleanup recheck (GD14327 retained; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced `Find_PCI_Card()` success and failure cleanup (`rom/hidds/vesagfx/vesagfx_support.c:230-269`). OpenScreen failed-MakeVPort publication rollback recheck (GD5179 retained; no new ID or LOC credit; 2026-11-02): re-read the selected synchronous caller and rollback rather than relying on the summary. `int_openscreen()` first adds a public `PubScreenNode`, links the `Screen` into `FirstScreen`/`ActiveScreen` (or the tail), may assign `DefaultPubScreen`, sets `msg->Success` from `MakeVPort()`, and unconditionally adds the embedded screen node to the resource list (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:2431-2476,2500`). `OpenScreen()` copies that result into `ok`; on failure its cleanup frees the ColorMap, layers, bitmap and RasInfo, then disposes the `IntScreen` (`:2303-2305,2317-2399`) without a call to `CloseScreen()` or corresponding unpublish/unlink/resource-removal helpers. The screen dispose method only releases decoration state before its superclass call (`rom/intuition/screenclass.c:46-79`); normal close performs public-node removal and resource removal (`rom/intuition/closescreen.c:331-351`). This confirms the existing high-confidence finding: a nonzero `MakeVPort()` result during an otherwise initialized OpenScreen leaves global/public/resource links to freed screen state. No new finding, body/path credit or LOC credit; no screen or failure was induced. Source-only.

OpenScreen-preassociated ViewPortExtra failure ownership follow-up (GD5919 expanded; 2026-11-02; no body/path/LOC credit): traced `OpenScreen()`'s VPE creation and `VTAG_ATTACH_CM_SET`/`VTAG_VIEWPORTEXTRA_SET` ordering (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1485,1542-1545,1590-1594`) through `VideoControl()` association (`rom/graphics/videocontrol.c:73-75,391-395`). `MakeVPort()` finds that existing node, leaves `own_vpe` false, and still allocates `HIDD_ViewPortData` (`rom/graphics/makevport.c:97-114`); after a later mode/display setup error its failure path frees only an owned VPE (`:218-243`). This establishes the same VPD leak on the selected OpenScreen path even though MakeVPort did not create the VPE. It is incorporated into GD5919 rather than counted as a separate root cause. ## `ObtainDataTypeA()` named RAM group-filter caller recheck (GD14329; 2026-11-02; no body/LOC credit)

Re-read the complete `ObtainDataTypeA()` body (`workbench/libs/datatypes/obtaindatatypea.c`) and traced both RAM branches plus `NewDTObjectA()` callers. The selected `NewDTObjectA()` path with `DTST_RAM` and a nonzero group ID maps the group to a built-in datatype name before its own construction path; a repository C-source search found no direct `ObtainDataTypeA(DTST_RAM, ...)` call. ## Datatypes file-probe read-result trace (GD14330; 2026-11-02; no body/LOC credit)

Rechecked the full `ExamineLock()`/`ExamineData()` bodies and the DOS `Read()` contract through the `ObtainDataTypeA(DTST_FILE)` caller. `CheckArray` is allocated at `initial CheckSize + 1`, with initial size at least 64 (`workbench/libs/datatypes/helpfuncs.c:232-244`); for initial sizes below 65,534 bytes, the resulting 65,535-byte scan exceeds that allocation. DOS `Read()` returns `LONG` and documents `-1` on error (`rom/dos/read.c:32-43,50-76`). Assigning the result directly to `UWORD CheckSize` converts `-1` to 65,535, and the positive check passes. The resulting count is forwarded to `ExamineData()`, whose initial type check may use the IFF shortcut but whose ordinary ASCII/binary scan iterates for the full count (`helpfuncs.c:274-282,434-505`). Thus a probe read error can make the classifier read past its allocated buffer. Added GD14330. The full-body credit for `helpfuncs.c` already exists; no new LOC. The related GD14329 named-RAM group-filter mismatch remains separately scoped. No file read error, datatype query or build was induced; source-only.


## Wanderer AppObjects remaining direct-caller census (2026-11-02; no new finding or body/LOC credit)

Searched the repository for all AppObjects helper symbols and traced every checked-in C caller. `GetNextAppIconLocked()` has one caller, the volume-list refresh loop, which pairs `AppObjectsLock()`/`AppObjectsUnlock()` around enumeration; `AppIcon_GetDiskObject()` and `AppIcon_GetLabel()` recursively acquire the same Workbench semaphore inside that held region. Exec's `InternalObtainSemaphore()` increments `ss_NestCount` when the current task already owns the semaphore (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:95-107`), so this is supported nesting and not a deadlock. The returned disk object and label pointers remain protected by the outer lock through entry construction. `SendAppIconMessage()` and all menu-message calls are outside this traversal and validate list membership under the lock before using the AppIcon; reply cleanup is called from Wanderer's periodic task path. The existing GD6244 render-hook post-unlock dereference, GD6245 raw AppIcon-pointer reads, GD6246 reply-port initialization failure, and GD10140 nullable getter race remain separate existing findings. GELS unsupported-depth validation-result caller check (no GD added; 2026-11-02; no body/path/LOC credit): followed `AddVSprite()` through `_CreateIntVSprite()` and `_ValidateIntVSprite()` into `DrawGList()` (`rom/graphics/addvsprite.c:81-85`; `gels_internal.c:16-36,64-73`; `drawglist.c:127-166`). `_ValidateIntVSprite()` returns FALSE for `Depth > 32`, but `_CreateIntVSprite()` ignores that result and publishes the allocated internal record; subsequent DrawGList validation also ignores FALSE before using its bitmap pointers. GD10289 minterm truth-table and software-blitter recheck (finding strengthened; 2026-11-02; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read `DrawGList()`'s active/disabled `VS_MINTERM` definitions and followed its unmasked branch through `BltBitMapRastPort()` into `int_bltbitmap()` and `BltBitMap()` (`drawglist.c:137-166`; `bltbitmaprastport.c:26-38,100-128`; `bltbitmap.c:54-61,342-383`). The API defines A as the in-rectangle mask, B as source and C as destination; `copyonepixel()` implements the truth table directly. Therefore `0xc0` copies source and `0xe0` computes source OR destination within the rectangle, so zero-valued source pixels are destructive with the active minterm. Kept GD10289 scoped to unmasked VSprite/shadowless-Bob clients; no maintained checked-in caller was established. The involved bodies already have full credit; no totals change. No sprite, bitmap or rendering operation was run; source-only.


<a id="gels-clear-path-bob-vsprite-mix-gd14336"></a>GELS ClearPath Bob/VSprite caller pass (GD14336 added; 2026-11-02; no body/path/LOC credit): traced the `DrawGList()` traversal's unconditional predecessor-to-current `ClearPath` assignment (`rom/graphics/drawglist.c:192-207`) through its Bob-only clear entry (`:80-93`) into `_ClearBobAndFollowClearPath()` (`rom/graphics/gels_internal.c:181-203`). The recursive helper dereferences `CurVSprite->VSBob->Flags` before checking whether the node is a Bob. `AddVSprite()` publishes a standalone VSprite without setting a Bob owner (`rom/graphics/addvsprite.c:54-85`); `AddBob()` initializes the Bob wait flag and inserts its contained VSprite (`rom/graphics/addbob.c:53-68`). Existing GELS bodies already have full-body credit; totals do not change. No list, draw, removal, or fault was run; source-only.

Vulkan-Hpp external-memory query wrapper pass (GD14345 expanded; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): reviewed contiguous `vulkan_structs.hpp:88975-89574`, including extended-dynamic-state features, NV extended-sparse-address-space feature/property records, external-buffer query info, and external-compute-queue properties. Found `PhysicalDeviceExternalBufferInfo` defaults its `handleType` to `eOpaqueFd` both in constructor and member (`:89349-89357,89449-89453`); `PhysicalDevice::getExternalBufferProperties()` forwards the wrapper directly to `vkGetPhysicalDeviceExternalBufferProperties` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:6668-6676,6682-6696`). Expanded GD14345 to cover this query case; subsequent contiguous reads confirmed the same root cause in external image, fence, semaphore, and ARM tensor query records (see report). The Vulkan specification defines the query input's `handleType` as the type used with the associated memory and the query returns properties for that type ([reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkPhysicalDeviceExternalBufferInfo.html)); omitting the wrapper argument while intending a non-FD type therefore queries a different handle type. No query or build was run; generated header already has full-body credit and no path/LOC change. Source-only.

GD2719 visible consequence and failure-state distinction recheck (2026-11-02; retained, no body/path/LOC credit): traced the selected MultiView notification setup from `NewDTObject()` to its `ICA_TARGET` model configured for IDCMP (`workbench/utilities/MultiView/main.c:478-484,754-765`), then followed the subclass `NotifyAttrChanges()` wrapper to `OM_NOTIFY` (`ascii/asciiclass.c:43-46`) and MultiView’s `IDCMP_IDCMPUPDATE` handler, which sets `WA_BusyPointer` for `DTA_Busy=TRUE` (`main.c:1724-1737`). On `AllocVec(LayoutMessage)` or `CreateNewProc()` failure, `DoAsyncLayout()` clears its internal `DTSIF_LAYOUT|DTSIF_LAYOUTPROC` flags but sends no matching `DTA_Busy=FALSE`; the superclass layout result is TRUE and the subclass adds the helper’s FALSE result. This confirms the selected user-visible consequence as a stale busy pointer in MultiView despite a successful layout return, rather than an internally busy datatype object. Other viewers may consume the same notification differently; aggregate/package inclusion and later pointer-clearing behavior remain open. No allocation failure or GUI operation was induced; source-only.

`AndRectRegionND()` / `ScrollRegion()` caller and failure-path reconciliation (2026-11-02; GD8947 and GD9415 retained; no body/path/LOC credit): followed the only checked-in direct caller `ScrollRegion()` into `MoveRaster()` (`rom/graphics/scrollregion.c:61-88`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:859-862`). The explicit-rectangle path constructs the intersection, translates it, clips it with the infallible in-place `AndRectRegion()`, then builds the preserved remainder and commits only after the final region union succeeds. `MoveRaster()` ignores the Boolean result and continues the raster blit, leaving the old damage list unshifted if this transaction fails; its later damage-list allocation/union failures are separately covered by GD8947. Thus the caller confirms the existing finding; no duplicate was added. `ScrollRegion()`'s NULL-rectangle behavior remains GD9415 and is not reached by this caller. <a id="amigavideo-copperlist-aggregate-count-overflow-gd14349"></a>AmigaVideo user copper-list destination-capacity/count pass (GD14349 expanded; 2026-11-02; no body/LOC credit): verified `USE_UCOP_DIRECT=1` in `amigavideo_intern.h:9`, then traced selected viewport allocation and base capacity through `get_copper_list_length()` (`amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1142-1188,1274`; `amigavideo_chipset.c:486-495`). Also confirmed the aggregate Count sum is stored in signed WORD and narrows without a bound at much larger totals. Expanded GD14349 to make the fixed-capacity write the primary finding and retain the arithmetic issue as a secondary defect. Existing source body and LOC credit are unchanged. However, the interactive `scrolllayer()` command prompts for unrestricted integer deltas and forwards them directly to `ScrollLayer()` (`:354-375`), and is exposed by the command loop (`:1185-1200`). Entering `dx=-92` advances `Scroll_X` beyond the backing origin; on the next nonzero `ScrollLayer()` call, `SyncSBitMap()` computes a negative destination (`syncsbitmap.c:64-74`) and `BltBitMap()`'s lower-edge check remains absent (`bltbitmap.c:257-272`). Expanded GD9615 to state this concrete optional in-tree caller trigger; the previous conclusion that no maintained caller established the condition was incomplete. The `WORD` offset narrowing question remains unpromoted. No layer, bitmap or build operation was run.

GD10581 fixed-address recovery attribute/target recheck (no new finding; 2026-11-02): traced `compat_map_mmio()` through the selected Nouveau source list (`sources.drm.mak:65`) and compared its AArch64 mapping flags with `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/mmu.c:301-337`. Its RW-only `KrnMapGlobal()` call would select Normal-WB rather than Device memory on AArch64; however, the checked-in Nouveau target aliases name only i386, x86-64 and RISC-V64 (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/mmakefile.src:22-28`), with no AArch64 alias or selected image edge. I therefore did not add an AArch64 MMIO-attribute finding to the selected-target report. RISC-V's selected `KrnMapGlobal()` delegates to `krnMMUMapPages()`, whose platform comment says MMIO cacheability follows physical memory attributes (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_mmu.c:142-150`), so the AArch64 attribute result cannot be generalized to that target. GD10581 remains the separately qualified fixed-address/platform-map candidate; no additional consequence was established for its checked-in target aliases. No mapping, reset, build or device operation was run; source-only.


AmigaVideo copper tail count-exhaustion caller census (GD14350 rechecked; 2026-11-02; no new finding or body/LOC credit): searched all checked-in `UCopperListInit`, `CWait`, `CMove`, and copper-list attachment call sites, then traced the manually constructed list in the selected optional `test-graphics` source (`developer/debug/test/graphics/copper.c:92-110`; `developer/debug/test/graphics/mmakefile.src`). The test omits the `CEND()` macro but appends `CWait(uCop,10000,0xFF)` as its final counted entry. `limitheight()` caps selected AmigaVideo viewport height at 256 lines NTSC or 311 PAL (doubled in interlace; `arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/chipset.h:18-33`), so this wait is past `displayheight` and the parser takes the `default` termination path without emitting the entry; that one skipped counted instruction balances the extra emitted `0xFFDF/0xFFFE` line-wrap wait in the same list. The test therefore does not exercise GD14350's short-tail path. No checked-in count-exhausted copper list lacking an equivalent parser-skipped terminal entry was found; retained GD14350 as a conditional public-API finding because the API docs do not require a terminator and the parser explicitly accepts count exhaustion. No copper list, viewport or build was run; source-only.

The only active graphics test producer is `developer/debug/test/graphics/copper.c:92-110`, which initializes capacity for seven instructions and appends seven entries; this cannot reach the 500-instruction destination cap. <a id="graphics-copper-test-list-init-failure-gd14352"></a> Graphics debug copper-list initialization failure caller pass (GD14352 added; 2026-11-02; no body/path/LOC credit): traced the `USERCOPPER` branch in `developer/debug/test/graphics/copper.c:78-111` through `UCopperListInit()`'s two allocation steps (`rom/graphics/ucopperlistinit.c:59-78`) and `CWait()` (`rom/graphics/cwait.c:57-63`). The utility checks allocation of the outer `UCopList`, but ignores the initializer's result. Failure to allocate the `CopList` leaves `uCop->CopList` NULL; failure to allocate `CopIns` leaves the active list's `CopPtr` NULL. The very next `CWait()` dereferences the active list/cursor before any cleanup or error path. Added GD14352 for the explicit optional `test-graphics` target (`developer/debug/test/graphics/mmakefile.src:5-28`), conditional on either initializer allocation failing. `FreeCopList()`/`FreeMem(NULL, size)` can safely release the partial inner state if the caller handles the return, but the utility currently does not. No allocation failure, copper list or build was run; source-only; no body/path/LOC credit.

GD9615 IntelGMA/Radeon accelerated-backend audit (finding expanded; no new ID or source-body credit; 2026-11-02): checked the remaining direct `Hidd_Gfx::CopyBox` overrides against the existing backend list. IntelGMA's optional driver source is included in its explicit `devs-monitors-intelgma-driver` target while parent aggregate edges are disabled (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/mmakefile.src:13-26,60-67`; `arch/all-pc/drivers/mmakefile.src:7-13`); same-depth framebuffer copies pack signed destination Y with `<< 16` (`intelgma_hiddclass.c:795-865`). Radeon has a parallel explicitly buildable HIDD target with disabled aggregate inclusion (`workbench/hidds/radeon/mmakefile.src:4,10-15`; `arch/all-pc/drivers/mmakefile.src:7-13`); its same-depth blit packs signed `ya/yb` with `<< 16` (`ati_class.c:293-340`; method declared in `radeon.conf`). `CopyBox` declares signed `WORD` destination coordinates, and `BltBitMap()` forwards negative destinations into the HIDD path. Thus a negative destination Y whose rectangle still intersects the target reaches undefined signed-left-shift behavior in both backends before command submission; GPU clipping behavior is not relied on for this consequence. The SAGA override delegates every CopyBox case to its superclass and adds no separate accelerated path (`sagagfx_hiddclass.c:647-678`). The optional backend membership is now stated in GD9615 and the master index. No target, blit, GPU command or runtime operation was used; source-only.

GD9615 NVIDIA coordinate-packing audit (finding expanded; no new ID or source-body credit; 2026-11-02): rechecked the explicitly buildable NVIDIA HIDD (`workbench/hidds/nvidia/mmakefile.src:4,10-14`; parent aggregate disabled by `:4`, `arch/all-pc/drivers/mmakefile.src:7-13`) and its `Hidd_Gfx::CopyBox` registration (`nvidia.conf:15-21`). The same-depth blit and different-depth stretch paths both encode destination Y with `msg->destY << 16` (`nvidiaclass.c:539-542,617-623`). The signed `WORD` CopyBox parameter and generic `BltBitMap()` no-low-edge-clipping path (`gfx.conf:396`; `rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:142-162`) establish that a negative destination Y can reach those expressions when the rectangle still intersects the bitmap. This is C undefined behavior before GPU submission, independent of the unknown device-side clipping behavior. No device or command was exercised; source-only.

GD9615 Raspberry Pi VCGfx CopyBox audit (finding expanded; no new ID or source-body credit; 2026-11-02): traced the method selected by `vcgfx.conf:16-23` through the ARM32 and AArch64 Raspberry Pi package HIDD lists (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:187`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:226`) and its manifest (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vcgfx/mmakefile.src:8-25`). In Copy mode, for two four-byte-per-pixel buffers, the selected method computes `drow_base` directly from signed `destY`/`destX` and the row pitch without low-edge checks, then iterates writes through that pointer (`vcgfx_hiddclass.c:559-598,656-664`). The public CopyBox coordinates are signed WORDs and the selected `BltBitMap()` HIDD branch passes negative destination values through after clipping only the source's negative edge (`gfx.conf:396`; `bltbitmap.c:142-162`). An intersecting rectangle with a negative destination origin therefore reaches out-of-range pointer arithmetic and writes before the destination buffer. No framebuffer or copy was exercised; source-only.

Printer graphics source-hook caller added to GD5744 (2026-11-02; no new finding, body or LOC credit): traced `DRPA_SourceHook` selection and temporary RGB24 HIDD bitmap creation in the already credited `workbench/devs/printer/gfx.c` (`:286-287,563-581`). Each converted source row is copied with `WritePixelArray()` and its returned pixel count is ignored. For a supported source width of 32,769, the inclusive endpoint 32,768 narrows negative in the signed-`WORD` `Rectangle`; `do_render_with_gc()` rejects the rectangle and returns zero (`workbench/libs/cgfx/writepixelarray.c:183-188`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:113-116`). Printer graphics nevertheless scales the unwritten temporary bitmap and continues the job (`gfx.c:581-582,607-651`). Added this optional in-tree caller path to GD5744; the root cause remains CyberGraphX coordinate narrowing, and printer module default-package inclusion is not asserted. Bitmap allocation and printing were not exercised; source-only.


<a id="gd77-wanderer-image-background-caller"></a> GD77 Wanderer image-background caller pass (no new root-cause ID or LOC credit; 2026-11-02): traced the selected `ImageBackFill_CopyScaledBitMap()` wrapper and its scaled-cache setup/draw consumers (`workbench/system/Wanderer/iconwindowbackfill.c:136-171,616-646,845-871`). The root desktop path allocates a destination bitmap without `BMF_CLEAR`, invokes the void `BitMapScale()`, then increments and publishes the cache record without a success indication; later background drawing reads that bitmap through the tiled copy path. Therefore a generic HIDD scratch-allocation failure or planar `LinePattern` allocation failure (depending on the screen bitmap class inherited by the friend allocation) can leave incomplete destination pixels in the retained background cache and still return successful setup. Added this maintained consequence to GD77; this is the existing generic scaler no-write/status-loss root cause, not a separate defect. The planar scratch-allocation path remains independently silent. No allocation failure, scale, cache setup or redraw was run; source-only.


<a id="allocspritedata-old-format-height-boundary-pass"></a> `AllocSpriteDataA()` old-format height boundary pass (GD14457 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-02): re-read the full conversion branch in the already fully credited `rom/graphics/allocspritedataa.c` and checked the public tag plus `SimpleSprite`/`ExtSprite` field widths (`compiler/include/graphics/sprite.h:18-30,37-44`). The tag sets an ULONG height; old-format conversion assigns it to UWORD `height2`, sizes two temporary planes from that truncated value, and loops with UWORD `k` against the original ULONG. At 65,537 rows, the allocation is one row per plane but the loop continues after `k` wraps, writing beyond it. Added GD14457, conditional on an out-of-range height; `SetPointer()` routes old-format input through `MakePointerFromData()` without rejecting negative signed-WORD heights, while `MakePointerFromPrefs()` uses 16-by-16 dimensions. No sprite data, allocation or build was used; source-only.

<a id="amigavideo-wide-sprite-fetch-mode-gd14464"></a>
AmigaVideo wide-sprite fetch-mode mismatch (GD14464 added; no body/path/LOC credit): compared numbered-sprite size validation and advertised maximum with the encoder (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_hiddclass.c:982-1007`; `amigavideo_chipset.c:909,930-977`). Validation accepts up to 64 pixels when `csd->aga` is true. The encoder only selects the 64-pixel fetch width when `csd->aga_enabled` is also true; otherwise it sets the conversion width to 16, loops only over those 16 columns, and returns success. AGA-capable hardware with AGA features disabled can therefore report success while omitting the right side of a 17–64-pixel sprite. Added GD14464 with that configuration condition. No sprite, hardware operation or build was run; source-only.

<a id="amigavideo-shared-sprite-fetch-mode-gd14465"></a>
AmigaVideo shared sprite fetch-mode/buffer-layout pass (GD14465 added; no body/path/LOC credit): compared `new_setsprite()` mode selection, per-buffer layout and VBlank handling (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_chipset.c:930-977,134-145,1844-1851`). Each shape update sets the shared `fmode_spr` to 2 for a wide AGA sprite or 0 otherwise and allocates/populates only that sprite using the selected `fetchsize`. The VBlank loop writes every active sprite's control word at the offset dictated by the current shared value, while `setfmode()` places that value into the copper list. With active sprites of different widths, the mode and control-word location cease to match at least one buffer's layout; the write can land in its image data. Added GD14465, conditional on mixed-width active numbered sprites on AGA-enabled hardware. No sprite, VBlank or hardware operation/build was run; source-only.

Compositor fallback bitmap ownership pass (GD14648 added; no body/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): traced `HIDDCompositorShowSingle()` from both callers (`BitMapStackChanged()` with a NULL stack and its stack-node-allocation failure branch) and checked how its prior display bitmap is created and destroyed. Non-framebuffer display bitmaps come from `AllocBitMap()`, which returns a separate `BitMap` wrapper around the HIDD object; `FreeBitMap()` disposes the object and frees the wrapper (plus an owned screen pixel table where present). `HIDDCompositorShowSingle()` only disposes the HIDD object and clears `displaybitmap`, so the wrapper is leaked on either fallback when an allocated composition bitmap is active. Compared with `HIDDCompositorToggleCompositing()`'s wrapper-aware disposal. Added GD14648. No screen close, allocation failure, or build was run; source-only.
Compositor first-rectangle failure route reconciliation for GD14521 (2026-11-03; no new finding or body/LOC credit): reread `HIDDCompositorRedrawVisibleRegions()` and `OrRectRegion()`. The redraw helper ignores the first rectangle insertion result; failure leaves its new region empty, so opaque-region loops render nothing. The existing GD6251 already lists this call among unchecked region operations; GD14521 records the distinct first-composition caller consequence: toggle still shows the just-allocated composition bitmap after the void redraw returns. Also traced the helper's incremental `drawrect` caller in `BitMapRectChanged()`; the same failed insertion can suppress that damage redraw, while the caller continues update/copy processing. No allocation failure or display operation was run; source-only.
Compositor redraw and damage caller continuation (existing GD10415/GD10416/GD6251/GD10485/GD14521 rechecked; no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): reread `HIDDCompositorRedrawVisibleRegions()`, `HIDDCompositorRedrawAlphaRegions()`, `HIDDCompositorRedrawBitmap()`, `HIDDCompositorRecalculateVisibleRegions()`, and their `BitMapRectChanged()` / `BitMapPositionChange()` callers. Reconciled alpha-region NULL dereference (GD10415), unchecked visibility-region operations and stale/empty regions (GD10416/GD6251), signed damage-message narrowing (GD10485), and full/incremental redraw suppression after region allocation failure (GD14521). Bitmap damage is intersected with per-node visible rectangles before blitting; alpha damage reconstructs the intersecting display area then copies the intermediate result. The caller's final display update uses the source-relative full damage rectangle, while the HIDD driver implementations checked clip against display edges. No separate impact established from this update rectangle in the inspected VESA and SM502 mirroring paths. No region allocation failure, bitmap update, display operation, or build was run; source-only.
Compositor initial redraw region-allocation failure pass (GD14521 added; no body/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): followed `HIDDCompositorRedrawVisibleRegions()` from its render-target check and visible-region recalculation to the `NewRegion()` guard (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:402-424`). On allocation failure it skips the complete redraw and returns void. `NewRegion()` returns NULL on its object allocation failure (`rom/graphics/newregion.c:58-68`). Traced first composition activation: `HIDDCompositorToggleCompositing()` calls the redraw before showing the new bitmap (`compositor_class.c:734-739,757-766`) and does not observe a redraw failure; the outer method then reports active and returns its screen bitmap (`:1247-1265`), which Graphics.library accepts (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:552-604`). BindDrivers product-ID wildcard caller recheck (GD10404 rechecked; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): re-read the `PRODUCT` parser and exact helper signature (`workbench/c/BindDrivers.c:79,123-150,199-210`) against `ExpansionRom.er_Product` (`compiler/include/libraries/configregs.h:16-21`) and the `FindConfigDev()` prototype, documentation and implementation (`rom/expansion/expansion.conf:33`; `findconfigdev.c:24-43,73-105`). The board product field is one byte, but wildcard matching requires signed LONG `-1`. Manufacturer-only tooltypes store `PROD_ANY` (`~0`) as 0xffff; the `UBYTE prod` helper parameter narrows this to 255 before FindConfigDev, so only product-255 boards match. This is the existing GD10404 cause, not a distinct finding; GD10405 separately covers the DiskObject ownership leak. No board, icon, driver load, binding, command or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="gfxfree-videocontrol-color-map-association-lifetime-recheck-gd14540"></a>
GfxFree and VideoControl ColorMap association lifetime recheck (GD14540 added; no new body/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): traced `VTAG_VIEWPORTEXTRA_SET` assignment and the explicitly supported separate-tag ordering through zero-initialized `ViewPortExtra.ViewPort`, `GfxFree()`'s back-pointer-based `cm_vpe` clearing, and `FreeColorMap()`'s subsequent cleanup call (`videocontrol.c:70-75,386-395`; `gfxnew.c:87-96`; `gfxfree.c:72-100`; `freecolormap.c:63-65`). With the ColorMap's VPE set before any attached ViewPort, the node has no back-pointer for `GfxFree()` to follow; explicit free leaves `cm_vpe` stale and later ColorMap cleanup passes the freed node to `GfxFree()` again. No VideoControl, free, memory-reuse or build operation was run; source-only.



<a id="graphics-conf-selected-function-list-signature-and-vector-reconciliation-2026-11-03"></a>
Graphics function-list declaration and implementation signature reconciliation (2026-11-03): compared all 167 parsed function declarations in `rom/graphics/graphics.conf` with their selected `AROS_LH`/`AROS_LHI` implementations. Parameter types, argument counts, register assignments and LVOs matched for the compared entries. Found three return-type declaration differences: `AddDisplayDriverA` is `LONG` in the conf and `ULONG` in its implementation, `DoRenderFunc` is `LONG` versus `ULONG`, and `ReadPixelArray8` is `WORD` versus `LONG`. The first two are same-width signedness differences: current `AddDisplayDriverA` results are the nonnegative `DD_*` constants, and `DoRenderFunc` is an internal pixel-count accumulator; no distinct concrete caller-visible defect was established for them. `ReadPixelArray8` documents a pixel count and computes/returns a `LONG`, while the declared vector result is signed `WORD`; added GD14541 for counts above 32767. All three bodies and representative direct callers were inspected. This is a signature cross-check, not generated ABI output or a compile/runtime test.

<a id="eject-doslist-read-flag-implementation-and-writer-recheck-gd14576"></a>
Eject DOS-list read-flag implementation and writer recheck (GD14576 confirmed; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): inspected the selected Eject lookup (`workbench/c/Eject.c:225-253`) against the actual `LockDosList()`, `UnLockDosList()`, and `FindDosEntry()` implementations. `LockDosList(LDF_READ)` passes the mode validation and returns the non-NULL pseudo-list pointer, but the device semaphore is acquired only under `flags & LDF_ALL` (`rom/dos/lockdoslist.c:55-66,87`); `UnLockDosList(LDF_READ)` similarly releases none (`rom/dos/unlockdoslist.c:49-56`). `FindDosEntry()` requires the DOS list to remain locked (`rom/dos/finddosentry.c:28-39`). The selected console handler provides a concrete concurrent device-list mutation path, acquiring `LDF_DEVICES | LDF_WRITE` during shutdown while walking and updating `dn_Task` (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:1232-1245`). This confirms the missing synchronization in Eject and that the null check on the returned handle does not detect it. Eject reads `dn_Startup` only after the no-op unlock (`Eject.c:240-253`); whether the specific node's storage is reclaimed in an overlapping path remains unproven, so the finding retains a conditional stale-node consequence and does not claim a reproduced use-after-free. No list mutation, Eject command, or build was run; source-only.


<a id="waitforport-break-and-timer-signal-overlap-recheck-gd14571"></a>
WaitForPort break/timer signal overlap and request teardown recheck (GD14571 expanded; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): traced the break loop against Exec `Wait()`, `WaitIO()`, `DeleteIORequest()`, `DeleteMsgPort()` and timer completion/abort (`workbench/c/WaitForPort.c:110-168`; `rom/exec/wait.c:128-135`; `rom/exec/waitio.c:57-76`; `deleteiorequest.c:45-47`; `deletemsgport.c:48-53`; `rom/timer/lowlevel.c:187-220,365-375`; `rom/timer/abortio.c:69-83`). `Wait()` returns every currently active requested bit; WaitForPort checks Ctrl-C/D first and can skip `GetMsg()` when the timer bit is also set. Thus the original pending-request case remains: the timer list can still reference the request when teardown frees it. A second completion race is supported: if the timer has already replied, the early break leaves the request as `NT_REPLYMSG` in the reply-port queue, then `DeleteIORequest()` frees the linked message and `DeleteMsgPort()` discards the remaining queue. `WaitIO()` is the selected API that removes an already replied request from the port. Expanded GD14571 to record both states; the post-reply case does not require claiming later timer access, and no signal, timer request, or build was exercised. Source-only.

<a id="clip-large-chunk-aggregation-overflow-gd14589"></a>
Clip large CHRS chunk aggregation pass (GD14589 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): re-read `fromClip()` buffer growth (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Clip.c:241-320`), the fixed-width AROS `LONG`/`ULONG` definitions (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:35-39`), `ContextNode.cn_Size` (`compiler/include/libraries/iffparse.h:59-66`), and `ReadChunkBytes()` (`workbench/libs/iffparse/readchunkbytes.c:58-85`). Appending a later chunk computes `filebuffer_size + cn_Size + 1` at 32 bits, then copies the full old length into the newly allocated buffer before reading the next chunk. `ReadChunkBytes()` caps against the IFF chunk extent, not the destination capacity. Added GD14589 for a 64-bit `workbench-c-shellcommands` build with sufficient memory and multiple positive CHRS chunks totaling more than 4 GiB; this is separate from GD14588's unchecked `StartNotify()` return. No clipboard, command, file, or build was used; source-only.

<a id="areaend-ellipse-tmpras-error-restoration-gd5759-2026-11-03"></a>
AreaEnd ellipse TmpRas error-restoration recheck (GD5759 expanded; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): compared both capacity-error returns in `rom/graphics/areaend.c:139-140,211-212` with the saved cursor and cleanup at `:79-85,259-281`. The earlier finding covered the polygon CLOSEDRAW return after its MOVE record. The ELLIPSE return has the same missing restore when a preceding closed polygon has already produced a MOVE and fit its own mask; `AreaEllipse()` closes that polygon and appends the ellipse (`rom/graphics/areaellipse.c:84-107`), so AreaEnd processes the MOVE/polygon before it can fail the ellipse-size check. Expanded GD5759's source and trigger to cover both early returns. Existing direct caller audit and public-state scope remain unchanged; no new caller consequence was established. No AreaInfo, TmpRas or raster operation was used; source-only.

<a id="areaend-selected-caller-sequence-audit-2026-11-03"></a>
`AreaEnd()` selected caller sequence recheck (GD5759 retained and scoped to the public API boundary; no new finding or LOC credit; 2026-11-03): enumerated the checked-in direct Workbench calls and re-read the ColorWheel sequences in `workbench/classes/gadgets/colorwheel/support.c:420-423,472-479,713-716,916-925`, Reaction DrawList fill handling (`workbench/classes/reaction/drawlist/drawlistclass.c:218-233`), and Zune Clock/Graph area fills (`workbench/classes/zune/clock/clock.c:270-287`; `workbench/classes/zune/graph/graph.c:700-721`). ColorWheel's `buf[10]` provides two five-word vector records and each shown ellipse is followed by `AreaEnd()` before another area operation; its TmpRas is allocated from the full bitmap or mask dimensions. The inspected DrawList, Clock and Graph paths submit polygon records and do not append an AreaEllipse record in the same AreaInfo sequence. Thus no selected maintained call sequence establishes GD5759's undersized-TmpRas error after a MOVE, and these callers ignore AreaEnd's error result. This does not invalidate the public API state-restoration defect, but scopes its demonstrated trigger to clients whose AreaInfo/TmpRas capacity can produce those error returns. No graphics operation, undersized buffer, or build was used; source-only.

Compositor framebuffer Show-failure teardown pass (GD14652 added; compositor body already credited; no body/path/LOC increment; 2026-11-03): traced the mode-change call at `workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:748-790` and the single-bitmap fallback at `:831-844` into generic framebuffer-backed `Display::Show()` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:1210-1249`). `Show()` copies back the previously shown bitmap before trying to set the framebuffer ModeID; on mode-set failure it returns NULL without replacing `data->shownbm`. Both compositor paths ignore that failure and dispose `olddisplaybitmap`/`displaybitmap`; the generic display object retains the now-freed old bitmap and the next Show path can query it. Added GD14652, scoped to a failed framebuffer mode switch in either transition. Kept separate from GD14520's AllocBitMap failure and GD14649's stale alpha-intermediate dimensions. No mode switch, display or failure was run; source-only.

GD14652 stale-pointer conclusion withdrawn after call-path recheck (2026-11-03; no body/path/LOC credit): reread both compositor cleanup branches and the framebuffer-backed Show failure exit. In the affected framebuffer-backed transitions, the previous compositor display bitmap is `compdata->fb`, and both cleanup paths explicitly avoid disposing it; this pass does not establish a freed `shownbm` or later use-after-free. The narrower caller defect remains: Toggle/ShowSingle keep the NULL Show result as `screenbitmap`, while `display_LoadViewPorts()` records `frontbm = NULL` and returns success, although the failed generic Show leaves the prior framebuffer state and `shownbm` in place (`compositor_class.c:762-790,831-844`; `gfx_displayclass.c:1210-1249`; `graphics_display.c:552-604`). Rewrote GD14652 to state this graphics.library/compositor bookkeeping mismatch and removed the unsupported stale-pointer claim. No mode change or display operation was run; source-only.

GD14652 Show-failure caller and DirectFB restoration pass (2026-11-03; no body/path/LOC credit): rechecked the generic framebuffer `Display::Show()` mode-rejection exit and its caller beyond the earlier compositor trace. A NULL return makes `display_LoadViewPorts()` set `mdd->frontbm = NULL` without `display_FBUninstall()` (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:552-604`); on a direct-FB display, an earlier install leaves `mdd->bm_bak` non-NULL and the old bitmap's object replaced (`:452-475`). The next successful Show calls `display_FBUninstall()` before setting a new `frontbm`, and uninstall writes the saved fields through the now-NULL pointer (`:478-500,576-594`). This establishes a conditional NULL dereference after a rejected ModeID and a later successful Show. The prior claim that compositor cleanup frees a bitmap retained by `data->shownbm` was unsupported and has been removed; compositor is optional to this graphics.library bug. No display operation or mode failure was run; source-only.

GD14652 framebuffer-install caller census (2026-11-03; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): enumerated all `frontbm` assignments and `bm_bak` install/uninstall sites in `rom/graphics/graphics_display.c`, `graphics_intern.h`, and `scrollvport.c`. `display_LoadViewPorts()`'s failed-Show branch is the only path that clears `frontbm` without also unwinding a non-NULL `bm_bak`; its next successful Show reaches the unsafe uninstall before publishing the replacement front bitmap. The other uninstall caller is `ScrollVPort()` (`scrollvport.c:89-98`), which calls uninstall only when `compositor_ScrollBitMap()` reports active composition. After this failed passthrough Show, compositor `displaybitmap` is NULL and its position-change method returns inactive (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:1443-1450`), so this caller does not precede the next-successful-Show trigger. Retained GD14652's narrower trigger and no additional candidate was found in this caller census. No display or scroll operation was run; source-only.



VGAGfx refresh-source boundary recheck (GD5330 restored to detailed findings; 2026-11-03; no body/LOC credit): re-read the existing `vgagfx_support.c` and cursor caller evidence, then traced `erase_mouse()`'s inclusive endpoint (`displayclass.c:392-405`) through `vgaRefreshArea()` (`support.c:445-480`) and bitmap allocation/dimension handling (`bitmapclass.c:48-91,265-288`). Confirmed the box extends one pixel beyond the cursor in each dimension and the refresh clips only to physical display bounds. The cursor origin is clamped to bitmap width/height (`displayclass.c:295-317`), so erasing at the bottom edge of a displayable bitmap smaller than its mode can traverse source rows beyond the allocated `VideoData`; the extra column can cross the logical row end. Replaced the report's unverified GD5330 placeholder with this source-supported, configuration-qualified finding and added its master-index link. All relevant VGA bodies already have full-body credit; no additional path or LOC credit. No bitmap, cursor operation, or hardware was used; source-only.

MST manager enable-failure/retry candidate disposition (no new GD; caller trace; 2026-11-03): in the full `drm_dp_mst_topology_mgr_set_mst()` body, enabling sets `mgr->mst_state` before DPCD/branch/enable writes, so local inspection suggested an early failure could leave the state flag set and make a repeated enable return immediately. Traced the only checked-in enable caller in Nouveau `nv50_mstm_detect()` through `nouveau_dp_detect()`'s common exit (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/dispnv50/disp.c:1521-1544`; `drm/nouveau/nouveau_dp.c:270-289`): every nonzero detection result takes the error path, and the common exit calls `nv50_mstm_remove()` whenever the result is not `NOUVEAU_DP_MST` and the manager is not suspended; removal clears `mstm->is_mst` and calls `drm_dp_mst_topology_mgr_set_mst(..., false)`, which resets manager state and releases any partial primary branch. Thus the candidate's repeated-enable wedge is repaired by the selected caller and is not reported for this path. Nouveau remains excluded from the default target graph; no enable failure, AUX transaction or build was run.

BMP pixel-offset arithmetic follow-up (GD14755; 2026-11-03; no body/path/LOC credit): checked the `ULONG` declaration against `exec/types.h`'s fixed 32-bit `ULONG`/`LONG` types and the loader's `long` buffer counters on 32-bit ABI. On 32-bit builds, the subsequent `filebufbytes -= bfOffBits` is performed in unsigned 32-bit arithmetic and can avoid the guarded refill, after which `filebufpos += bfOffBits` uses the wrapped offset. Added GD14755 with target-dependent consequence qualification. No malformed file was loaded; source-only.

<a id="bmp-reduced-palette-review-gd14760"></a>
BMP reduced-palette length pass (GD14760 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): traced `biClrUsed` extraction through depth-based `numcolors`, `LoadBMP_Colormap()`'s read length, and the pixel-offset calculation. The indexed BI_RGB header field is parsed but ignored; the loader always reads the depth maximum. Microsoft BITMAPINFOHEADER documentation states that for <=8-bpp BI_RGB, the color-table size comes from `biClrUsed`, with zero selecting 2^bpp. A valid small 8-bpp image with two entries is therefore rejected when the loader cannot read 1,024 palette bytes; larger pixel payloads can be consumed as palette data. Added GD14760, distinct from GD14755's malformed pixel-offset input. Existing body and path credits stand. No image or datatype operation was run; source-only.

<a id="vc4-pool-wait-timeout-caller-recheck"></a>
VC4 pool-reuse and OOM-reclaim wait-timeout caller recheck (GD14762 distinguished; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): traced both ignored `v3d_wait_seqno()` results: OOM pool reclamation (`vc4_drm_aros.c:473-490`) and per-pool-set reuse (`:2214-2221`). The helper's timeout path does more than return an error: it resets both V3D control threads, clears `pending_render`, advances `finished_seqno` to the newest submitted sequence, and resnapshots completion counters before returning (`:1184-1225`). Thus the checked callers continue after the helper has aborted in-flight jobs and reconciled the state; the ignored return alone does not establish active GPU reads from freed/reused frame pools. This is distinct from GD14762, where the submission drain has its own timeout and proceeds without invoking that reset. No stuck GPU, pool reuse, reclaim, or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="vc4-pool-reuse-wait-and-rcl-builder-recheck"></a>
VC4 pool wait and RCL construction bounds recheck (GD14762/GD14766 reconciled; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): followed `do_submit_cl()` from tile-count prescan through pool sizing, RCL size estimation, `build_rcl()` writes, and the later prior-job drain. The per-pool `v3d_wait_seqno()` return is ignored, but its timeout path resets both hardware threads and reconciles all submitted sequence numbers before returning; this means the caller's continuation follows an explicit engine abort, distinct from GD14762's later drain timeout that breaks without reset. RCL byte writers suppress stores beyond their supplied capacity and advance a logical offset; `build_rcl()` checks the final offset before reporting success, so the examined bounded builder does not itself write past the allocated RCL. Tile extents are UBYTE-sized and the 256-tile full-span conversion to UBYTE zero, but this pass did not establish a supported VC4 framebuffer/Mesa configuration reaching that dimension or a defined encoding requiring a 256-iteration RCL; no finding promoted. No pool wait, RCL, GPU or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="gd5184-gfxcontrol-public-port-lifetime-caller"></a>
GfxControl caller added to GD5184 (2026-11-03; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): traced `Start()`'s `FindPort("GfxControl")` and `ADBA` `PutMsg()` (`workbench/c/GfxControl.c:139-164`) against `PatchTask`'s `WaitPort()`, `RemPort()` and `DeleteMsgPort()` teardown (`:95-103`). Two concurrent ADBA command invocations can leave one caller using the borrowed port pointer after the other wakes the patch task and frees the port. ExecSMP permits this cross-CPU interval; the `FindPort()` read lock does not pin the returned port after return, and `PutMsg()` subsequently accesses the queue. This is the existing public-port lifetime root cause GD5184, not a separate bug. The command is an explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` target. No command, message or interleaving was run; source-only.

Workbench registered-port lifetime caller trace (GD14774 added; no body/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): traced `RegisterWorkbench()`/`UnregisterWorkbench()` semaphore scope against both handler send sites and the selected Wanderer teardown. The lock protects only the global-pointer assignment/clear; handler reads and `PutMsg()` calls are outside it. The handler separately reads the field for its non-NULL guard and `PutMsg()` argument, so the clear can produce a NULL argument as well as a stale freed pointer. Wanderer unregisters then immediately deletes `wd_CommandPort`; Workbook likewise unregisters and later deletes `AppPort`. Both application parent dependency edges are commented out, so the callers are explicit optional targets. Exec frees either port allocation without coordinating with a sender. A concurrent handler can therefore use the previously read pointer after free. This is distinct from GD14773's screen-object lifetime and GD5184's unrelated public command-port clients. Vulkan-Hpp Queue checkpoint enumeration count/capacity recheck (GD10223/GD10264 reconciliation; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): followed Queue's raw and enhanced `getCheckpointDataNV()`/`getCheckpointData2NV()` declarations at `vulkan_handles.hpp:10975-11020`, implementations at `vulkan_funcs.hpp:20056-20170`, and RAII vector helpers at `vulkan_raii.hpp:22972-23003`. The `uint32_t` count is written by the initial void count query, then the vector is resized and that same count supplies the output-array capacity on the fill call; Vulkan specifies the fill call overwrites it with the number actually written and writes at most the supplied capacity ([NV](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetQueueCheckpointDataNV.html), [NV2](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetQueueCheckpointData2NV.html)). The wrappers trim the vector if fewer records are written. No uninitialized-count or over-capacity path established; no Vulkan call/build was run; source-only.

<a id="vulkan-query-pool-scalar-result-capacity-gd14809"></a>Vulkan-Hpp scalar query-result capacity trace (GD14809 added; 2026-11-04; no whole-file or LOC credit): read the complete overload declaration at `vulkan_handles.hpp:11625-11634` and implementation at `vulkan_funcs.hpp:2019-2039`. `queryCount` is an unrestricted `uint32_t`; implementation creates one `DataType`, passes `sizeof(DataType)` as `dataSize`, and forwards the caller's count and stride unchanged. `rg` found no checked-in calls to `getQueryPoolResult()` / explicit template instantiations. The Vulkan command reference defines `queryCount` as the number retrieved, requires `dataSize` to hold each query result, and requires a valid `dataSize`-byte output array (VUID 00817): https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetQueryPoolResults.html. A scalar type and `queryCount > 1` therefore make the convenience overload's supplied capacity insufficient for ordinary multi-result layouts; retained as conditional because driver behavior after the violated valid-usage condition is not specified and a custom `DataType` could represent a larger fixed buffer. Added GD14809 to the detailed report and index. No API call or build was run; source-only.

<a id="do-collision-callback-selection-recheck-gd5763"></a>GELS collision-mask callback selection recheck (GD5763 retained; 2026-11-04; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): re-read the complete `DoCollision()` body and compared its collision-table lookup with `SetCollision()`, `InitGels()`, and the public `collTable`/`GelsInfo` declarations (`rom/graphics/docollision.c:189-204`; `setcollision.c:44-55`; `initgels.c:78-85`; `compiler/include/graphics/gels.h:204-206`; `rastport.h:33-48`). A collision computes the directed intersection `CurVSprite->MeMask & _CurVSprite->HitMask`, scans from bit zero, and breaks after the first set bit whether or not that slot contains a callback. `SetCollision()` stores one callback at the requested table index; `InitGels()` clears only slot zero. The public local comments do not specify whether multiple matching mask bits must dispatch every available callback or only the lowest matching index, and no checked-in `InitGels()`/`DoCollision()` caller resolves initialization ownership. Therefore this behavior is recorded as an API-contract question, not a new defect. Reconfirmed the separate one-word row overread under GD5763. No collision list, table, callback, or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="muiscreen-autoclose-worker-failed-close-race-gd5097"></a>MUIScreen AutoClose worker failed-close race (GD5097 expanded; 2026-11-04; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit): traced the task's `SA_PubTask`/`SA_PubSig` setup (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/openpubscreen.c:60-75`) through `UnlockPubScreen()` signaling the owner when `psn_VisitorCount` reaches zero (`rom/intuition/unlockpubscreen.c:78-105`) and the worker scan (`muiscreen_init.c:72-88`). The worker tests only `screen->FirstWindow`, removes the AutoClose node, then calls `CloseScreen()`; Intuition's close action also rejects a public screen with nonzero `psn_VisitorCount` (`rom/intuition/closescreen.c:331-348`). A new `LockPubScreen()` between the zero-count signal and worker processing therefore leaves `FirstWindow` empty but can make the close fail; after the visitor later unlocks, the worker has no node to retry. Expanded GD5097's same AutoClose-record-loss root cause to include this task path, distinct from GD5098's `PubScreenNode` lifetime race. The worker's CloseScreen result is ignored as well. No visitor timing, screen close, or task scheduling was exercised; source-only.

<a id="muiscreen-autoclose-worker-startup-readiness-gd14812"></a>MUIScreen AutoClose worker startup readiness pass (GD14812 added; 2026-11-04): reread the complete selected initializer and `MUIS_OpenPubScreen()` path (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/muiscreen_init.c:20-53,56-96`; `openpubscreen.c:60-75,89-118`). `libInit()` returns success once `AddTask()` succeeds; the worker publishes `muisb_taskMsgPort` only after it starts and `CreateMsgPort()` succeeds. The open routine checks that field once and silently omits allocation of the AutoClose node and `SA_PubTask`/`SA_PubSig` tags when it is NULL, while still opening the screen. Traced `AddTask()` through `NewAddTask()`/`TaskLaunch()` (`rom/exec/addtask.c:82-88`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:25-75,325-329`): task launch has no readiness handshake, and an equal- or higher-priority caller need not yield before its next call. VMware SVGA cursor-shape allocation-failure caller recheck (GD14656/GD14662/GD14663 retained; no new GD or source-body/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): followed `VMWareSVGADisplay__Hidd_Display__SetCursorShape()` through `AllocVec()` failure and its caller `MonitorClass__MM_SetPointer()` (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/vmwaresvga_displayclass.c:160-187`; `rom/intuition/monitorclass.c:1920-1957`). HEIC import support-process priority/acknowledgement follow-up (GD6304–GD6308 rechecked; no new finding or body/LOC credit; 2026-11-04): traced `CreateImportProcess()`'s `CreateNewProcTags()` without `NP_Priority` through DOS `CreateNewProc` defaults: the child inherits the creator's `pr_Task.tc_Node.ln_Pri` (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:121-135,399-404`). Thus the child busy-wait after `ReplyMsg()` does not by itself establish the suspected lower-priority-caller starvation path; parent and support process start at equal priority. The selected PC scheduler explicitly reschedules equal-priority ready work after the current quantum (`arch/all-pc/kernel/kernel_scheduler.c:114-132`), and `WaitPort()` blocks the caller until the reply. After replying, the worker's loop reads only its own volatile stack flag and the saved result; the caller reads that flag, acknowledges it, and then frees the reply message, so no post-reply use of the freed message was found (`workbench/classes/datatypes/heic/heicclass.c:270-307,309-359`). This closes only the support-process priority/acknowledgement concern; codec implementation and external HEIC support-library behavior remain open as recorded in the original adapter pass. No decoder process, priority change, message or build was run; source-only.

Generic display software-cursor coordinate-width trace (GD14855 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-05): compared `cursor_Draw()` arithmetic with the shared HIDD contracts. Mouse position and hotspot are signed WORD parameters; bitmap LeftEdge/TopEdge are WORD attributes; the computed `LONG` result is stored in WORD cursor_drawX/Y and read back before off-screen clipping. Thus valid signed inputs can produce an out-of-range intermediate that wraps before clipping. HIDD bitmap dimensions are UWORD, so a wrapped coordinate can be within a larger valid framebuffer. GD14858 palette/conversion race ordering recheck (existing finding retained; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): inspected the current implementations in statement order. Generic bitmap `SetColors()` calls colormap `SetColors()` before clearing `invlut`, and neither operation holds `data->lock` (`gfx_bitmapclass.c:1308-1359`). ColorMap growth allocates and copies a new array, frees the old array, then publishes `clut.colors` (`gfx_colormapclass.c:249-264`). `true_to_pal()` reads the colormap entries and cache directly and writes a computed cache value after its palette scan (`gfx_bitmapconvertpixels.c:267-275,298-343`); the selected generic `PutImage()` path calls conversion without acquiring the bitmap lock (`gfx_bitmapclass.c:2899-2931`). This confirms the concurrent read/free window, stale cache republish after invalidation, and first-allocation lost-pointer leak already described by GD14858. No second root or revised scope is needed. No palette or bitmap operation was run; source-only.

NVIDIA HIDD CopyBox GD9615 path-state recheck (no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-05): inspected both registered `NV__Hidd_Gfx__CopyBox()` engines against the NV DMA command definitions (`workbench/hidds/nvidia/nvidiaclass.c:461-650`; `nv_dma.h:155-185`). Compositor alpha intermediate mode-transition path recheck (GD14649 retained; 2026-11-05; no new LOC credit): traced `UpdateDisplayMode()` through selected mode/depth and `displayrect` update, then `HIDDCompositorToggleCompositing()` allocation/disposal and both full and partial redraw copies (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/displaymode.c:82-95,232-260`; `compositor_class.c:621-641,692-731,778-811,402-540`). The generic HIDD copy path forwards same-format chunky requests to the raw row-copy helpers without clipping to bitmap bounds (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1045-1095`; helpers in `gfx_bitmapmemblit.c`).
