Existing GD14649 retained, with its configuration boundary confirmed. No build or display operation was run; source-only.

Compositor alpha direct-source bounds and format recheck (2026-11-05; no new finding or LOC credit): traced every `HIDDCompositorRedrawBitmap()` alpha call through visible-region construction and stack admission (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:147-280,283-327,1168-1215`). Each source rectangle is clipped by intersecting the screen display rectangle with the bitmap's screen-space bounding rectangle, and the source pointer subtracts that same bitmap offset. Position changes are clamped to display/bitmap extents before being stored (`:109-140,1360-1415`). Alpha is retained only for ARGB32/BGRA32/RGBA32/ABGR32 standard pixel formats, matching the four-byte source offset (`:1183-1208`). The returned direct-access dimensions are not used, but the traced rectangle construction establishes in-bounds coordinates for ordinary non-overflowing bitmap dimensions; no additional defect established. No bitmap access or display operation was run; source-only.

GD9832 8-bit chunky blit alignment recheck (retained; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): recalculated the minimal overlapping request `srcX=0,destX=1,width=4,height=1` with a 4-byte-aligned shared buffer. The backward branch sets end pointers to `base+4` and `base+5`; phase is computed only from `src_start`, so its zero phase reaches a 32-bit store at `base+1` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapmemblit.c:215-295`). The generic GFX HIDD selects this helper for same-format one-byte chunky buffers (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1024-1074`) and does not require a destination-alignment match; the helper comment itself warns that these long accesses can trap on 68k. The shared GFX HIDD module includes this implementation (`rom/hidds/gfx/mmakefile.src:10-28`), and the m68k-Amiga architecture-specific HIDD build imports that generic source tree (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/gfx/mmakefile.src:1-14`). GD9832 remains supported for processors with strict alignment (including the 68000/68010 class); no CPU access or build was run. Source-only.

GD9832 forward-copy alignment extension (finding scope broadened; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): rechecked the non-overlap branch of `CopyMemBox8()`. With separately allocated 8-bit bitmap buffers aligned to four bytes, `srcX=0`, `destX=1`, and width at least four, source alignment yields phase zero while the destination address is one-byte misaligned; the first bulk `ULONG` store is therefore odd-addressed even though the buffers do not overlap. The generic HIDD dispatch still selects this helper for matching one-byte formats (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1040-1074`). Expanded GD9832's trigger in the detailed report to include this independent public `BltBitMap()` case as well as its overlapping backward-copy case. No operation or 68k execution was run; source-only.

Generic 16-bit CopyMemBox row-alignment audit (GD14870 added; 2026-11-05; no source-body/LOC credit): traced the HIDD constructor's explicit `BytesPerRow` tag through its minimum-only validation, `ChunkyBM` allocation and row pitch, generic `CopyBox` dispatch, and `CopyMemBox16()`'s typed accesses (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:776-803,923-929,1038-1050`; `gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:50-75`; `gfx_hiddclass.c:1024-1074`; `gfx_bitmapmemblit.c:300-383`). A width-one 16-bit bitmap has default minimum stride 32 bytes (default alignment 16 pixels); explicit stride 33 is accepted, and row 1's source/destination `UWORD` access is odd-addressed. Confirmed the generic HIDD is included for the m68k-Amiga build (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src:158,375`; `arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/gfx/mmakefile.src:1-14`). No checked-in odd-stride producer was found, so GD14870 is limited to direct HIDD clients; strict-alignment CPU path is source-established, not executed. No bitmap or copy was created; source-only.

Generic ChunkyBM ModeID-change allocation-failure trace (GD14871 added; 2026-11-05; no body/LOC credit): followed `CBM__Root__Set()` through `OOP_DoSuperMethod()` into `BM__Root__Set()`'s ModeID mutation, then through pixel-size refresh, size-growth allocation, early failure return, and `PutPixel()` address calculation (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:1018-1065,109-150`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:4435-4480`). On failed buffer growth, base attributes describe the new mode, cached bytes-per-pixel has changed, cached bytes-per-row and owned buffer size remain old; a subsequent write at a valid new-mode row can exceed old `bufsize`. Checked the Display_CreateObject contract: a display driver chooses the framebuffer's bitmap class; generic ChunkyBM can own memory when no buffer tag is supplied (`gfx_displayclass.c:735-755,800-875`; `gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:56-82`). No checked-in producer of that exact framebuffer/class combination was found, so retained as a conditional direct-driver configuration finding. No allocation failure or mode switch was induced; source-only.

GD14871 Set return and post-failure consumer recheck (retained, trigger qualified; 2026-11-05; no LOC credit): confirmed ChunkyBM overrides Root::Set in the registered `CLID_Hidd_ChunkyBM` method list (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:338-359`) and its override is declared `VOID`, calls the superclass without preserving a result, then returns immediately on buffer-growth allocation failure (`gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:980-1018,1046-1058`). `OOP_SetAttrs()` documents its result as undefined (`rom/oop/setattrs.c:39-64`), although generic display Show checks it after changing framebuffer ModeID (`gfx_displayclass.c:1232-1241`); that check does not restore the already-mutated base bitmap fields. `PutPixel()` remains a registered bitmap method and computes the write pointer from the refreshed bytes-per-pixel and stale cached row stride (`gfx.conf:349-359`; `gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:107-118`; Set refresh at `:1028-1065`). This supports the state inconsistency and possible out-of-buffer access when the conditional owned-buffer framebuffer mode-change path is used. No allocator failure, Set call or pixel write was induced; source-only.

ChunkyBM buffer replacement synchronization check (GD14871 boundary; 2026-11-05; no new finding): the ModeID setter reallocates/frees `data->buffer` without taking the base bitmap `data->lock`, and `CBM__Hidd_BitMap__PutPixel()` reads that pointer without taking the lock (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:97-100,107-118,1046-1065`; the base lock is used for visibility/update coordination in `gfx_bitmapclass.c:5099-5132,5250-5252`). Display `Show()` holds `fbsem` while changing ModeID (`gfx_displayclass.c:1199-1239`), but the pixel method does not acquire that semaphore. This leaves a source-level unsynchronized path if those APIs execute concurrently on the same framebuffer. I did not promote a separate race finding because the repository sources reviewed here do not establish whether external HIDD clients/graphics callers must serialize bitmap drawing with display mode changes; GD14871 remains focused on its deterministic post-allocation-failure state inconsistency. No concurrent operation was run; source-only.

GD14535 64-bit configuration-scope recheck (finding scope corrected; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): confirmed `ULONG` is explicitly 32-bit while `IPTR` is pointer-width (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:35-44,82-86`), and `chunkybm_data.bufsize` is declared `ULONG` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_intern.h:76-85`). For GD14535's 32,768×32,769 ARGB32 bitmap, `height * bytesperrow` is 4,295,098,368 bytes. On 32-bit it wraps modulo 2^32; on 64-bit the product fits `IPTR` but narrows to 131,072 when assigned to `bufsize`, and `AllocVec()` receives that stored value (`gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:75-76`). Thus the same undersized allocation applies on both pointer widths. Updated GD14535's affected configuration in the detailed report; the master index summary already stated 32-bit `ULONG`. No large bitmap or image write was performed; source-only.

GD14535 resize-path extension (finding scope broadened; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): rechecked the owned-buffer mode-change branch of `CBM__Root__Set()`. After testing the full `height * bpr` product against existing `bufsize`, it narrows that product into `ULONG newsize`, passes the narrowed value to `AllocVec()`, and stores it as the new buffer size (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:1045-1061`). On 64-bit builds the comparison can see the full product but allocation still receives the narrowed value; on 32-bit builds the comparison product can itself wrap. Thus successful undersized allocation is possible through both constructor and resize paths. This is the GD14535 size-narrowing defect, separate from GD14871's allocation-failure rollback issue. No resize or allocation was performed; source-only.

Generic input HIDD pending-event extent recheck (GD10092/GD10093 retained; no new finding or path/LOC credit; 2026-11-05): traced the `aHW_Input_EventSize` tag from `InputHW__Root__New()` to `InputHW__BufferPendingEvent()` and both event sources (`rom/hidds/input/inputsubsystem.c:79-92,128-168,240-257`). The subsystem stores the size only when it is at most `IHD_PENDING_EVSIZE` (8); larger values become zero, which disables copying, so the fixed pending-slot write is bounded. The selected keyboard subsystem declares `sizeof(struct pHidd_Kbd_Event)`; mouse declares no fixed size and its PushEvent path can forward an original or stack-converted extended event, so it intentionally does not get buffered. No overflow finding is established. The shared pending count remains unsynchronized on ExecSMP (GD10092); consumer callback traversal versus dispose remains a separate finding (GD10093). No event or concurrent operation was run.

ChunkyBM ModeID-change versus concurrent framebuffer-operation boundary (GD14871 concurrency qualification; 2026-11-05; no new finding or path/LOC credit): traced the selected generic display Show route through `Display__Hidd_Display__Show()`'s `fbsem` and framebuffer ModeID setter (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:1199-1240`), then compared CursorFB's drawing semaphore with `cursorfb_set()` forwarding (`gfx_cursorfbclass.c:43-75,119-150`) and the direct ChunkyBM buffer accesses in `CBM__Hidd_BitMap__PutPixel()`/`CBM__Root__Set()` (`gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:97-119,980-1065`). The mode change's `fbsem` is not the CursorFB operation's cursor semaphore, and the ChunkyBM setter itself does not take the bitmap lock. This leaves a plausible interval for an operation to overlap the update/free, but the full Intuition/layer and external HIDD caller serialization contract has not been established; no separate race finding is promoted. Existing GD14871 remains scoped to the independently established allocation-failure state mismatch. No mode change, drawing operation or concurrency test was run.

ChunkyBM/Framebuffer semaphore reconciliation (supersedes the tentative overlap boundary above; GD14871 unchanged; 2026-11-05): completed the lock identity check. `GfxDisplay_CursorSem()` returns `&HIDDDisplayData::fbsem` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:287-294`); `Display__Hidd_Display__Show()` holds that semaphore across `OOP_SetAttrsTags(data->framebuffer, ModeID, ...)` and buffer-mode transition (`:1199-1240`); and CursorFB pixel/drawing methods acquire the semaphore through `CFB_INIT` before forwarding to the real bitmap (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_cursorfbclass.c:43-75,207-230`). Thus selected draw calls routed through the installed CursorFB framebuffer wrapper cannot overlap the selected Show-driven ModeID change. The earlier statement that those paths used different semaphores is corrected. Direct SetAttrs or direct real-bitmap method calls outside this selected wrapper route were not established from in-tree callers; no separate concurrency finding is supported. GD14871's post-failure stale-state consequence is unchanged. No display operation or interleaving was run.


CursorFB direct-access lease versus ChunkyBM mode replacement (GD14872 added; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): traced the direct-access method table and wrapper forwarding (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_cursorfbclass.c:43-75,481-482`), generic ChunkyBM pointer/lease methods (`gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:932-960`), Cybergraphics public lock/unlock path (`workbench/libs/cgfx/lockbitmaptaglist.c:100-118,145-152`; `unlockbitmap.c:45-66`), and mode-change buffer replacement under the Display Show semaphore (`gfx_displayclass.c:1199-1240`; `gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:1045-1064`). Normal CursorFB drawing methods hold the display semaphore, but direct access only forwards and does not retain that semaphore until Release; generic ChunkyBM frees the prior owned buffer when a growth allocation succeeds. Added GD14872 for the conditional cross-task stale-pointer lifetime. This is independent of GD14871's allocation-failure state mismatch. No bitmap lock, mode switch, interleaving or build was run.


GD14871/GD14872 HeadlessGfx reachability qualification (2026-11-05; no LOC credit): traced `HeadlessGfxDisplay::CreateObject()` selecting its `HeadlessGfxBM` subclass for displayable bitmaps, and that subclass's `Root::New()` delegating to generic ChunkyBM without an external buffer tag (`rom/hidds/gfx/headless/headlessgfx_hiddclass.c:344-375`; `headlessgfx_bitmapclass.c:34-43`; `headlessgfx.conf:45-51`). Generic Gfx reports no hardware cursor support by default, so display setup selects CursorFB (`gfx_hiddclass.c:860-869`; `gfx_displayclass.c:519-531`). HeadlessGfx exposes LUT8, RGB15_LE, RGB16_LE and BGRA32 modes; the Cybergraphics conversion table has entries for those standard pixel formats (`headlessgfx_hiddclass.c:66-126`; `gfx_pixfmtclass.c:96-120`). This establishes a concrete in-tree optional route for both the owned-buffer mode-change findings. The HeadlessGfx aggregate target remains commented out in its makefile (`headless/mmakefile.src:4-5,23-24`), so default-image inclusion is not asserted. GD14871 still requires allocation failure; GD14872 still requires direct access overlapping a growth mode change. No build, allocation failure, bitmap access, or mode switch was performed.


X11 clipboard read-state recheck (GD14846/GD14847 retained; GD14873 added; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): reread all of `arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11_clipboard.c` in source order and traced command admission, direct and INCR selection replies, property acknowledgements, byte-buffer ownership, and the waiting message. Confirmed GD14846 remains limited to accepting an unexpected 8-bit property type as UTF8 text, and GD14847 to the valid empty-INCR completion path returning failure. Added GD14873: in INCR state a property with `actual_format != 8` bypasses every reply/cleanup branch, but is still deleted; `hostclipboardmsg` and the INCR state remain set, causing `x11clipboard_handle_commands()` to reject later commands while the current caller waits indefinitely (`x11_clipboard.c:88-92,273-317,397-404`). This requires an external owner to send an invalid-format chunk; it is a separate stuck-request consequence from GD14846's incorrect successful data return. No clipboard transfer, X11 event, caller wait, allocation failure, or build was run; source-only.

X11 clipboard outstanding-request caller confirmation (GD14873 strengthened; 2026-11-05; no body/path/LOC credit): traced the public `HOST_CLIPBOARD` read request in `developer/debug/test/misc/hostcb.c:118-121,146-153` through the X11 event task (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11.c:595-596`) into the serialized command handler. The caller does `WaitPort(replyport)` and then consumes the reply without a timeout or alternate cancellation path. On GD14873's non-8-bit INCR chunk, the X11 handler deletes the property but does not `ReplyMsg()`, while retaining `hostclipboardmsg`; subsequent commands are also held by the early return at `x11_clipboard.c:88-92`. This confirms the selected hostcb path blocks indefinitely for that malformed external response. No clipboard request, X11 event, or task was run.

Intuition asynchronous-action result consumer census (GD14825 boundary; 2026-11-05; no new finding or path/LOC credit): enumerated all 14 selected `DoASyncAction()` call expressions in `rom/intuition/` (`ChangeWindowBox`, move/front/back, show/hide, activation, screen depth/title, decorator removal, and raster scrolling). All ignore the Boolean result. `DoASyncAction()` executes inline only on `InputDeviceTask`; otherwise a failed `AllocVecPooled()` returns FALSE without queuing the action (`inputhandler_actions.c:642-672`). The PopupMenu `ChangeWindowBox()` path remains the confirmed selected caller that immediately waits for the resulting `IDCMP_NEWSIZE` (`workbench/libs/popupmenu/window.c:130-143`; `pm.c:408,431`). This census does not establish that each other public action has a caller that waits for, or otherwise requires, the action to complete; no broader finding is promoted without those caller contracts. No action-pool failure, window operation, or build was run.


<a id="vmm-manager-early-library-failure-leaves-start-message-gd14874"></a>
Optional VMM manager early library-failure launch-message ownership trace (GD14874 added; 2026-11-05; no new body/path/LOC credit): traced `StartVMM()`'s sender allocation and enqueue through `VM_Manager()` and `Init_VM_Manager()`. The manager runs `OpenLibs()` before receiving the startup request; a required-library/version failure returns before the process-port `WaitPort()`/`GetMsg()`, after which the manager sends a distinct `VMCMD_InitFailed` reply and exits. Also checked the manager-reply allocation failure branch: it signals the starter and exits before consuming the request, so `StartVMM()` wakes to an empty starter port and overwrites its pointer with NULL. In both branches the queued sender-owned `StartMsg` has no remaining release path. Expanded GD14874 to cover both early exits, scoped to the explicitly buildable optional VMM MUI/handler path. Existing EK9488 remains the distinct failure where allocation of the manager's reply causes the starter's WaitPort to wait indefinitely. No VMM launch, library failure or allocation was induced; source-only.
CursorFB direct-access race selected-caller recheck (GD14872; 2026-11-05; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): enumerated checked-in `LockBitMapTagList()` callers. `workbench/libs/decorator/drawfuncs.c:958,1018-1024,1085-1105,1144-1161` holds access across direct `HIDD_BM_PutPixel()` writes on a RastPort bitmap, providing an in-tree sustained lock interval; the font datatype uses a newly allocated offscreen bitmap (`fontclass.c:314-342`), and AHIRecord only probes pixel size before immediately unlocking (`AHIRecord.c:331-341`). This narrows those latter two as non-triggers but does not remove the decorator/other-task mode-switch overlap: CursorFB forwards obtain/release without pinning the old buffer, while generic ChunkyBM mode changes can free it. No direct lock or mode switch was exercised; source-only.
GD14874 all-call-site and partial-library-cleanup closure (2026-11-05; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): enumerated every `StartVMM()` call in the optional MUI GUI and commodities handlers (`main.c`, `mui.c`, `menus.c`, `aloha.c`). These callers may continue to GUI shutdown after a failed start, but do not regain ownership of the already-enqueued message. Rechecked `Cleanup_VM_Manager()` on both pre-receive failure paths: its `CloseLibs()` helper closes each non-NULL library base, including any libraries opened before a later `OpenLibs()` failure, so partial library acquisition is not a separate confirmed leak. GD14874 is scoped to the still-queued launch-message allocation. No VMM process, library failure, or allocation failure was induced; source-only.
Generic GFX HIDD CopyBox implementation recheck (GD14875 added; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:972-1290`, focused implementation review; no new whole-file/LOC credit): traced dispatch from the documented UWORD width through the direct chunky-buffer fast path and per-pixel fallback, including overlap direction, pixel-format conversion, palette mapping, GC foreground restoration and CursorFB semaphore/cursor bracketing. Added GD14875: fallback loop endpoints/counters are signed WORD while the public width is UWORD; widths above 32767 wrap, and unchecked planar GetPixel/PutPixel derive offsets from the resulting negative coordinates. No checked-in caller with a >32767 width or configured display route was found, so the finding is conditional on a direct valid HIDD client using a sufficiently wide bitmap and fallback path. No bitmap operation or build was run; source-only.

Generic framebuffer Show mode-rejection caller recheck (GD14652; 2026-11-05; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): re-read the base `Display::Show()` mode-change failure branch and `display_LoadViewPorts()` plus `display_FBInstall()`/`display_FBUninstall()` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:1173-1294`; `rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:440-500,520-604`). Confirmed the failure occurs after cursor erase and before target restoration; the NULL return enters the graphics.library empty-screen bookkeeping branch, which clears `frontbm` without uninstalling an existing direct-framebuffer substitution. A subsequent successful Show calls uninstall while `bm_bak` is still set, and uninstall uses the now-NULL `frontbm` as its destination bitmap. This matches GD14652's existing trigger and consequence; no independent defect or additional selected caller was established. No mode switch, display call, or build was run; source-only.

GD14652 framebuffer-mode configuration boundary recheck (2026-11-05; no new finding or coverage credit): compared graphics.library's `vHidd_FrameBuffer_Direct`/`Mirrored` flag setup with the generic GFX fallback and LinuxFB's explicit `vHidd_FrameBuffer_Mirrored` attribute (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:157-169`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:760-770`; `arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/linuxfbgfx_hiddclass.c:86-96`). This confirms LinuxFB is relevant only to GD14652's generic software-cursor disappearance on rejected mode change; it cannot enter the direct-framebuffer `DF_DirectFB`/`frontbm` plus `bm_bak` uninstall failure. The report already scopes these consequences separately. No display mode, Show call, or build was run; source-only.


GD14872 direct-access lock contract comparison (2026-11-05; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): checked Cybergraphics `LockBitMapTagList()` documentation, which promises exclusive direct access until unlock (`workbench/libs/cgfx/lockbitmaptaglist.c:31-45`), against the selected bitmap method implementations. The CursorFB-to-ChunkyBM route returns an owned-buffer pointer without retaining a lock and has an empty release method (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_cursorfbclass.c:481-482`; `gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:932-960`); Nouveau and Radeon implementations hold bitmap/engine locks across their corresponding Obtain/Release calls (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_bitmapclass.c:764-781`; `workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_bitmap.c:1176-1219`). This confirms the missing lease protection is a contract mismatch in the optional HeadlessGfx route, not merely an inferred expectation of the generic method. No bitmap access, mode switch or build was performed; source-only.


GD10522 mixed-font IntuiText producer follow-up (2026-11-05; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit): rechecked selected producers that assign `ITextFont` in linked or array-backed text. GadTools `BuildGadgetText()` links the underline-split second node and assigns both nodes custom `TextAttr` records (`workbench/libs/gadtools/basicfuncs.c:137-150`); its ordinary generated entry is unlinked. `requester_makebody()` assigns the same supplied font to every generated line (`rom/intuition/requesters.h:130-158`), and the checked AHIRecord screen GUI assigns the screen font to each displayed entry with a NULL font before `PrintIText()` (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/AHIRecord.c:299-306`; the low-level hard-disk recorder does likewise for its sole displayed entry at `workbench/devs/AHI/Examples/Low-level/HardDiskRecord/GUI.c:215-225`). These checked producers do not establish a custom-font entry followed by an unfonted entry; GD10522 remains a public-caller conditional, not an established in-tree rendering defect. Source-only.


GD14875 signed-overflow and public-caller qualification (2026-11-05; finding wording corrected; no body/path/LOC credit): rechecked the fallback loops and planar pixel offsets, then traced the public graphics.library `BltBitMap()` vector (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:27-38,128-174`). `BltBitMap()` accepts a signed `WORD` width and clips that width to source/destination bounds before the HIDD call, so this maintained route cannot pass a positive width above 32,767. The HIDD CopyBox method itself accepts a `UWORD` width. For a direct HIDD request above the signed range, assignment to `WORD` is implementation-defined and subsequent counter overflow is undefined behavior; the prior report's definite wraparound phrasing was too strong. Under wraparound target code generation, negative coordinates reach planar `GetPixel()`/`PutPixel()` offsets without bounds checks, but that concrete access effect is compiler/target-dependent. No other checked-in wide-width caller was established. No bitmap operation or build was run; source-only.


Generic GFX HIDD `CopyBoxMasked` overlap recheck (GD4129 confirmed; duplicate GD14876 withdrawn; 2026-11-05; focused body/caller review, no whole-file or LOC credit): reread `copyboxmasked_impl()` and wrapper (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1380-1651`), method overlap contract (`:1340-1370`), public `BltMaskBitMapRastPort()` bridge (`rom/graphics/bltmaskbitmaprastport.c:28-38,96-145`), and the existing GD4129 section. Confirmed the existing report's 1,000-pixel-wide example: 4,000 bytes per row against the 4,096-pixel `NUMPIX` budget gives one row per chunk; the first downward-overlap write changes the next chunk's source row. The maintained public caller supports using the same bitmap for source and destination, and the generic CopyBox path explicitly reverses row traversal for downward overlap (`gfx_hiddclass.c:1003-1010`). GD14876 was a duplicate and is removed from the detailed report and index. GD4130 separately covers unsupported draw modes and remains distinct. No bitmap operation, allocation failure, or build was induced; source-only.


Masked-blit in-tree minterm caller census (GD4130 scope rechecked; 2026-11-05; no new finding/path/LOC credit): enumerated active `BltMaskBitMapRastPort()` call expressions across ROM, Workbench, datatypes, and classes, excluding generated vector thunks, inline comments, and the unrelated `NewBltMaskBitMapRastPort()` compatibility helper. Checked explicit minterms at the selected callers: the maintained rendering calls use `0xE0`/`ABC|ABNC|ANBC` (mapped GC Or), `0xC0` (Copy), or `0xE2` (same high minterm bits, mapped Or); the colorwheel's `minterm` parameter is called with `0xE0` from its sole selected caller. Decorator `BLIT_MINTERM_COPYTM` is defined as `0xE0`. No maintained caller was found passing one of the unsupported modes to the generic `CopyBoxMasked()` path. GD4130 therefore remains an API/direct-HIDD conditional behavior with high confidence in the implementation defect and no demonstrated in-tree trigger. No masked blit or build was run; source-only.


<a id="amigavideo-masked-draw-mode-audit"></a>
AmigaVideo accelerated masked-copy draw-mode audit (GD14877 added; 2026-11-05; implementation and dispatch recheck, no whole-file or LOC credit): read `AmigaVideoCl__Hidd_Gfx__CopyBoxMasked()` and `blit_copybox_mask()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_hiddclass.c:935-951`; `amigavideo_blitter.c:245-420`), checked the selected method entry in `amigavideo.conf`, the HIDD documented GC-mode contract (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:397`), generic fallback handling (`gfx_hiddclass.c:1518-1547`), and public minterm mapping. The override passes mode, but the helper never reads it and always programs `0xCA`; generic AndInverted complements the source under the mask. Added GD14877 for that output mismatch when both bitmaps take the AmigaVideo Chip RAM blitter path. The current in-tree `BltMaskBitMapRastPort()` caller census found Copy/Or-style minterms, not the triggering `0x20`; public/direct clients remain the trigger. No operation or build was run; source-only.


<a id="amigavideo-blitter-size-limit-audit"></a>

<a id="wav-sample-length-type-trace-gd14883"></a>
### WAV sample-length type trace (GD14883)

Reread the WAV writer's `GetDTAttrs()` call and traced the `SDTA_SampleLength` output through the public `GetDTAttrsA()` storage contract into `Sound_GET()`. The API passes each caller address as `IPTR *`, and `Sound_GET()` writes a full `IPTR`; WAV supplies a `LONG *`. On 64-bit targets that is a 4-byte destination for a pointer-sized output. On 32-bit targets, the WAV writer still stores the `ULONG` length as signed `LONG`, so values at or above `0x80000000` make its positive-only frame loop skip sample encoding. The 8SVX reader sources this attribute from unsigned sample-count fields and assigns the resulting length to the Sound datatype. Added GD14883 covering these target-dependent consequences. No large object was allocated or exported, no build was run; source-only.

<a id="sound-sample-replacement-ownership-trace-gd14884"></a>
### Sound sample replacement ownership trace (GD14884)

Traced the public `SetDTAttrsA()` route into the Sound datatype's `OM_SET` and `parsetaglist()`. A newly created instance defaults `FreeSampleData` to TRUE. Replacing `SDTA_Sample` or `SDTA_LeftSample` overwrites `id->Sample` without retaining or freeing the old buffer; `OM_DISPOSE` only frees the current sample and right-channel pointer. Thus replacing an owned sample on a non-continuous object leaks the old allocation. Added GD14884 as a public-API conditional finding; no checked-in sample-replacement caller was found. The Sound body already has full-body credit, so no path/LOC increment. No sample was replaced or allocation measured; source-only.

More non-seekable handler caller reconciliation (GD14887 added; 2026-11-05; targeted caller/error-path pass, no body/path/LOC credit): traced More's `OpenFile()` seek/read/close branch (`workbench/utilities/More/more.c:351-399`) through DOS `Seek()`/`InternalSeek()` (`rom/dos/seek.c:34-41,83-91`; `rom/dos/internalseek.c:18-35`) and the console handler's positive `ACTION_SEEK` reply (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:1211-1215`). The returned `DOSTRUE` plus `ERROR_ACTION_NOT_KNOWN` becomes position 1 and the one-byte input length. Expanded the same caller finding after tracing the pipe-handler producer: an unimplemented `ACTION_SEEK` hits its default reply `0` plus `ERROR_ACTION_NOT_KNOWN` (`workbench/fs/pipe/pipe-handler.c:346-352`), while Shell's selected pipe helper establishes a named reader endpoint by opening `PIPE:*`, calling `NameFromFH()`, then opening that name for reading (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Pipe.c:115-123`); `OpenPipe()` resolves the existing name into a single reader endpoint (`workbench/fs/pipe/pipecreate.c:95-139,167-209`). More consequently treats that stream as zero bytes and sends a zero-length read. If the pipe is empty but its writer remains open, the request waits for data; `CheckWaiting()` completes it when data arrives but moves zero bytes (`pipesched.c:149-167,211-229`). More then closes its reader (`pipecreate.c:333-353`); enough later output can fill the pipe buffer and leave the writer request pending because the closed reader no longer drains it (`pipesched.c:171-181`). The console path's one-byte read and close behavior remain traced above; the finding now covers both handler statuses. Active `#MM-` rules select More through `workbench-utilities`, which is a prerequisite of `workbench-complete`. No console input, pipe data, seek, or build was used; source-only.

<a id="skip-back-console-script-caller-trace-gd14888"></a>
Skip `/BACK` console-script caller trace (GD14888 added; 2026-11-05; targeted caller/path pass, no body/path/LOC credit): read the `Skip` documentation and full backward-search control flow (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Skip.c:25-30,65-147`) and verified the command is in both the shell-command and built-in resource source lists (`workbench/c/shellcommands/mmakefile.src:1-39,55-98`). Traced `Execute` opening the supplied path and replacing `cli_CurrentInput` when invoked from the standard input (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Execute.c:108-122`); `Execute CON:` therefore passes `Skip`'s `cli_CurrentInput != cli_StandardInput` script-only gate (`Skip.c:75-80`) with a console-backed input. `/BACK` flushes then attempts a beginning seek but discards its result, and the following line scan continues on the same input (`:90-98,128-144`); the console handler does not implement `ACTION_SEEK` (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:1211-1215`). A matching earlier label cannot be revisited, so subsequent input is consumed while the scan waits for that label or EOF. Added GD14888 as a caller defect separate from GD14887's More file-size assumption. No console stream or command was run; source-only.

GD14888 Shell dispatch and non-seekable input expansion (2026-11-05; finding retained; no new body/path/LOC credit): traced both `Execute CON:` and a named `Execute PIPE:` source through Shell. Shell classifies any distinct current input as script input (`workbench/c/Shell/Shell.c:47,51-63`), reads it through `readLine()` (`readLine.c:54`), and closes/restores it at end-of-stream (`Shell.c:159-177`). The console handler rejects seek; the pipe handler has no seek case and returns zero plus `ERROR_ACTION_NOT_KNOWN` by its default (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:1211-1215`; `workbench/fs/pipe/pipe-handler.c:346-352`). Shell's pipe setup establishes the reader path through `NameFromFH()` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Pipe.c:115-123`). In each case `Skip /BACK` discards the seek result and the scan consumes only forward input. Re-read `Execute.c` argument-injection failure handling and its selected Shell `RunCommand()` caller (`Shell.c:555-599`); the error is propagated and no separate incorrect command result or input ownership defect was established. The complete Execute/Skip body credits remain the earlier 2026-11-03 entries. No command, console input, pipe data, allocation failure, or build was run; source-only.

DOS `ACTION_SEEK` unsupported-reply producer census for GD14887/GD14888 (2026-11-05; targeted whole-tree handler search; no body/path/LOC credit): searched selected handler sources for `ACTION_SEEK` dispatch and `ERROR_ACTION_NOT_KNOWN` response pairs. The console handler is the only checked handler that answers an unsupported action with positive `DOSTRUE` (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:1211-1215`); the pipe handler's unknown-action default instead replies with zero plus the error (`workbench/fs/pipe/pipe-handler.c:346-352`). Both nonnegative values are passed back by `InternalSeek()`, and More consumes them as one-byte and zero-byte lengths respectively. Port, speak, debug and hosted emulation handlers use `DOSFALSE` for unknown actions (`workbench/fs/port/port-handler.c:485-488`; `workbench/fs/speak/speak-handler.c:916-919`; `workbench/fs/debug/debug-handler.c:162-165`; `arch/all-hosted/filesys/emul_handler/emul_handler.c:1364-1368`). This producer search is scoped to checked-in selected handlers and does not claim external handler coverage. No seek packet or filesystem was used; source-only.

VMware SVGA LUT-write pixel-width and LUT-null lead dispositions (2026-11-06; no new GD or body/LOC credit): rechecked `PutImageLUT()`'s missing three-byte case and direct `pixlut->pixels` access against both bitmap constructors and the selected public `WritePixelArray8()` route (`vmwaresvga_bitmap_common.c:347-399`; `vmwaresvga_onbitmapclass.c:144-157`; `vmwaresvga_offbitmapclass.c:91-111`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:699-713`). On-screen VMware bitmaps use the fixed 32-bpp framebuffer (four bytes per pixel). Offscreen bitmaps derive storage as one byte for depth <=8, two for depth 9-16, and four for depth >16; none uses three-byte storage. Thus the absent 24-bit branch is unreachable for these VMware bitmap classes. The checked `WritePixelArray8()` path synthesizes and supplies a LUT from the HIDD bitmap's `HIDD_BM_PIXTAB` when the caller provides none; displayable bitmap construction allocates or inherits that table. No selected trigger for a NULL LUT reaching this override was established. No bitmap operation or build was run; source-only.

X11 synchronous notification caller closeout (2026-11-06; no new GD or path/LOC credit): reread all five `X11DoNotify()` callers in `x11gfx_displayclass.c` and `x11gfx_onbitmap.c`, the helper in `x11.h`, the worker notification dispatch and MapNotify reply path in `x11.c`, and the only task-kill sender in `x11_init.c`. Each caller uses a one-shot private `CreateMsgPort()` reply port and consumes the reply before deleting it. The deliberately deferred `NOTY_MAPWINDOW` notification is placed on `nmsg_list` and replied by the matching MapNotify event; the ordinary dispose notification is issued only after the constructor's map wait returns. The worker kill path is only used when `initclasses()` fails, and `initclasses()` only obtains the pixel-format attribute base, so no in-tree synchronous notification caller is active in that rollback path. No independent pending-reply hang established beyond existing GD6107's close-display/task-shutdown race. Source-only; no X server operation or build.
X11 framebuffer mode-resize failure propagation closeout (2026-11-06; no new GD or path/LOC credit): traced the remaining reply-port allocation site in `X11BM_SetMode()` through `X11BM__Root__Set()`. If the mode is already the current size and mapping is not delayed, the helper returns success without a message; otherwise a failed `CreateMsgPort()` returns `FALSE`, which the root Set method propagates before superclass mutation as required by the mode-ID attribute contract. A successful notification updates cached dimensions only after the event task's synchronous reply. No independent state or ownership defect established. No mode change or allocation failure was run; source-only.

GD14898 angle-storage correction and caller-path recheck (2026-11-06; supersedes the signed-minimum renderer claim in the earlier coverage note; no body/LOC credit): checked `MUI_ImageSpec_intern.gradient.angle` and confirmed it is `UWORD`, not `ULONG` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/imspec_intern.h:93-95`). Confirmed the independent deterministic narrowing: the parser accepts `-1`/`65536` through `StrToLong()` and assigns them to the 16-bit field, while truecolor drawing uses the resulting nonnegative field and `% 360`/fast paths (`imspec_gradientdraw.c:510-612`). MUI gradient accumulator overflow derivation and caller trace (GD14899 added; 2026-11-06; no body/LOC credit): for angle 180, the draw helper selects `yw = -height`, then the 180-degree branch sets `ystart = height` and transforms `ys` to zero (`workbench/libs/muimaster/imspec_gradientdraw.c:375-415`). With conventional `sin(pi)`/`cos(pi)` conversion this yields `vy=0`, `vx=255`, `r=0`; the first-row accumulator `r - yw * vx * y` with `y=height` computes `255*height^2`. At 3,000 rows this is 2,295,000,000 for `vx=255` and remains 2,286,000,000 for `vx=254`, above 32-bit signed `INT_MAX`; endpoints 0..2999 fit the helper's `WORD` arguments. Traced scaled/tiled mode-0 calls from `zune_imspec_draw()` and the selected Image class through show/draw and the truecolor-depth flag (`imspec.c:858-883`; `classes/image.c:433-440,539-544`; `classes/window.c:512-515`). This is distinct from GD9657's 135-degree zero denominator. No large image caller or truecolor gradient was exercised; practical reachability remains conditional. Source-only.

EraseRect selected layer-lock/backfill caller closeout (2026-11-06; no new GD or body/LOC credit): re-read `rom/graphics/eraserect.c:63-102` and traced its layered path through `DoHookClipRects()` and `_CallLayerHook()` (`rom/hyperlayers/dohookcliprects.c:67-209`; `basicfuncs.c:110-162`). `EraseRect()` holds `LockLayerRom()` while `DoHookClipRects()` takes `LockLayer()` on the same `Layer.Lock`; both wrappers call `ObtainSemaphore()`, and their API contracts explicitly allow same-task nested locking, with one matching unlock per acquisition (`rom/graphics/locklayerrom.c:22-63`; `rom/hyperlayers/locklayer.c:19-58`; `rom/graphics/unlocklayerrom.c:22-59`). The helper releases its nested lock before `EraseRect()` releases the outer lock. The default `LAYERS_BACKFILL` hook is NULL and `_CallLayerHook()` handles it by clearing the clipped bitmap area; `LAYERS_NOBACKFILL` exits before helper locking and still reaches the outer unlock. No independent lock leak or deadlock established. Existing inclusive-endpoint behavior is already represented by GD's EraseImage caller finding. External RastPort validity, arbitrary custom backfill behavior, and target rendering remain open; no graphics operation or build was run. Source-only.

OpenWindow BorderRPort versus system-gadget cleanup ownership (GD14900/GD10127 overlap check; 2026-11-06; no new finding or LOC credit): compared `intui_OpenWindow()`'s failed extra-port branch with the outer `OpenWindow()` failure label and system-gadget failure branch (`rom/intuition/openwindow.c:1088-1097,1201-1228,1514-1520,1643-1654`; `rom/intuition/closewindow.c:459-488`). In the BorderRPort case, `intui_CloseWindow()` performs layer/RastPort/pointer teardown but does not free the `IntWindow`; the outer `failexit` owns and frees that struct, and `driver_init_done` remains false, so it does not call the helper a second time. This is distinct from GD10127, where public `CloseWindow()` frees the window before outer failure cleanup accesses it. GD14900's NULL dereference still occurs before the outer cleanup; no extra double-free finding established. No allocation failure or window operation was induced; source-only.

OpenWindow synchronous driver-action failure-edge reconciliation (GD10127 and GD14900 retained; 2026-11-06; no new finding or LOC credit): enumerated every `goto failexit` in the outer `OpenWindow()` implementation and the corresponding `int_openwindow()` error exits (`rom/intuition/openwindow.c:622-713,931,1041,1088-1097,1201-1228,1390-1654`). Before the driver action, failures are owned by the outer cleanup. A false action result leaves `driver_init_done` false; the system-gadget failure arm reaches public `CloseWindow(w)` and frees the window before outer `failexit` reads/frees it (GD10127), while the BorderRPort failure arm directly calls `intui_CloseWindow()` and faults on its NULL port before outer cleanup frees `w` (GD14900). There are no `goto failexit` edges after successful driver initialization; later optional gadget/layout/pointer calls do not return failure into this cleanup label. This confirms the two distinct rollback routes and does not establish a third double-cleanup case. No allocation failure or window operation was induced; source-only.

Vulkan loader instance-version output follow-up (GD14910 added; 2026-11-06; targeted caller/callback trace; no new path/LOC credit): re-read `vkEnumerateInstanceVersion()` at `workbench/hidds/vulkan/vulkan_loader.c:270-288`, the public HIDD message field (`vulkan_hidd.h:1252-1257`), and the class callback (`vulkan_class.c:953-961`). The loader reads the caller's `*pApiVersion` into a local before passing its address to a callback whose field is output-only; a normal client may supply an uninitialized output scalar, making the read undefined before the callback writes. The no-HIDD fallback writes Vulkan 1.0 directly and skips the read. The official Vulkan reference describes `pApiVersion` as output and permits only a valid pointer. Added GD14910, scoped to successful loader initialization with a HIDD object. No API call or build was run; source-only.

Screen-buffer alloc/free caller and error-path recheck (2026-11-06; GD4763/GD5422 retained; no new finding or LOC credit): re-read `rom/graphics/allocdbufinfo.c`, `freedbufinfo.c`, `changevpbitmap.c`, `rom/intuition/allocscreenbuffer.c`, `freescreenbuffer.c`, and `changescreenbuffer.c`; searched all maintained `AllocDBufInfo`, `FreeDBufInfo`, `ChangeVPBitMap`, and `FreeScreenBuffer` calls. Intuition is the only in-tree allocator/disposer client for DBufInfo. `AllocScreenBuffer()` checks both DBufInfo allocations and unwinds its ScreenBuffer on failure; its internally allocated bitmap path frees the bitmap if allocation fails. When freeing the currently displayed owned buffer, `FreeScreenBuffer()` submits a restore swap and waits for the restore DBufInfo safe message before freeing the ScreenBuffer's own DBufInfo/bitmap; this recheck did not establish a separate early-free defect in that wrapper. The public direct `FreeDBufInfo()` API has no in-tree client that frees a pending record, so no external-client misuse is promoted. Reconfirmed `ChangeVPBitMap()` ignores `MakeVPort()`'s status and still queues completion, retaining GD4763's selected AmigaVideo rebuild-failure path; the shared pending-list race remains GD5422. No screen, bitmap allocation failure, VBlank, or concurrency interleaving was run; source-only.

Each checks or converts the nonzero status and avoids the subsequent full display reload on failure. The one live direct graphics caller is `ChangeVPBitMap()` (`rom/graphics/changevpbitmap.c:66-105`), which ignores the result and continues into display reload/completion; this is already GD4763. The apparent `SetRGB4()` call is in an entirely commented legacy block (`rom/graphics/setrgb4.c:61-99`). `MrgCop()` documents and assumes prepared viewports; its `GfxLookUp()` dereference follows that API precondition and no new selected caller violation was established here. No VPort allocation failure, display rebuild or graphics operation was run; source-only.


GD5919 selected display-backend failure qualification (2026-11-06; no new finding or LOC credit): compared generic `Display::MakeViewPort()` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:1861-1866`), P96 (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/p96gfx/p96gfx_hiddclass.c:817-831`), and AmigaVideo (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1214-1259`). The generic superclass and P96 override return `MVP_OK`; AmigaVideo returns `MVP_NO_MEM` when allocating its per-viewport state or replacement copper list. Independently, `MakeVPort()` can fail creating the planar HIDD wrapper (`rom/graphics/makevport.c:132-171`) before the backend callback. Therefore the `HIDD_ViewPortData` leak remains generic to later `MakeVPort()` failure after VPD allocation, while backend-confirmed post-wrapper failure is specific to the selected AmigaVideo path. Added this definite, conditional AmigaVideo state-object leak to GD5919. The existing finding already scopes the owned-wrapper leak as conditional and does not assert P96 failure. Found that GD5919 had a detailed report section but no AROS.md index entry; restored the link and summary. No backend setup, allocation failure, display operation, or build was run; source-only.

Graphics font open/close/extension path full-body pass (2026-11-06; no new GD): read all 131 `cloc 2.06` C code lines in `rom/graphics/openfont.c`, `closefont.c`, and `extendfont.c`, then checked them against `AddFont()`/`RemFont()` and the font-extension hash helpers. `OpenFont()` holds `fontsem` and calls `ExtendFont()`, which obtains the same semaphore recursively; Exec's `InternalObtainSemaphore()` increments `ss_NestCount` when the current task already owns it, so this is not a self-deadlock. The nested hash-table semaphore is released before return; font-list iteration/accessor increment and removal/accessor decrement share the font semaphore and local `Forbid()` protection. `ExtendFont()` releases partially allocated extension/tag state on the checked failure paths, and `CloseFont(NULL)` is explicitly harmless. No independent font-list or extension defect established in these bodies. Direct maintained caller search found Intuition, diskfont, Workbench and datatype clients, but their per-call ownership/error paths are not closed here. No font was opened, closed, allocated, or rendered; source-only.

QuickPart pending-operations Scrollgroup caller correction (GD9458; no new finding or path/LOC credit; 2026-11-07): derived the MinMax chain for the second `ScrollgroupObject` in QuickPart (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_Main.c:509-517`). It contains a virtual vertical group with one `QPOpGrp`; that row fixes its height at 60 and is a horizontal group (`QP_ccOpGrp.c:72-95`). Each pending operation is also fixed at 50x60 (`QP_ccOperation.c:108-120`), and the row adds a Rectangle spacer whose maximum width is `MUI_MAXMAX` (`rectangle.c:176-220`). Horizontal-group MinMax therefore yields a maximum height of 60 and unbounded maximum width, while its minimum width grows with the operation children; Virtgroup preserves the child minimum dimensions for Scrollgroup (`group.c:1930-1949`). This supplies the asymmetric maxima in GD9458 when enough pending operations make minimum width exceed 60. A vertical bar can be required when the 60-pixel row is taller than the remaining viewport; if that bar reduces the width below the row's minimum, the wrong `virt_maxheight` upper clamp can then suppress the horizontal bar. The conditional source-level trigger is now established in a maintained, explicitly buildable QuickPart target (`mmakefile.src:22-33`), but no layout/runtime outcome or default-image inclusion was checked. The first QuickPart drive-pane Scrollgroup still depends on dynamic drive-row constraints and remains open. No QuickPart layout or build was run; source-only.

Graphics color-font raster width and long-string bounds recheck (GD14929 added; no body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-07): followed `Text()`'s color-font dispatch (`rom/graphics/text.c:70-88`) through `ColorFontBasedText()` and `TextExtent()` (`text.c:559-593`; `textextent.c:80-123`). Both keep proportional horizontal positions/extrema in signed `WORD`; the renderer narrows raster row stride and per-glyph `wx` to `WORD`, then computes `raster + wx` without checking the glyph interval (`text.c:617-654`). For an in-range positive text count and proportional font whose advances exceed 32,767 (e.g. 32,767 two-pixel glyphs), compilers that retain low 16 bits on out-of-range signed-word conversions can produce a negative `wx` and writes preceding the raster allocation. Added GD14929 with the conversion behavior explicitly qualified because C defines such signed narrowing as implementation-defined; no target compiler result or maintained long-string caller was established. Existing GD9833 concerns a different signed-width boundary in BltPattern; GD2716 was a separate Text datatype path and withdrawn after selected-build reachability failed. No string, font, allocation, or build was used; source-only.

<a id="adddatatypes-exclusion-pattern-capacity-gd14931"></a>
AddDataTypes fixed exclusion-pattern capacity and matcher caller trace (GD14931 added; no source-body/LOC credit; 2026-11-07): revisited the previously grouped fixed-literal caller at `workbench/c/AddDataTypes.c:267`. Counted the source pattern `#?.(info|dbg|backdrop|ppc|arm|i386|x86_64)` and its emitted representation: one `P_ANY`, one dot, `P_ORSTART`, 31 alternative literal bytes, six `P_ORNEXT` tokens, `P_OREND`, and NUL, totaling 42 bytes. `EXCL_LEN` is 18, so `ExclPat[2*EXCL_LEN+3]` has only 39 bytes (`AddDataTypes.c:170-171,211-215`). `patternParse()` returns `ERROR_BUFFER_OVERFLOW` before writing beyond its destination (`rom/dos/patternmatching.c:439-442,633-635`); `main()` ignores the return and `ScanDirectory()` later passes the buffer to `MatchPatternNoCase()` (`AddDataTypes.c:262-268,436-477`). The final `P_OREND` was reserved in the destination's last byte, so the earlier claim that the matcher scans without a closing token across the struct was incorrect. The emitted final alternative is only `x86_`, and the matcher fails to exclude `.x86_64` files. Added GD14931 and its master-index link. This supersedes the earlier classification that this fixed-literal caller had no issue. No command, directory scan, or build was run; source-only.

ColorWheel `SetDrMd()` caller trace (2026-11-07; no new GD or body/LOC credit): checked all three maintained calls in the selected `workbench/classes/gadgets/colorwheel/support.c` body. `RenderWheel()` uses `SetDrMd(&temprp, JAM1)` on its private offscreen RastPort before clearing the bitmap (`:581-650`), so this does not alter the caller's RastPort. `DrawKnob()` sets JAM1 on the supplied port immediately before its own knob fills (`:833`); `DrawDisabledPattern()` likewise sets JAM1 before setting the fill pattern and painting the disabled region (`:877-944`). In the latter, both the allocated-raster and fallback branches clear `AreaInfo`/`TmpRas` as applicable and remove the area pattern before return; the allocation-failure path falls through to the rectangular fill. No state leak or error-path omission was established for these callers. Other `SetDrMd()` sites remain for caller-by-caller review; no GUI or drawing operation was run; source-only.
GradientSlider `SetDrMd()` caller trace (2026-11-07; no new GD or body/LOC credit): followed all three calls in `workbench/classes/gadgets/gradientslider`. `GradientSlider__GM_RENDER()` renders the frame, background and knob into the class-owned `data->trp`/`savebm` RastPort (`gradientsliderclass.c:290-460`); its background and `DrawKnob()` set JAM1 only for their following fills (`:418`; `support.c:455-494`). <a id="mui-list-clear-active-entry-lifetime-gd14938"></a>
MUI List active-Off and clear-path caller audit (GD14938 corrected; 2026-11-07; targeted shared-class/caller pass, no new file or LOC credit): the initial report incorrectly treated `entries[-1]` as out of bounds. Rechecked the backing allocation and found `ENTRY_TITLE == -1` is an allocated title slot (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/list.c:33,520-558,1310-1318`), so setting Active Off by itself does not establish that defect; the Locale map and Poplist string-miss routes are withdrawn as triggers. The actual issue is in `List__MUIM_Clear()` (`:2266-2294`): it frees all `ListEntry` objects first, then sets Entries to zero and Active Off if a row was selected. The active setter (`:1510-1537`) keeps the old index and writes `data->entries[old]->flags` in the writable branch, establishing a write through the freed entry pointer. Traced the selected Zune Preferences public-screen picker: its `PopPublicScreenStrObjFunc()` clears and rebuilds its `InputListFrame` on popup open (`workbench/prefs/Zune/systemp.c:72-125,147-155`); on successful close, `PopPublicScreenObjStrFunc()` reads the selected row into the StringObject, and the close hook invokes it (`:128-140`; `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/popobject.c:227-234`). Reopening after a selection therefore reaches the clear path with the old row active. The target is explicitly buildable via `workbench/prefs/Zune/mmakefile.src:8-17`; no default image inclusion is claimed. No GUI, list operation, or build was run; source-only.

Every resulting value matches a table row, so this data set does not produce a separate `tz == -1`/`timezone_table[-1]` path. Nine non-hour city offsets are truncated by the current conversion; this remains the previously reported GD14609 behavior. No city selection or timezone operation was run; source-only.

GD14931 parser-overflow consequence recheck (2026-11-08; finding corrected; no body/path/LOC credit): re-read `patternParse()`'s reverse marker reservation and AddDataTypes' `StackVars` layout. When the 39-byte `ExclPat` fills, the saved `P_OREND` remains at its last byte; the 42-byte fixed output cannot emit the full final alternative or its in-array NUL. The whole `StackVars` object is zeroed before parsing, and on the selected naturally aligned layouts the following byte is padding, so the earlier claim of an unbounded OR scan into arbitrary adjacent fields was unsupported. The actual retained defect is a truncated final `x86_` alternative, which does not exclude `.x86_64` names; whether this makes AddDataTypes register an unwanted item depends on a matching valid datatype file. Corrected GD14931's report/index wording and lowered visible-impact confidence. No command, file scan, or build was run; source-only.

A colon suffix is converted with `atoi()` (`devices.c:49-55`); `findHDs()` raises its default scan count of eight to any larger positive value and runs `for (i = 0; i < maxunits; i++)` synchronously (`harddisks.c:86-90`). It continues after `OpenDevice()` failures, allocating/initializing and then freeing a node for each unavailable unit (`:92-138`). Thus a mistakenly large but representable suffix makes preference loading or the Add Device callback spend an impractical time probing units and can leave the application unresponsive. Nonpositive/invalid-to-zero values fall back to eight. Replaced the earlier disposition that found no independent defect; no cap or validation was found. No device, preferences file, GUI action, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="decoration-singleton-check-publish-gd4436"></a>Decoration singleton check/publish race (GD4436 restored and scope corrected; 2026-11-08; existing body credit retained): traced the selected `workbench-c-decoration` target from its active `workbench-c` aggregate through `main()`'s `Forbid(); FindPort("Decorator"); Permit();` sequence and delayed `AddPort()` (`workbench/c/Decoration/mmakefile.src`; `decoration.c:227-262`). Exec's Forbid is processor-local on ExecSMP, while FindPort and AddPort take separate port-list lock sections (`rom/exec/forbid.c:47-50`; `rom/exec/findport.c:48-57`; `addport.c:50-75`); AddPort permits duplicate names. Two launchers can therefore pass the check before either publishes on SMP, or after a task switch between Permit and later AddPort on a uniprocessor. Both successful instances detach and enter the long-lived receive loop (`decoration.c:258-286`; the Ctrl-C branch does not stop it). Name lookup then selects one duplicate, leaving the other service and its old state alive. Corrected the prior ExecSMP-only summary to include the uniprocessor preemption window. No process, port, display or schedule was run; source-only.

Vulkan-Hpp Device mapping result recheck (GD14913 strengthened; 2026-11-08; `workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_handles.hpp:11132-11400`, local implementation `vulkan_funcs.hpp:1113-1131`, result helpers `vulkan.hpp:7459-7480,7527-7560`; no new file/path/LOC credit): re-traced the enhanced `Device::mapMemory()` output through `resultCheck()` into `ResultValue<void *>`. Under `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS`, `resultCheck()` delegates only to `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT_ON_RESULT`; when configured away, the `ResultValue` constructor copies `pData` even when dispatch reports failure. The Khronos command reference describes `ppData` as the mapped pointer returned on success and lists mapping, host/device memory, unknown, and validation failures without defining a failure output value. Therefore an implementation that leaves `ppData` untouched on one of those errors triggers the indeterminate-pointer read. Updated GD14913 from pending contract review to an implementation-conditional finding; no particular driver behavior or runtime reproduction is claimed. Rechecked adjacent Device dispatch, queue, allocation/free/map, mapped-range, commitment, binding, and memory-requirement declarations and representative generated definitions; no other independent issue established. No Vulkan call, C++ instantiation, build or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

GD9615 `CopyBox` caller-boundary follow-up (2026-11-08; unresolved, no new GD or body/path/LOC credit): traced the selected generic `BltBitMap()` fallback through `int_bltbitmap()` (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:469-471,642-649`) and its caller-side RastPort clipping (`:118-180`), and traced the Compositor's visible-region calls (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:283-305,1281-1335`). GD9615 direct `HIDD_Gfx_CopyBox()` caller census extension (2026-11-08; unresolved, no new GD or body/path/LOC credit): enumerated every direct in-tree call and traced the remaining non-compositor callers. Graphics `BltBitMap()` reaches CopyBox only after bitmap/layer clipping (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:118-180,642-649`); IntelGMA and Nouveau compositor updates intersect with the screen-visible rectangle before copying (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_compositorclass.c:286-312`; `workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_compositorclass.c:290-316`); CGFX `ScalePixelArray()` calls through `DoRenderFunc()`, whose render helper intersects with the RastPort/layer clip (`workbench/libs/cgfx/scalepixelarray.c:197-223`; `rom/graphics/cgx_support.c:47-58`; helper in `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:88-180`). The generic display Show and SDL Show paths instead forward whole bitmap/framebuffer extents (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:40-84,1204-1248`; `arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdlgfx_hiddclass.c:490-503`); the generic Show path sets the framebuffer mode from the bitmap ModeID but does not clamp the new copy dimensions to the framebuffer dimensions (`gfx_displayclass.c:1232-1248`). AROS `OpenScreen()` can retain raster dimensions larger than its viewport (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1144-1158,1532-1539`), so that full-extent call can exceed the visible area; whether each selected direct backend clips it remains dependent on the backend implementation/API. No source-only proof of an out-of-bounds consequence for a selected backend was established in this pass; GD9615 remains unresolved, with the display Show extent contract now a specific caller boundary to close. GD14854 generic software-cursor size trigger refinement (existing finding strengthened; no new finding ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-08): traced the generic `SetCursorShape()` allocation and full-image extraction through the signed-`WORD` `HIDD_BM_GetImage()` implementation, then followed `cursor_Draw()`'s visible-area clipping into the save-under transfer. A 32,768×32,769 shape makes the ARGB and, for a four-byte native pixel format, save-under size products wrap to 131,072 bytes on 32-bit builds. Initial full-shape extraction gets negative signed extents and writes no pixels, overlapping GD10435; a later 1024×768 clipped save has positive extents and writes 3,145,728 bytes into the undersized save-under buffer. This establishes GD14854's conditional out-of-bounds write independently of the uninitialized ARGB case. The ordinary public raw-data `SetPointer()` dimensions cannot express 32,768, so this exact trigger remains dependent on a large HIDD bitmap supplied through the private bitmap path or an external HIDD client. No bitmap, allocation, or cursor operation was created; source-only.

GD14854 maintained cursor-input caller trace (scope refined; no new finding ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-08): searched tracked `POINTERA_BitMap` callers and traced the selected Intuition route for V39 pointer preferences. `SetIPrefs(IPREFS_TYPE_POINTER_V39)` reads its caller-supplied `IPointerPrefs.BitMap`, creates a PointerClass object, and installs it (`rom/intuition/setiprefs.c:135-156`; `pointerclass.c:60-103`; `misc.c:274-320`); later screen pointer installation reaches `MonitorClass__MM_SetPointerShape()` and the generic HIDD `SetCursorShape()` (`monitorclass.c:1954-1960`). Static Zune pointer producers use 7-16 pixel widths, while the ordinary raw-data `SetPointer()` API has signed-WORD dimensions and cannot express 32,768. No checked-in producer supplies an exceptionally large V39 bitmap, so GD14854 remains conditional on caller input and successful large bitmap/save-under allocation. No preferences payload, bitmap, cursor, or allocation was created; source-only.

<a id="setiprefs-pointer-v39-construction-failure-gd14973"></a>SetIPrefs V39 pointer construction failure caller trace (GD14973 added; no new body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-08): traced `IPREFS_TYPE_POINTER_V39` from `SetIPrefs()` through PointerClass construction and `InstallPointer()`. PointerClass returns NULL when `AllocSpriteDataA()` or `CreateSharedPointer()` fails; the V39 branch passes that result to `InstallPointer()` without a check. `InstallPointer()` immediately queries `POINTERA_SharedPointer`, and `OOP_GetAttr()` dispatch dereferences `OOP_OCLASS(object)`. `SetIPrefs()` acquired `LockIBase()` before the switch and only unlocks at its common exit, so the NULL dispatch fault leaves the base lock held. Compared V37 handling, which checks the pointer before installation. Added GD14973 and its index link. No allocation failure, preference update, or Intuition operation was run; source-only.
GD14973 caller reachability refinement (no finding/body/path/LOC change; 2026-11-08): traced the maintained `workbench/c/iprefs` pointer-preference producer. Its `PointerPrefs_Handler()` creates a bitmap from either an `ID_PNTR` record or a decoded pointer image; `InstallBitMap()` packages that bitmap in `IPointerPrefs` and calls `SetIPrefs()` (`pointerprefs.c:22-34,43-77,120-158`). This confirms an in-tree V39 caller on the explicitly buildable `workbench-c-iprefs` target. The utility's aggregate edges are commented (`mmakefile.src:27-29`), so this is not presented as a default-image path. PointerClass can still fail during the subsequent sprite bitmap/shared-pointer allocations; the V39 caller does not check the returned object before `InstallPointer()`. No preference file, allocation failure, or update was run; source-only.
GD10435/GD14854 IPrefs dimension propagation correction (existing findings strengthened; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-08): refined the earlier V39 caller trace by reading `PointerClass__OM_NEW()` and `AllocSpriteDataA()` tag defaults through the generated sprite bitmap dimensions. `workbench/c/iprefs/pointerprefs.c` parses `pp_Width/pp_Height` as UWORD, initializes a planar `BitMap`, and calls `SetIPrefs()` through `InstallBitMap()`. The V39 pointer tags do not supply `POINTERA_WordWidth`; PointerClass therefore derives the sprite width from `BMA_WIDTH` rounded to a 16-pixel word and lets `AllocSpriteDataA()` default output height to the source height. A well-formed 32,768×32,769 PNTR bitmap can thus reach the generic cursor path, subject to successful source and converted bitmap allocations. This corrects the preceding note's implication that PointerClass always reduces the V39 shape to a 16-pixel width. The route is in the explicit `workbench-c-iprefs` target, whose aggregate edge remains commented; no matching large preference file was found. No preference file, bitmap, allocation, or cursor operation was used; source-only.

GD5731 Intuition pointer-position caller trace (2026-11-08; existing finding strengthened; no new ID or source/LOC credit): traced the maintained input path from `inputhandler.c`'s display-bound clamp and `IntuitionBase->MouseX/MouseY` publication through `SetActiveMonPointerPos()` into `MonitorClass__MM_SetPointerPos()` and `HIDD_Display_SetCursorPos()` (`rom/intuition/inputhandler.c:1514-1618`; `rom/intuition/misc.c:21-32`; `monitorclass.c:81-105,1895-1903`; `monitorclass_intern.h:49-50`). The positions are signed-WORD fields in Intuition/InputEvent but are copied into the monitor's ULONG fields without an additional 16,384 clamp. Thus a host mode width/height of at least 16,385 can admit coordinates missed by CursorFB's `CFB_REMOVE_ALL` rectangle. Existing SDL/X11 mode-supplier constraints and the headless cap remain as stated in GD5731; actual host mode availability and an overlapping whole-bitmap operation remain conditional. No pointer movement, display query or drawing operation was run; source-only.

GFX histogram pool-size overflow disposition (GD5728 scope; 2026-11-08; no new GD or source/LOC credit): re-read the histogram constructor's `sizeof(BMHistEntry) * width * height` `CreatePool()` size and its per-entry allocation method (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_histogramclass.c:37-80,102-140`). Bitmap dimensions are read as `IPTR`; on 32-bit builds the maximum UWORD dimensions can overflow this product, but the value sets only `Pool.PuddleSize`. A later `AllocPooled()` allocation grows a puddle to at least the single requested block plus allocator overhead (`rom/exec/memory.c:1080-1157`), so product wrap alone does not establish an undersized block write; at most it can change default pool growth/fragmentation. The selected constructor's cached method offsets remain GD5728, and there is no separate pool-size finding. No large bitmap, histogram, or allocation was created; source-only.

Vulkan-Hpp batch owner-reserve census (GD10227 expanded; 2026-11-08; no body/path/LOC credit): rechecked every `.reserve()` site in `vulkan_funcs.hpp` and `vulkan_raii.hpp` against the existing ownership-transfer trace. All 22 generated-function reserves populate raw handles before a destination `UniqueHandle` vector; all remain under GD10227. The RAII header has 13 reserve sites: 11 follow native creation/allocation into owning wrappers, including `Device::createDataGraphPipelinesARM()` (`:27126-27146`); these can lose created objects if owner-vector allocation throws. The other two reserve lists are physical-device and display query results (`:15128,18726`), not newly created native resources, so reserve failure there does not add this leak. Added the ARM data-graph RAII instance to GD10227; its accepted non-success partial-output case remains separate in GD10225. No allocation failure, Vulkan call, or build was run.

AmigaVideo's display class inherits `CLID_Hidd_Display` and does not override `Show()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo.conf:46-47,55-120`); the generic GFX HIDD defaults an unset framebuffer type to Direct (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:172-174,766-784,861-869`; `gfx_displayclass.c:434`), allowing the generic display copy path to dispatch to AmigaVideo. This establishes an in-tree backend callsite carrying UWORD sizes, but no maintained caller creating/showing a displayable bitmap wider or taller than 32,767 was found. Replaced the earlier blanket statement that no in-tree direct HIDD caller was found with this narrower reachability qualification. No display or blit was run; source-only.

`GetRGB32()` selected Zune pointer-color caller recheck (2026-11-08; no new GD or body/LOC credit): traced the maintained texteditor, betterstring, nlist, and nbalance pointer helpers that read colormap entries 17–19 (`workbench/classes/zune/{texteditor,betterstring,nlist}/mcc/Pointer.c`; `nbalance_mcc/Pointer.c`). These consumers receive the active Intuition window screen colormap. `OpenScreen()` requests at least 32 entries even when the screen bitmap depth yields fewer colors (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1393-1406`), so the checked paths do not hit `GetRGB32()` out-of-range access for ordinary AROS-created screens. The unchecked vector remains conditional on other callers supplying a custom short ColorMap or invalid index; this does not widen GD4292/GD9578 beyond their separately traced triggers. No screen or color query was run; source-only.

GradientSlider high-pen conversion caller trace (GD15065 added; 2026-11-08; no body/LOC credit): traced the public UWORD `GRAD_PenArray` through `GradientSlider__OM_SET()`, `GM_RENDER`, `DrawGradient()`, the CyberGraphics truecolor branch, and `TrueDitherV/H()` into `GetRGB32()`/`color_get()` (`compiler/include/gadgets/gradientslider.h:20-21`; `gradientsliderclass.c:142-166,424-432`; `support.c:262-334,340-402`; `rom/graphics/getrgb32.c:58-70`; `color_support.c:87-104`). A valid UWORD index 32768 is narrowed to signed WORD before promotion to ULONG on common two's-complement toolchains, producing an out-of-range palette read. `GetColorMap()` can represent 32,769 entries, but ordinary OpenScreen-created maps do not provide that size; the trigger requires a client-installed custom map and matching pen list. Added GD15065 with that scope. No rendering or build was run; source-only.

GradientSlider producer impact recheck for GD15065 (2026-11-08; no new finding or body/LOC credit): searched all in-tree `GRAD_PenArray` producers. The ColorWheel demo starts with pens 1 and 2 and obtains two exclusive pens from its ordinary OpenScreen ColorMap (`developer/demos/colorwheel.c:42,122-128`); Gamma's test uses pens 2/1 and obtains its red/green/blue pens from its own OpenScreen (`developer/debug/test/intuition/gamma.c:43-48,170-178`); Coloradjust uses DrawInfo shine/shadow pens plus one obtained screen pen (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/coloradjust.c:566-583`); ReqTools obtains a short gradient palette from the active screen map (`workbench/libs/reqtools/palettereq.c:1085-1115`). These checked callers do not create/install a ColorMap above 32,767 entries. No in-tree producer establishes the combined high-pen/custom-map condition; GD15065 remains a public component candidate with conditional external reachability. Source-only.
